units.tr: 8. The law concerning the suspected virginity of a woman whom a man has taken as wife. Deut. 22, verse 13.

units.la: 9. Lex zelotypiae. Num. 5.
units.tr: 9. The law of jealousy. Num. 5.

units.la: 10. Lex de vxore repudiatâ non iterum ducendâ. Deut. 24. verf. 1.
units.tr: 10. The law that a woman who has been divorced may not be taken again. Deut. 24, verse 1.

units.la: 11. Lex de vitandis coniugiis cum infidelibus. Deut. 7. verf. 3.
units.tr: 11. The law on avoiding marriages with unbelievers. Deut. 7, verse 3.

units.la: 12. Lex de muliere captiuâ ducendâ in vxorem. Deut. 21. verf. 10. 14.
units.tr: 12. The law on taking a captive woman as wife. Deut. 21, verses 10, 14.

units.la: 13. Lex de iure primogenituræ, si aliquis habuerit duas vxores. Deut. 21. v. 15.
units.tr: 13. The law on the right of the firstborn when a man has two wives. Deut. 21, verse 15.

units.la: 14. Lex de femine fratri excitando. Deut. 25. v. 5.
units.tr: 14. The law on raising up seed for a brother. Deut. 25, verse 5.

units.la: 15. Lex de connubiis inter contribules. Num. 36. v. 8.
units.tr: 15. The law on marriages within the tribe. Num. 36, verse 8.

units.la: 16. Lex de vitiatâ virgine ducendâ. Exod. 22. verf. 16. Deut. 22. v. 28.
units.tr: 16. The law on taking a violated virgin as wife. Exod. 22, verse 16; Deut. 22, verse 28.

units.la: 17. Lex de filiâ sacerdotis fornicante. Leu. 21.v.9[?].
units.tr: 17. The law concerning the daughter of a priest who commits fornication. Lev. 21, verse 9[?].

units.la: 18. Lex de filiâ non prostituendâ. Leu.19.v.29.
units.tr: 18. The law that a daughter is not to be prostituted. Lev. 19, verse 29.

units.la: 19. Lex de non ferendo meretricem & scortatorem. Deut.23.v.17.
units.tr: 19. The law that a prostitute and a whoremonger are not to be tolerated. Deut. 23, verse 17.

units.la: 20. Lex de mercede meretricis non adducendâ in domum Iehouæ. Deut. 23.v.18.
units.tr: 20. The law that the wages of a prostitute are not to be brought into the house of Jehovah. Deut. 23, verse 18.

units.la: 21. Lex de immunitate illius, qui duxit recens uxorem. Deut.24.v.5.
units.tr: 21. The law on the exemption of a man who has recently taken a wife. Deut. 24, verse 5.

units.la: 22. Lex de uxore apprehendente verenda viri. Deut.25. verf. 11.
units.tr: 22. The law concerning a wife who seizes a man's private parts. Deut. 25, verse 11.

units.la: 23. Lex de faciendis fimbriis in quatuor oris operimenti. Deut.22.v.12.
units.tr: 23. The law concerning making tassels on the four corners of a garment. Deut. 22, verse 12.

units.la: 24. Lex de non mutando vestitu & habitu sexus. Deut. 22.verf.5.
units.tr: 24. The law forbidding the changing of dress and the habit of the sexes. Deut. 22, verse 5.

units.la: Ad octauum præceptum.
units.tr: For the eighth commandment.

units.la: 1. Lex de pœnâ furti, quod est plagium, abigeatus, sacrilegium &c. simplex vel violentum. Exod. 21. v. 17. c. 22. v. 1. 2. 4. Deut. 24. v. 7.
units.tr: 1. Law concerning the penalty for theft, whether it is kidnapping, cattle-rustling, sacrilege, etc., whether simple or violent. Exod. 21. v. 17. c. 22. v. 1. 2. 4. Deut. 24. v. 7.

units.la: 2. Lex de fodiente & non cooperiente cisternam. Exod. 21. v. 33.
units.tr: 2. Law concerning one who digs a cistern and does not cover it. Exod. 21. v. 33.

units.la: 3. Lex de boue cornupetâ damnum dante proximo. Exod. 21. v. 35.
units.tr: 3. Law concerning an ox that gores and causes loss to a neighbour. Exod. 21. v. 35.

units.la: 4. Lex de immisso iumento in agrum alterius. Exod. 22. verf. 5.
units.tr: 4. Law concerning a beast turned loose into another's field. Exod. 22. verf. 5.

units.la: 4. Lex de igni, quo aliquis læsit agrum proximi fui. Exod. 22. v. 6.
units.tr: 4. Law concerning fire by which someone harms the field of his neighbour. Exod. 22. v. 6.

units.la: 5. Lex de boue aut asino inimici reducendo. Exod. 23. v. 4. Deut. 22. v. 1.
units.tr: 5. Law concerning returning the ox or ass of an enemy. Exod. 23. v. 4. Deut. 22. v. 1.

units.la: 6. Lex de commodato. Exod. 22. v. 14.
units.tr: 6. Law concerning loan for use. Exod. 22. v. 14.

units.la: 7. Lex de depositò. Exod. 22. verf. 7. 9. 10. Levit. 6. verf. 2. Num. 5. v. 6.
units.tr: 7. Law concerning deposit. Exod. 22. verf. 7. 9. 10. Levit. 6. verf. 2. Num. 5. v. 6.

units.la: 8. Lex de iusto & iniusto pondere & mensurâ. Levit. 19. v. 35. Deut. 25. v. 13.
units.tr: 8. Law concerning just and unjust weight and measure. Levit. 19. v. 35. Deut. 25. v. 13.

units.la: 9. Lex de non transferendo terminos. Deut. 19. ver. 14. & [?] 27. v. 17. 10. Lex de ingrediente vineam proximi fui. Deut. 23. verf.25.
units.tr: 9. Law concerning not moving boundaries. Deut. 19. ver. 14. & [?] 27. v. 17. 10. Law concerning one who enters the vineyard of his neighbour. Deut. 23. verf. 25.

units.la: 11. Lex de vsuris. Exod. 22. v. 25. Leuit. 25. v. 35. Deut. 23. verf.19.
units.tr: 11. Law concerning usury. Exod. 22. v. 25. Leuit. 25. v. 35. Deut. 23. verf. 19.

units.la: 12. Lex de mendicis misericorditer tractandis. Deut. 15. verf.7.
units.tr: 12. Law concerning treating beggars with mercy. Deut. 15. verf. 7.

units.la: 13. Lex de pignore. Exod. 22. verf.26. Deut. 24. verf.6. 10.17.
units.tr: 13. Law concerning pledges. Exod. 22. verf. 26. Deut. 24. verf. 6. 10. 17.

units.la: 14. Lex de anno remissionis. Deut. 15. v. 1.
units.tr: 14. Law concerning the year of release. Deut. 15. v. 1.

units.la: 15. Lex de non transferendâ possessione de tribu ad tribum aliam. Num. 36. v. 6.
units.tr: 15. Law concerning not transferring a possession from one tribe to another tribe. Num. 36. v. 6.

units.la: 16. Lex de transferendâ hæreditate ad filiam in casu non existentium filiorum, Num. 27. v. 8.
units.tr: 16. Law concerning transferring an inheritance to a daughter in the case where there are no sons. Num. 27. v. 8.

units.la: 17. Lex de venditione & redemtione terræ. Leuit. 25. verf.23.
units.tr: 17. Law concerning the sale and redemption of land. Leuit. 25. verf. 23.

units.la: 18. Lex de venditione & redemtione domus. Leu. 25. verf.29.
units.tr: 18. Law concerning the sale and redemption of a house. Leu. 25. verf. 29.

units.la: 19. Lex de redemtione urbium & domorum Leuitarum. Leu. 25. v. 32. 34.
units.tr: 19. Law concerning the redemption of the cities and houses of the Levites. Leu. 25. v. 32. 34.

units.la: 20. Lex de non ferendis mendicis. Deut. 15. v. 4.
units.tr: 20. Law concerning not oppressing beggars. Deut. 15. v. 4.

units.la: 21. Lex de messe & vindemiatione. Leuit. 19. ver. 9. & 23. v. 22. Deut. 24. v. 19.
units.tr: 21. Law concerning the harvest and the vintage. Leuit. 19. ver. 9. & 23. v. 22. Deut. 24. v. 19.

units.la: 22. Lex de septimo anno sabbatario. Exod. 23. verf. 10. Leu. 25. v. 2. 20.
units.tr: 22. Law concerning the seventh, sabbatical year. Exod. 23. verf. 10. Leu. 25. v. 2. 20.

units.la: 23. Lex de mercenario benignè tractando. Leu. 19. v. 13. Deut. 24. v. 14.
units.tr: 23. Law concerning treating the hired servant kindly. Leu. 19. v. 13. Deut. 24. v. 14.

units.la: 24. Lex de non obturando os boui trituranti. Deut. 25. verf. 4.
units.tr: 24. Law concerning not muzzling the ox that treads out the grain. Deut. 25. verf. 4.

units.la: 25. Lex de manumissione. Exod. 21. verf. 2. Leu. 25. verf. 39. Deut. 15. v. 12.
units.tr: 25. Law concerning manumission. Exod. 21. verf. 2. Leu. 25. verf. 39. Deut. 15. v. 12.

units.la: 26. Lex de seruitute Leu. 25. v. 44.
units.tr: 26. Law concerning servitude. Leu. 25. v. 44.

units.la: 27. Lex de redemptione serui, qui se vendidit peregrino. Leuit. 25. v. 47.
units.tr: 27. Law concerning the redemption of a servant who has sold himself to a foreigner. Leuit. 25. v. 47.

units.la: Ad præceptum nonum.
units.tr: For the ninth commandment.

units.la: Leges de iudiciis sunt appendices huius præcepti, hocmodo
units.tr: The laws concerning judgments are appendices to this commandment, in this way:

units.la: 1. Lex de constituendis iudicibus. Deut. 16. v.18.
units.tr: 1. Law concerning the appointment of judges. Deut. 16. v. 18.

units.la: 2. Lex de vitandâ iniquitate & profopolepfiâ in iudicio. Exod. 23. verf. 3. 8. Leuit. 19. v.15. 35. Deut. 1. verf. 17. c. 16. verf. 19.
units.tr: 2. Law concerning avoiding iniquity and partiality in judgment. Exod. 23. verf. 3. 8. Leuit. 19. v. 15. 35. Deut. 1. verf. 17. c. 16. verf. 19.

units.la: 3. Lex de non peruertendo iudicio pauperis, peregrini, pupilli, vel viduæ. Exod. 23. verf. 6. Deut. 10. v. 18. c. 14. v. 17. c. 27. v. 19.
units.tr: 3. Law concerning not perverting the judgment of the poor, the stranger, the orphan, or the widow. Exod. 23. verf. 6. Deut. 10. v. 18. c. 14. v. 17. c. 27. v. 19.

units.la: 4. Lex de non approbando iniquam sententiam maioris vel potentioris partis in iudicio. Exod. 23. v. 2.
units.tr: 4. Law concerning not approving an unjust sentence of the greater or more powerful part in a judgment. Exod. 23. v. 2.

units.la: 5. Lex de falso testimonio. Exod. 23. ver. 1. Deut. 17. v. 4. c. 19. v. 18. Leuit. 19. v. 16.
units.tr: 5. Law concerning false witness. Exod. 23. ver. 1. Deut. 17. v. 4. c. 19. v. 18. Leuit. 19. v. 16.

units.la: 6. Lex de distinctione iudiciorum. Exod. 18. verf. 22. Deut. 1. v. 17.
units.tr: 6. Law concerning the distinction of judgments. Exod. 18. verf. 22. Deut. 1. v. 17.

units.la: 7. Lex de consulendo sacerdote in re dubiâ. Deut. 17. verf. 8.
units.tr: 7. Law concerning consulting the priest in a doubtful matter. Deut. 17. verf. 8.

units.la: 8. Lex de numero testium in re capitali. Num. 35. v. 30. Deut. 17. v. 6. c. 19. v. 15.
units.tr: 8. Law concerning the number of witnesses in a capital case. Num. 35. v. 30. Deut. 17. v. 6. c. 19. v. 15.

units.la: 9. Lex de pœnâ falsi testis. Deut. 19. v. 16.
units.tr: 9. Law concerning the penalty for a false witness. Deut. 19. v. 16.

units.la: 10. Lex de ordine seruando in lapidatione. Deut. 17. verf. 7.
units.tr: 10. Law concerning the order to be observed in stoning. Deut. 17. verf. 7.

units.la: 11. Lex de non occidendo innocente. Exod. 23. verf. 7. Deut. 27. v. 25. c. 24. v. 16.
units.tr: 11. Law concerning not killing the innocent. Exod. 23. verf. 7. Deut. 27. v. 25. c. 24. v. 16.

units.la: 12. Lex de non absoluendo homicidâ. Num. 35. v. 31.
units.tr: 12. Law concerning not acquitting a murderer. Num. 35. v. 31.

units.la: 13. Lex de occidendo reo mortis. Deut. 13. v. 8. Leuit. 20. verf. 4.
units.tr: 13. Law concerning putting to death a guilty person. Deut. 13. v. 8. Leuit. 20. verf. 4.

units.la: 14. Lex de non relinquendo suspenso in ligno. Deut. 21. verf. 22.
units.tr: 14. Law concerning not leaving the hanged man on the tree. Deut. 21. verf. 22.

units.la: 15. Lex de non redimendo anathemate. Leuit. 27. v. 29.
units.tr: 15. Law concerning not redeeming the devoted thing (anathema). Leuit. 27. v. 29.

units.la: Solent hoc loco colligere exempla actionum & procefsuum iudicialium ex sacris literis: ubi primò se offert processus iudicialis diuinus cum primis parentibus. Gen. 3. & cum Aharone & Mariâ contra Moisen. Num. 12. Deinde sunt duo processus humani legitimi, alter Iosuæ contra Achanum Iof. 7. alter Salomonis, inter duas mulieres meretrices 1. Reg. 3. Denique sunt tres processus humani illegitimi: videl. contra Nabothum i.Reg.21. contra Christum. Matth.26.27. & contra Stephanum. Act.6. & 7.
units.tr: Under this head they commonly gather examples of judicial actions and proceedings from Holy Scripture. Here first there presents itself the divine judicial process with the first parents, Gen. 3. and with Aaron and Miriam against Moses, Num. 12. Then there are two lawful human proceedings: one of Joshua against Achan, Josh. 7. the other of Solomon between two harlots, 1 Kings 3. Finally there are three unlawful human proceedings: namely against Naboth, 1 Kings 21. against Christ, Matt. 26, 27. and against Stephen, Acts 6 and 7.

units.la: Ad decimum praeceptum.
units.tr: For the tenth commandment.

units.la: Huc pertinent ea, quae in legibus forensibus secundae tabulae a nobis requiruntur affectuum compositionem. Explanationem harum legum vide in Harmonia Iohannis Caluini & Explanatione legum forensium Mosaicarum Wilhelmi Zepperi. Pertinet etiam huc Pauli Ricij tractatus de 613. Mosaicae legis mandatis.
units.tr: To this belong those things which we are required to observe in the civil laws of the second tablet, the regulation of the affections. For an explanation of these laws see John Calvin's Harmony and Wilhelm Zepper's Explanation of the Mosaic Civil Laws. Also belonging here is Paul Ricci's treatise on the 613 commandments of the Mosaic law.

units.la: XXX. MEDICINA SACRA.
units.tr: XXX. SACRED MEDICINE.

units.la: I. Medicina sacra est facultas bene medendi, ex sacris literis collecta. Mederi autem est idem hoc loco, quod curare valetudinem. Aliás sumitur strictè, vt in illo Christi Matth.9.ver.12. Qui valent, non egent medico.
units.tr: I. Sacred medicine is the skill of healing well, drawn from the Holy Scriptures. Here "to heal" means the same as "to care for health." Elsewhere the word is taken in a narrower sense, as in Christ's words in Matt. 9:12: "Those who are well have no need of a physician."

units.la: II. Eius partes duae sunt, Hygieina & Therapeutica.
units.tr: II. It has two parts: Hygieina and Therapeutica.

units.la: III. Hygieina est prima medicinae pars de sanitate tuenda.
units.tr: III. Hygieina is the first part of medicine, concerned with preserving health.

units.la: IV. Causae sanitatem tuentes sunt prima, vel secunda.
units.tr: IV. The causes that preserve health are either first or secondary.

units.la: V. Causa prima, sanitatem conferuans, est Deus. Hic enim valetudinem prosperam confert & aufert. Deut.8. verf.3.4.c.28.v.21.22. Psal.38. Matth.10.v.30. Nostri ergo muneris est precibus quotidianis & pia vita impetrare benedictionem a Deo Patre per Christum in virtute Spiritus sancti, & cogitare illud,
units.tr: V. The first cause, which preserves health, is God. For he both grants and withholds good health. Deut. 8:3, 4; 28:21, 22; Ps. 38; Matt. 10:30. It is therefore our task, by daily prayer and a godly life, to obtain the blessing of God the Father through Christ in the power of the Holy Spirit, and to keep in mind that saying:

units.la: Orandum est vt sit mens sana in corpore sano.
units.tr: One must pray for a sound mind in a sound body.

units.la: VI. Causa secunda, conseruans sanitatem, est partim diæta, partim remedium præseruatiuum. Hinc hygieina diuiditur in Diæteticam, & Prophylacticam.
units.tr: VI. The secondary cause, which preserves health, is partly diet and partly preventive remedy. Hence hygieina is divided into dietetics and prophylactics.

units.la: VII. Diæta est ratio vitus hominis fani; & consistit in hisce tribus: nempe in recto alimentorum vsu, in motu, & in quiete.
units.tr: VII. Diet is the regimen of a healthy person's life, and it consists of three things: the right use of food, movement, and rest.

units.la: VIII. Rectus alimentorum vsus cernitur in legitima ipsorum quantitate, qualitate, ordine, & tempore.
units.tr: VIII. The right use of food lies in its proper quantity, quality, order, and time.

units.la: IX. Quantitas alimentorum ea est tenenda, quæ medium tenet inter excessum & defectum. Nam cibo potuque immoderato grauantur corda Luc.21. v.34. & in vino immodice sumto est ἀσωτία. Eph.5.v.18. Eccles.31.v.34. sed pauculo vino corrigitur imbecillitas ventriculi 1. Tim.5. v.23. & fructulo cibi fulcituranimus. Iudic. 19.v.5. & moderato vino exhilaratur cor Psal.104.v.15. Eccles.31.v.30. & seqq. & quicunque edit ad satietatem, non vero vltra satietatem, valet animo & corpore. Deut.8.v.10. Vide infra Hygiasticam sacram.
units.tr: IX. The quantity of food is to be kept at the mean between excess and deficiency. For hearts are weighed down by immoderate food and drink Luke 21:34, and wine taken to excess brings dissolute living Eph. 5:18; Ecclus. 31:34. Yet a little wine corrects the weakness of the stomach 1 Tim. 5:23, and a little food sustains the spirit Judg. 19:5, and wine taken in moderation gladdens the heart Ps. 104:15; Ecclus. 31:30ff.. Whoever eats to satisfaction, but not beyond it, is well in mind and body Deut. 8:10. See below, in the Sacred Hygiastics.

units.la: X. Qualitas alimentorum ita nobis est exploranda, vt non solùm nouerimus ipsorum facultates in genere, sed etiam in specie obseruemus, quæ nobis inprimis bene conueniant. Nam non tantùm cauere debemus, ne assumamus illa, quæ sua-natura sunt noxia 2.Reg.4.vers.38.& seqq. sed etiam vt eligamus alimenta nostro temperamento & quoque palato conuenientia. Gen.21.v.5.6. Luc.24.v.42. Esa.7.v.15. 1.Sam.14. v.28. Habenda etiam est ratio ætatis Gen.21.vers.7. 1.Sam.1. v.23. item status & conditionis nostræ Dan.1.ver.12.16. Sic Iohannes Baptista neque comedit, neque bibit more vulgari Matt.11.v.18. Comedit siquidem acrides, id est, locustas edules, & mel siluestre. Matt.3.& Marc.1. At vero Christus promiscuo more vixit. Matt.11. v.19. Quia nempe status & vocatio Iohannis requirebat eiusmodi austeram vi. &tus [?] rationem, Christi non item.
units.tr: X. The quality of food must be so examined by us that we not only know its properties in general but also observe in particular which foods agree best with us. For we must take care not only to avoid those things that are harmful by their very nature 2 Kings 4:38ff., but also to choose foods suited to our constitution and to our palate Gen. 21:5, 6; Luke 24:42; Isa. 7:15; 1 Sam. 14:28. Account must also be taken of age Gen. 21:7; 1 Sam. 1:23, and likewise of our station and condition Dan. 1:12, 16. So John the Baptist neither ate nor drank in the ordinary manner Matt. 11:18. He ate locusts, that is, edible locusts, and wild honey Matt. 3; Mark 1. Christ, however, lived in a common manner Matt. 11:19. The reason is that the station and calling of John required such an austere way of life, but Christ's did not.

units.la: XI. Ordo legitimus in assumendis alimentis congruere debet cum rectâ ratione & consuetudine. In Scripturis hic ordo est admodum simplex, ideoque naturae convenientissimus. Vide Gen. 18. v. 6. 7. 8. Iohan. 6. v. 11.
units.tr: XI. The lawful order in taking food ought to agree with right reason and custom. In the Scriptures this order is very simple, and therefore most suited to nature. See Gen. 18:6, 7, 8; John 6:11.

units.la: XII. Tempus in assumendis alimentis debet esse certum & statum. Ut enim omnia suum habent tempus Eccl. 3. sic etiam refectio naturae nostrae per cibum & potum. Deut. 8. v. 10.
units.tr: XII. The time for taking food ought to be fixed and regular. For as all things have their time Eccl. 3, so also the refreshment of our nature by food and drink does Deut. 8:10.

units.la: XIII. Motus coducens valetudini complectitur exercitia animi & corporis. Exercitia animi consistunt in moderatione affectuum, ut illi sint secundum naturam, & proinde illam conservent. Ita enim est, ut sapiens dicit Prov. 17. v. 22. Animus latus bene medicinam facit, Spiritus autem fractus exsiccat ossa. Exercitia corporis consistunt in moderata corporis agitatione, quae excitat, auget atq; custodit calorem naturalem, alimentorum digestione adiuvat, membra corroborat, & superfluitates expellit: item in lotione manuum, pedum, & totius corporis. Gen. 18. Exod. 2.
units.tr: XIII. Movement conducive to health embraces exercises of mind and body. The exercises of the mind consist in moderating the passions, so that they are according to nature and thereby preserve it. For it is as the wise man says: Prov. 17:22: A cheerful mind makes good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones. The exercises of the body consist in moderate bodily activity, which stirs up, increases and preserves natural heat, aids the digestion of food, strengthens the limbs, and expels superfluities; likewise in washing the hands, feet and whole body. Gen. 18; Exod. 2.

units.la: XIV. Quies, postrema diaetae pars, est simplex, vel composita. Quies simplex est, cum interdiu à laboribus & exercitijs tum animi, tum corporis, aliquantisper vacamus, per certa quaedam intervalla, idque sedendo, stando, moderate ambulando, vel iacendo. Iohan. 6. v. 10. Quies composita est somnus moderatus, qui diei non potest quantopere conducat ad sanitatis tuitionem. Eccl. 31. v. 2.
units.tr: XIV. Rest, the last part of diet, is either simple or compound. Simple rest is when during the day we are for a while free from labours and exercises, both of mind and body, for certain intervals, and this by sitting, standing, walking moderately, or lying down. John 6:10. Compound rest is moderate sleep, which contributes greatly, as is well known, to the preservation of health. Ecclus. 31:2.

units.la: XV. Remedium praeservatiuum est, quo natura corporis integra, praeservatur à morbo. Hoc quò fuerit simplicius, eò melius.
units.tr: XV. A preservative remedy is one by which the integrity of the body's nature is kept safe from disease. The simpler this is, the better.

units.la: XVI. Therapeutica est secunda medicinae pars de restituenda sanitate.
units.tr: XVI. Therapeutics is the second part of medicine, concerned with restoring health.

units.la: XVII. Hic requritur cognitio morbi, & applicatio remedij. Hinc Therapeutica dividitur in Pathologicam & Pharmaceuticam.
units.tr: XVII. Here a knowledge of the disease and the application of a remedy are required. Hence therapeutics is divided into pathology and pharmacy.

units.la: XVIII. Cognitio morbi debet institui a priori & posteriori. Ita nimirum ut causam morbi moralem, quae est peccatum; & naturalem, quae est qualitas morbifica in corpore, indagemus: & huius causae effecta & symptomata observemus. 2.Reg.20.v.1.&seqq. Variorum morborum hinc inde in S. literis fit mentio: puta phrenitidis, surditatis, pestis, febris, paralyseos, asthmatis, podagrae, epilepsiae, apoplexiae, hydropis, lepra, pustularum, caecitatis &c. Leuit.16. Deut.28. Psal.38. & 91. Iob.32.v.20. 2.Chron.16.v.12. Marc.9.v.17. & seqq. 1.Sam.4. v.18. & 25. v.37.38. Matth.18. v.14.15. Luc.14.v.2. Leuit.13. Matth.9.v.27.
units.tr: XVIII. The knowledge of disease must be pursued from cause and from effect. Namely, we must investigate both the moral cause, which is sin, and the natural cause, which is a morbid quality in the body, and observe the effects and symptoms of this cause. 2 Kings 20:1ff. Various diseases are mentioned here and there in the Holy Scriptures: for example, phrenitis, deafness, plague, fever, paralysis, asthma, gout, epilepsy, apoplexy, dropsy, leprosy, pustules, blindness, etc. Lev. 16; Deut. 28; Ps. 38 and 91; Job 32:20; 2 Chron. 16:12; Mark 9:17ff.; 1 Sam. 4:18 and 25:37, 38; Matt. 18:14, 15; Luke 14:2; Lev. 13; Matt. 9:27.

units.la: XIX. Applicatio remedij debet esse pia, & circumspecta. Pietatis est, non confidere in medicina, ut fecit Asa. 2.Chron.16.v.12. neque diabolum aut ministros eius consulere, ut fecit Ahafias 2.Reg.1.v.2.&seqq. sed a solo Deo pendere 2.Reg.20.v.1.&seqq. ad preces se convertere Jacob.5.v.14.15. medicum honorare Eccles.38. v.1.2.3.4.9.10.12. & si ille faciat suum officium, neq; tamen nos sanet, meminisse, ipsum nihil posse citra benedictionem Dei 1.Cor.3.v.7. Marc.5.v.26. Luc.8.v.43. Circumspectionis partes aliae sunt in aegro, aliae in medico. Et aeger quidem debet esse circumspectus in tempestive adhibendo medicum peritum, & in parendo ipsius monitis. Medicus autem non contentus peritia rei medicae, prudentiae quoque studebit, ut exploratis omnibus circumstantiis recte adhibeat remedia, quorum syluulam ex sacris collectam hic proponimus.
units.tr: XIX. The application of a remedy ought to be godly and circumspect. It belongs to piety not to trust in medicine, as Asa did 2 Chron. 16:12, nor to consult the devil or his ministers, as Ahaziah did 2 Kings 1:2ff., but to depend on God alone 2 Kings 20:1ff., to turn to prayer James 5:14, 15, to honour the physician Ecclus. 38:1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 10, 12, and, if he does his duty and yet does not heal us, to remember that he can do nothing apart from the blessing of God 1 Cor. 3:7; Mark 5:26; Luke 8:43. The parts of circumspection are different in the patient and in the physician. The patient indeed ought to be circumspect in calling in a skilled physician in good time, and in obeying his instructions. The physician, however, not content with skill in the medical art, will also apply prudence, so that, having examined all the circumstances, he may apply the remedies rightly; a small collection of these, gathered from the Scriptures, we set out here.

units.la: Exod.15.v.25. Deus ostendit Mosi lignum, quo edulcatae sunt aquae amarae.Sic medicus interdum necesse habet Potiones idoneas praeparare.
units.tr: Exod. 15:25. God showed Moses a tree by which the bitter waters were made sweet. So the physician sometimes needs to prepare suitable draughts.

units.la: Leuit. 13. Lepra certis signis cognoscitur, & leprosus a consortio hominum separatur. Hinc discet medicus, morbos fere habere sua signa, & morbis contagiosis infectos esse ita tractandos, ne alij inficiantur.
units.tr: Lev. 13. Leprosy is recognised by certain signs, and the leper is separated from the company of men. Hence the physician learns that diseases generally have their own signs, and that those infected with contagious diseases must be so treated that others are not infected.

units.la: Num. 21. v. 9. 10. Qui serpentem æneum fuerunt intuiti, sanitatem receperunt. Hoc remedium, vtpote singulare & extraordinarium, non est trahendum in regulam.
units.tr: Num. 21:9, 10. Those who looked upon the bronze serpent received health. This remedy, being singular and extraordinary, is not to be drawn into a rule.

units.la: 2. Reg. 4. v. 41. Elisæus cibum mortiferum emendat. Sic medici est habere sua alexipharmaca.
units.tr: 2 Kings 4:41. Elisha corrects deadly food. So it is the physician's part to have his own antidotes.

units.la: 2. Reg. 20. ver. 7. Esaias palatham ficuum imposuit ulceri Hiskiæ. Confer Esa. 38. v. 21. Hoc medicamentum, vt pote naturale & licitum, medicus potest imitari.
units.tr: 2 Kings 20:7. Isaiah laid a poultice of figs on Hezekiah's ulcer. Compare Isa. 38:21. This medicine, being natural and lawful, the physician may imitate.

units.la: Psal. 45. v. 9. Vestimenta sponsi vncta dicuntur myrrhâ, [?]antalis, casiâque, id est, unguento confecto ex istis præstantissimis aromatibus. Hinc medicus discit, medicamenta composita non esse contemnenda, vt nonnulli faciunt. Item, medicamenta odorifera suum habere vsum.
units.tr: Ps. 45:9. The garments of the bridegroom are said to be scented with myrrh, [?]antalis and cassia, that is, with an ointment compounded from these most excellent aromatics. Hence the physician learns that compound medicines are not to be despised, as some do. Likewise, fragrant medicines have their use.

units.la: Matth. 8. v. 3. & 8. Christus sanat verbo. Sic alibi passim in historia euangelica. Hæc sanatio fuit miraculosa, & proinde ἀμίμητῳ[?].
units.tr: Matt. 8:3, 8. Christ heals by a word. So elsewhere throughout the gospel history. This healing was miraculous, and therefore inimitable [ἀμίμητῳ].

units.la: Marc. 6. v. 13. apostoli multos ægrotos sanant[?] oleo. Hoc oleum fuit symbolum mirificæ virtutis, non vero medicamentum. Est itaque κακοζηλία[?], si quis hoc factum velit imitari. Idem iudicium est de loco Luc. 5. v. 14.
units.tr: Mark 6:13. The apostles anointed many sick people with oil. This oil was a symbol of wonderful power, not a medicine. It is therefore misplaced zeal [κακοζηλία] if anyone wishes to imitate this action. The same judgement applies to the passage Luke 5:14.

units.la: Luc. 10. v. 34. Samaritanus obligat vulnera illius hominis, qui inciderat in latrones, infundens oleum ac vinum. Vino mundata fuerunt vulnera, oleo mitigata. Hoc possunt imitari chirurgi.
units.tr: Luke 10:34. The Samaritan bound up the wounds of the man who had fallen among robbers, pouring in oil and wine. The wounds were cleansed by the wine and softened by the oil. Surgeons may imitate this.

units.la: Iohan. 19. v. 39. 40. corpus Christi obuoluitur linteis cum mistura aloës & myrrhæ. Quæ duo aromata singularem habent vim resistendi putredini. Unde ipsorum vsus est tempore pestis, & alias quoque ad purgandum noxios humores.
units.tr: John 19:39–40: the body of Christ is wrapped in linen cloths with a mixture of aloes and myrrh. These two spices have a singular power to resist putrefaction, and so they have been used in time of plague, and also elsewhere to purge harmful humours.

units.la: Tob. 6. v. 6. 19. &c. 11. v. 8. 10. describitur medicamentum ex pisce, quo Tobias iunior curauit cæcitatem parentis. Idem quoque fuit amuletum, quo dæmon fuit fugatus. Sed quidem rident hoc ceu fabulosum.
units.tr: Tobit 6:6, 19, etc.; 11:8, 10: a remedy made from a fish is described, with which the younger Tobias cured his father's blindness. It was also an amulet by which a demon was put to flight. But people laugh at this as a fable.

units.la: Solent etiam nonnulli ex Scripturis excerpere nomina quædam propria Dei & hominum, item versus integros vel mutilatos v. g. partem aliquam exc. 1. euangelij Iohannis, & conantur hoc modo prohibere vel etiam profligare morbos. Sed hic est abusus verbi Dei, quod destinatum est salutianimæ[?], non vero corporis, nisi quatenus illud adhibetur in legitimo usu prædicationis, precationis, & meditationis, ad benedictionem Dei pro salute animæ & corporis impetrandam.
units.tr: Many also are accustomed to pick out of Scripture certain proper names of God and of men, and likewise whole or mutilated verses (for example, some part of the first chapter of John's Gospel), and by this means they try to prevent or even drive out diseases. But this is an abuse of the word of God, which is intended for the salvation of the soul, not of the body, except insofar as it is used in the lawful practice of preaching, prayer and meditation, to obtain God's blessing for the salvation of soul and body.

units.la: XXXI.
units.tr: XXXI.

units.la: THEOLOGIA POSITIVA.
units.tr: POSITIVE THEOLOGY.

units.la: Theologia est doctrina reddens hominem sapientem & prudentem ad vitam æternam. Estque positiva, vel methodica.
units.tr: Theology is the teaching that makes a man wise and prudent unto eternal life. It is either positive or methodical.

units.la: Theologia positiua est ipsissima Scriptura sacra, sic dicta, quòd tradat meras positiones, hoc est, principia firmiter posita. Eiusmodi positiones hinc inde sparsæ sunt in Scripturis, & utiliter ad certa capita siue locos communes revocantur hoc pacto.
units.tr: Positive theology is Holy Scripture itself, so called because it delivers mere positions, that is, firmly laid down principles. Such positions are scattered here and there through the Scriptures, and they are usefully gathered under certain heads or common places in the following manner.

units.la: LOCUS I.
units.tr: LOCUS I.

units.la: De sacra Scriptura.
units.tr: On Holy Scripture.

units.la: 1. Scriptura est θεόπνευστος[?], id est, diuinitus inspirata.
units.tr: 1. Scripture is God-breathed [θεόπνευστος], that is, divinely inspired.

units.la: 2. Tim. 3. vers. 16. Tota Scriptura diuinitus est inspirata.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 3, vers. 16. All Scripture is divinely inspired.

units.la: 2. Petr. 1. vers. 21. Non voluntate hominis allata est olim prophetia; sed acti a Spiritu sancto locuti sunt sancti Dei homines.
units.tr: 2 Pet. 1, vers. 21. For prophecy never came by the will of man; but holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: 2. Scriptura est lucerna, id est, perspicua, & regula fidei & vitæ.
units.tr: 2. Scripture is a lamp, that is, clear, and the rule of faith and life.

units.la: Psal. 119. v. 105. Lucerna pedi meo verbum tuum est, & lux itinerimeo.
units.tr: Ps. 119, v. 105. Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.

units.la: 2. Petr. 1. v. 19. Habemus firmissimum sermonem propheticum: cui recte facitis quod attendatis velut lucerna splendenti in obscuro loco, vsque dum dies illucescat, & lucifer exoriatur in cordibus vestris.
units.tr: 2 Pet. 1, v. 19. We have also a more sure word of prophecy, whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts.

units.la: 2. Corinth. 4. v. 3. 4. Quod si tectum est euangelium nostrum, iis qui pereunt tectum est. In quibus deus huius seculi excaecauit mentes, nempe in infidelibus, ne irradiet eos lumen euangelij gloriæ Christi.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 4, v. 3, 4. But if our gospel is hidden, it is hidden to those who are perishing. In them the god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers, lest the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ should shine on them.

units.la: 3. Scriptura est perfecta.
units.tr: 3. Scripture is perfect.

units.la: Deut. 4. v. 2. Non addetis ad verbum hoc quod vobis loquor: nec auferetis ex eo.
units.tr: Deut. 4, v. 2. You shall not add to the word which I command you, nor take from it.

units.la: Gal. 1. v. 8. Etiamsi nos, aut angelus e cœlo annuntiauerit vobis prater id quod annuntiamus, anathema esto.
units.tr: Gal. 1, v. 8. But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel to you than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed.

units.la: 2. Timoth. 3. verf. 16. 17. Tota Scriptura diuinitus est inspirata, & vtilis ad doctrinam, ad redargutionem, ad correctionem, ad institutionem quæ est in iustitia: Vt perfectus sit homo Dei, ad omne opus bonum perfecte instructus. Confer Psal. 19. verf. 8.9.10.11.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 3, vers. 16, 17. All Scripture is divinely inspired and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work. Cf. Ps. 19, vers. 8, 9, 10, 11.

units.la: 4. Scriptura omnibus Christianis est legenda.
units.tr: 4. Scripture is to be read by all Christians.

units.la: Deuteronom. 6. v. 6. 7. 8. 9. Et erunt verba ista, quæ ego tibi præcipio hodie, in corde tuo: Eaque acute ingeres filiis tuis, ac loqueris de eis cum sedes domi tuæ, & cum ambulas per viam, cum cubas, & cum surgis: Etiam alligabis ea in signum manui tuæ, & erunt pro frontalibus inter oculos tuos: Denique inscribes ea-postibus domus tuæ, & portis tuis.
units.tr: Deut. 6, v. 6, 7, 8, 9. And these words, which I command you today, shall be in your heart. You shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, when you lie down, and when you rise up. You shall also bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes. And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.

units.la: Psalm. 1. verf. 2. Sed cuius oblectatio est in lege Iehoua; & qui de lege illius meditatur interdiu ac noctu. Confer Psal. 119.
units.tr: Ps. 1, vers. 2. But his delight is in the law of the LORD, and on his law he meditates day and night. Cf. Ps. 119.

units.la: Luc. 16. verf. 29. Habent Mosen & Prophetas: audiant illos.
units.tr: Luke 16, vers. 29. They have Moses and the Prophets; let them hear them.

units.la: 2. Timoth. 3. verf. 15. Teque à puero nouisse sacras literas.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 3, vers. 15. and that from childhood you have known the sacred writings.

units.la: 5. Scriptura dispari euentu legitur & auditur à piis & impiis.
units.tr: 5. Scripture is read and heard by the godly and the ungodly with different outcomes.

units.la: Rom. 1. v. 16. Non enim me pudet euangelij Christi. Potentia siquidem est Dei ad salutem cuiuis credenti.
units.tr: Rom. 1, v. 16. For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ; for it is the power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes.

units.la: 1. Cor. 1. v. 23. 24. Nos autem prædicamus Christum crucifixum, Iudæis quidem offendiculum, Græcis verò stultitiam: Ipsis autem vocatis, tum Iudæis tum Græcis, Christum Dei potentiam, ac Dei sapientiam.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 1, v. 23, 24. But we preach Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles, but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.

units.la: 2. Cor. 2. v. 15. 16. Nam Christi bona fragrantia sumus Deo, in iis qui seruantur, & in iis qui pereunt: His quidem odor mortis ad mortem: illis verò odor vitæ ad vitam. Confer 2. Cor. 4. v. 3.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 2, v. 15, 16. For we are to God the fragrance of Christ among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing: to the one a fragrance from death to death, to the other a fragrance from life to life. Cf. 2 Cor. 4, v. 3.

units.la: 2. Petr. 3. v. 16. In quibus (epistolis Pauli) sunt nonnulla difficilia intellectu, quæ indocti parumque stabiles detorquent, vt & reliquas Scripturas, suo ipsorum exitio.
units.tr: 2 Pet. 3, v. 16. In them (the letters of Paul) there are some things hard to understand, which the untaught and unstable distort, as they do the other Scriptures, to their own destruction.

units.la: LOCVS II. De Deo.
units.tr: LOCUS II. Of God.

units.la: 1. Deus reuera est.
units.tr: 1. God truly exists.

units.la: Psal. 14. v. 1. Dicit stultus cum animo suo, non est Deus.
units.tr: Ps. 14. v. 1. The fool says in his heart, There is no God.

units.la: Esa. 44. v. 1. Sic ait Dominus rex Israelis & vindex eius, Dominus exercituum: ego sum primus & vltimus, ac præter me nullus est Deus.
units.tr: Isa. 44. v. 6. Thus says the Lord, the King of Israel and his Redeemer, the Lord of hosts: I am the first and the last, and besides me there is no God.

units.la: Apoc. 1. v. 4. Gratia sit vobis & pax à Qui est, & Qui erat, & Qui venturus est.
units.tr: Rev. 1. v. 4. Grace be to you and peace from him who is, and who was, and who is to come.

units.la: 2. Deus est spiritus.
units.tr: 2. God is spirit.

units.la: Ioh. 4. v. 24. Deus est spiritus: & qui adorant eum, oportet vt spiritu ac veritate adorent.
units.tr: John 4. v. 24. God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.

units.la: 1. Tim. 1. v. 17. Regi æterno, immortali, inuisibili, soli sapienti Deo honor sit & gloria in secula seculorum, Amen.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 1. v. 17. To the eternal, immortal, invisible, only wise God be honour and glory for ever and ever, Amen.

units.la: 3. Deus nulli creaturæ potest assimilari.
units.tr: 3. God cannot be likened to any creature.

units.la: Esa. 40. v. 17. 18. Omnes gentes velut nihil sunt coram eo, minus nihilo & inanitate reputantur ei. Cui ergo assimilabitis Deum, & quam similitudinem comparabitis ei?
units.tr: Isa. 40. v. 17, 18. All nations are before him as nothing; they are counted by him as less than nothing and emptiness. To whom then will you liken God, or what likeness will you set up for him?

units.la: 4. Deus est vnus.
units.tr: 4. God is one.

units.la: Deut. 6. v. 4. Audi Israel; Dominus Deus noster Dominus vnus est.
units.tr: Deut. 6. v. 4. Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.

units.la: Esa. 44. v. 1. Sic ait Dominus rex Israëlis & vindex eius, Dominus exercituum: ego sum primus & vltimus, ac praeter me nullus est Deus.
units.tr: Isa. 44. v. 6. Thus says the Lord, the King of Israel and his Redeemer, the Lord of hosts: I am the first and the last, and besides me there is no God.

units.la: Eph. 4. v. 6. Vnus Deus & pater omnium, qui est super omnes, & per omnes, & in omnibus vobis.
units.tr: Eph. 4. v. 6. One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.

units.la: 5. Solus Deus est Iehoua, Iah, Eheieh, & Schaddai.
units.tr: 5. God alone is Jehovah, Jah, Eheieh, and Shaddai.

units.la: Exod. 6. v. 2. Nomine MEO Iehoua non cognitus sum illis.
units.tr: Exod. 6. v. 2. By my name Jehovah I was not known to them.

units.la: Psal. 118. v. 14. Robur meum & carmen Iah.
units.tr: Ps. 118. v. 14. The Lord is my strength and my song, Jah.

units.la: Exod. 3. v. 14. Dixit Dominus Mosi, Eheieh, qui sum: dixitque, ita dices filiis Israëlis, Eheieh misit me ad vos.
units.tr: Exod. 3. v. 14. God said to Moses, Eheieh, I am who I am; and he said, Thus you shall say to the children of Israel, Eheieh has sent me to you.

units.la: Gen. 17. v. 1. Ego אֵל שַׁדַּי [?] Deus omnipotens.
units.tr: Gen. 17. v. 1. I am El Shaddai [אֵל שַׁדַּי] [?], God Almighty.

units.la: 6. Deus viuit.
units.tr: 6. God lives.

units.la: Psal. 18. v. 47. Viuit Dominus & benedicta rupes mea.
units.tr: Ps. 18. v. 47. The Lord lives, and blessed be my rock.

units.la: Ier. 46. v. 18. Vt viuo ego, dictum regis illius, cuius nomen est Dominus exercituum.
units.tr: Jer. 46. v. 18. As I live, says the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts.

units.la: Apoc. 15. v. 7. Vnum ex quatuor animalibus dedit septem angelisphialas aureas, plenas irae Dei viuentis in secula seculorum.
units.tr: Rev. 15. v. 7. One of the four living creatures gave to the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God who lives for ever and ever.

units.la: 7. Deus est immutabilis, impatibilis, & immortalis.
units.tr: 7. God is unchangeable, impassible, and immortal.

units.la: Psal. 102. v. 27. 28. Ista (coeli & terra) peritura sunt: tu autem permanes, ista, inquam, omnia vt vestimentum veterascent, vt indumentum mutabis ea atque mutabuntur: tu vero idem es, & anni tui non finiuntur.
units.tr: Ps. 102. v. 27, 28. They (the heavens and the earth) will perish, but you remain; they will all grow old like a garment, and like a robe you will change them, and they will be changed; but you are the same, and your years will not end.

units.la: 1. Tim. 6. v. 15. 16. Quem temporibus suis ostendet ille beatus & solus Princeps, Rex illeregum, & Dominus dominorum: Qui solus habet immortalitatem, lucem habitans inaccessam, quem vidit nemo hominum, neque videre potest.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 6. v. 15, 16. Which the blessed and only Ruler will show in its own time, the King of kings and Lord of lords, who alone has immortality, dwelling in light unapproachable, whom no man has seen or can see.

units.la: Iacob. 1. v. 17. Omnis donatio bona, & omne perfectum donum est superne, descendens a patre luminum, apud quem non inest transmutatio aut conuersionis obumbratio.
units.tr: Jas. 1. v. 17. Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning.

units.la: 8. Deus est immensus, & proinde omnipraesens & incomprehensibilis.
units.tr: 8. God is immense, and therefore omnipresent and incomprehensible.

units.la: 1. Reg. 8. v. 27. An reuera habitaret Deus in terra? Ecce cœli ipsi & cœli cœlorum non capiunt te: quanto minus domus hæc, quam ædificaui?
units.tr: 1 Kings 8. v. 27. But will God indeed dwell on the earth? Behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain you; how much less this house which I have built?

units.la: Esa.66.v.1. Sic ait Dominus: Cœlum ipsum est solium meum, & terra scabellum pedum meorum: ubinam esset domus, quam ædificaueritis mihi? & ubinam locus quietis mea? Confer Act.7. vers.49.
units.tr: Isa. 66. v. 1. Thus says the Lord: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool; where then is the house that you would build for me, and where is the place of my rest? Compare Acts 7. v. 49.

units.la: Ierem.23[?].v.24. An non cœlum & terram ego impleo? Confer Psal.139.vers.7. & seqq.
units.tr: Jer. 23[?]. v. 24. Do I not fill heaven and earth? Compare Ps. 139. v. 7 and following.

units.la: Act.17.v.27.28. Deus profecto non longe abest ab vnoquoque nostrum. In ipso enim viuimus, mouemur, & sumus.
units.tr: Acts 17. v. 27, 28. Indeed God is not far from each one of us. For in him we live, and move, and have our being.

units.la: Psal.145.v.3. Magnum esse Iehouam & laudandum valde, imo magnitudini eius non esse peruestigationem.
units.tr: Ps. 145. v. 3. Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised, and his greatness is past finding out.

units.la: 9. Deus est æternus.
units.tr: 9. God is eternal.

units.la: Gen.21.v.33. Et inuocauit illic (Abraham) nomen Dei æterni.
units.tr: Gen. 21. v. 33. And there Abraham called upon the name of the eternal God.

units.la: Esa.44.v.6. Ego sum primus, & ego vltimus.
units.tr: Isa. 44. v. 6. I am the first, and I am the last.

units.la: Esa.57.v.15. Sic ait sublimis, cuius nomen est, Inhabitans æternitatem.
units.tr: Isa. 57. v. 15. Thus says the High and Lofty One, whose name is, He who inhabits eternity.

units.la: Rom.1.v.20. Inuisibilia Dei inde à creatione mundi ex rebus conditis intelliguntur & peruidentur: æterna videlicet eius cumpotentia, tum diuinitas.
units.tr: Rom. 1. v. 20. The invisible things of God from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood through the things that are made: namely his eternal power also, and divinity.

units.la: Apoc.1.v.18. Ego sum A & Ω, id est, principium & finis, dicit Dominus, id est, Qui est, & qui erat, & qui venturus est, ille, inquam, omnipotens. Confer cap.21.v.6.c.22.v.13.
units.tr: Rev. 1. v. 18. I am the Alpha and the Omega, that is, the beginning and the end, says the Lord, that is, he who is, and who was, and who is to come, the Almighty, I say. Compare Rev. 21. v. 6 and 22. v. 13.

units.la: 10. Deus est omniscius & omnisapiens, & proinde καρδιογνώστης[?].
units.tr: 10. God is all-knowing and all-wise, and therefore heart-knower [καρδιογνώστης].

units.la: 1.Sam.2.v.3. Deus notitiarum est Iehoua.
units.tr: 1 Sam. 2. v. 3. The Lord is a God of knowledge.

units.la: 1.Sam.16.v.7. Iehoua intuetur in cor.
units.tr: 1 Sam. 16. v. 7. The Lord looks upon the heart.

units.la: 1.Chron.28.v.9. Omnia corda exquirit Iehoua, & quodque figmentum cogitationum intelligit.
units.tr: 1 Chron. 28. v. 9. The Lord searches all hearts and understands every figment of the thoughts.

units.la: Psalm.7.vers.10. Explorator es cordium & renum, Deus iuste. Confer Act.1.v.24.c.15.v.8.
units.tr: Ps. 7. v. 10. You are the searcher of hearts and reins, O righteous God. Compare Acts 1. v. 24 and 15. v. 8.

units.la: Actor.15.vers.18. Nota sunt Deo ab omni ævo omnia sua opera.
units.tr: Acts 15. v. 18. All his works are known to God from eternity.

units.la: Iob.12.v.13. Penes illum (Deum) est sapientia & fortitudo: illius est consilium & intelligentia.
units.tr: Job 12. v. 13. With him (God) is wisdom and strength; his is counsel and understanding.

units.la: Prou.3.vers.19.20. Iehoua sapientia fundauit terram, statuit cœlos cælos intelligentiâ. Scientiâ eius abyssi diffissæ sunt, & superiores nubes destillant rorem.
units.tr: Prov. 3. v. 19, 20. The Lord by wisdom founded the earth, he established the heavens by understanding. By his knowledge the deeps were broken up, and the clouds drop down dew.

units.la: Hebr.4. v.13. Nulla res creata non est manifesta in conspectu ipsius: imò omnia sunt nuda & intimè patentia oculis eius.
units.tr: Heb. 4. v. 13. No created thing is hidden in his sight; but all things are naked and laid open to his eyes.

units.la: 11. Voluntas Dei est immutabilis.
units.tr: 11. The will of God is immutable.

units.la: 1. Sam. 15. vers. 29. Æternitas Israelis non committet mendacium, neque pœnitebit eum. Non enim homo est, vt pœniteat eum.
units.tr: 1 Sam. 15. vers. 29. The Eternal One of Israel will not lie, nor will he repent; for he is not a man, that he should repent.

units.la: Esa. 46. vers. 10. Consilium meum stabit: & omnis voluntas mea fiet.
units.tr: Isa. 46. vers. 10. My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure.

units.la: Rom. 11. v. 29. Dona Dei eiusmodi sunt, vt ipsum eorum non pœniteat.
units.tr: Rom. 11. v. 29. The gifts of God are such that he does not repent of them.

units.la: Hebr. 6. vers. 17. Deus volens ex abundanti hæredibus promissionis ostendere immutabilitatem consilij sui, fideiussit iureiurando.
units.tr: Heb. 6. vers. 17. God, willing to show more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it with an oath.

units.la: 12. Voluntas Dei est liberrima.
units.tr: 12. The will of God is most free.

units.la: Ion. 1. v.14. Tu Domine, quemadmodum vis, facis.
units.tr: Jonah 1. v. 14. O Lord, you do as you please.

units.la: Rom. 9. v.15. Miserebor cuius miserebor.
units.tr: Rom. 9. v. 15. I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy.

units.la: Et vers. 18. Itaque cuius vult, miseretur: quem autem vult, indurat.
units.tr: And vers. 18. So then he has mercy on whom he wills, and whom he wills he hardens.

units.la: Iacob. 1. vers. 18. Is (pater luminum) quia voluit, progenuit nos sermone veritatis, vt essemus quædam primitiæ eorum, quæ creauit.
units.tr: Jas. 1. vers. 18. Of his own will he begot us by the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.

units.la: 13. Deus est omnipotens.
units.tr: 13. God is almighty.

units.la: Genef. 17. vers. 1. Ego sum Deus omnipotens.
units.tr: Gen. 17. vers. 1. I am God Almighty.

units.la: Psalm. 115. vers. 3. Deus noster in cælis est, quidquid placet, facit.
units.tr: Ps. 115. vers. 3. Our God is in the heavens; he does whatever pleases him.

units.la: Ier. 32. vers. 17. 18. 19. Domine, Domine, ecce tu fecisti cælos, & terram virtute tuâ maximâ, & brachio extento: non potest occultari tibi res vlla. Exerces benignitatem in millesimos, & rependis iniquitatem patrum in sinum filiorum ipsorum post ipsos. Deus iste fortis, maximus, potentissimus, cuius nomen est Iehoua exercituum. Magnus es consilio & amplus actione: cum oculi tui aperti spectent in omnes vias hominum, vt des vnicuique secundum vias ipsius, & secundum fructum actionum ipsius.
units.tr: Jer. 32. vers. 17, 18, 19. Ah, Lord GOD! Behold, you have made the heavens and the earth by your great power and by your outstretched arm; nothing is too hard for you. You show mercy to thousands, and repay the iniquity of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them. The great, the mighty God, whose name is the LORD of hosts. Great in counsel and mighty in work; your eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of men, to give every one according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.

units.la: Luc. 1. v. 37. Apud Deum non erit vllum verbum, quod fieri non possit.
units.tr: Luke 1. v. 37. With God no word shall be without power.

units.la: Apoc. 4. v. 8. Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus est Dominus Deus ille omnipotens. Confer cap. 11. v. 17. c. 19. v. 6.
units.tr: Rev. 4. v. 8. Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God Almighty. Compare chap. 11. v. 17, chap. 19. v. 6.

units.la: 1. Sam. 14. v. 7. Non est Domino impedimentum, quin feruet multis aut paucis.
units.tr: 1 Sam. 14. v. 6. There is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few.

units.la: Esa. 14. v. 27. Dominus exercituum iniuit consilium, & quis irritum faciat? & manum eius extentam ecquis auertat? Confer c. 42. v. 38.
units.tr: Isa. 14. v. 27. The LORD of hosts has purposed, and who shall disannul it? And his hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it back? Compare chap. 42. v. 38.

units.la: 14. Deus est summe sanctus.
units.tr: 14. God is supremely holy.

units.la: Leuit. 19. v. 2. Sancti estote: quia sanctus sum ego Dominus Deus vester.
units.tr: Lev. 19. v. 2. Be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.

units.la: Iof. 24. v. 19. Dixit Iosua populo: Non poteritis colere Dominum, quia Deus sanctissimus est.
units.tr: Josh. 24. v. 19. Joshua said to the people: You cannot serve the LORD, for he is a holy God.

units.la: 1. Sam. 2. v. 2. Nullus est sanctus, vt Dominus.
units.tr: 1 Sam. 2. v. 2. There is none holy like the LORD.

units.la: Esa. 6. v. 3. Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus est Dominus exercituum. Confer cap. 12. v. 6. & Apoc. 4. v. 8.
units.tr: Isa. 6. v. 3. Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts. Compare chap. 12. v. 6 and Rev. 4. v. 8.

units.la: 15. Deus est summe iustus.
units.tr: 15. God is supremely just.

units.la: Deut. 32. v. 4. Rupis illius opus est perfectum. Omnes enim viae illius sunt ius. Deus fortis, fidelis, & expers iniquitatis, iustus & rectus est.
units.tr: Deut. 32. v. 4. He is the Rock, his work is perfect; for all his ways are judgment. A God of faithfulness and without iniquity, just and right is he.

units.la: Psal. 11. v. 7. Iustus Dominus, quae iusta sunt, diligit: rectum aspicit vultus ipsius.
units.tr: Ps. 11. v. 7. The LORD is righteous; he loves righteous deeds; the upright shall behold his face.

units.la: Esa. 45. v. 21. Ego Iehoua sum Deus iustus & seruator.
units.tr: Isa. 45. v. 21. I, the LORD, am a just God and a Saviour.

units.la: Apoc. 16. v. 5. Iustus es Domine, qui es, & qui eras, & qui eris, quod haec iudicaris.
units.tr: Rev. 16. v. 5. Just are you, O Lord, who are and who were, because you have judged these things.

units.la: 16. Deus est summe verax.
units.tr: 16. God is supremely true.

units.la: Num. 23. v. 23. Deus non est homo, vt mentiatur.
units.tr: Num. 23. v. 19. God is not a man, that he should lie.

units.la: Psal. 36. v. 6. Veritas tua vsq; ad nubes pertingit.
units.tr: Ps. 36. v. 6. Your truth reaches to the clouds.

units.la: Rom. 3. v. 4. Esto Deus verax, omnis autem homo mendax: sicut scriptum est, vt iustificeris in sermonibus tuis, & vincas, quando tu iudicas.
units.tr: Rom. 3. v. 4. Let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, that you may be justified in your words, and may overcome when you are judged.

units.la: Tit. 1. v. 2. Spem vitae aeternae promiserat Deus ille mentiri nescius.
units.tr: Titus 1. v. 2. In hope of eternal life, which God, who cannot lie, promised.

units.la: Apoc. 19. v. 11. Vidi coelum apertum, & ecce, adsuit equus albus, albus, & qui insidebat ei, vocabatur Fidelis & Verax, & qui iuste iudicat & pugnat.
units.tr: Rev. 19. v. 11. I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he who sat on it was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he judges and makes war.

units.la: 17. Deus est summè bonus, clemens, & misericors.
units.tr: 17. God is supremely good, merciful, and compassionate.

units.la: Exod.34.v.6.7. Iehoua transiens ante faciem Mosis inclamauit: Iehoua, Iehoua, Deus misericors & gratiosus, longanimis, & multus benignitate ac fide: custodiens benignitatem millibus &c.
units.tr: Exod. 34. v. 6, 7. The LORD passed before Moses and proclaimed: The LORD, the LORD God, merciful and gracious, long-suffering, and abundant in goodness and truth, keeping mercy for thousands, etc.

units.la: Psal.80.v.15. Tu Domine, Deus misericors & gratiosus es.
units.tr: Ps. 80. v. 15. You, O Lord, are a merciful and gracious God.

units.la: Psal.103.v.8. Misericors & gratiosus est Iehoua.
units.tr: Ps. 103. v. 8. The LORD is merciful and gracious.

units.la: Et v.13. Vt miseretur pater filiorum, miseretur Iehoua timentium ipsum. Confer Malach.3.v.16.
units.tr: And v. 13. As a father pities his children, so the LORD pities those who fear him. Compare Mal. 3. v. 16.

units.la: Psal.149.v.5. Bonus est Iehoua omnibus: & miserationes eius sunt in omnibus operibus eius.
units.tr: Ps. 149. v. 5. The LORD is good to all, and his mercies are over all his works.

units.la: Marc.10.v.18. Nemo bonus nisi vnus nempe Deus.
units.tr: Mark 10. v. 18. No one is good but one, namely God.

units.la: Rom.2.v.4. An diuitias benignitatis eius, & tolerantiæ, & lenitatis contemnis?
units.tr: Rom. 2. v. 4. Or do you despise the riches of his goodness, forbearance, and long-suffering?

units.la: 18. Deus est summè beatus.
units.tr: 18. God is supremely blessed.

units.la: Esa.42.v.8. Ego sum Dominus, illud est nomen meum, & gloriam meam alteri non dabo, & laudem meam sculptilibus.
units.tr: Isa. 42. v. 8. I am the LORD; that is my name; and I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to graven images.

units.la: Dan.7.v.9.10. Videbam, donec sedes positæ sunt, & antiquus dierum sedit: cuius vestimentum, vt nix, album erat, & pili capitis vt lana munda, solium vt scintillæ ignis, rotæ vt ignis ardens: à cuius conspectu fluuius ignis manabat prodiens: cui millies mille ministrabant, & coram quo myrias myriadum stabant, dolnec, iudicio considente, libri aperti sunt.
units.tr: Dan. 7. v. 9, 10. I watched until thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days sat; his garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was like fiery flames, and its wheels like burning fire. A river of fire flowed and came forth from before him; thousands upon thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him; until the court sat in judgment, and the books were opened.

units.la: Psal.104.v.1. Benedic anima mea Domino: Domine, Deus meus, magnus es valde; decorem & maiestatem induisti.
units.tr: Ps. 104. v. 1. Bless the LORD, O my soul: O Lord my God, you are very great; you are clothed with honour and majesty.

units.la: Act.7.v.2. Deus ille gloriæ visus est patri nostro Abrahamo.
units.tr: Acts 7. v. 2. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham.

units.la: 1.Tim.1.v.11. Secundum euangelium beati Dei. Confer cap.6.v.15. & Iud.v.24.25.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 1. v. 11. According to the gospel of the blessed God. Compare chap. 6. v. 15 and Jude v. 24, 25.

units.la: 19. Tres sunt personæ in vnâ essentiâ Dei.
units.tr: 19. There are three persons in one essence of God.

units.la: 1.Ioh.5.v.5. Tres sunt qui testificantur in cœlo: Pater, Sermo, & Spiritus sanctus: & hi tres vnum sunt.
units.tr: 1 John 5. v. 7. There are three who bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one.

units.la: Matth.28.verf.19. Profecti docete omnes gentes: baptizantes eos in nomen Patris & Filij & Spiritus sancti. Confer Matth.3.
units.tr: Matt. 28. vers. 19. Go therefore and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Compare Matt. 3.

units.la: Gen.1.v.26. Postea dixit Deus, faciamus hominem ad imaginem nostram. Confer Gen.11.v.7. & c.19.v.24.
units.tr: Gen. 1. v. 26. Then God said: Let us make man in our image. Compare Gen. 11. v. 7 and chap. 19. v. 24.

units.la: Pfalm.45.verf.8. Dilexisti iustitiam & odisti improbitatem: propterea unxit te, ô Deus, Deus tuus oleo lætitiæ præ consortibus tuis.
units.tr: Ps. 45. vers. 8. You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions.

units.la: Hag.2.v.5. Sum enim vobiscum, dictum Domini exercituum: cum Verbo, quo pepigeram vobiscum, exeuntibus vobis ex Ægypto, & Spiritu meo stante in vobis.
units.tr: Hag. 2. v. 5. For I am with you, says the LORD of hosts, according to the word that I covenanted with you when you came out of Egypt, and my Spirit remains among you.

units.la: 20. Christus est Filius Dei unigenitus, & verus Deus.
units.tr: 20. Christ is the only-begotten Son of God, and true God.

units.la: Psal.2.verf.7. Dominus dixit mihi: Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te.
units.tr: Ps. 2. vers. 7. The LORD said to me: You are my Son; today I have begotten you.

units.la: Iohan.1. verf.1. In principio erat Sermo ille, & Sermo ille erat apud Deum, eratq; ille Sermo Deus. Confer v.14.18. & Hebr. 1.verf.3.
units.tr: John 1. vers. 1. In the beginning was that Word, and the Word was with God, and that Word was God. Compare v. 14, 18 and Heb. 1. vers. 3.

units.la: Iohan.3.v.16. Ita Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum illum dederit.
units.tr: John 3. v. 16. God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son.

units.la: Ierem.23.v.6. Atq; hoc nomen eius est, quo vocabit eum Israel, Dominus iustitia nostra.
units.tr: Jer. 23. v. 6. And this is his name by which Israel will call him: The LORD our righteousness.

units.la: Psal.110.verf.1. Dixit Dominus Domino meo.
units.tr: Ps. 110. vers. 1. The LORD said to my Lord.

units.la: Rom.9.verf.5. Ex quibus est Christus, quod ad carnem attinet, qui est supra omnes, Deus benedictus in secula.
units.tr: Rom. 9. vers. 5. Of whom, as concerning the flesh, Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever.

units.la: Matth.3.v.17. Hic est filius ille meus dilectus, in quo valde acquiesco.
units.tr: Matt. 3. v. 17. This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

units.la: 1.Iohan.5.v.20. Summus in verace illo, in filio eius Iesu Christo. Hic est verus ille Deus, & vita aeterna.
units.tr: 1 John 5. v. 20. We are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life.

units.la: 21. Spiritus sanctus est verus Deus, procedens à Patre & Filio.
units.tr: 21. The Holy Spirit is the true God, proceeding from the Father and the Son.

units.la: Act.5.verf.3.4. Dixit Petrus: Anania, cur impleuit Satan cor tuum, ut mentireris in Spiritum sanctum ? non es mentitus hominibus, sed Deo.
units.tr: Acts 5. vers. 3, 4. Peter said: Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart, that you should lie to the Holy Spirit? You have not lied to men, but to God.

units.la: Iohan.15.v.26. Cum venerit Aduocatus ille, quem ego mittam vobis à Patre, Spiritus, inquam, ille veritatis, qui à Patre emanat: ille testabitur de me.
units.tr: John 15. v. 26. When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, I say, who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness of me.

units.la: Gal.4.v.6. Quoniam estis filij, emisit Deus Spiritum Filij sui in corda vestra, clamantem abba, id est, pater.
units.tr: Gal. 4. v. 6. Because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, that is, Father.

units.la: LOCUS III.
units.tr: Topic III.

units.la: De operibus Dei in genere.
units.tr: On the works of God in general.

units.la: 1. Omnia Dei opera sunt ab ipso & propter ipsum.
units.tr: 1. All the works of God are from him and for him.

units.la: Esa.66.v.2. Omnia ista fecit manus mea, & per eam existunt omnia ista: dictum Domini.
units.tr: Esa.66.v.2. All these things my hand has made, and through it all these things exist, says the Lord.

units.la: Rom.11. v.36. Ex eo, & per eum, & in ipsum sunt omnia.
units.tr: Rom.11.v.36. From him, and through him, and unto him are all things.

units.la: Prou.16.v.4. Omnia operatus est Dominus propter se, etiamq; improbum addiem malum.
units.tr: Prou.16.v.4. The Lord has made all things for himself, even the wicked for the day of evil.

units.la: 2. Opera Dei fiunt à Deo liberè.
units.tr: 2. The works of God are done by God freely.

units.la: Psal.115.v.3. Deus noster in cœlis est, quidquid placet, facit.
units.tr: Psal.115.v.3. Our God is in the heavens; whatever he pleases, he does.

units.la: Apoc.4.v.11. Dignus es Domine, qui accipias gloriam, & honorem, & virtutem: quia tu condidisti omnia, & per voluntatem tuam sunt, & creata sunt.
units.tr: Apoc.4.v.11. Worthy are you, O Lord, to receive glory, honour and power, for you created all things, and by your will they are and were created.

units.la: 3. Opera Dei sunt bona, ampla, magna, & omninò indicia naturæ Dei.
units.tr: 3. The works of God are good, ample, great, and altogether indications of the nature of God.

units.la: Psal.33.v.4 5. Rectum est verbum Domini, & omne opus eius constans: amat iustitiam & iudicium: benignitate Domini plena est terra.
units.tr: Psal.33.v.4,5. The word of the Lord is right, and all his work is steadfast; he loves righteousness and judgment; the earth is full of the goodness of the Lord.

units.la: Psalm.104.vers.24. Quàm ampla sunt opera tua, ô Domine! quàm ea omnia sapienter fecisti! quàm plena est terra possessione tuâ!
units.tr: Psalm.104.vers.24. How ample are your works, O Lord! How wisely you have made them all! How full the earth is of your possession!

units.la: Psalm.iii.vers.2.3.4. Magna opera Domini, expositaomnibus, qui delectantur illis: gloriosum & decorum opus eius, & iustitiam eius perstantem in æternum. Memoriam comparavit mirabilibus suis, gratiosus & misericors Dominus.
units.tr: Psalm.iii.vers.2.3.4. Great are the works of the Lord, sought out by all who delight in them; his work is glorious and splendid, and his righteousness endures for ever. He has made a memorial of his wonders; the Lord is gracious and merciful.

units.la: Et vers.7.8. Opera manuum eius sunt veritatis & iudicij: constantia omnia mandata eius.
units.tr: And vers.7.8. The works of his hands are truth and judgment; all his commandments are sure.

units.la: Dan.4.vers.37. Nunc ego Nebucadnezar laudo, extolloq;, & glorifico regem cœli, cuius omnia opera veritatis, & cuius viæ sunt viæ iudicij.
units.tr: Dan.4.vers.37. Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, extol and glorify the King of heaven, whose works are all truth, and whose ways are judgment.

units.la: 4. Omnia Dei opera sunt ipsi nota.
units.tr: 4. All the works of God are known to him.

units.la: Psal.94.v.9. An plantator auris non audiat? aut formator oculi annon intueatur? Psal. 147. v. 4. Supputat (Deus) numerum stellarum, quotquot sunt, nominibus vocans.
units.tr: Psal.94.v.9. He who planted the ear, shall he not hear? Or he who formed the eye, shall he not see? Psal.147.v.4. (God) counts the number of the stars, calling them all by their names.

units.la: Hebr. 4. v. 13. Non est ulla res creata non manifesta in conspectu ipsius; imo omnia sunt nuda & intime patentia oculis eius.
units.tr: Hebr.4.v.13. No created thing is hidden in his sight; indeed all things are naked and laid open to his eyes.

units.la: LOCVS IV.
units.tr: LOCUS IV.

units.la: De decretis Dei.
units.tr: On the decrees of God.

units.la: 1. Deus ab æterno iudicauit bonum esse, ut aliquæ res in tempore extra ipsum existerent.
units.tr: 1. God from eternity judged it good that certain things should exist outside himself in time.

units.la: Esa. 46. v. 9.10. Ego sum Deus & nullus praeterea, & nemo par est mihi. Indico a principio finem, & ab antiquitate, quæ nondum facta sunt, dicens: Consilium meum stabit, & omnem delectationem meam faciam.
units.tr: Isa. 46. v. 9, 10. I am God, and there is none besides; I am God, and there is none like me. I declare the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying: My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure.

units.la: Eph. 1. v. 4. Elegit nos Deus in Christo ante iactum mundi fundamentum. Pertinet huc vox προορίζω[?] q. d. antedecretum, & προέγνω[?] q. d. praedecreuit Act. 2. v. 23. Rom. 8. v. 29. c. II. v. 2.
units.tr: Eph. 1. v. 4. He chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world. To this belongs the word [προορίζω], that is, "fore-decreed," and [προέγνω], that is, "foreknew" or "fore-decreed." Acts 2. v. 23. Rom. 8. v. 29. c. II. v. 2.

units.la: 2. Decretum Dei est immutabile.
units.tr: 2. The decree of God is immutable.

units.la: Psal. 33. v. 11. Consilium (Domini) in seculum consistit; cogitationes animi eius in aetates singulas.
units.tr: Ps. 33. v. 11. The counsel of the LORD standeth for ever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations.

units.la: Esa. 14. v. 27. Dominus exercituum inivit consilium, & quis irritum faciat? & manum eius extentam quis avertat?
units.tr: Isa. 14. v. 27. The LORD of hosts hath purposed, and who shall disannul it? And his hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it back?

units.la: Hebr. 6. v, 17. Deus volens ex abundanti hæredibus promissionis ostendere immutabilitatem consilii sui, fideiussit iureiurando.
units.tr: Heb. 6. v. 17. God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath.

units.la: 3. Quidquid Deus in tempore facit vel permittit, ab æterno facere vel permittere decreuit.
units.tr: 3. Whatever God does or permits in time, he decreed from eternity to do or to permit.

units.la: Iob. 14. v. 6. Quandoquidem sunt præcisi dies eius (hominis) numerus mensium eius penes te est: determinationes fecisti, quas non transgrediatur.
units.tr: Job 14. v. 5. Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months is with thee; thou hast appointed his bounds, that he cannot pass.

units.la: Prou. 16. v. 33. In gremium conijcitur sors, a Domino autem est tota ratio eius.
units.tr: Prov. 16. v. 33. The lot is cast into the lap, but the whole disposing thereof is of the LORD.

units.la: Act. 2. v. 22. 23. Iesum Nazarenum definito consilio & praecognitione Dei deditum cum accepissetis, manibus sceleratis cruci affixum interemistis.
units.tr: Acts 2. v. 22, 23. Jesus of Nazareth, being delivered by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, ye have taken, and by wicked hands have crucified and slain.

units.la: Etc.4.v.28. Vt facerent quæcunque manus tua & consilium tuum priùs definierat vt fierent.
units.tr: Acts 4. v. 28. To do whatsoever thy hand and thy counsel determined before to be done.

units.la: Eph.1.v.11. Omnia agit (Deus) ex consilio voluntatis suæ.
units.tr: Eph. 1. v. 11. God worketh all things after the counsel of his own will.

units.la: 4. Deus ab æterno præscit opera sua & creaturarum.
units.tr: 4. God from eternity foreknows his own works and those of creatures.

units.la: Psal.139.v.2.3.12.16. Tu intelligis cogitationem meam è longinquo, omnium viarum mearum gnarus es, Ne tenebræ quidem ita obtenebrare possunt, quin tu peruideas: sed nox, vt dies illustrat. Massam meam vident oculi tui, in libro tuo hæc omnia scripta sunt; ex quibus diebus formabantur, cùm nondum vllum ex eis exstaret.
units.tr: Ps. 139. v. 2, 3, 12, 16. Thou understandest my thought afar off. Thou art acquainted with all my ways. Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee, but the night shineth as the day. Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.

units.la: Esa.44.v.2. Quis prædicat & indicat istud, aut ordinat istud mihi, ex quo disposui populum æternum, vt futura, & quæ eventura sunt, indicentur illis.
units.tr: Isa. 44. v. 2. Who declareth and sheweth it, and setteth it in order for me, since I appointed the ancient people? Let them shew unto them the things that are coming, and shall come.

units.la: Etc.48.v.3.4.5. Priora illa ab eo tempore indicaueram, & ex ore meo prodeuntia pronuntiaueram; ea repente effeci: atque euenerunt. Expræscientiâ meâ erat, te durum esse: & neruum ferreum esse ceruicem tuam, frontemq; tuam chalybeam. Quapropter indicaui tibi ex eo tepore, cùm nondum eueniret, pronuntiaui tibi.
units.tr: Isa. 48. v. 3, 4, 5. I have declared the former things from the beginning, and they went forth out of my mouth, and I shewed them; I did them suddenly, and they came to pass. Because I knew that thou art obstinate, and thy neck is an iron sinew, and thy brow brass; therefore I have declared it to thee from the beginning, before it came to pass I shewed it thee.

units.la: Act.15.v.18. Nota sunt Deo ab omni ævo omnia opera sua.
units.tr: Acts 15. v. 18. Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world.

units.la: 5. Deus ab æterno nouit & decreuit ea, quæ non sunt futura.
units.tr: 5. God from eternity knows and has decreed those things which are not going to be.

units.la: Esa.8.v.9.10. Consociamini ô populi, & conteremini, auremque præbete quotquot istis in locis longinquis terræ, accingimini & conteremini; inite consilium, & irritum fiet: & loquimini verbum, & non existet. Nam Immanuelis existet verbum.
units.tr: Isa. 8. v. 9, 10. Associate yourselves, O ye people, and ye shall be broken in pieces; and give ear, all ye of far countries; gird yourselves, and ye shall be broken in pieces; take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand; for God is with us.

units.la: LOCVS V. De prouidentiâ Dei æternâ.
units.tr: Locus V. On the eternal providence of God.

units.la: 1. Deus ab æterno decreuit creare & gubernare mundum.
units.tr: 1. God from eternity decreed to create and govern the world.

units.la: Apoc.4.v.11. Tu (Domine) condidisti omnia, vt per voluntatem tuam sunt, & creata sunt.
units.tr: Rev. 4.11. Thou, O Lord, hast created all things, and by thy will they are and were created.

units.la: Esa.45.v.12. Ego feci terram, & hominem super eam creaui, ego manibus meis, extendentibus cælos, omni quoque exercitui eorum præcepta dedi.
units.tr: Isa. 45.12. I have made the earth and created man upon it; I, with my own hands, stretched out the heavens, and I have given commands to all their host.

units.la: 2. Prouidentiâ Dei omnia gubernantur. Esa.46.v.10. Consilium meum stabit, & omnem delectationem meam facturus sum.
units.tr: 2. All things are governed by the providence of God. Isa. 46.10. My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure.

units.la: Matth.10.v.29.30. Nonne duo passerculi assario veneunt, & vnus ex eis non cadet in terram sine Patre vestro? Vestri vero etiam capilli capitis omnes numerati sunt.
units.tr: Matt. 10.29-30. Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? And one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father. But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

units.la: 3. Prouidentia Dei æterna est immutabilis. Act.4.v.28. Vt facerent quæcunque manus tua & consilium tuum prius definierat vt fierent. Vide paulo ante ad num.1. Esa.46.v.10.& loc.præced.num.2. 1.Sam.15.v.29. Quin etiam qui est æternitas Israelis non committet mendacium, neque pœnitebit eum: non enim homo est, vt pœniteat eum.
units.tr: 3. The eternal providence of God is immutable. Acts 4.28. To do whatever your hand and your counsel had determined beforehand to be done. See above, at no. 1. Isa. 46.10, and the preceding place, no. 2. 1 Sam. 15.29. Moreover, the Eternity of Israel will not lie nor repent; for he is not a man, that he should repent.

units.la: 4. Decretum prouidentiæ non excludit officium nostrum,sed includit. Matth.4.v.7. Scriptum est: Non tentabis Dominum Deum tuum.
units.tr: 4. The decree of providence does not exclude our duty but includes it. Matt. 4.7. It is written: You shall not tempt the Lord your God.

units.la: Psal.50.v.14.15. Sacrifica Deo laudem,& redde excelso vota tua: Atque inuoca me tempore angustiæ, eripiam te vt honore assicias me.
units.tr: Ps. 50.14-15. Offer to God a sacrifice of praise, and pay your vows to the Most High. And call upon me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you shall honour me.

units.la: Psal.91.per totum, nominatim v.11.12.15.16. Nam angelis suis præcipiet de te,vt conseruent te in omnibus viis tuis: Ambabus palmis sustineant te, ne offendas ad lapidem pedem tuum. Simulac inuocauerit me, exaudiam eum, ipsi adero in angustia: eripiam eum, & honore afficiam eum: Longitudine dierum satiabo eum, denique [?] efficiam vt fruatur salute mea.
units.tr: Ps. 91, throughout, especially vv. 11, 12, 15, 16. For he will give his angels charge over you, to keep you in all your ways. They shall bear you up in their hands, lest you dash your foot against a stone. When he calls upon me, I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him and honour him. With long life will I satisfy him, and I will cause him to enjoy my salvation.

units.la: LOCVS VI.
units.tr: Topic VI.

units.la: De prædestinatione.
units.tr: On predestination.

units.la: 1. Deus ab æterno decreuit salutem & damnationem quorundam, hoc est, alios elegit, alios reprobauit, seu non-elegit. Esa.44.v.2. Quis, vt ego, prædicat, & indicat istud, aut ordinat istud mihi, ex quo disposui populum æternum? Et c.45.v.17. Israel seruatur per Dominum salute æterna: non erubeerubescetis, neq; ignominiosi reddemini in sempiterna secula.
units.tr: 1. From eternity God decreed the salvation and the damnation of some, that is, he chose some and rejected or did not choose others. Isa.44.v.2. Who proclaims and declares this, as I do, and sets it in order for me, since I established the eternal people? And c.45.v.17. Israel is saved by the Lord with an everlasting salvation; you shall not be ashamed or humiliated into the ages of eternity.

units.la: Soph.3.v.17. Dominus Deus tuus in medio tui potens, seruaturus est, gauisurus de te latitia, conquieturus in amore suo, exultaturus de te cantu.
units.tr: Zeph.3.v.17. The Lord your God is mighty in your midst; he will save, he will rejoice over you with gladness, he will rest in his love, he will exult over you with singing.

units.la: Matth.11.v.25.26.Iesus dixit, Gloriam tibi tribuo, Pater, Domine cœli & terræ, quòd hæc occultaueris à sapientibus & intelligentibus: & ea retexeris infantibus. Etiam, Pater, quia ita placuit tibi.
units.tr: Matth.11.v.25.26. Jesus said, I give thanks to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the understanding, and have revealed them to infants. Yes, Father, for so it has pleased you.

units.la: Et cap.20.v.16.&c.22.v.14. Multi sunt vocati, pauci verò electi.
units.tr: And c.20.v.16. etc., and c.22.v.14. Many are called, but few are chosen.

units.la: Marc.13.v.20. Propter electos, quos elegit, contraxit Deus dies illos: scil. obsidionis Hierosolymitanæ.
units.tr: Mark 13.v.20. For the sake of the elect, whom he chose, God shortened those days: namely, of the siege of Jerusalem.

units.la: Luc.2.v.34. Ecce positus est iste (Iesus) in casum & resurrectionem multorum in Israel.
units.tr: Luke 2.v.34. Behold, this one (Jesus) is set for the fall and the rising again of many in Israel.

units.la: Act.13.v.48. Crediderunt quotquot erant ordinati ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: Acts 13.v.48. As many as had been ordained to eternal life believed.

units.la: Rom.8.v.28.29.30. Nouimus iis qui diligunt Deum omnia simul conferre ad bonum, iis videlicet qui ex proposito ipsius vocati sunt. Nam quos prædecreuit (προέγνω)[?] eos etiam prædestinauit, vt conformes fiant imagini filij eius: quos autem prædestinauit, eos etiam vocauit: & quos vocauit, eos etiam iustificauit: & quos iustificauit, eos etiam glorificauit.
units.tr: Rom.8.v.28.29.30. We know that for those who love God all things work together for good, namely for those who are called according to his purpose. For whom he foreknew [προέγνω], those he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son; and whom he predestined, those he also called; and whom he called, those he also justified; and whom he justified, those he also glorified.

units.la: Rom.9.v.11.12.13. Nondum nati pueris (Esau & Iacob) cum nihil fecissent boni vel mali, vt propositum Dei quod est secundum electionem maneret, non ex operibus, sed ex vocante, dictum est ei (Rebeccæ) Maior seruiet minori. Sicut scriptum est, Iacobum dilexi, Esavum verò odio habui.
units.tr: Rom.9.v.11.12.13. Although the children (Esau and Jacob) were not yet born and had done neither good nor evil, so that God's purpose according to election might stand, not by works but by him who calls, it was said to her (Rebekah): The elder shall serve the younger. As it is written, Jacob I have loved, but Esau I have hated.

units.la: Et cap.11.v.2. Non abiecit Deus populum suum, quem prædecreuit.
units.tr: And c.11.v.2. God has not cast off his people, whom he foreknew.

units.la: 1.Thess.5.verf.9. Non constituit nos Deus ad iram, sed ad salutem.
units.tr: 1 Thess.5.v.9. God has not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation.

units.la: Iudæ v.4. Subrepserunt quidam homines, prius iam olim descripti ad hanc damnationem.
units.tr: Jude v.4. Certain men have crept in, who were long ago marked out for this condemnation.

units.la: 2. Prædestinatio pendet à mero Dei beneplacito.
units.tr: 2. Predestination depends on the sheer good pleasure of God.

units.la: Matth.11.v.26.Etiam, Pater: quia sic placuit tibi; seu, vt Syrus habet, quia sic fuit beneplacitum coram te. Rom.9.v.18. Cuius vult, miseretur: quem autem vult, indurat.
units.tr: Matth.11.v.26. Yes, Father, for so it has pleased you; or, as the Syriac has it, for so it was well-pleasing before you. Rom.9.v.18. He has mercy on whom he wills, and he hardens whom he wills.

units.la: Eph.1.v.5. Praedestinauit nos ad adoptionem filiorum per Iesum Christum ad seipsum, secundum beneplacitum voluntatis suae.
