units.tr: Eph.1.v.5. He predestined us to adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.

units.la: Et verf.11. Praedestinati sumus secundum propositum eius, qui omnia efficit ex consilio voluntatis suae.
units.tr: And v.11. We were predestined according to the purpose of him who works all things according to the counsel of his will.

units.la: 3. Christus ab aeterno electus est, ut esset mediator noster.
units.tr: 3. Christ was elected from eternity, that he might be our mediator.

units.la: Esa.42.v.1. En seruus meus, quem sustento, electus meus, quem benigne accipit anima mea. Confer Matth.12.v.18.
units.tr: Isa.42.v.1. Behold my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights. Compare Matth.12.v.18.

units.la: Act.2.v.23. Iesum, definito consilio, praecognitione Dei, deditum, cum accepisset, manibus sceleratis cruci affixum interemistis. Confer Act.4. v.28.
units.tr: Acts 2.v.23. Jesus, delivered up by the determined counsel and foreknowledge of God, you took and by lawless hands crucified and killed. Compare Acts 4.v.28.

units.la: 1.Petr.1. v.20. Praesciti quidem (Christi) ante iacta mundi fundamenta, patefacti vero vltimis temporibus propter vos. Confer cap.2. v. 4. vbi Christus dicitur lapis ab hominibus reprobatus, apud Deum vero electus.
units.tr: 1 Pet.1.v.20. Indeed he was foreknown (Christ) before the foundation of the world, but was made manifest in the last times for your sake. Compare c.2.v.4., where Christ is said to be a stone rejected by men, but chosen by God.

units.la: 4. Quidam angeli ab aeterno sunt electi ad vitam aeternam.
units.tr: 4. Certain angels were elected from eternity to eternal life.

units.la: 1.Timoth.5.verf.21. Obtestor in conspectu Dei & Domini Iesu Christi, & electorum angelorum.
units.tr: 1 Tim.5.v.21. I charge you before God and the Lord Jesus Christ and the elect angels.

units.la: 5. Quidam homines ab aeterno sunt electi ad vitam aeternam.
units.tr: 5. Certain men were elected from eternity to eternal life.

units.la: Rom.9.v.23. Notas fecit diuitias gloriae suae erga vasa misericordiae, quae praeparauit ad gloriam.
units.tr: Rom.9.v.23. He made known the riches of his glory toward vessels of mercy, which he prepared for glory.

units.la: 1.Thess.5.v.9. Non constituit nos Deus ad iram, sed ad salutem obtinendam per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum.
units.tr: 1 Thess.5.v.9. God has not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: 2.Tim.1.v.9. Seruauit nos (Deus) & vocauit vocatione sancta: non ex operibus nostris, sed ex suo proposito & gratia.
units.tr: 2 Tim.1.v.9. He (God) saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace.

units.la: Esa.44.v.2. Quis praedicat & indicat istud mihi, ex quo disposui populum aeternum.
units.tr: Isa.44.v.2. Who proclaims and declares this to me, since I established the eternal people?

units.la: Iohan.17.v.6. Manifestum feci nomen tuum hominibus, quos dedisti mihi, selectos e mundo.
units.tr: John 17.v.6. I have made your name known to the men whom you gave me out of the world, chosen.

units.la: 6. Homines qui sunt electi, in Christo sunt electi.
units.tr: 6. Those who are elect are elect in Christ.

units.la: Ephes.1. v.4. Deus elegit nos in ipso (Christo) ante iactum mundi fundamentum.
units.tr: Eph.1.v.4. God chose us in him (Christ) before the foundation of the world.

units.la: Ioh.3.v.16. Ita Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum illum unigenitum dederit, ut, quisquis credit in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam aeternam.
units.tr: John 3.v.16. God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, so that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

units.la: Ephes.3.v.11. Praestitutum aeternum constituit Deus in Christo Iesu Domino nostro. Confer 1.Petr.1.v.20. ad num. præ-ced. 3.
units.tr: Eph.3.v.11. God established the eternal purpose in Christ Jesus our Lord. Compare 1 Pet.1.v.20., at the preceding number 3.

units.la: 7. Electio non excludit, sed includit, studium bonorum operum, tanquam effectum & infallibile signum.
units.tr: 7. Election does not exclude but includes the pursuit of good works, as its effect and infallible sign.

units.la: Eph.1.v.4. Deus elegit nos in ipso (Christo) ante iactum mundi fundamentum, ut simus sancti & inculpati in conspectu eius cum charitate.
units.tr: Eph.1.v.4. God chose us in him (Christ) before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before him in love.

units.la: 2.Thess.2.v.13.14. Nos debemus gratias agere Deo semper de vobis, fratres dilecti à Domino, quòd elegerit vos Deus ab initio ad salutem per sanctificationem spiritus & fidem habitam veritati.
units.tr: 2 Thess.2.v.13.14. We ought always to give thanks to God for you, brethren beloved by the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning for salvation through sanctification of the Spirit and faith in the truth.

units.la: 8. Electio nostri ad vitam aeternam est gratuita.
units.tr: 8. Our election to eternal life is gratuitous.

units.la: Rom.9.v.16. Electio non est eius qui vult, neq; eius qui currit, sed eius, qui miseretur, nempe Dei. Confer num.2. & paulo post Deut.7. ad num.12.
units.tr: Rom.9.v.16. Election is not of him who wills, nor of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy. Compare number 2, and shortly after Deut.7 at number 12.

units.la: 9. Electio ad vitam aeternam est immutabilis.
units.tr: 9. Election to eternal life is unchangeable.

units.la: 2.Tim.2.v.19. Solidum fundamentum Dei stat, habens hoc sigillum: Novit Dominus, qui sint sui.
units.tr: 2 Tim.2.v.19. The firm foundation of God stands, having this seal: The Lord knows those who are his.

units.la: Iohan.17.v.9. Ego pro eis rogo: non pro mundo rogo, sed pro iis, quos dedisti mihi, quia tui sunt.
units.tr: John 17.v.9. I pray for them; I do not pray for the world, but for those whom you have given me, because they are yours.

units.la: 1.Petr.2.v.6. Ecce statuo in Sion lapidem angularem, electum, pretiosum:in quem qui credit, nequaquam pudefiet.
units.tr: 1 Pet.2.v.6. Behold, I lay in Zion a cornerstone, chosen and precious; whoever believes in him will by no means be put to shame.

units.la: 10. Pauci sunt electi respectu reproborum.
units.tr: 10. The elect are few in comparison with the reprobate.

units.la: Matth.22.v.14. Multi sunt vocati, pauci vero electi.
units.tr: Matth.22.v.14. Many are called, but few are chosen.

units.la: Etc.[?]7.v.13.14. Introite per angustam portam: quoniam lata est porta, & spatiosa via, quae abducit in exitium, multiq; sunt, qui introeunt per eam. Quia angusta est porta, & stricta via, quae ducit ad vitam, & pauci sunt, qui inveniant eam.
units.tr: Matth.7.v.13.14. Enter by the narrow gate; for the gate is wide and the way is broad that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter through it. Because the gate is narrow and the way is hard that leads to life, and few are those who find it.

units.la: 11. Electionis aeternae consideratio est fundamentum gaudij spiritualis.
units.tr: 11. The consideration of eternal election is the foundation of spiritual joy.

units.la: Luc.10.vers.20. Gaudete, quod nomina vestra sint scripta in cœlis.
units.tr: Luke 10.v.20. Rejoice that your names are written in heaven.

units.la: 12. Deus ab æterno non elegit quosdam angelos.
units.tr: 12. God did not elect certain angels from eternity.

units.la: 2.Petr.2.v.4. Deus angelis, qui peccauerunt, non pepercit, sed in tartarum detrusos catenis caliginis tradidit, damnationi seruatos.
units.tr: 2 Pet.2.v.4. God did not spare the angels who sinned, but cast them down into hell and delivered them into chains of darkness, reserved for judgment.

units.la: Iudæ v.6. Angelos, qui non conseruarunt originem suam, sed reliquerunt suum domicilium, iudicio magni illius diei vinculis æternis sub caligine reseruauit.
units.tr: Jude v.6. The angels who did not keep their first estate, but left their own dwelling, he has kept in everlasting chains under darkness until the judgment of the great day.

units.la: 13. Deus ab æterno quosdam homines non elegit ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: 13. God from eternity did not elect certain men to eternal life.

units.la: Rom.9.v.13. Iacobum dilexi, Esauum odio habui.
units.tr: Rom.9.v.13. Jacob I have loved, Esau I have hated.

units.la: Et v.18. Itaq; cuius vult, miseretur, quem autem vult, indurat.
units.tr: And v.18. So then he has mercy on whom he wills, and he hardens whom he wills.

units.la: Et v.22. Volens (Deus) ostendere iram, & notam facere potentiam suam, pertulit multa lenitate vasa iræ, coagmentata ad interitum.
units.tr: And v.22. God, willing to show his wrath and make his power known, endured with much patience the vessels of wrath, fitted for destruction.

units.la: Iudæ v.4. Subrepserunt quidam homines iam olim præscripti ad hanc damnationem, impij, qui Dei nostri gratiam transferunt ad lasciuiam.
units.tr: Jude v.4. Certain men have crept in, who were long ago marked out for this condemnation, ungodly men, who turn the grace of our God into licentiousness.

units.la: Deut.7.v.6.7.8. Nam populus sanctus es Iehoua Deo tuo:te selegit Iehoua Deus tuus, vt sis ei populus peculiaris præ omnibus populis qui sunt sub vniuerso cælo. Non eò quòd plures essetis omnibus reliquis populis, amore propendit Iehoua in vos: vos enim eratis populus paucissimus omnium populorum: Sed eò quòd diligit Iehoua vos. Confer Act.14. v.16.17.
units.tr: Deut.7.v.6.7.8. For you are a holy people to the Lord your God; the Lord your God has chosen you to be his own special people above all the peoples who are on the face of the earth. It was not because you were more in number than all other peoples that the Lord set his love on you, for you were the fewest of all peoples; but because the Lord loves you. Compare Acts 14.v.16.17.

units.la: LOCVS VII.
units.tr: Locus VII.

units.la: De Creatione.
units.tr: Concerning Creation.

units.la: 1. Solus Deus, Pater, Filius & Spiritus sanctus, creauit cælum, terram, & omnia quæ in iis sunt.
units.tr: 1. God alone, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, created heaven, earth, and all things that are in them.

units.la: Gen.[?]1.v.1. In principio creauit Deus cælum & terram.
units.tr: Gen. [?]1. v. 1. In the beginning God created heaven and earth.

units.la: Exod.20.v.11. Sex diebus perfecit Dominus cælum ipsum, & terram, mare, & quidquid est in eis.
units.tr: Exod. 20. v. 11. In six days the Lord made heaven itself, and earth, the sea, and whatever is in them.

units.la: Esa.40.v.12. Quis mensus est pugillo suo aquas, & cælos spithamâ expandit, aut complexus est trientali puluerem terræ? & ponderauit statera montes, & colles lancibus?
units.tr: Isa. 40. v. 12. Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the heavens with a span, and gathered the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales and the hills in a balance?

units.la: Prou.3.v.19.20. Dominus sapientia fundauit terram, statuit cœlos intelligentia: scientia eius abyssi diffissæ sunt, & superiores nubes destillant rorem.
units.tr: Prov. 3. v. 19, 20. The Lord by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding he established the heavens. By his knowledge the deeps were broken up, and the clouds drop down dew.

units.la: Ier.51.v.15. Deus fecit terram virtute suâ, stabilit orbem habitabilem sapientia suâ, & prudentia suâ extendit cœlos.
units.tr: Jer. 51. v. 15. God made the earth by his power, he established the habitable world by his wisdom, and by his understanding he stretched out the heavens.

units.la: Iohan.1.v.3. Omnia per hunc Sermonem facta sunt, & absq; eo factum est nihil, quod factum sit.
units.tr: John 1. v. 3. All things were made through this Word, and without him was made nothing that was made.

units.la: Et v.10. Mundus per eum factus est.
units.tr: And v. 10. The world was made through him.

units.la: Coloss.1.v.16.17. Per eum (Christum) condita sunt omnia, quæ in cœlis sunt, & quæ in terra, visibilia & inuisibilia, siue throni, siue dominia, siue imperia, siue potestates: omnia, inquam, per eum, & eius respectu condita sunt.
units.tr: Col. 1. v. 16, 17. All things were created through him (Christ), in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things, I say, were created through him and for him.

units.la: Gen.1.v.2. Et spiritus Dei incubabat superficiei aquarum.
units.tr: Gen. 1. v. 2. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.

units.la: 2. Prima creatio intra primos sex mundi dies peracta est.
units.tr: 2. The first creation was completed within the first six days of the world.

units.la: Gen.1.& 2.nominatim c.2.v.2. Cum perfecisset Deus die septimo opus suum, quod fecerat. Vide Exod.20.verf.11.ad num. præced.
units.tr: Gen. 1 and 2, especially 2. v. 2. When God had finished on the seventh day his work which he had made. See Exod. 20, verse 11, at the preceding number.

units.la: 3. Deus omnia creauit simplici nutu & iussu.
units.tr: 3. God created all things by a simple nod and command.

units.la: Gen.1.v.3. Dixit Deus, esto lux: & fuit lux.
units.tr: Gen. 1. v. 3. God said, Let there be light: and there was light.

units.la: Et v.11. Dixit Deus, herbascat terra herbulis.
units.tr: And v. 11. God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, herbs.

units.la: Psal.148.v.5. Laudent nomen Domini, quia, ipso præcipiente, illico creata sunt.
units.tr: Ps. 148. v. 5. Let them praise the name of the Lord, for at his command they were created at once.

units.la: 2.Cor.4.v.6. Dixit (Deus) vt è tenebris lux splendesceret.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 4. v. 6. He (God) said, Let light shine out of darkness.

units.la: 4. Deus ex nihilo creauit mundum.
units.tr: 4. God created the world out of nothing.

units.la: Roman.4.verf.17. Vocante (Deo) quæ non sunt, tanquam sunt.
units.tr: Rom. 4. verse 17. Calling those things which are not as though they were.

units.la: Hebr.11.v.3. Per fidem intelligimus constructum fuisse mundum verbo Dei, vt quæ cernimus non sint ex apparentibus facta.
units.tr: Heb. 11. v. 3. By faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that what we see was not made out of things which appear.

units.la: 5. Deus creauit omnia valde bona.
units.tr: 5. God created all things very good.

units.la: Gen.1.verf.31. Inspexit Deus, quidquid fecerat: ecce autem, bonum erat valde.
units.tr: Gen. 1. verse 31. God saw everything that he had made, and behold, it was very good.

units.la: 1.Tim.4.v.4. Quidquid condidit Deus, bonum est.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 4. v. 4. Whatever God has created is good.

units.la: 6. Deus omnia fecit propter seipsum, & propter hominem, inprimis propter electos suos.
units.tr: 6. God made all things for his own sake, and for man, and above all for his elect.

units.la: Prou.16.v.4. Omnia operatus est Iehova propter se. Rom.II. verf.vlt. Nam ex eo, & per ipsum, & in ipsum sunt omnia.
units.tr: Prov. 16. v. 4. The Lord has made all things for himself. Rom. 11, last verse. For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things.

units.la: Gen.1.v.28.29.30. Deinde benedixit eis (Adamo & Euæ) Deus, & dixit eis: Fœtificate, ac augescite & implete terram, eamq; subijcite: & dominamini in pisces maris, & in volucres cœli, & in omnes bestias reptantes super terram. Præterea dixit Deus, ecce dedi vobis omnes herbas sementantes semen, quæ sunt in superficie totius terræ, omnesq; arbores, in quibus est fructus arboreus, sementantes semen: vestra ad comedendum erunt. Confer Psalm.8.&10 Gen.9.v.1.2.3.
units.tr: Gen. 1. v. 28, 29, 30. Then God blessed them (Adam and Eve) and said to them: Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the heavens, and over every beast that creeps upon the earth. Moreover God said, Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is on the surface of the whole earth, and every tree in which is fruit bearing seed; they shall be yours for food. Compare Ps. 8 and 10, Gen. 9. v. 1, 2, 3.

units.la: Hebr.1.v.vlt. Nonne omnes (angeli boni) sunt ministratores spiritus, qui ministerii causâ emittuntur propter eos, qui hæredes erunt salutis.
units.tr: Heb. 1, last verse. Are they not all (the good angels) ministering spirits, sent forth to serve for the sake of those who will inherit salvation?

units.la: I.Cor.3.verf.21.22.23. Omnia enim vestra sunt: Et Paulus,& Apollos, & Cephas, & mundus, & vita, & mors, & præsentia, & futura: omnia, inquam, vestra sunt. Vos autem Christi: Christus vero Dei.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 3. verses 21, 22, 23. For all things are yours: whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or the present, or the future; all things, I say, are yours. And you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.

units.la: LOCVS VIII. De gubernatione mundi, siue prouidentia Dei qua regit vniuersa.
units.tr: Chapter VIII. On the government of the world, or the providence of God by which he rules all things.

units.la: 1. Deus omnia regit vniuersè.
units.tr: 1. God rules all things universally.

units.la: Nehem.9.v.6. Tu ille Dominus solus es, tu fecisti cœlos, cœlos cœlorum, & omnem exercitum illorum, terram, & quidquid est in eis, & tu viuificas hæc omnia: etiam exercitus cœlorum tibi seincuruant, honorem exhibentes.
units.tr: Neh. 9.6. You are the LORD, you alone; you have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, and all their host, the earth and all that is in it, and you give life to all of them; the host of heaven worships you.

units.la: Psal.104.per totum: nominatim v.27.28.29.30. Omnia ista in te expectationem habent, vt des escam ipsorum tempore suo: Te dante ipsis colligunt, aperiente manum tuam satiantur bono: Abscondente faciem tuam conturbantur; recipiente spiritum ipsorum exspirant, & in pulverem suum reuertuntur: Emittente spiritum tuum recreantur: denique renouas faciem terræ.
units.tr: Ps. 104 throughout, especially vv. 27–30. All these wait upon you, that you may give them their food in due season. When you give it to them, they gather it; when you open your hand, they are satisfied with good things. When you hide your face, they are troubled; when you take away their breath, they die and return to their dust. When you send forth your Spirit, they are created, and you renew the face of the earth.

units.la: Esa.45.verf.57. Cognoscent, me esse Dominum formantem lucem, & creantem tenebras, facientem pacem, & creantem malum, me Dominum facere omnia ista.
units.tr: Isa. 45.7. That they may know that I am the LORD, who forms the light and creates darkness, who makes peace and creates evil; I, the LORD, do all these things.

units.la: Thren.3.v.37.38. Ecquo dicente existit aliquid,si Dominus non præceperit? Ex ore excelsi an non prodit malum quodque & bonum?
units.tr: Lam. 3.37–38. Who is there who speaks and it comes to pass, unless the Lord has commanded it? Do not good and evil both come out of the mouth of the Most High?

units.la: Amos 3.v.6. An erit malum in ciuitate, quod Dominus non efficiat?
units.tr: Amos 3.6. Can there be evil in a city which the LORD has not done?

units.la: Act.17.v.25. Cùm ipse (Dominus) det omnibus vitam,& halitum,& omnia.
units.tr: Acts 17.25. Since he himself (the Lord) gives to all life and breath and all things.

units.la: Etv.28. In ipso enim viuimus,& mouemur,& sumus.
units.tr: And v. 28. For in him we live, and move, and have our being.

units.la: 2. Deus Pater, Filius, & Spiritus sanctus, regit mundum, & omnia in ipso.
units.tr: 2. God the Father, Son and Holy Spirit rules the world and all things in it.

units.la: Gen.19.v.24. Iehoua demisit super Sodomam & Gomorrham, pluuiam sulphuris & ignis; à Iehoua è cœlis.
units.tr: Gen. 19.24. The LORD rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven.

units.la: Iohan.5.v.17. Iesus autem respondit eis, Pater meus vsq; adhuc operatur,& ego operor.
units.tr: John 5.17. But Jesus answered them, My Father works until now, and I work.

units.la: Hebr.1.vers.3. Qui (Filius Dei) cùm sit effulgentia gloriæ,& character personæ illius, sustineatq; omnia verbo illo suo potente.
units.tr: Heb. 1.3. He (the Son of God), who being the brightness of his glory and the express image of his person, upholds all things by the word of his power.

units.la: Gen.1.v.2. Spiritus Dei incubabat superficiei aquarum.
units.tr: Gen. 1.2. The Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.

units.la: 1.Cor.12.v.11. Sed omnia hæc efficit vnus ille & idem Spiritus, distribuens priuatim illa singulis sicut vult. Exempla vide Exod. 28.v.3.c.31.v.3.c.35.v.31. Num.11.v.17.25.26.29.c.24.vers.2. c.27.v.18. Deut.34.v.9. Iudic.3.v.10.c.6.v.34.c.11.vers.29. c.14.v.6.19.1.Sam.10.v.6.10.c.11.v.6. quibus locis homines quidam dicuntur repleti fuisse Spiritu Dei,&Spiritus Domini dicitur irruisse siue insiliisse super ipsos.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 12.11. But all these things one and the same Spirit works, dividing to each one severally as he will. For examples see Exod. 28.3; 31.3; 35.31; Num. 11.17, 25, 26, 29; 24.2; 27.18; Deut. 34.9; Judg. 3.10; 6.34; 11.29; 14.6, 19; 1 Sam. 10.6, 10; 11.6. In these places certain men are said to have been filled with the Spirit of God, and the Spirit of the Lord is said to have come upon them or leapt upon them.

units.la: 3. Deus regit mundum fermè ordinariè, nonnunquam etiam extraordinariè.
units.tr: 3. God rules the world for the most part ordinarily, and sometimes also extraordinarily.

units.la: Hos.2.v.21.22. Erit etiam die illo,vt exaudiam, dictum Iehoua; exaudiam cœlos, & ipsi exaudiant terram; Et terra exaudiat frumentum,& mustum,& oleum; & ista exaudiant Iizrehelem.
units.tr: Hos. 2.21–22. And it shall come to pass in that day, says the LORD, that I will hear; I will hear the heavens, and they shall hear the earth; and the earth shall hear the corn, the wine and the oil; and they shall hear Jezreel.

units.la: Psal.104.v.9. Terminum opposuisti abysso,ne transeant aquæ, ne reuertantur ad operiendum terram.
units.tr: Ps. 104.9. You have set a boundary that they may not pass over, that they may not return to cover the earth.

units.la: Et147.vers.9.[?] Dat iumentis cibum suum,pullis coruorum,qui crocitant.
units.tr: And Ps. 147.9 [?]. He gives to the beasts their food, and to the young ravens which cry.

units.la: Gen.8.v.21.22. Dixit Iehoua cum animo suo:non iterum maledicturus sum amplius terræ propter hominem, eò quòd figmentum cordis hominis sit malum à pueritiâ ipsius: iterumq; non percutiam amplius omnia viuentia, quemadmodum feci. Deinceps quamdiu erit terra; sementis & messis, frigus q; & æstus, & æstas & hiems, dies q; & nox non cessabunt. Confer Deut.28. Psal.104. Matt. 5.v.45.c.6.v.26.30.
units.tr: Gen. 8.21–22. The LORD said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man's sake, because the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth; neither will I again smite any more every living thing, as I have done. While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night, shall not cease. Compare Deut. 28; Ps. 104; Matt. 5.45; 6.26, 30.

units.la: Act.14. v.17. Quanquam non passus est se esse expertem testimonij, bona tribuendo, dans nobis cælitus pluuias ac tempora fructibus edendis apta, implens cibo & lætitia corda nostra.
units.tr: Acts 14.17. Yet he did not leave himself without witness, in doing good and giving us rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.

units.la: Psalm.135.v.9. Deus immisit signa & prodigia in medium tui, Ægypte; contra Pharaonem, & seruos eius. De hac extraordinaria gubernatione vide Psal.105.106. Huc pertinent seqq. beneficia & iudicia Dei: diluuium Gen.7.verf.11. confusio Babylonica Genes.11.v.7.8.9. decem plagæ Ægypti, Exod. 7.&seqq. transitus per mare rubrum Exod.14. petra percussa fundens aquam Exod.17.v.6. varia miracula in deserto, annis quadraginta Act.7.v.36. transitus per Iordanem Ios.3.v.16.17. statio solis & lunæ Ios.10.v.13. miraculosa multiplicatio farinæ, olei, panis. 1.Reg.17.v.16. Matth.14. verf.20. umbra solis retrograda 2.Reg.20.verf.10.11. conseruatio sociorum Danielis in fornace Babylonica. Dan.3. verf.24.25.26. aqua in vinum versa à Christo Iohan.2.v.8.9. 10. & alia ipsius miracula.
units.tr: Ps. 135.9. God sent signs and wonders into the midst of you, O Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants. On this extraordinary government see Ps. 105 and 106. To this belong the following benefits and judgments of God: the flood, Gen. 7.11; the confusion at Babel, Gen. 11.7–9; the ten plagues of Egypt, Exod. 7 ff.; the passage through the Red Sea, Exod. 14; the rock struck and yielding water, Exod. 17.6; the various miracles in the wilderness during forty years, Acts 7.36; the passage over the Jordan, Josh. 3.16–17; the standing still of the sun and moon, Josh. 10.13; the miraculous multiplication of meal, oil and bread, 1 Kings 17.16; Matt. 14.20; the shadow of the sun turned back, 2 Kings 20.10–11; the preservation of Daniel's companions in the Babylonian furnace, Dan. 3.24–26; water turned into wine by Christ, John 2.8–10; and his other miracles.

units.la: 4. Deus regit mundum sapienter, & valde bene.
units.tr: 4. God rules the world wisely and very well.

units.la: Deut.32.verf.4. Rupis illius opus est perfectum. Omnes enim viæ illius sunt iusti: Deus fidelis, & expers iniquitatis, iustus & rectus est.
units.tr: Deut. 32.4. His work is perfect. For all his ways are just; God is faithful and without iniquity, just and right is he.

units.la: Psalm.104.verf.24. Quàm ampla sunt opera tua, ô Domine! quàm ea omnia sapienter fecisti! quàm plena est terra possessione tua!
units.tr: Ps. 104.24. How manifold are your works, O LORD! In wisdom have you made them all; the earth is full of your possessions.

units.la: Psalm.111.v.2.3.4. Magna opera Domini, expositæ omnibus, qui delectantur illis: gloriosum & decorum opus eius, & iustitiam eius perstantem in æternum. Memoriam comparauit mirabilium suis, gratiosus & misericors Dominus.
units.tr: Ps. 111.2–4. The works of the LORD are great, sought out by all who delight in them; his work is glorious and majestic, and his righteousness endures forever. He has made his wonderful works to be remembered; the LORD is gracious and merciful.

units.la: Et verf.7.8. Opera manuum eius sunt veritatis & iudicij: confirmantia omnia mandata eius. Confer Dan.4.v.37.
units.tr: And vv. 7–8. The works of his hands are truth and judgment; all his commandments are sure. Compare Dan. 4.37.

units.la: Rom.8.v.28. Nouimus, iis, qui diligunt Deum, omnia simul in adiumento esse ad bonum.
units.tr: Rom. 8.28. We know that to those who love God all things work together for good.

units.la: 5. Deus regit magna & parua.
units.tr: 5. God rules great things and small.

units.la: Iere.5.verf.22. An me non reuerebimini? dictum Domini: an à facie meâ non contremiscetis? qui disposui arenam terminum maris, statuto perpetuo, quod non transgredietur; quamuis incutiant se, non tamen praualent; quamuis fremant fluctus eius, non tamen transgrediuntur illud.
units.tr: Jer. 5.22. Do you not fear me? says the LORD; will you not tremble before my face? I who have set the sand as the boundary of the sea, by a perpetual decree, which it cannot pass; though the waves toss themselves, they cannot prevail; though they roar, they cannot pass over it.

units.la: Psal.147.verf.7.8.9. Acclamate Domino gratiarum actione: qui obtegit cœlos densis nubibus, qui comparat terræ pluuiam, qui facit, vt proferant montes fœnum: dat iumentis cibum suum, pullis coruorum, qui crocitant: qui edit niuem, sicut lanam, pruinam quasi cinerem dispergit: deiicit gelu suum tanquam frusta, emittens verbum suum, liquefacit ista: simulac efflat ventum, effluunt aquæ. Confer Iob.36.37.38.39.
units.tr: Ps. 147.7–9. Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving; who covers the heavens with thick clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes the mountains bring forth grass; he gives to the beasts their food, and to the young ravens which cry. He gives snow like wool, and scatters frost like ashes; he casts forth his ice like morsels; who can stand before his cold? He sends out his word and melts them; he makes the wind blow and the waters flow. Compare Job 36, 37, 38, 39.

units.la: Pfalm.34.verf.21. Seruat (Dominus) omnia ossa eius (iusti) vnum ex illis non frangitur.
units.tr: Ps. 34.21. He (the LORD) keeps all his (the righteous man's) bones; not one of them is broken.

units.la: Prou.21.verf.1. Vt riui aquarum, sic animus regis est in manu Domini: quocunque vult, inclinat eum.
units.tr: Prov. 21.1. As the rivers of water, so is the heart of the king in the hand of the LORD; he turns it wherever he will.

units.la: Ion.4.v.7. Parauit Deus vermem ascendente aurorâ, postero mane: quo ladente ricinum, exaruit.
units.tr: Jon. 4.7. God prepared a worm when the dawn rose the next morning, which attacked the gourd, and it withered.

units.la: Matth.6.v.26.30. Intuemini in volucres cœli: non enim serunt, neq; metunt, neque cogunt in horrea, sed Pater ille vester cœlestis alit eas. Si herbam agri, quæ hodie extat, & cras in clibanum immittitur, Deus ita circumuestit: nonne vos multò magis, ô exiguæ fidei praditi.
units.tr: Matt. 6.26, 30. Look at the birds of the air; for they neither sow nor reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feeds them. If God so clothes the grass of the field, which today is and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will he not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?

units.la: Etc.10.v.29. Nonne duo passerculi assario veneunt, & vnus ex eis non cadet in terram sine Patre vestro?
units.tr: And 10.29. Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? And not one of them falls to the ground without your Father.

units.la: 6. Deus regit peccata sanctè, ita vt non sit author peccati.
units.tr: 6. God governs sins holily, so that he is not the author of sin.

units.la: Pfal.5.verf.5. Nones[?] Deus, qui delectetur improbitate: non est commoraturum apud te malum.
units.tr: Ps. 5.5. For you are not a God who delights in wickedness; evil shall not dwell with you.

units.la: Iac.1.v.13. Nemo cùm tentatur, dicat, à Deo tentor. Nam Deus tentari malis non potest, nec quenquam tentat.
units.tr: James 1.13. Let no one say when he is tempted, I am tempted by God; for God cannot be tempted with evil, and he himself tempts no one.

units.la: 1.Ioh.1.v.5. Hic est nuntius ille, quem audiuimus ex ipso, & renuntiamus vobis, Deum lucem esse, nec tenebras in eo vllas esse.
units.tr: 1 John 1.5. This is the message which we have heard from him and declare to you, that God is light, and in him there is no darkness at all.

units.la: Exod.7.verf.6. Ego vero obdurabo cor Pharaonis.
units.tr: Exod. 7.6. But I will harden the heart of Pharaoh.

units.la: 2.Sam.12.verf.11.12. Sic ait Iehoua, Ecce ego suscitaturus sum contra te malum è domo tuâ: & accipiens vxores tuas ante oculos tuos tradam proximo tuo: qui cubabit cum vxoribus suis coram isto sole. Quia tu fecisti clam, etiam ego facturus sum rem hanc coram toto Israële, & coram sole.
units.tr: 2 Sam. 12.11–12. Thus says the LORD, Behold, I will raise up evil against you out of your own house; and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbour, who shall lie with your wives in the sight of this sun. For you did it secretly, but I will do this thing before all Israel and before the sun.

units.la: 2.Sam.16.v.10.11. Si Iehoua dixit ei (Simei) Maledic Dauidi: ecquis dicat, Quare sic facis? Sinite eum vt maledicat: quia edixit ei Iehoua.
units.tr: 2 Sam. 16.10–11. If the LORD has said to him (Shimei), Curse David, who then shall say, Why have you done so? Let him alone, that he may curse, because the LORD has bidden him.

units.la: 1.Reg.22.v.21.22. Prodijt quidam spiritus, qui consistens coram Domino, dixit: Ego pelliciam eum. (Achabum) Dicente vero Domino, quo pacto? Dixit: Egressus ero spiritus mendacij in ore omnium prophetarum eius. Tunc dixit, Pellicies etiamq; praualebis: exi, & fac ita.
units.tr: 1 Kings 22.21–22. A certain spirit came forth, and stood before the LORD and said, I will entice him (Ahab). And when the LORD said, How? he said, I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. Then he said, You shall entice him and prevail also; go out and do so.

units.la: Esa.10. verf.5.& deinceps. Va Assyrio (Sanheribo) virga iræ meæ: quamuis in manu baculus est indignationis meæ: In gentem hypocritam immittam ipsum, & contra populum, in quem excandui, dabo mandata ipsi; vt prædetur prædam, & vt diripiat rapinam, &c.
units.tr: Isa. 10.5 and following. Woe to the Assyrian (Sennacherib), the rod of my anger; though in his hand is the staff of my indignation. I will send him against a hypocritical nation, and give him commands against the people with whom I am angry, to seize the spoil and to take the prey, etc.

units.la: Actor.2.v.23. Hunc (Iesum) definito consilio & antedecreto Dei deditum cum accepissetis, manibus sceleratorum affixum interemistis.
units.tr: Acts 2.23. Him (Jesus), delivered up by the determined counsel and foreknowledge of God, you have taken and by wicked hands have crucified and slain.

units.la: Et cap.4.verf.27.28. Congregati vero sunt contra sanctum puerum tuum Iesum, quem vnxisti. Herodes & Pontius Pilatus, cum gentibus & populis Israël, vt facerent quæcunque manus tua & consilium tuum prius definierat, vt fierent.
units.tr: And 4.27–28. For truly against your holy child Jesus, whom you anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel, were gathered together, to do whatever your hand and your counsel had determined before to be done.

units.la: LOCVS IX.
units.tr: LOCVS IX.

units.la: De angelis.
units.tr: On angels.

units.la: 1. Angeli sunt spiritus meri, hoc est, à corpore liberi.
units.tr: 1. Angels are pure spirits, that is, free from the body.

units.la: Hebr.i.v.14. Nonne omnes (angeli boni) sunt ministratores Spiritus?
units.tr: Heb. 1. v. 14. Are they not all (the good angels) ministering spirits?

units.la: Matth.10. verf.1. Dedit eis potestatem aduersus spiritus immundos.
units.tr: Matt. 10. v. 1. He gave them power against unclean spirits.

units.la: Luc.24.v.39. Spiritus carnem & ossa non habet.
units.tr: Luke 24. v. 39. A spirit does not have flesh and bones.

units.la: 2. Angeli sunt à Deo creati.
units.tr: 2. Angels were created by God.

units.la: Colos.1.v.16. Per eum (Christum) condita sunt omnia, quæ in cœlis sunt, & quæ in terrâ, visibilia & invisibilia.
units.tr: Col. 1. v. 16. By him (Christ) all things were created, whether in heaven or on earth, visible and invisible.

units.la: 3. Angeli boni sunt sancti, & Deo promptè obsequuntur.
units.tr: 3. The good angels are holy and promptly obey God.

units.la: Luc.9.v.26. Quando venerit (Filius hominis) cum gloriâ suâ, & Patris, sanctorumq;angelorum.
units.tr: Luke 9. v. 26. When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.

units.la: Psal.103.vers.20.21. Benedicite Iehoua, angeli eius, valentissimi robore, efficientes verbum eius, auscultantes voci verbi eius. Benedicite Iehoua omnes exercitus eius: ministri eius, facientes placitum eius. Confer Zach.1.vers.16. vbi de angelis dicitur: Hi sunt, quos misit Dominus, ad perambulandam terram.
units.tr: Ps. 103. vv. 20, 21. Bless the LORD, you his angels, mighty in strength, who do his word, hearkening to the voice of his word. Bless the LORD, all you his hosts, you ministers of his, who do his pleasure. Compare Zech. 1. v. 16, where of the angels it is said: These are they whom the Lord has sent to walk to and fro through the earth.

units.la: 4. Boni angeli ordinariè habitant in cœlo beatorum.
units.tr: 4. The good angels ordinarily dwell in the heaven of the blessed.

units.la: Matth.18.v.10. Videte ne contemnatis aliquem ex paruis istis: dico enim vobis, angelos eorum in cœlis per omne tempus videre faciem Patris mei qui in cœlis est.
units.tr: Matt. 18. v. 10. See that you do not despise one of these little ones; for I tell you that in heaven their angels always see the face of my Father who is in heaven.

units.la: 5. Bonorum angelorum numerus est longè maximus.
units.tr: 5. The number of the good angels is far the greatest.

units.la: Dan.7.v.10. A cuius (Dei) conspectu fluvius ignis manabat, prodiens, cui millies mille ministrabant, & coram quo myrias myriadum stabant.
units.tr: Dan. 7. v. 10. A river of fire flowed from his presence (God's); thousands upon thousands ministered to him, and myriads upon myriads stood before him.

units.la: Matth.26.v.53. An putas, me nonposse nunc precari Patrem meum,qui huc mihi sistat plures, quàm duodecim legiones angelorum? id est, 79992. si nempe legio constet 6666.
units.tr: Matt. 26. v. 53. Do you think that I cannot now pray to my Father, who would at once send me more than twelve legions of angels? That is, 79,992, if a legion consists of 6,666.

units.la: Hebr.12.v.22. Accessistis ad montem Sion, & civitatem Dei vivi,Hierusalem cœlestem,& myriadas angelorum.
units.tr: Heb. 12. v. 22. You have come to Mount Zion, and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels.

units.la: Apoc.5.v.11. Aspexi, & audiui in circuitu throni & animalium,& senum, vocem angelorum multorum, numero millies centies mille & decies centies mille.
units.tr: Rev. 5. v. 11. I looked, and I heard around the throne and the living creatures and the elders the voice of many angels, numbering myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands.

units.la: 6. Bonorum angelorum potentia est admodum magna.
units.tr: 6. The power of the good angels is very great.

units.la: Psalm.103.vers.20. Benedicite Domino angeli eius, valentissimi robore.
units.tr: Ps. 103. v. 20. Bless the LORD, you his angels, mighty in strength.

units.la: 2.Petri 2.vers.12. Ipsi angeli, qui sunt robore ac potestate maiores.
units.tr: 2 Pet. 2. v. 11. Angels, who are greater in strength and power.

units.la: 2.Reg.19.verf.35. Nocte prodiens angelus Domini percussit in castris Assyriorum centum octoginta quinque millia.
units.tr: 2 Kings 19. v. 35. In the night the angel of the Lord went out and struck down in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and eighty-five thousand.

units.la: 7. Deus per bonos angelos solet
units.tr: 7. God is accustomed to use the good angels

units.la: a) hominibus impiis vel piis, plurimum tamen piis, aliquid nuntiare.
units.tr: a) to announce something to men, whether impious or pious, but chiefly to the pious;

units.la: b) pios protegere, illorumq; animas in cœlum deferre.
units.tr: b) to protect the pious and carry their souls into heaven;

units.la: c) pios castigare.
units.tr: c) to chastise the pious;

units.la: d) impios punire.
units.tr: d) to punish the impious;

units.la: e) impios reges coercere, ne noceant piis.
units.tr: e) to restrain impious kings, lest they harm the pious;

units.la: f) homines in fine seculi a quatuor mundi plagis colliget.
units.tr: f) to gather men from the four quarters of the world at the end of the age.

units.la: a) Impio Bileamo Num.22.v.32.& deinceps. Piis: vt, Lotho, Gen.19.v.13. Manoacho, parenti Simsonis, Iudic.c.13. v.3.4.5. Danieli, Dan.8.verf.16.cap.9.verf.21. & seqq. Zachariæ, patri Iohannis Baptistæ, Luc.1. verf.13. Mariæ virgini, ibid.verf.26. & deinceps. Pastoribus Bethlehemiticis Luc.2. verf.10.& seqq. Iosepho, marito Mariæ virginis, Matth.1. verf.20.& deinceps.cap.2.v.13.19.20. mulieribus Christum quærentibus in sepulchro, Matth.28. verf.5. apostolis spectantibus Christum ascendentem in cœlum, Actor.1.v.10. & seqq. Iohanni apostolo in ecstasin rapto, Apoc.1.v.1.
units.tr: a) To the impious Balaam, Num. 22. v. 32 and following. To the pious: as to Lot, Gen. 19. v. 13; to Manoah, the father of Samson, Judg. 13. vv. 3, 4, 5; to Daniel, Dan. 8. v. 16, 9. v. 21 and following; to Zechariah, the father of John the Baptist, Luke 1. v. 13; to the Virgin Mary, ibid. v. 26 and following; to the shepherds of Bethlehem, Luke 2. v. 10 and following; to Joseph, the husband of the Virgin Mary, Matt. 1. v. 20 and following, 2. vv. 13, 19, 20; to the women seeking Christ in the sepulchre, Matt. 28. v. 5; to the apostles watching Christ ascend into heaven, Acts 1. v. 10 and following; to the apostle John, rapt into ecstasy, Rev. 1. v. 1.

units.la: b) Psal.34. verf.8. Castra metatur angelus Iehovæ circa timentes eum, & eripit eos.
units.tr: b) Ps. 34. v. 8. The angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.

units.la: Psal.91.verf.11.12. Angelis suis præcipiet de te, vt conseruent te in omnibus viis tuis: ambabus palmis sustinebunt te, ne offendas ad lapidem pedem tuum. Confer Hebr.1. verf.14. Exempla vide Genes.19.verf.10.16. in historia Lothi, Genes.32.verf.1. in historia Iacobi, 1.Reg.19.verf.5.& seqq. de Elia, 2.Reg.6.verf.16. & seqq. de Elisæo, 2.Reg.19.verf.35. de Sennacheribo cæso, & Hiskia liberato. Dan.3.verf.35. de tribus sociis Danielis, Dan.6.verf.23. de Daniele in fovea leonum.
units.tr: Ps. 91. vv. 11, 12. He will give his angels charge over you, to keep you in all your ways; they shall bear you up in their hands, lest you dash your foot against a stone. Compare Heb. 1. v. 14. Examples: see Gen. 19. vv. 10, 16 in the story of Lot; Gen. 32. v. 1 in the story of Jacob; 1 Kings 19. v. 5 and following concerning Elijah; 2 Kings 6. v. 16 and following concerning Elisha; 2 Kings 19. v. 35 concerning Sennacherib slain and Hezekiah delivered; Dan. 3. v. 25 concerning the three companions of Daniel; Dan. 6. v. 22 concerning Daniel in the lions' den.

units.la: Luc.16.verf.22. Lazarus apportatur ab angelis in sinum Abrahæ.
units.tr: Luke 16. v. 22. Lazarus was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom.

units.la: c) 2.Sam.24. verf.15.17. Angelus Iehovæ percussit peste viros septuaginta mille.
units.tr: c) 2 Sam. 24. vv. 15, 17. The angel of the LORD struck down with pestilence seventy thousand men.

units.la: Luc.1.v.[?]o. Angelus Gabriel Zachariam effecit mutum, propterea quod non crediderat ipsi promittenti ei filium ex vxore.
units.tr: Luke 1. v. 20. The angel Gabriel made Zechariah dumb, because he had not believed him when he promised him a son by his wife.

units.la: d) Gen.19. Duo angeli perdunt Sodomitas & illorum vicinos.
units.tr: d) Gen. 19. Two angels destroy the Sodomites and their neighbours.

units.la: 2 Reg.19.verf.35. Angelus occidit centum octoginta quinque millia in castris Assyriorum.
units.tr: 2 Kings 19. v. 35. The angel killed a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians.

units.la: Act. 12. verf. 23. Angelus percussit Herodem, vt exederetur a vermibus.
units.tr: Acts 12. v. 23. An angel struck Herod, so that he was eaten by worms.

units.la: e) Dan.10.verf.13. Angelus Gabriel dicebat Danieli: Princeps regni Persici stetit coram me vno & viginti diebus, cùm ecce Michaël primus è principibus primariis venisset ad adiuuandum me.
units.tr: e) Dan. 10. v. 13. The angel Gabriel said to Daniel: The prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me for twenty-one days, until behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me.

units.la: Et verf.20. Reuertor ad pugnandum contra principem Persidis.
units.tr: And v. 20: I will return to fight against the prince of Persia.

units.la: f) Matth.24.verf.31. Mittet angelos suos cum tuba voce magna, & cogent electos eius, &c. Confer 1.Thess.4.v.16.
units.tr: f) Matt. 24. v. 31. He will send out his angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather his elect, etc. Compare 1 Thess. 4. v. 16.

units.la: 8. Angeli boni non sunt adorandi, sed imitatione virtutis honorandi.
units.tr: 8. Good angels are not to be worshipped, but honoured by imitating their virtue.

units.la: Apoc.19.verf.10. Cùm Iohannes cecidisset ante pedes angeli vt adoraret eum, dixit ille: Vide ne feceris. Conserus tuus sum. Idem repetitur cap.22.verf.9.
units.tr: Rev. 19. v. 10. When John had fallen down before the angel's feet to worship him, he said: See that you do not do it. I am your fellow servant. The same is repeated in chapter 22, verse 9.

units.la: Matth.6.verf.10. Fiat voluntas tua sicut in cœlo, ita & in terra. Et omninò si volumus post hanc vitam esse ἰσάγγελοι[?], hoc idem in hac vita à nobis requiritur. Luc.20.verf.35, 36. Matth.23.verf.30.
units.tr: Matt. 6. v. 10. Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. And altogether, if we wish to be isangeloi [ἰσάγγελοι] after this life, the same is required of us in this life. Luke 20. vv. 35, 36. Matt. 23. v. 30.

units.la: 9. Christus est caput angelorum.
units.tr: 9. Christ is the head of the angels.

units.la: Apoc.12.verf.7. Michael & angeli eius praliati sunt cum dracone.
units.tr: Rev. 12. v. 7. Michael and his angels fought with the dragon.

units.la: 10. Angeli mali fuerunt boni creati.
units.tr: 10. The evil angels were created good.

units.la: Iohan.8.verf.44. Ille (diabolus) fuit homicida à principio, & in veritate non perstitit.
units.tr: John 8. v. 44. He (the devil) was a murderer from the beginning, and did not stand in the truth.

units.la: Iudae verf.6. Angelos, qui non conseruarunt suam originem, sed reliquerunt suum domicilium, iudicio magni illius diei vinculis aeternis sub caligine reseruauit.
units.tr: Jude v. 6. The angels who did not keep their first estate, but left their own dwelling, he has kept in everlasting chains under darkness until the judgement of the great day.

units.la: 11. Angeli mali sunt multi.
units.tr: 11. There are many evil angels.

units.la: Lucae 8.verf.30. Interrogauit autem eum (Spiritum immundum) Iesus, dicens, Quod tibi nomen est? Ipse vero dixit, Legio. Nam dæmonia multa ingressa erant in ips[?]um.
units.tr: Luke 8. v. 30. Jesus asked him (the unclean spirit), saying: What is your name? And he said: Legion. For many demons had entered into him.

units.la: 12. Princeps malorum angelorum nominatur Satan, Iob. 1. vers. 6. Zach. 3. vers. 1. Luc. 10. vers. 18. Apoc. 12. v. 9. 1. Thess. 2. v. 18.
units.tr: 12. The prince of the evil angels is called Satan: Job 1. v. 6; Zech. 3. v. 1; Luke 10. v. 18; Rev. 12. v. 9; 1 Thess. 2. v. 18.

units.la: Beelzebub, Matth. 12. vers. 24.
units.tr: Beelzebub: Matt. 12. v. 24.

units.la: Diabolus, Matth. 25. v. 41. Iohan. 8. v. 44. 1. Iohan. 3. v. 8. Apoc. 12. v. 9. Eph. 6. v. 11. Iac. 4. v. 7.
units.tr: Devil: Matt. 25. v. 41; John 8. v. 44; 1 John 3. v. 8; Rev. 12. v. 9; Eph. 6. v. 11; Jas. 4. v. 7.

units.la: ὁ πονηρός, id est, nequam ille, Matth. 6. v. 13. Eph. 6. vers. 16.
units.tr: ho ponēros [ὁ πονηρός], that is, that wicked one: Matt. 6. v. 13; Eph. 6. v. 16.

units.la: 1. Iohan. 3. vers. 12.
units.tr: 1 John 3. v. 12.

units.la: ὁ πειράζων[?], id est, tentator, Matth. 4. vers. 3. 1. Thess. 3. vers. 5.
units.tr: ho peirazōn [ὁ πειράζων], that is, the tempter: Matt. 4. v. 3; 1 Thess. 3. v. 5.

units.la: Princeps mundi, Iohan. 12. vers. 31.
units.tr: Prince of the world: John 12. v. 31.

units.la: Draco magnus, Apoc. 12. v. 9.
units.tr: Great dragon: Rev. 12. v. 9.

units.la: Serpens antiquus, ibid.
units.tr: Ancient serpent: ibid.

units.la: Deus huius seculi, 2. Cor. 4. v. 4.
units.tr: God of this age: 2 Cor. 4. v. 4.

units.la: Aduersarius fidelium, 1. Petri 5. v. 8.
units.tr: Adversary of the faithful: 1 Pet. 5. v. 8.

units.la: Accusator fidelium, Apoc. 12. v. 10.
units.tr: Accuser of the faithful: Rev. 12. v. 10.

units.la: 13. Mali angeli sunt tales affectu & effectu.
units.tr: 13. Evil angels are such in disposition and in effect.

units.la: Hoc testantur ipsorum nomina, quibus appellantur, Spiritus mali, 1. Sam. 16. v. 15.
units.tr: Their names, by which they are called, testify to this: evil spirits, 1 Sam. 16. v. 15.

units.la: Sehirim, id est, horridi, Ier. 17. v. 7.
units.tr: Sehirim, that is, the horrid ones, Jer. 17. v. 7 (sic).

units.la: Schedim, id est, vastatores, Deut. 32. v. 17.
units.tr: Schedim, that is, destroyers, Deut. 32. v. 17.

units.la: Spiritus immundi, Matth. 10. v. 1.
units.tr: Unclean spirits, Matt. 10. v. 1.

units.la: Principatus, potestates, domini mundi, rectores tenebrarum seculi huius, spirituales malitiæ, seu spiritus nequam, Eph. 6. vers. 12. Vide etiam num. praeced.
units.tr: Principalities, powers, rulers of the darkness of this world, spiritual wickednesses, or wicked spirits, Eph. 6. v. 12. See also the preceding number.

units.la: 14. Angeli mali ex inferno emittuntur, ad castigandum & exercendum pios, & seducendum atque vexandum impios.
units.tr: 14. Evil angels are sent out from hell to chastise and exercise the pious, and to seduce and torment the impious.

units.la: 1. Petri 2. vers. 4. Deus angelis, qui peccauerunt, non pepercit, sed in tartarum detrusos catenis caliginis tradidit, damnationi seruatos. Vide Iudæ vers. 6. ad num. 10.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 2. v. 4. God did not spare the angels who sinned, but cast them down into hell and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be kept for judgement. See Jude v. 6, under number 10.

units.la: 1. Sam. 16. v. 15. Nam spiritus Iehoua recesserat à Saule, perturbat eum spiritus malus à Iehoua. Confer cap. 18. vers. 10. & 19. vers. 9. Iob.i.v.7.Satan dicit,se venire à peragrandâ terrâ. Confer cap.2.verf.2.
units.tr: 1 Sam. 16. v. 15. For the Spirit of the LORD had departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD troubled him. Compare chapter 18, verse 10, and 19, verse 9. Job 1. v. 7. Satan says that he comes from going to and fro on the earth. Compare chapter 2, verse 2.

units.la: Et cap.1.verf.12.& seqq. Exiuit Satan à conspectu Iehoua, ut nempe affligeret Iobum. Confer cap.2.
units.tr: And chapter 1, verse 12 and following: Satan went out from the presence of the LORD, to afflict Job. Compare chapter 2.

units.la: 1.Reg.22.v.22.Dixit spiritus malus:Egressus,ero spiritus mendax in ore omnium prophetarum eius, Achabi.
units.tr: 1 Kings 22:22: "The evil spirit said, I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets," of Ahab.

units.la: 1.Petri 5.verf.8.9. Sobrÿ estote & vigilate. Nam aduersarius vester diabolus, tanquam leo rugiens, obambulat, quærens, quem devoret: cui resistite firmi per fidem.
units.tr: 1 Peter 5:8-9: "Be sober and watchful. For your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walks about seeking whom he may devour. Resist him, steadfast in the faith."

units.la: Eph.6.v.11.Induite uniuersam armaturam Dei,ut possitis stareaduersus insidias diaboli.
units.tr: Eph. 6:11: "Put on the whole armour of God, that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil."

units.la: 1.Thess.2.v.18.Impediuit nos Satanas.
units.tr: 1 Thess. 2:18: "Satan hindered us."

units.la: Apoc.12.v.9.Qui (Satanas)seducit totum terrarum orbem.
units.tr: Rev. 12:9: "Who (Satan) deceives the whole world."

units.la: Et v.12. Vae incolis terrae & maris! Nam descendit diabolus ad vos, excandescentia magna plenus, ut qui sciat, se exiguum tempus habete. Confer cap.20.v.1.2.3.8.
units.tr: And v. 12: "Woe to the inhabitants of the earth and the sea! For the devil has come down to you in great wrath, knowing that he has a short time." Compare Rev. 20:1, 2, 3, 8.

units.la: Luc.8.verf.30. Daemonia multa ingressa erant in eum. Vide passim in historiâ euangelistarum de hominibus à diabolo obsessis.
units.tr: Luke 8:30: "Many demons had entered into him." See throughout the evangelists' history concerning men possessed by the devil.

units.la: 15. Diabolus, & ipsius angeli, non possunt hominem plus laedere, quam Deus eis permittit.
units.tr: 15. The devil and his angels cannot harm a man more than God permits them.

units.la: Iob.1.v.12.Itaq; dixit Iehoua Satana, ecce quaecunque sunt ei (Iobo) in manu tua sunto, tantummodò ne in ipsum mittito manum tuam: & exiuit Satan à conspectu Iehoua.
units.tr: Job 1:12: "And the LORD said to Satan, Behold, all that he has is in your hand; only do not put forth your hand against him. So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD."

units.la: Et cap.2.v.6. Tum Iehoua Satana,ecce eum, inquit,in manu tua; veruntamen vitam eius serua.
units.tr: And Job 2:6: "Then the LORD said to Satan, Behold, he is in your hand; only spare his life."

units.la: Matth.8.verf.31.32. Daemones vero precabantur eum, dicentes, Si eicis nos,permitte nobis abire in gregem pecorum illorum. Et ait eis,Abite. Illi vero egressi abierunt in illum gregem porcorum.
units.tr: Matt. 8:31-32: "And the demons begged him, saying, If you cast us out, send us into the herd of swine. And he said to them, Go. And they came out and went into the swine."

units.la: 16. Mali angeli non sunt adorandi aut consulendi, sed piis precibus sanctaque vitâ à nobis pellendi.
units.tr: 16. Evil angels are not to be worshipped or consulted, but driven away from us by pious prayers and a holy life.

units.la: Matth.4.v.9. Dixitq3[?] (diabolus) ei (Iesu.) Haec omnia tibi dabo, si prostratus adoraueris me. Tunc dicit ei Iesus. Abi Satana: scriptum est enim, Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, & ei soli seruies.
units.tr: Matt. 4:9-10: "The devil said to him, All these things will I give you, if you will fall down and worship me. Then Jesus said to him, Begone, Satan: for it is written, You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him only."

units.la: Deut.18.verf.10. Non inuenitor in te diuinam, diuinationes, praestigiator, & augur, neq; maleficus, neque incantator, neque interrogans Pythonem, neq; magus, neque quaerens a mortuis. Abominatio enim Iehoua est, qui facit haec. Vide historiam Saulis 1.Sam.28.
units.tr: Deut. 18:10-11: "There shall not be found among you anyone who makes his son or daughter pass through the fire, or who uses divination, or is an augur, a sorcerer, or an enchanter, or a consulter of spirits, or a wizard, or one who calls up the dead. For whoever does these things is an abomination to the LORD." See the history of Saul, 1 Sam. 28.

units.la: 1.Petri 5.v.8.9. Sobrij estote & vigilate. Nam aduersarius vester diabolus, &c. Vide num. praeced. 14. & ibid. Ephes. 6. verf. 11.
units.tr: 1 Peter 5:8-9: "Be sober and watchful. For your adversary the devil," etc. See the preceding number 14, and ibid.; Eph. 6:11.

units.la: Matth. 17. v. 21. Hoc verò genus daemoniorum non egreditur nisi per precationem & ieiunium. Confer Marc. 9. v. 29. Etc. 16. verf. 41. Vigilate & orate, ne introeatis in tentationem. Confer Marc. 13. v. 13.
units.tr: Matt. 17:21: "But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting." Compare Mark 9:29. Etc. Luke 16:41. "Watch and pray, that you may not enter into temptation." Compare Mark 13:13.

units.la: Iacob. 4. verf. 7. Resistite diabolo, & fugiet a vobis. Confer Matth. 4. verf. 11.
units.tr: James 4:7: "Resist the devil, and he will flee from you." Compare Matt. 4:11.

units.la: LOCVS X.
units.tr: LOCUS X.

units.la: De gratia primi hominis.
units.tr: On the grace of the first man.

units.la: 1. Homo à Deo conditus fuit bonus.
units.tr: 1. Man was created good by God.

units.la: Gen. 1. v. 27. Itaq; creauit Deus hominem ad imaginem suam; ad imaginem, inquam, Dei creauit eum.
units.tr: Gen. 1. v. 27. So God created man in his own image; in the image of God, I say, he created him.

units.la: Eccles. 7. v. 29. Deus fecit hominem rectum.
units.tr: Eccles. 7. v. 29. God made man upright.

units.la: 2. Gratia animae in homine protoplasto erat sapientia & iustitia originalis, hoc est, naturaliter propaganda.
units.tr: 2. The grace of the soul in the first man, the protoplast, was original wisdom and righteousness, that is, to be propagated naturally.

units.la: Coloss. 3. v. 10. Induite nouum illum hominem, qui renouatur in agnitionem (Dei) secundum imaginem eius, qui creauit eum.
units.tr: Col. 3. v. 10. Put on the new man, which is renewed in the knowledge of (God) after the image of him that created him.

units.la: Eph. 4. v. 24. Induite nouum illum hominem, qui secundum Deum conditus est in iustitia & sanctitate vera.
units.tr: Eph. 4. v. 24. Put on the new man, which after God is created in true righteousness and holiness.

units.la: 3. Gratia corporis in primo homine erat immortalitas & eximia pulchritudo, vtraque naturaliter propaganda, hoc est, pendens à iure creationis.
units.tr: 3. The grace of the body in the first man was immortality and exceeding beauty, both to be propagated naturally, that is, depending on the right of creation.

units.la: Gen. 2. v. 17. Nam quo die comederis deo, vtiq; morituru[?] es. Et cap.3.v.19. Puluis es, & in pulveremreverteris.
units.tr: Gen. 2. v. 17. For in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die. And ch. 3. v. 19. Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.

units.la: Et cap.2. v.25. Erant ambo nudi, Adam & uxor eius, ac non pudebat eos.
units.tr: And ch. 2. v. 25. And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.

units.la: 4. Gratia loci erat in paradisi amœnissimo ornatu, & usu sufficientissimo.
units.tr: 4. The grace of place was in the paradise of the most delightful adornment and in the most abundant sufficiency of use.

units.la: Gen.2.v.8. Ornaverat autem plantis Iehova Deus hortum in Edene ab oriente, ubi collocavit hominem illum, quem finxerat.
units.tr: Gen. 2. v. 8. And the LORD God had planted a garden eastward in Eden, and there he put the man whom he had formed.

units.la: Et vers.16. De fructu quidem omnis arboris huius horti liberè comedes.
units.tr: And v. 16. Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat.

units.la: 5. Gratia totius personæ in primo homine consistebat in dominio super animalia.
units.tr: 5. The grace of the whole person in the first man consisted in dominion over the animals.

units.la: Gen.1.v.28. Dominamini in pisces maris, & in volucres cœli, & in omnes bestias reptantes super terram. Confer Gen.2. v.19. 20.unde colligitur, hominem a bestiis pro domino fuisse cognitum. Bestiæ siquidem sese stiterunt coram Adamo, ut eis nomina imponeret.
units.tr: Gen. 1. v. 28. Have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth. Compare Gen. 2. v. 19, 20, whence it is gathered that man was recognised by the beasts as their lord. For the beasts indeed presented themselves before Adam, that he might give them names.

units.la: 6 Continuatio gratiæ primi hominis, seu integritatis naturæ, nitebatur fœdere naturæ, cuius sacramentum erat arbor vitæ.
units.tr: 6 The continuation of the grace of the first man, or of the integrity of nature, rested on the covenant of nature, whose sacrament was the tree of life.

units.la: Genes.2.v.16.17. Interdixit Dominus Deus homini dicendo: De fructu quidem omnis arboris huius horti libere comedes: de fructu vero arboris cognitionis boni & mali, de isto ne comedas. Nam quo diecomederis de eo, vtique moriturus es. Confer Gen.3.vers. 1.2.3.4.
units.tr: Gen. 2. v. 16, 17. And the LORD God commanded the man, saying: Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat; but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die. Compare Gen. 3. v. 1, 2, 3, 4.

units.la: Genes.2.vers.9. Arbor quoq; vitæ in horto illo. Confer Genes.3.vers.22.
units.tr: Gen. 2. v. 9. The tree of life also in the midst of the garden. Compare Gen. 3. v. 22.

units.la: LOCVS XI.
units.tr: Topic XI.

units.la: De coniugio.
units.tr: On marriage.

units.la: 1. Coniugium est arctissimum fœdus inter unum virum & unam fœminam.
units.tr: 1. Marriage is the closest covenant between one man and one woman.

units.la: Malach.2.vers.14. Propterea quod Iehova testificatus est inter te & uxorem adolescentiæ tuæ, contra quam tu perfide agis, cùm sit sociatua, & uxor fœderis tui.
units.tr: Mal. 2:14. Because the LORD hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant.

units.la: Gen.2.v.23.24.Dixit Adam: Hac ipsa demum est os ex ossibus meis, & caro ex carne mea: hac vocabitur vira, eo, quod hac ex viro desumpta est. Idcirco relicturus est vir patrem suum & matrem suam, & adhaerebit uxori suae, erunt in carnem unam.
units.tr: Gen. 2:23-24. Adam said: This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife, and they shall be one flesh.

units.la: Matth.19. verf.4.5.6. Ille vero (Iesus) respondens dixit eis, Non legistis opificem ab initio fecisse masculum & fœminam? Et dixisse, Propterea derelinquet homo patrem & matrem, & agglutinabitur uxori suae: & qui duo fuerant, erunt una caro? Itaq; non amplius sunt duo, sed una caro. Confer Eph.5.v.31.
units.tr: Matt. 19:4-6. He answered and said unto them, Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female, and said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. Compare Eph. 5:31.

units.la: 2. Fœcundum coniugium pendet à benedictione Dei cùm generali, tùm speciali.
units.tr: 2. Fruitful marriage depends on the blessing of God, both general and special.

units.la: Gen.1.v.28.Benedixit eis (hominibus) Deus: & dixit Deus, fœtificate, ac augescite, & implete terram.
units.tr: Gen. 1:28. God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.

units.la: Gen.16. verf.2. Dixit ergo Sarai Abramo, Ecce nunc occlusit me Iehoua, ne parerem.
units.tr: Gen. 16:2. And Sarai said unto Abram, Behold now, the LORD hath restrained me from bearing.

units.la: Et cap.30. verf.1.2. Cùm autem videret Rachel se non parere Iacobo, aemulata est Rachel sorori suae, dixitq; Iacobo, Cedo mihi liberos, sin minus, morior. Sed accensa est ira Iacobi in Rachelam: adeò ut diceret, an loco Dei sum ego? qui prohibuit a te fructum ventris?
units.tr: And ch. 30:1-2. When Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister; and said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die. And Jacob's anger was kindled against Rachel, and he said, Am I in God's stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?

units.la: Psal.127.verf.3. Ecce possessio Iehouae sunt filij: merces est fructus ventris. Confer Psal.128.
units.tr: Ps. 127:3. Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward. Compare Ps. 128.

units.la: 3. Coniugium, etiam post lapsum, est status Deo placens.
units.tr: 3. Marriage, even after the Fall, is a state pleasing to God.

units.la: Hebr.13.v.4. Honorabile est inter quosuis coniugium, & cubile impollutum: scortatores autem & adulteros damnabit Deus.
units.tr: Heb. 13:4. Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.

units.la: Vide etiam Matth.19. ad num. præced. 1. Pertinent huc exempla patriarcharum, sacerdotum, prophetarum, & aliorum sanctorum, qui vixerunt in coniugio.
units.tr: See also Matt. 19 under the preceding number 1. The examples of the patriarchs, priests, prophets and other saints who lived in marriage belong here.

units.la: De coniugio [?]sacerdotum vide Leuit.21.v.9.13. & deinceps: de coniugio episcoporum. 1.Tim.3.v.2, Tit.1.v.6.
units.tr: On the marriage of priests see Lev. 21:9, 13 and following; on the marriage of bishops, 1 Tim. 3:2, Titus 1:6.

units.la: 4. Coniugium non debet contrahi à personis, quæ propter consanguinitatem vel affinitatem prohibentur id facere.
units.tr: 4. Marriage ought not to be contracted by persons who are forbidden to do so on account of consanguinity or affinity.

units.la: Vide Leuit. 18. & 20. Confer supra cum Iurisprudentiâ sacrâ.
units.tr: See Lev. 18 and 20. Compare above with sacred jurisprudence.

units.la: 5. Adulterium dissoluit matrimonium.
units.tr: 5. Adultery dissolves marriage.

units.la: Matth. 19. verf. 6. Quod ergo Deus coniunxit, homo non se-iungat.
units.tr: Matt. 19:6. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

units.la: Et verf. 9. Dico autem vobis, Quicunque dimiserit uxorem suam nisi ob scortationem, & aliam duxerit, moechatur, & qui dimissam duxerit, moechatur.
units.tr: And v. 9. And I say unto you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.

units.la: 6. Coniugium conseruatur officiis coiugum mutuis.
units.tr: 6. Marriage is preserved by the mutual duties of spouses.

units.la: De officio mariti vide Eph.5.v.25.28.29.33. Colos.3.v.19, 1.Petr.3.v.7. 1.Tim.2.v.8.
units.tr: On the husband's duty see Eph. 5:25, 28, 29, 33; Col. 3:19; 1 Pet. 3:7; 1 Tim. 2:8.

units.la: De officio vxoris vide Ephes.5.v.22.23.24. Colos.3.verf.18. 1.Tim.2.v.9.&feqq.c.3.v.11.Tit.2.v.4.5. 1.Petr.3.v.1.&feqq.
units.tr: On the wife's duty see Eph. 5:22, 23, 24; Col. 3:18; 1 Tim. 2:9 and following, and ch. 3:11; Titus 2:4, 5; 1 Pet. 3:1 and following.

units.la: LOCVS XII.
units.tr: Locus XII.

units.la: De peccato.
units.tr: On sin.

units.la: 1. Peccatum est discrepantia à lege Dei.
units.tr: 1. Sin is a departure from the law of God.

units.la: 1. Iohan.3.v.4. ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐστὶν ἡ ἀνομία, id est, Peccatum est illegalitas, seu discrepantia à lege.
units.tr: 1. Iohan.3.v.4. ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐστὶν ἡ ἀνομία, that is, Sin is lawlessness, or departure from the law.

units.la: 2. Peccatum cognoscitur ex lege.
units.tr: 2. Sin is known from the law.

units.la: Rom.3.v.20. Per legem est agnitio peccati.
units.tr: Rom.3.v.20. Through the law comes the knowledge of sin.

units.la: Etc.7.v.7. Peccatum non cognoui nisi per legem.
units.tr: Rom.7.v.7. I had not known sin except through the law.

units.la: 3. Omne peccatum meretur mortem æternam.
units.tr: 3. Every sin deserves eternal death.

units.la: Rom.6.v.vlt. Stipendia peccati mors. Confer c.5.v.21.
units.tr: Rom.6.v.last. The wages of sin is death. Compare c.5.v.21.

units.la: Matth.12.v.36. Sed dico vobis, quodcunque verbum otiosum locuti fuerint homines, de eo reddituros rationem in die iudicij.
units.tr: Matth.12.v.36. But I say to you, that for every idle word men speak, they will render an account of it on the day of judgment.

units.la: 4. Adam & Eva peccarunt inobedientiâ erga Deum.
units.tr: 4. Adam and Eve sinned by disobedience toward God.

units.la: Rom.5.verf.14. Peccatum primum primi hominis appellatur παράβασις[?], id est, transgressio mandati. Confer 1.Timoth.2.verf.14.
units.tr: Rom.5.v.14. The first sin of the first man is called παράβασις, that is, transgression of a command. Compare 1 Tim.2.v.14.

units.la: Rom.5.v.19. Sicut enim per inobedientiam unius hominis peccatores constituti sunt multi.
units.tr: Rom.5.v.19. For as through the disobedience of one man many were made sinners.

units.la: Vide Gen.3.vbi verf.1. est suspicio inuidiæ de Deo: verf. 4.5.6. infidelitas & dubitatio de veritate comminationis Dei: per.6. intemperantia gulæ: ibidem, curiositas, seu cupiditas plura sciendi quàm erat necessarium: ibidem, cupiditas gloriæ diuinæ. Tandem secutus est contemtus mandati diuini, παρακοὴ [?], Rom.5.v.19. & παράβασις [?], transgressio mandati de non edendo fructu arboris cognitionis boni & mali.Rom.5.v.14.
units.tr: See Gen.3, where in v.1 there is a suspicion of envy toward God; in vv.4, 5, 6 unbelief and doubt about the truth of God's threat; in v.6 the intemperance of gluttony; in the same place, curiosity, or the desire to know more than was necessary; in the same place, the desire for the glory of God. Finally came contempt of the divine command, παρακοή, Rom.5.v.19, and παράβασις, transgression of the command not to eat the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, Rom.5.v.14.

units.la: 5. Omnes homines (solo Christo excepto) peccauerunt in Adamo.
units.tr: 5. All men (Christ alone excepted) sinned in Adam.

units.la: Rom.5. v.12. Per vnum hominem peccatum in mundum introiit, ac per peccatum mors, & ita in omnes homines mors peruafit, in quo omnes peccarunt.
units.tr: Rom.5.v.12. Through one man sin entered the world, and through sin death, and so death spread to all men, in whom all sinned.

units.la: Etv.19. Per inobedientiam vnius illius hominis peccatores constituti sunt multi, οἱ πολλοί, nempe quotquot ex illo naturaliter sunt orti, ex sanguine videlicet, & ex libidine carnis, & ex libidine viri.Iohan.1.v.13.
units.tr: And v.19. Through the disobedience of that one man many were made sinners, οἱ πολλοί, namely, all who are naturally descended from him, that is, from blood, and from the lust of the flesh, and from the lust of man. Iohan.1.v.13.

units.la: 1.Cor.15.v.22. In Adamo omnes moriuntur.
units.tr: 1 Cor.15.v.22. In Adam all die.

units.la: 6. Omnes homines (solo Christo excepto) cum peccato concipiuntur & nascuntur.
units.tr: 6. All men (Christ alone excepted) are conceived and born with sin.

units.la: Psal.51.vers.7. En cum iniquitate genitus sum, & cum peccato concepit me mater mea.
units.tr: Psal.51.v.7. Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity, and my mother conceived me in sin.

units.la: Eph.2.v.3. Eramus natura filij ira, vt & reliqui.
units.tr: Eph.2.v.3. We were by nature children of wrath, as the rest also were.

units.la: Genes.5.v.3. Adam autem vixerat triginta & centum annos, cum genuit filium ad similitudinem suam, ad imaginem suam.
units.tr: Gen.5.v.3. Adam lived a hundred and thirty years, and begot a son in his own likeness, after his image.

units.la: Vide Rom. 7. vbi peccatum originale appellatur cupiditas, vers.7. peccatum summe peccans, vers.13. peccatum inhabitans, vers.17.20. malum adiacens, vers.21. lex in membris nostris belligerans aduersus legem mentis, & captiuos nos reddens legi peccati, quæ est in membris nostris, vers.23.25.
units.tr: See Rom.7, where original sin is called concupiscence, v.7; sin exceedingly sinful, v.13; indwelling sin, vv.17, 20; evil lying close at hand, v.21; the law in our members warring against the law of the mind, and making us captive to the law of sin which is in our members, vv.23, 25.

units.la: Iacob.1.v.14.15. Sed vnusquisq; tentatur, dum à propria cupiditate abstrahitur & inescatur. Deinde cupiditas, postea quam concepit, parit peccatum: peccatum vero peractum gignit mortem.
units.tr: James 1.v.14, 15. But each one is tempted when he is drawn away and enticed by his own desire. Then desire, after it has conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full grown, brings forth death.

units.la: 7. Peccata sunt inæqualia.
units.tr: 7. Sins are unequal.

units.la: Ioh.19.vers.11. Christus dicit Pilato: Qui me tradidit tibi, maius peccatum habet.
units.tr: John 19.v.11. Christ says to Pilate: He who delivered me to you has the greater sin.

units.la: Matth.10. v.15. Tolerabilior erit conditio terra Sodomorum & Gomorrhæorum in die iudicij, quàm vrbis illius.
units.tr: Matth.10.v.15. It will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city.

units.la: Pertinent huc varij casus peccati in Scripturis: puta, peccatum ignorantiæ,1.Tim.1.v.3.peccatum irremissibile, Matth.12.v.32. 1.Ioh.5.v.16. peccatum cū scandalo coniunctum,Matth.18.v.6.7. peccatum clamans in cœlum,Genef. 4.verf.10.peccatum ante manifestum,quod præit damnationem; cui opponitur peccatum subsequens,1.Tim.5. v.24. peccatum alienum, & communicatio cū alieno peccato,1.Tim.5.v.21. peccatum,quod fit elatâ manu,Num.15. v.30. peccatum extra proprium corpus, vel in proprium corpus,1.Cor.6.v.18. peccatum regnans, vel non-regnans, Rom.6.v.12.c.7.v.19. peccatum mortuum, vel viuens,Roman.7.v.9. peccatum priuatum, vel publicum & manifestarium,Matth.18.v.15.& deinceps:peccatum occultum plané,vel cognitum,Psal.19.verf.13.Matth.10.verf.26.2.Cor.4. verf.2. denique cogitatum, dictum, vel factum malum Gen.6.v.5.Matth.15.v.19.
units.tr: Here belong the various kinds of sin found in the Scriptures: for example, (1) sin of ignorance, 1 Tim.1.v.3; (2) unforgivable sin, Matth.12.v.32, 1 John 5.v.16; (3) sin joined with scandal, Matth.18.v.6, 7; (4) sin crying out to heaven, Gen.4.v.10; (5) sin that is manifest beforehand, which goes before condemnation, as opposed to sin that follows, 1 Tim.5.v.24; (6) another's sin, and communion in another's sin, 1 Tim.5.v.21; (7) sin committed with a high hand, Num.15.v.30; (8) sin outside one's own body, or within one's own body, 1 Cor.6.v.18; (9) reigning sin, or sin that does not reign, Rom.6.v.12, c.7.v.19; (10) dead sin, or living sin, Rom.7.v.9; (11) private sin, or public and manifest sin, Matth.18.v.15 and following; (12) sin wholly hidden, or known, Psal.19.v.13, Matth.10.v.26, 2 Cor.4.v.2; and finally, evil thought, word, or deed, Gen.6.v.5, Matth.15.v.19.

units.la: 8. Peccati author est diabolus.
units.tr: 8. The author of sin is the devil.

units.la: Ioh.8.v.44. Ille (diabolus)fuit homicida à principio. Vide Genef.3.
units.tr: Iohan.8.v.44. He (the devil) was a murderer from the beginning. See Gen.3.

units.la: 1.Ioh.3.verf.8. Qui facit peccatum, ex diabolo est:quoniam à principio diabolus peccat.
units.tr: 1 John 3.v.8. He who commits sin is of the devil, for the devil has sinned from the beginning.

units.la: 9. Peccatum ex se parit reatum & poenam.
units.tr: 9. Sin of itself brings forth guilt and punishment.

units.la: Rom.5. verf.16. Nam reatus quidem est ex uno lapsu ad condemnationem.
units.tr: Rom.5.v.16. For the guilt indeed arises from one fall, leading to condemnation.

units.la: Et v.18. Nempe igitur per unum lapsum reatus venit in omnes homines ad condemnationem.
units.tr: And v.18. Therefore, through one fall, guilt came upon all men to condemnation.

units.la: Poena peccati est mors temporalis & æterna, prima & secunda, corporis & animi, omnisque afflictio, quæ est malum animi,corporis,vel fortunæ. Vide Gen.2.v.17. Rom. 6.verf.vlt.Apoc.20.v.14.c.22. v.15.
units.tr: The punishment of sin is death, temporal and eternal, first and second, of body and of soul, and every affliction, which is an evil of the soul, of the body, or of fortune. See Gen.2.v.17, Rom.6.v.last, Apoc.20.v.14, c.22.v.15.

units.la: LOCVS XIII.
units.tr: LOCVS XIII.

units.la: De lege De- i.
units.tr: On the Law of God

units.la: 1. Deus in primâ creatione legem suam inscripsit cordi hominis. Rom.2.v.14.15. Nam cum gentes qua legem non habent, natura qua legis sunt faciant, isti legem non habentes, sibi ipsis sunt lex: vt qui ostendant opus legis scriptum in cordibus suis.
units.tr: 1. God, at the first creation, inscribed his law on the heart of man. Rom. 2:14-15: For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves: which shew the work of the law written in their hearts.

units.la: 1.Cor.11.v.14. Anne natura quidem ipsa hoc vos docet?
units.tr: 1 Cor. 11:14: Doth not even nature itself teach you?

units.la: 2. Deus speciali quadam lege circumscripsit primi hominis libertatem.
units.tr: 2. By a special law God restricted the liberty of the first man.

units.la: Gen.1.v.16.17. Interdixitq3 Iehoua Deus homini, dicendo: De fructu quidem omnis arboris horti huius libere comedes: De fructu vero arboris scientiæ boni & mali, de isto ne comedas: nam quo die comederis de eo, vtique moriturus es.
units.tr: Gen. 1:16-17: And the LORD God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat: but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.

units.la: 3. Lex naturæ, siue moralis, est æterna iustitiæ regula.
units.tr: 3. The natural or moral law is the eternal rule of righteousness.

units.la: Hæc lex à Deo est præscripta in monte Sinai, tanquam regula vitæ, Exod.19. v.5.8. Eius compendium est decalogus, Exod.20. qui ad omnes pertinet.
units.tr: This law was prescribed by God on Mount Sinai as the rule of life, Exod. 19:5, 8. Its summary is the Decalogue, Exod. 20, which pertains to all.

units.la: Summa decalogi est Matth.22.verf.37. & deinceps, his verbis: Diliges Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, & ex tota anima tua, & ex tota cogitatione tua. Islud est primum & maximum mandatum. Secundum autem simile est huic (id est, etiam generale, & multa in se complectens; & æque observandum.) Diliges proximum tuum vt te ipsum. Ab istis duobus mandatis tota lex & prophetæ pendent.
units.tr: The sum of the Decalogue is in Matt. 22:37 and following, in these words: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it (that is, also general, and comprehending many things within itself, and equally to be observed): Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.

units.la: Iacob.2.v.8. Quod si legem regiam præstatis secundum Scripturam, Diliges proximum tuum vt teipsum, bene facitis.
units.tr: James 2:8: If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well.

units.la: Matth.5.v.16.17. Ita splendeat lux vestra coram hominibus, vt videant vestra bona opera, glorificent q3 patrem vestrum qui est in cælis. Ne existimate me venisse vt dissoluam legem aut prophetas. Non veni vt dissoluam, sed vt impleam.
units.tr: Matt. 5:16-17: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven. Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.

units.la: 1.Tim.1.v.8. Scimus autem bonam esse legem, si quis ea legitime vtatur.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 1:8: But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully.

units.la: 4. Lex tum moralis, tum iudicialis, tum denique ceremonialis, est speculum peccati.
units.tr: 4. The law, whether moral, judicial, or finally ceremonial, is a mirror of sin.

units.la: Rom.3.v.20. Per legem est agnitio peccati.
units.tr: Rom. 3:20: By the law is the knowledge of sin.

units.la: Etc.7.v.7. Peccatum non cognoui nisi per legem.
units.tr: Rom. 7:7: I had not known sin but by the law.

units.la: Coloss.2.v.14. Deleto, quod aduersum nos erat, rituum chirographo: quod erat nobis occulte contrarium.
units.tr: Col. 2:14: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us.

units.la: Exod.21.v.1. Hæc autem sunt iudicia illa, quæ proponeseis: ut nempe illa obseruent, & inde discant natiuam propensionem ad peccandum.
units.tr: Exod. 21:1. Now these are the judgments which thou shalt set before them: that they may observe them and from them learn our innate tendency to sin.

units.la: 5. Lex moralis est electis abrogata, quantum ad rigidum suum postulatum, adeoque quantum attinet ad iustificationem & maledictionem.
units.tr: 5. The moral law has been abrogated for the elect as to its rigid demand, and so far as it concerns justification and condemnation.

units.la: Gal.3.v.13. Christus nos redemit ab execratione legis, dum pro nobis factus est execratio.
units.tr: Gal. 3:13: Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us.

units.la: Et v.11. Nullum autem per legem iustificari apud Deum, manifestum est: quoniam iustus ex fide viuet.
units.tr: Gal. 3:11: But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith.

units.la: Rom.8.v.2.3.4. Lex spiritus vitæ, qui est in Christo Iesu, liberauit me à lege peccati & mortis. Nam quæ legis erat impotentia, cum viribus esset destituta per carnem, Deus Filio suo misso in forma consimili carni peccato obnoxia, idq; pro peccato, condemnauit peccatum in carne: Ut ius illud legis compleatur in nobis, qui non secundum carnem incedimus, sed secundum spiritum.
