units.tr: Rom. 8:2-4: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death. For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh: that the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

units.la: 6. Ex legibus forensibus Mosaicis illæ sunt perpetuæ, quæ sunt iuris communis, siue quæ habent aliquid morale: illæ vero sunt abrogatæ, quæ sunt iuris particularis, id est, eius iuris, quod fuit proprium politiæ Mosaicæ; & quæ habent aliquid ceremoniale additum.
units.tr: 6. Among the forensic laws of Moses, those are perpetual which belong to the common law, or which contain something moral; but those are abrogated which belong to particular law, that is, to that law which was proper to the Mosaic polity, and which have something ceremonial added.

units.la: Deut.1.v.17. Iudicium Dei est.
units.tr: Deut. 1:17: The judgment is God's.

units.la: 2.Chron.19.v.6. Videte, quid fitis[?] facturi: Non enim pro homine iudicaturi estis, sed pro Iehouâ: qui nobiscum futurus est in rebus iudiciariis.
units.tr: 2 Chron. 19:6: Take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for the LORD, who is with you in the judgment.

units.la: Sic lex illa Exod. 21. v. 17. est æterna: Qui maledicit patri suo aut matri suæ, omnino morte plectitor.
units.tr: So that law in Exod. 21:17 is eternal: He that curseth his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.

units.la: At lex ibid.v.2.est propria istius politiæ: Cum emeris seruum Hebræum, sex annis seruiet.
units.tr: But the law in the same chapter, verse 2, is proper to that polity: If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve.

units.la: Denique lex ista Exod. 22. v. 29. est mixta ceremoniâ: Primogenitum filiorum tuorum dato mihi.
units.tr: Finally, the law in Exod. 22:29 is mixed with ceremony: The firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me.

units.la: 7. Leges ceremoniales in N.T. non amplius durant.
units.tr: 7. The ceremonial laws no longer remain in the New Testament.

units.la: Galat. 3. v. 24. 25. Lex pædagogus noster fuit in Christum respiciens: vt ex fide iustificaremur. At postquam venit fides, non amplius sub pædagogo sumus.
units.tr: Gal. 3:24-25: Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.

units.la: Eph.2.v.14.15.16. Ipse (Christus) est pax nostra: qui vtraq; fecit vnum, & intergerini parietis septum soluit: inimicitiis, id est, lege mandatorum quæ in ritibus posita est, per carnem suam abolitis: vt ex duobus illis conderet in semetipso vnum nouum hominem, faciens pacem: & vtrosque in vno corpore reconciliaret Deo per crucem, peremtis inimicitiis per eam.
units.tr: Eph. 2:14-16: For he (Christ) is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us; having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances, for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace; and that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby.

units.la: Coloss.2.v.14. & deinceps. Christus deleto quod aduersum nos erat rituum chirographo, quod erat nobis contrarium: ipsum sustulit è medio, affixo eo cruci, &c. Ne quis igitur vos damnet ob cibum vel potum, vel respectu festi, aut nouilunij, aut sabbatorum. Quæ sunt vmbra futurorum: corpus autem est Christi.
units.tr: Col. 2:14 and following: Christ, blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross, etc. Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.

units.la: Hebr.10.vers.1. Lex vmbram obtinens futurorum bonorum, non expressam formam rerum, &c. Vide quoque Dan.9.vers. 24.27.
units.tr: Heb. 10:1: For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, etc. See also Dan. 9:24, 27.

units.la: LOCVS XIV.
units.tr: LOCUS XIV.

units.la: De libero arbitrio.
units.tr: On free will.

units.la: 1. Per peccatum mens hominis ita est obtenebrata, vt in rebus spiritualibus cœca fit.
units.tr: 1. Through sin the mind of man is so darkened that it becomes blind in spiritual matters.

units.la: 1.Cor.2.vers.14. Animalis (ψυχικὸς) homo non capit ea quæ sunt spiritus Dei. Sunt enim ei stultitia: nec potest ea cognoscere.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 2.14. The natural [ψυχικὸς] man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God; for they are foolishness to him, and he cannot know them.

units.la: Iohan.1.vers.5. Lux ista in tenebris lucet: sed tenebræ eam non comprehenderunt.
units.tr: John 1.5. That light shines in the darkness, but the darkness did not comprehend it.

units.la: Et v.18. Deum nemo vidit vnquam. Filius ille vnigenitus qui est in sinu Patris, ille nobis exposuit.
units.tr: And v. 18. No one has ever seen God. The only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has made him known to us.

units.la: 2. Voluntas hominis per peccatum ita est deprauata, vt toto impetu feratur contra legem Dei.
units.tr: 2. Through sin the will of man is so depraved that it is carried with its whole force against the law of God.

units.la: Gen.6.vers.5. Omne figmentum cogitationum cordis hominis tantummodo malum est omni tempore.
units.tr: Gen. 6.5. Every imagination of the thoughts of man's heart is only evil, at all times.

units.la: Et cap.8.v.21. Figmentum cordis hominis malum est à pueri-tiâ ipsius.
units.tr: And ch. 8.21. The imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth.

units.la: Rom.8.vers.7. Affectus carnis inimicitia est aduersus Deum. Legienim Dei non subiicitur. Nam nepotest quidem. Huc pertinent loca, quibus homo dicitur esse mortuus, vt Matth.8. v.22. Iohan.5.v.25. Eph.2.v.1.5. Coloss.2.v.13.
units.tr: Rom. 8.7. The mind of the flesh is enmity against God; for it is not subject to the law of God. For neither is it able. To this belong the passages in which man is said to be dead, such as Matt. 8.22; John 5.25; Eph. 2.1, 5; Col. 2.13.

units.la: 3. Deus in homine efficit potentiam, quâ potest credere, & ipsum fidei actum: similiter potentiam, quâ potest velle, & ipsum velle, ipsumq; agere.
units.tr: 3. God works in man both the power by which he can believe, and the act of faith itself; likewise the power by which he can will, and the willing itself, and also the doing.

units.la: Phil.1. v.29. Vobis datum est in Christi negotio in ipsum credere.
units.tr: Phil. 1.29. It has been given to you, on behalf of Christ, to believe in him.

units.la: Et c.2.v.13. Deus est is, qui efficit in vobis velle & perficere pro suo beneplacito.
units.tr: And ch. 2.13. It is God who works in you both to will and to do, according to his good pleasure.

units.la: Pertinent huc illa Scripturae loca, quibus dicitur, Deum circumcidere cor nostrum, Deut.30. v.6: Deum dare nobis cor, vt intelligamus, oculos vt videamus, aures vt audiamus, Deut.29.v.4: Deum dare nobis cor nouum & spiritum nouum, auferre cor lapideum, dare carneum, Ezech.36.v.26.27: Deum nos conuertere, Ierem.31. verf.18. Deum inscribere legem suam cordibus nostris, Ier.31.verf. 33: Deum aperire nobis cor, Act.16.v.14: Deum illuminare oculos mentis nostrae, vt videamus, Ephes.1. verf.18.19: Deum omnia nobis donare, quae ad vitam & pietatem pertinent, 2.Petr.1.v.3: Charitatem Dei effundi in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctum, Rom.5.v.5: denique nos iterum gigni, & excitari ex morte. Iohan.3. verf.3. cap.5.verf. 25. Ephes.2. verf.5.
units.tr: To these belong those passages of Scripture in which it is said that God circumcises our heart (Deut. 30.6); that God gives us a heart to understand, eyes to see, and ears to hear (Deut. 29.4); that God gives us a new heart and a new spirit, takes away the heart of stone and gives a heart of flesh (Ezek. 36.26, 27); that God converts us (Jer. 31.18); that God writes his law on our hearts (Jer. 31.33); that God opens our heart (Acts 16.14); that God enlightens the eyes of our mind so that we may see (Eph. 1.18, 19); that God gives us all things that pertain to life and godliness (2 Pet. 1.3); that the love of God is poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit (Rom. 5.5); and finally that we are born again and raised from death (John 3.3; 5.25; Eph. 2.5).

units.la: 4. Homo in primo conuersionis momento se habet mere passiue.
units.tr: 4. In the first moment of conversion, man is related purely passively.

units.la: Iohan.6.v.44. Nemo potest venire ad me, nisi Pater traxerit eum. Confer cum num. praeced.
units.tr: John 6.44. No one can come to me unless the Father draws him. Compare with the preceding number.

units.la: 5. Homo in progressu conuersionis agit actus à Spiritu sancto.
units.tr: 5. In the progress of conversion, man performs acts by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Cant.1.v.4. Trahe me, post te curremus.
units.tr: Song 1.4. Draw me, we will run after you.

units.la: 2.Cor.3. v.5.6. Non quod idonei sumus per nos ipsos ad cogitandum quidquam, velut ex nobis ipsis: sed quod idonei sumus, id ex Deo est. Qui etiam effecit, vt idonei esseimus ministri noui foederis.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 3.5, 6. Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think anything as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God. who also made us sufficient as ministers of the new covenant.

units.la: 1.Cor.15.verf.10. Gratia Dei sum id quod sum: & gratia eius, quæ in me collata est, non fuit inanis, sed amplius quàm illi omnes laboraui: non ego tamen, sed gratia Dei quæ mecum est.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 15.10. By the grace of God I am what I am; and his grace bestowed on me was not in vain, but I laboured more abundantly than they all; yet not I, but the grace of God which is with me.

units.la: 1.Cor.3.verf.5. Quis igitur est Paulus, quis autem Apollos, nisi ministri per quos credidistis, & vt cuiq;[?] Dominus dedit.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 3.5. Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers through whom you believed, and as the Lord gave to each.

units.la: Et v.9. Etenim Dei sumus cooperarij, συνεργοί.
units.tr: And v. 9. For we are God's fellow workers [συνεργοί].

units.la: Et v.10. Secundum gratiam Dei, quæ data est mihi, vt peritus architectus fundamentum posui.
units.tr: And v. 10. According to the grace of God which was given to me, as a wise master builder I laid the foundation.

units.la: LOCVS XV.
units.tr: LOCVS XV.

units.la: De magistratu.
units.tr: De magistratu.

units.la: 1. Functio magistratus Deo probatur.
units.tr: 1. The office of the magistrate is proved from God.

units.la: Psal.81.vers.1.Deus stat in cætu Dei:in medio deorum (id est, magistratuum, qui sunt vicarij Dei in administrandoiure) iudicat.
units.tr: Psal. 81:1, God stands in the assembly of God; in the midst of the gods (that is, of the magistrates, who are God's vicars in administering justice) he judges.

units.la: Et v.6. Dixi, Vos dii estis, & filii Excelsi omnes.
units.tr: And v. 6: I said, You are gods, and all of you are sons of the Most High.

units.la: Deut.1.v.17. Iudicium Dei est.
units.tr: Deut. 1:17: The judgment is God's.

units.la: 2.Chron.19. v.6. Non hominis iudicium exercetis, sed Dei.
units.tr: 2 Chron. 19:6: You exercise not the judgment of man, but of God.

units.la: Proverb.8.v.15. Per me reges regnant, & legum conditores iuste decernunt.
units.tr: Prov. 8:15: By me kings reign, and makers of laws decree justice.

units.la: Dan.2.v.21. Deus transfert regna, atq; constituit.
units.tr: Dan. 2:21: God removes kingdoms and sets them up.

units.la: Rom.13.v.1.2. Omnis anima potestatibus superemineentibus[?] subiecta esto. non enim est potestas nisi a Deo: & quæ sunt potestates, sunt a Deo ordinatæ. Itaq; quisquis se opponit potestati, Dei ordinationi resistit: qui autem resistunt, ipsi sibi condemnationem auferent.
units.tr: Rom. 13:1-2: Let every soul be subject to the higher powers. For there is no power but of God, and the powers that exist are ordained by God. Therefore whoever resists the power resists the ordinance of God, and those who resist will bring condemnation upon themselves.

units.la: Ibid.v.4. Dei enim minister est (magistratus) tuo bono.
units.tr: Ibid. v. 4: For he is God's minister (the magistrate) for your good.

units.la: 2. Ad officium magistratus pertinet a) studiose legere verbum Dei. b) instituere ac tueri purum Dei cultum. c) exercere ius & iustitiam:tuendo scil. bonos, & puniendo malos. d) moderata tributa & vectigalia exigere à subditis.
units.tr: 2. It belongs to the office of the magistrate (a) to read the word of God diligently; (b) to establish and defend the pure worship of God; (c) to exercise right and justice, namely by protecting the good and punishing the wicked; (d) to levy moderate taxes and duties from his subjects.

units.la: {a} Deut.17.v.18.19. Sederit cùm insidebit (rex populi If-raëliraëlitici) folio regni sui, vt describat sibi exemplum huius legis in libro, ex eo qui erit in conspectu sacerdotum Leuiticorum: eritq; peneseum, & leget in eo omnibus diebus vitæ suæ: vt discat timere Iehouam Deum suum, obseruare omnia verba huius legis & statuta ista, faciendo ea.
units.tr: {a} Deut. 17:18-19: When the king of Israel sits on the throne of his kingdom, he shall write for himself a copy of this law in a book, taken from the one that is before the Levitical priests; and it shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear Jehovah his God, to observe all the words of this law and these statutes, by doing them.

units.la: Iosu.1, v.8. Ne discedito (Deus alloquitur Iosuam.) Liber iste legis ab ore tuo: sed meditaberis in eo interdiu & nocte: vt cum obseruantia facias omnino prout scriptum est in eo.
units.tr: Josh. 1:8 (God speaks to Joshua): Do not let this book of the law depart from your mouth; but meditate on it day and night, so that you may act carefully in accordance with everything written in it.

units.la: b) 2.Reg.18.v.3.& seqq. Fecit (Ezechias) quod rectum videtur in oculis Iehouae: omnino prout fecerat Dauid pater eius. Ipse amouit excelsa, fregitq; statuas, & excidit lucum: contudit etiam serpentem aeneum, quem fecerat Moses, eo quod usq; ad dies illos Israëlitae adolerent ei, &c. Confer 2.Chron.29.
units.tr: (b) 2 Kings 18:3ff.: (Hezekiah) did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, just as David his father had done. He removed the high places, broke the pillars, and cut down the grove; he also crushed the bronze serpent that Moses had made, because until those days the Israelites had burned incense to it, etc. Compare 2 Chron. 29.

units.la: Vide quoque exemplum Iosiae, 2.Reg. 23. & Iosaphati; 2.Chron.19.v.29.
units.tr: See also the example of Josiah, 2 Kings 23, and of Jehoshaphat, 2 Chron. 19:29.

units.la: c) Ier.22.verf.3. Sic ait Iehoua, Exercete (rex Iudae & principes) ius & iustitiam: & eripite eum, qui rapinam patitur è manu oppressoris: & peregrino, pupillo ac viduae ne vim faciatis: ne violentia utimini, & sanguinem innocentem ne effundite in locoisto.
units.tr: (c) Jer. 22:3: Thus says Jehovah: Exercise (O king of Judah, and princes) right and justice, and rescue the one who is robbed from the hand of the oppressor; and do no violence to the stranger, the orphan, or the widow; do not use force, and do not shed innocent blood in this place.

units.la: Psal.82.v.2.3.4. Quousque iudicabitis iniquè, & faciem improborum suscipietis? Iudicate secundum tenuem & pupillum: afflictum & pauperem iustum pronunciate. Liberate tenuem & egentem, è manu improborum eripite.
units.tr: Ps. 82:2-4: How long will you judge unjustly, and show favour to the wicked? Judge the poor and the fatherless; declare right the afflicted and the needy. Deliver the weak and the destitute; rescue them from the hand of the wicked.

units.la: Rom.3.v.3.4. Magistratus non sunt terrori bonis operibus, sed malis. Vis autem non metuere potestatem? Quod bonum est facito, & laudem ab ipso obtinebis. Dei enim minister est tuo bono. Quod si feceris quod malum est, metue: non enim temerè gestat gladium. Nam Dei minister est, ultor ad iram ei qui quod malum est fecerit.
units.tr: Rom. 13:3-4: Magistrates are a terror not to good works but to evil ones. Do you wish, then, not to fear the power? Do what is good, and you will have praise from it. For he is God's minister for your good. But if you do what is evil, be afraid; for he does not bear the sword in vain. For he is God's minister, an avenger for wrath against the one who does evil.

units.la: d) Rom.13.v.6.7. Propter hoc enim etiam tributa soluitis, &c. Reddite igitur omnibus quod debetis: cui tributum debetur, tributum: cui vectigal, vectigal. Confer Deuter.17.cum 1.Reg.8. de quâ collatione vide supra Iurisprudentiam sacram.
units.tr: (d) Rom. 13:6-7: For this reason you also pay taxes, etc. Render therefore to all what you owe: tribute to whom tribute is due, and custom to whom custom is due. Compare Deut. 17 with 1 Kings 8, on which comparison see above, in the Jurisprudence sacred.

units.la: 3. Magistratus bono exemplo debet praelucere subditis, ita ut meminerit, regiam personam decere virtutes regias.
units.tr: 3. The magistrate ought to shine forth with a good example to his subjects, remembering that royal dignity befits royal virtues.

units.la: Pfal.2. v.10.11.12. Nunc ergo Reges, animaduertite, eruditionem percipite, o iudices terra: Colite Iehouam cum reuerentia, & exultate cum tremore. Osculamini filium vt non irascatur, & pereatis in via, cum exarserit vel minimum ira eius. Beati omnes qui se recipiunt ad eum.
units.tr: Ps. 2:10-12: Now therefore, O kings, take heed; receive instruction, you judges of the earth. Serve Jehovah with reverence, and rejoice with trembling. Kiss the Son, lest he be angry and you perish in the way, when his anger flares up even a little. Blessed are all who take refuge in him.

units.la: Vide Pfal.101. per totum.
units.tr: See Ps. 101 throughout.

units.la: LOCVS XVI.
units.tr: TOPIC XVI.

units.la: De Euangelio.
units.tr: On the Gospel.

units.la: 1. Euangelium est laetum nuntium de foedere gratiae, quod Deus nobiscum iniit in manu mediatoris Iesu Christi.
units.tr: 1. The gospel is the glad news of the covenant of grace, which God made with us in the hand of the Mediator, Jesus Christ.

units.la: Esa.54.v.10. Quamuis hi montes recederent, & hi colles dimouerentur: attamen benignitas mea a te non recedet, & foedus pacis mea non dimouebitur, ait miserator tuus Iehoua.
units.tr: Isa. 54.10: Though these mountains depart, and these hills be removed, yet my kindness shall not depart from you, and the covenant of my peace shall not be removed, says the Lord your merciful Jehovah.

units.la: Eph.6.v.15. Praeparatione Euangelij pacis, (scil. induti estote.
units.tr: Eph. 6.15: Having shod your feet with the preparation of the gospel of peace (namely, be clothed).

units.la: Matth.11.v.4.5. Et respondens Iesus dixit ei, Ite & renunciate Iohanni, qua auditis & videtis: Caeci visum recipiunt, & claudi ambulant, leprosi mundantur, & surdi audiunt, mortui suscitantur, & pauperibus euangelizatur.
units.tr: Matt. 11.4-5: And Jesus answering said to them, Go and report to John what you hear and see: the blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.

units.la: Rom.1.v.16. Non enim me pudet euangelij Christi. potentia siquidem est Dei ad salutem cuiuis credenti.
units.tr: Rom. 1.16: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ; for it is the power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes.

units.la: Esa.55.v.3.4. Inclinate aurem vestram, & venite ad me, audite vt viuat anima vestra: & pangam vobiscum foedus perpetuum, benignitates Dauidis certissimas collaturus sum. En testem nationum constituo eum, antecessorem & praeceptorem nationum.
units.tr: Isa. 55.3-4: Incline your ear and come to me; hear, that your soul may live; and I will make with you an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David. Behold, I have made him a witness to the nations, a leader and commander of the nations.

units.la: Hebr.13[?].v.20. Qui magnum illum ouium per sanguinem foederis aeterni pastorem, Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, a mortuis reduxit.
units.tr: Heb. 13[?].20: Who brought again from the dead that great shepherd of the sheep, our Lord Jesus Christ, through the blood of the eternal covenant.

units.la: 2. Euangelium & foedus gratiae est vnum idemque in V. & N. T. quantum ad substantiam & fundamentum attinet. Nam vtrobique a) promittitur vita æterna. b) promissio fit ex gratia. c) promissio fit propter Christum.
units.tr: 2. The gospel and the covenant of grace are one and the same in the Old and New Testaments, as far as substance and foundation are concerned. For in both (a) eternal life is promised; (b) the promise is made out of grace; (c) the promise is made on account of Christ.

units.la: a) Gen.17.v.7. Stabilio fœdus meum inter me & te, &c. mefore tibiin Deum & femini tuo.
units.tr: a) Gen. 17.7: I will establish my covenant between me and you, etc., to be a God to you and to your seed.

units.la: Exod.3.v.6.Ego sum Deus patris tui, Deus Abrahami, & Deus Isaaci, & Deus Iacobi. Confer Matth.22.v.32.
units.tr: Exod. 3.6: I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. Compare Matt. 22.32.

units.la: Esa.51.v.6. Salus mea in sæculum erit.
units.tr: Isa. 51.6: My salvation shall be for ever.

units.la: Matth.8.vers.[?]11. Dico vobis, Multi ab oriente & occidente ve-nient, & discumbent cum Abrahamo, & Isaaco, & Iacobo, in regno cœlorum.
units.tr: Matt. 8.11: I say to you, many shall come from east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.

units.la: b) Actor.15.vers.11. Imò per gratiam Domini nostri Iesu Christi credimus nos seruatum iri: quemadmodum & illi, scilicet patres.
units.tr: b) Acts 15.11: But we believe that we shall be saved through the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, just as they also, namely the fathers, were.

units.la: c) Ioh.8.vers.56. Abraham gestiuit videre diem meum: & vidit, & gauisus est.
units.tr: c) John 8.56: Abraham rejoiced to see my day, and he saw it and was glad.

units.la: Hebr.11.v.4. Abel per fidem maioris pretij sacrificium obtulit Deo quàm Cain.
units.tr: Heb. 11.4: By faith Abel offered to God a sacrifice of greater worth than Cain's.

units.la: Et cap.13.vers.8. Iesus Christus heri & hodie idem est, & in sæcula.
units.tr: And ch. 13.8: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and for ever.

units.la: 3. Euangelium & fœdus gratiæ modo promulgationis & administrationis fuit diuersum in V.&N.T.quatenus
units.tr: 3. The gospel and the covenant of grace differ in the manner of their promulgation and administration in the Old and New Testaments, in that:

units.la: a) Soli Abrahamo & posteris eius fuit promulgatum & administratum in V.T. in N. autem aliis quoq; populis promulgatur & administratur.
units.tr: a) In the Old Testament it was promulgated and administered to Abraham and his posterity alone; in the New it is promulgated and administered also to other peoples.

units.la: b) In V.T. fuit obscurius promulgatum & administratum: in nouo promulgatur & administratur clarius.
units.tr: b) In the Old Testament it was promulgated and administered more obscurely; in the New it is promulgated and administered more clearly.

units.la: c) In V. T. minore cum efficacia Spiritus sancti fuit promulgatum & administratum: in nouo promulgatur & administratur maiore cum efficacia.
units.tr: c) In the Old Testament it was promulgated and administered with less efficacy of the Holy Spirit; in the New it is promulgated and administered with greater efficacy.

units.la: d) In V.T.administratio fœderis gratiæ fuit onerosior atq; operosior, quàm est in N.
units.tr: d) In the Old Testament the administration of the covenant of grace was more burdensome and laborious than it is in the New.

units.la: a) Gen.15.v.18. Hoc die pepigit Dominus cum Abrahamo fœdus,dicendo; Semini tuo dedi terram hanc.
units.tr: a) Gen. 15.18: On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abraham, saying: To your seed I have given this land.

units.la: Et cap.17.v.7. Stabilio fœdus meum inter me & te, ac semen tuum post te per ætates suas, vt fœdus sit perpetuum, me esse tibi Deum, & femini tuo post te.
units.tr: And ch. 17.7: I will establish my covenant between me and you, and your seed after you throughout their generations, as an everlasting covenant, that I should be a God to you and to your seed after you.

units.la: Psal.147. vers.20. Non fecit ita vlli genti; ideoq; iura [?]ista non nouerunt.
units.tr: Ps. 147.20: He has not dealt so with any nation; therefore they have not known his judgments.

units.la: Act.14.v.16. Prateritis atatibus suit Deus omnes gentes suis ipsarum viis incedere.
units.tr: Acts 14.16: In past ages God allowed all nations to walk in their own ways.

units.la: Matth.28.v.19. Profecti,docete omnes gentes: baptizantes eos in nomen Patris,& Filij,& Spiritus sancti. Confer Marc.16.v. 15.Esa.2.v.2. Hagg.2.v.7. Rom.1.v.5.16.Eph.3.v.5.6.
units.tr: Matt. 28.19: Go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Compare Mark 16.15; Isa. 2.2; Hag. 2.7; Rom. 1.5, 16; Eph. 3.5, 6.

units.la: b) Coloss.2.v.17. Quæ sunt vmbra rerum futurarum,at corpus est Christi.
units.tr: b) Col. 2.17: Which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is Christ.

units.la: Hebr.10.v.1. Lex vmbram obtinens futurorum bonorum,non ipsam expressam formam rerum.
units.tr: Heb. 10.1: The law, holding a shadow of the good things to come, and not the very image of the things themselves.

units.la: c) Ioh.7.v.38.39. Qui credit in me,sicut dicit Scriptura, flumina aquæ viuæ ex ventre ipsius fluent. Hoc autem dixit de spiritu isto, quem accepturi erant credentes in eum. Nondum enim erat Spiritus sanctus, quia Iesus nondum erat glorificatus.
units.tr: c) John 7.38-39: He who believes in me, as the Scripture says, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. But he said this of the Spirit, whom those who believed in him were to receive; for the Holy Spirit was not yet, because Jesus was not yet glorified.

units.la: Act.2. v.17. Erit vltimis temporibus (dicit Deus) effundam ex spiritu meo in quamuis carnem: & prophetabunt filij vestri, & filiæ vestræ, & iuuenes vestri visiones videbunt, & seniores vestri somnia somniabunt.
units.tr: Acts 2.17: In the last days, God says, I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams.

units.la: Galat.4.v.4. Postquam venit plenum tempus, emisit Deus Filium suum factum ex muliere,factum legi subiectum:vt eos,qui legi erant subiecti,redimeret.
units.tr: Gal. 4.4: When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, to redeem those who were under the law.

units.la: d) Actor.15.vers.10. Quid tentatis Deum imponendo iugum ceruici discipulorum: quod neque patres nostri neque nos portare potuimus.
units.tr: d) Acts 15.10: Why do you test God by putting a yoke on the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear?

units.la: Gal.3.v.24. Lex pædagogus noster fuit in Christum.
units.tr: Gal. 3.24: The law was our schoolmaster unto Christ.

units.la: Et cap.4. vers.1.2.3. Quamdiu hæres infans est, nihil differt à seruo, quamuis sit dominus omnium:sed sub tutoribus & curatoribus est vsq; ad tempus, quod pater præstituerit: ita & nos,cum essemus infantes, sub elementis mundi eramus in seruitutem redacti.
units.tr: And ch. 4.1-3: As long as the heir is a child, he differs nothing from a servant, though he is lord of all; but he is under guardians and stewards until the time set by the father. So we also, when we were children, were held in bondage under the elements of the world.

units.la: Confer cap.5. v.1. & Gal.4.v.9.
units.tr: Compare ch. 5.1 and Gal. 4.9.

units.la: 4. Euangelium & fœdus gratiæ studium bonorum operum non excludunt,sed includunt.
units.tr: 4. The gospel and the covenant of grace do not exclude, but include, the zeal for good works.

units.la: Ela.55.v.5.6.&c seqq. Engentem[?],quam non agnoueras, vocabis, & gentes, qua non agnouerant te, accurrent ad te:propter Iehouam Deum tuum, & propter sanctum Israëlis, cum ornauerit te. Requirite Iehouam, cum prasto est; inuocate eum, cum est propinquus.Derelinquat improbus viam suam,&c.
units.tr: Isa. 55.5-6 and following: A nation that you did not know you shall call, and nations that did not know you shall run to you, because of Jehovah your God and the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you. Seek Jehovah while he may be found; call upon him while he is near. Let the wicked forsake his way, etc.

units.la: Ier.31.v.33.Hoc illud est fœdus quod pangam cum domo Israëlis post dies hos, dictum Iehoua: Indam legem meam menti eorum, & cordi eorum inscribam eam; & ero eis Deus, & ipsi erunt mihi po-pulus.
units.tr: Jer. 31.33: This is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says Jehovah: I will put my law within them, and write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

units.la: 2.Tim.2. v.19. Solidum stat fundamentum Dei; habens sigillum hoc, Nouit Dominus eos qui sunt sui:& Abscedat ab iniustitiâ quisquis nominat nomen Christi.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 2.19: The firm foundation of God stands, bearing this seal: The Lord knows those who are his; and let everyone who names the name of Christ depart from iniquity.

units.la: 5. Fœdus gratiæ substantiâ differt à fœdere operum:proinde & euangelium à lege sic differt.
units.tr: 5. The covenant of grace differs in substance from the covenant of works; therefore the gospel also differs from the law in this way.

units.la: Iere.31.v.31.32. Ecce dies venturi sunt, dictum Iehoua; quibus pangam cum domo Israëlis & cum domo Iuda fœdus nouum: Non secundùm illud fœdus,quod pepigeram cum maioribus ipsorum, quo die prehendi manum eorum, vt educerem eos è terra Ægypti. Nam ipsi irritum fecerunt fœdus meum, & ego coniugio iunctus mansissem eis? dictum Iehoua. Confer Hebr.8.v.6.c.12.v.4.
units.tr: Jer. 31.31-32: Behold, the days are coming, says Jehovah, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt. For they broke my covenant, though I was a husband to them, says Jehovah. Compare Heb. 8.6 and 12.4.

units.la: Galat.3.v.11. Nullum autem per legem iustificari apud Deum, manifestum est:quoniam iustus ex fide viuet.
units.tr: Gal. 3.11: But that no one is justified before God by the law is evident, because the just shall live by faith.

units.la: LOCUS XVII.
units.tr: LOCUS XVII.

units.la: De persona & officio Christi.
units.tr: On the person and office of Christ.

units.la: 1. Christus est θεάνθρωπος[?], id est, Filius Dei vnigenitus, certo tempore homo factus, idque ex Mariâ virgine.
units.tr: 1. Christ is theanthrōpos [θεάνθρωπος], that is, the only-begotten Son of God, made man at a certain time, and that from the Virgin Mary.

units.la: 1.Tim.3.ver.16. Sine controuersiâ magnum est pietatis mysterium:Deus conspicuus factus est in carne.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 3:16. Without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh.

units.la: Matth.i. v.23. Ecce virgo illa pragnans erit, & pariet filium, & vocabis nomen eius Immanuel; quod est, si interpreteris, Nobiscum Deus. Gal.4.v.4. Postquam venit plenitudo temporis, emisit Deus filium suum factum ex muliere, id est, virgine Maria, Matth.1. Lucæ 2.
units.tr: Matt. 1:23. Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Immanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us. Gal. 4:4. When the fullness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, that is, of the virgin Mary; Matt. 1; Luke 2.

units.la: Pertinet huc nomen Ithiel, Prouerb.30. quod idem est cum nomine Immanuel, & cum Græco Θεανθρώπος[?].
units.tr: The name Ithiel belongs here, Prov. 30, which is the same as the name Immanuel, and as the Greek theanthrōpos [Θεανθρώπος].

units.la: 2. Christus, vnigenitus Dei Filius assumsit naturam humanam. a) veram. b) integram. c) sanctam. d) ex Maria virgine. e) operatione Spiritus sancti conceptam.
units.tr: 2. Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, assumed human nature: a) true; b) whole; c) holy; d) from the Virgin Mary; e) conceived by the operation of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: a) Esa.9.v.6.7. Cùm puer natus fuerit nobis, filius datus nobis, cuius humero adsit principatus ipse; cuius nomen vocat Dominus admirabilem, consiliarium, Deum robustissimum, &c.
units.tr: a) Isa. 9:6–7. For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given, and the government shall be upon his shoulder; and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, etc.

units.la: Matth.18.v.1. Venit filius hominis, ut feruet, quod perierat.
units.tr: Matt. 18:11. The Son of man is come to save that which was lost.

units.la: Hebr.2.v.17. Vnde debuit per omnia similis fratribus fieri.
units.tr: Heb. 2:17. Wherefore it behoved him in all things to be made like unto his brethren.

units.la: Ideo dicitur semen mulieris, Genef.3.v.15. semen Abrahami, Gen.22.v.18. filius Abrahami & Dauidis, Matth.1.v.1. Marc.10.v.47: factus ex semine Dauidis, Rom.1.verf.4: germen Dauidis, Ierem.23.v.5: frater noster, Deut.18.v.18. Hebr. 2.verf.17.
units.tr: Therefore he is called the seed of the woman, Gen. 3:15; the seed of Abraham, Gen. 22:18; the son of Abraham and of David, Matt. 1:1; Mark 10:47; made of the seed of David, Rom. 1:3; the branch of David, Jer. 23:5; our brother, Deut. 18:18; Heb. 2:17.

units.la: b) Hebr.2.v.14. Quoniam pueri participes sunt carnis & sanguinis, ipse quoq; consimiliter particeps factus est eorundem.
units.tr: b) Heb. 2:14. Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same.

units.la: Etc.10.v.5. Corpus adaptasti mihi.
units.tr: Heb. 10:5. A body hast thou prepared me.

units.la: Matth.22.verf.38. Dicit Iesus: Vndiquaque tristis est anima mea vsq; ad mortem.
units.tr: Matt. 26:38. Jesus says: My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death.

units.la: Vide Psal.16. & 22.
units.tr: See Ps. 16 and 22.

units.la: c) Ierem.23.v.5. Ecce, dies venturi sunt, dictum Iehoua, quibus excitabo Dauidi germen iustum.
units.tr: c) Jer. 23:5. Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch.

units.la: Zach.9.v.9. Exulta valde filia Sion, clange filia Hierosolymorum. Rex tuus aduenit tibi iustus.
units.tr: Zech. 9:9. Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just.

units.la: Luc.1.verf.35. Quod nascetur ex te sanctum, vocabitur filius Dei.
units.tr: Luke 1:35. That holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.

units.la: Act.4.verf.27. Congregati sunt in hac ciuitate vere aduersus sanctum filium tuum Iesum. Esa.7.
units.tr: Acts 4:27. For of a truth against thy holy child Jesus, whom thou hast anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate. Isa. 7.

units.la: d) Esa.7.v.14.Ecce virgo concipiet. Confer Matth.1.& 2.Luc.1.& 2.
units.tr: d) Isa. 7:14. Behold, a virgin shall conceive. Compare Matt. 1 and 2; Luke 1 and 2.

units.la: e) Luc.1.v.35.Spiritus sanctus superveniet in te, & virtus Altissimi inumbrabit te.
units.tr: e) Luke 1:35. The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee.

units.la: 3. Christus natura humanam vniuit personae suae.
units.tr: 3. Christ united the human nature to his person:

units.la: a) sine confusione &
units.tr: a) without confusion, and

units.la: b) sine diuulsione.
units.tr: b) without separation.

units.la: a) Iohan.1.v.1. In principio erat Sermo ille, & Sermo ille erat apud Deum, eratq; ille Sermo Deus.
units.tr: a) John 1:1. In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

units.la: Rom.1.v.3. 4. De filio suo, facto ex semine Dauidis secundum carnem : declarato Filio Dei potenter secundum spiritum sanctificationis.
units.tr: Rom. 1:3–4. Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh, and declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness.

units.la: Etc.9.verf.5. Ex quibus est Christus, quod ad carnem attinet, qui est supra omnes Deus, benedictus in secula.
units.tr: Rom. 9:5. Of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever.

units.la: 1.Petri 4.v.1.Cum Christus passus sit pro nobis carne. Confer cap.3.verf.18.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 4:1. Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh. Compare chap. 3, verse 18.

units.la: b) Col.2. verf.9. In eo inhabitat omnis plenitudo deitatis corporaliter.
units.tr: b) Col. 2:9. For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.

units.la: 1.Cor.8.v.6. Nobis vnus est Deus, Pater ille, a quo omnia, & nos in ipso : & vnus Dominus Iesus Christus, per quem omnia, & nos per ipsum.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 8:6. To us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.

units.la: 1.Tim.2.v.5. Vnus est Deus, vnus etiam mediator Dei & hominum, homo Christus Iesus.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 2:5. For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.

units.la: Hanc quoq; vnionem confirmat communicatio idiomatum, qua fit, vt Christo ab altera natura denominato alterius naturae proprietates tribuantur: vt, Iohan.3.v.13. Nemo ascendit in coelum, nisi is, qui descendit e coelo, filius hominis, qui est in coelo. Confer Ioh.6.v.62.
units.tr: This union is also confirmed by the communication of idioms, by which it comes about that, when Christ is named from one nature, the properties of the other nature are attributed to him: as in John 3:13. No man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven. Compare John 6:62.

units.la: Act.20.v.28. Deus ecclesiam acquisiuit proprio sanguine.
units.tr: Acts 20:28. God purchased the church with his own blood.

units.la: Confer 1.Cor.2.v.8. 1.Iohan.1.v.1.
units.tr: Compare 1 Cor. 2:8; 1 John 1:1.

units.la: 4. Christus est propheta, sacerdos, & rex noster.
units.tr: 4. Christ is our prophet, priest, and king.

units.la: Hebr.1.v.1.2.3. Multis vicibus, multisq; modis olim Deus locutus patribus in prophetis, vltimis diebus hisce locutus est nobis in Filio, quem constituit haeredem omnium, per quem etiam mundum condidit. qui cum sit fulgor gloriae, & character persona illius, sustineatq; omnia verbo illo suo potente, purificatione peccatorum nostrorum strorum per seipsum facta, sedit ad dextram maiestatis illius in locis excelsissimis.
units.tr: Heb. 1:1–3. God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds; who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high.

units.la: Apoc.i.v.5,6.Et a Iesu Christo, qui est fidus ille testis, primogenitus ille ex mortuis, ac princeps regum terrae:qui dilexit nos,& lauit nos a peccatis nostris per sanguinem suum : Et qui fecit nos reges & sacerdotes Deo & Patri suo.
units.tr: Rev. 1:5–6. And from Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness, and the first begotten of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth. Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood, and hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father.

units.la: Huc pertinent ea Scripturae dicta, quibus Christus appellatur pastor, & pastor ille bonus, & pastor magnus, Eccles.12.v.13. Esa.40.v.11. Ezech.34. Zach.13.v.7. Matth.26.v.31. Ioh.10.v.11.14. Hebr.13.verf.20.21. 1.Petri 2.verf.25. Nomen enim pastoris omnia Domini officia complectitur; quia pastoris est oues ad salubria pascua ducere, ægras sanare, pro iis vitam ponere, vt eas e periculo eruat, denique illas regere & defendere aduersus lupos.
units.tr: To this belong those sayings of Scripture by which Christ is called the shepherd, and the good shepherd, and the great shepherd: Eccles. 12:13; Isa. 40:11; Ezek. 34; Zech. 13:7; Matt. 26:31; John 10:11, 14; Heb. 13:20–21; 1 Pet. 2:25. For the name of shepherd embraces all the offices of the Lord; because it is the shepherd's task to lead the sheep to wholesome pasture, to heal the sick, to lay down life for them, to snatch them from danger, and finally to rule and defend them against wolves.

units.la: 5. Christus officio prophetae functus fuit, cum praedicauit euangelium in Iudaea; & hodie illo fungitur partim in ecclesia triumphante, partim in militante.
units.tr: 5. Christ discharged the office of prophet when he preached the gospel in Judea; and today he discharges it partly in the Church triumphant, partly in the Church militant.

units.la: Matth.4.v.17. Ex eo tempore cœpit Iesus prædicare & dicere, Resipiscite: appropinquauit enim regnum cœlorum.
units.tr: Matt. 4:17. From that time Jesus began to preach and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

units.la: Esa.61.v.1.Lucae 4.v.18.19. Spiritus Domini super me, propterea quod vnxit me, vt euangelizem pauperibus misit me, vt medear contritis corde, vt prædicem captiuis dimissionem, & cæcis visus recuperationem, vt confractos emittam in libertatem: vt prædicem annum Domini acceptum.
units.tr: Isa. 61:1; Luke 4:18–19. The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, to preach the acceptable year of the Lord.

units.la: Apoc.21.v.22. Nec templum vidi in eâ: Dominus enim Deus omnipotens, templum illius est, & Agnus.
units.tr: Rev. 21:22. And I saw no temple therein: for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it.

units.la: Ioh.1.v.9. Hic erat lux illa vera, quæ illuminat omnem hominem venientem in mundum.
units.tr: John 1:9. That was the true light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world.

units.la: Propter hoc officium Christus appellatur consiliarius,Esa.9.verf.6. testis nationum & praeceptor,Esa.55.v.4. lux,Esa.60.v.1.Luc.2.verf.32. apostolus confessionis nostrae, Hebr.3.v.1. fidus ille testis, Apoc.1.v.5. propheta,Deut.18.v.18. doctor noster,Matth.23.v.8.10. magister,Ioh.13.v.13.
units.tr: On account of this office Christ is called counsellor, Isa. 9:6; witness and teacher of the nations, Isa. 55:4; light, Isa. 60:1; Luke 2:32; apostle of our confession, Heb. 3:1; that faithful witness, Rev. 1:5; prophet, Deut. 18:18; our teacher, Matt. 23:8, 10; master, John 13:13.

units.la: 6. Functio muneris sacerdotalis Christi posita est in eo, quòd diuinâ & humanâ voluntate se obtulit obrulit victimam pro peccatis nostris, ad satisfaciendum pro nobis coram throno iustitiæ; & in humanitate suâ pro nobis intercessit & adhuc intercedit apud thronum gratiæ.
units.tr: 6. The exercise of Christ's priestly office consists in this: that, by the divine and human will, he offered himself as the victim for our sins, to make satisfaction for us before the throne of justice; and in his humanity he interceded for us and still intercedes before the throne of grace.

units.la: Esa.53.v.12. Partem dabo eipro multis, vt cum robustis partiantur prædam; pro eo, quòd profudit in mortem seipsum, & cum defectoribus annumeratus est. nam ipse peccatum multorum perserens pro defectoribus intercessit.
units.tr: Isa. 53:12. Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he hath poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.

units.la: Ier.30.v.21. Erit magnificus eius ex ipso, & dominator eius è medio ipsius prodibit, quem iubeo accedere, vt appropinquet ad me. Nam quis est, qui spondeat cum animo suo, se appropinquaturum ad me? dictum Domini.
units.tr: Jer. 30:21. And their nobles shall be of themselves, and their governor shall proceed from the midst of them; and I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me: for who is this that engaged his heart to approach unto me? saith the LORD.

units.la: Ioh.17.v.19. Eorum causâ sanctifico meipsum; vt sint & ipsi sanctificati in veritate.
units.tr: John 17:19. For their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also might be sanctified through the truth.

units.la: 1.Cor.6.v.20. Emti estis pretio.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 6:20. Ye are bought with a price.

units.la: Hebr.5.v.6.& c.9.v.28. Christus semel oblatus est, vt in seipso tolleret peccata multorum.
units.tr: Heb. 5:6; 9:28. Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many.

units.la: Et cap.10.v.12. Hic, vnâ victimâ oblatâ pro peccatis, sedet ad dextram Dei. Et v.22. Cùm habeamus sacerdotem magnum, præsectum domui Dei: accedamus cum vero corde, per certioratam fidem, aspersione purgatis cordibus à conscientiâ malâ.
units.tr: And ch. 10:12. But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God. And v. 22. Having therefore an high priest over the house of God; let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience.

units.la: 1.Petri 1.v.18.19. Vt qui sciatis vos non caducis rebus, auro vel argento, fuisse redemtos ex vanâ illâ conuersatione à patribus tradita: Sed pretioso sanguine, vtpote agni inculpati & incontaminati, nempe Christi.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 1:18–19. Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers; but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot.

units.la: 1.Petri 2.v.24. Peccata nostra ipsemet sursum tulit corpore suo super lignum, vt mortui peccatis, iustitiæ viueremus: cuius vibicibus sanatiestis.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 2:24. Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.

units.la: Iohan.17.v.9. Ego pro eis rogo non pro mundo rogo, sed pro iis, quos dedisti mihi, quia tui sunt.
units.tr: John 17:9. I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine.

units.la: 1.Iohan.1.vers.7. Sanguis Iesu Christi Filij eius purgat nos ab omni peccato.
units.tr: 1 John 1:7. The blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.

units.la: Hebr.9.v.24. Non enim in manufactum sacrarium ingressus est Christus, quòd sit exemplar vero sacrario respondens: sed in ipsum cœlum, vt appareat nunc in conspectu Dei pro nobis. Propter hoc officium Christus dicitur iustitia nostra; Ier.23.v.6. 1.Cor.1.v.30: & peccatum, 2.Cor.5.v.21: & sacerdos in folio suo, Zach.6.verf.13: & sacerdos in perpetuum, Hebr.7.v.1.2.3: & sacerdos in seculum, Psal.110.v.4: & altare aureum, super quo offeruntur preces sanctorum, Apoc. 8.verf.3.4.
units.tr: Heb. 9:24. For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us. On account of this office Christ is called our righteousness, Jer. 23:6; 1 Cor. 1:30; and sin, 2 Cor. 5:21; and a priest upon his throne, Zech. 6:13; and a priest for ever, Heb. 7:1–3; and a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek, Ps. 110:4; and the golden altar, upon which the prayers of the saints are offered, Rev. 8:3–4.

units.la: Vide quoque infra loc.20. num.2.
units.tr: See also below, locus 20, n. 2.

units.la: 7. Functio muneris regii Christi posita est in eo, quod instituit ministerium verbi & sacramentorum; & solenniter misit Spiritum sanctum in festo Pentecostes; & hodie quoque verbum suum in nobis efficax facit per Spiritum suum, ut fideles & obsequentes simus, atque salute potiamur; item contra hostes nos defendit, & sub cruce conservat; denique quod in fine mundi hostes suos & nostros relegabit in gehennam ad aeternos cruciatus, nos autem ad se assumet in coelum, ut ibi cum ipso regnemus.
units.tr: 7. The function of Christ's kingly office lies in this: that he instituted the ministry of the Word and the sacraments; that he solemnly sent the Holy Spirit on the feast of Pentecost; and that today too he makes his Word effective in us through his Spirit, so that we are faithful and obedient and obtain salvation. Likewise he defends us against our enemies and preserves us under the cross. Finally, at the end of the world he will consign his enemies and ours to hell for eternal torments, but will take us up to himself into heaven, so that we may reign there with him.

units.la: Matth.28.v.18.19. Data est mihi omnis potestas in coelo & in terra: Profecti ergo docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos.
units.tr: Matt. 28:18-19. All power is given to me in heaven and on earth. Go therefore and teach all nations, baptizing them.

units.la: Ephes.4.v.11. Is igitur dedit alios quidem, apostolos, alios vero, prophetas, alios autem evangelistas, alios autem pastores & doctores.
units.tr: Eph. 4:11. And he gave some to be apostles, and some prophets, and some evangelists, and some pastors and teachers.

units.la: Iohan.15.v.7. & seqq. Sed ego veritatem dico vobis, confert vobis ut ego abeam. Nisi enim abiero, Aduocatus ille non veniet ad vos: sin autem profectus fuero, mittam eum ad vos. Vide Actor.2. ubi narratur, quomodo Christus in die Pentecostes misit Spiritum sanctum in apostolos: quo acti illi praedicaverunt euangelium felici successu. Adducti enim sunt multi ad fidem Christi.
units.tr: John 15:7 and following. But I tell you the truth: it is expedient for you that I go away. For if I do not go away, that Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you. See Acts 2, where it is related how Christ on the day of Pentecost sent the Holy Spirit upon the apostles, and how they, moved by him, preached the gospel with happy success. For many were brought to faith in Christ.

units.la: Marc.16.verf.20. Illi vero profecti praedicarunt ubique, Domino cooperante, & sermonem eorum confirmante per signa subsequentia.
units.tr: Mark 16:20. And they went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming their word by the signs that followed.

units.la: Rom.1.v.16. Non enim me pudet euangelij Christi, potentia siquidem Dei est ad salutem cuiuis credenti.
units.tr: Rom. 1:16. For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ, for it is the power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes.

units.la: 1.Cor.1.v.23.24. Nos autem prædicamus Christum crucifixum, &c. Dei potentiam, ac Dei sapientiam.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 1:23-24. But we preach Christ crucified, etc., the power of God and the wisdom of God.

units.la: Matth.28.v.20. Ecce, ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus vsq; ad consummationem seculi. Vide Psal.110.
units.tr: Matt. 28:20. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age. See Ps. 110.

units.la: Matth.16.v.18. Ego tibi dico, Tu es Petrus, & super hanc petram ædificabo meam ecclesiam: & porta inferorum non superabunt eam.
units.tr: Matt. 16:18. I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

units.la: Rom.8.v.37. In his omnibus amplius quam victores sumus per eum, qui dilexit nos.
units.tr: Rom. 8:37. In all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.

units.la: Psal.110.v.2. Dominare in medio inimicorum tuorum.
units.tr: Ps. 110:2. Rule in the midst of your enemies.

units.la: Matth.25.v.34.41. Tunc dicet rex iis, qui ad dexteram ipsius erunt, Venite benedicti Patris mei, possidete regnum paratum vobis à iactis mundi fundamentis. Tunc dicet etiam iis, qui ad sinistram erunt, Maledicti, abite à me in ignem æternum, qui paratus est diabolo & angelis eius.
units.tr: Matt. 25:34, 41. Then the king will say to those on his right hand: Come, you blessed of my Father, possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. Then he will also say to those on the left: Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

units.la: 2.Thess.2.v.6.& deinceps. Iustum est apud Deum vicissim reddere iis qui affligunt vos afflictionem: vobis vero qui affligimini relaxationem nobiscum: cum patefiet Dominus Iesus de cælo cum angelis potentibus suis, cum flammæ incendio, infligens vltionem iis, qui Deum non noverunt, nec auscultant euangelio Domini nostri Iesu Christi.
units.tr: 2 Thess. 1:6 and following. It is a righteous thing with God to repay affliction to those who afflict you, and to give rest to you who are afflicted, along with us, when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, in flaming fire, taking vengeance on those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Propter hoc officium Christus appellatur rex Dei, Psal. 2.v.2. iudex, & procurans ius, & promtus ad iustitiam, Esa. 16.v.14: antecessor. Esa.55.v.4: rex regum, & dominus dominantium, Apoc.19.v.16: dominus, Psal.110.v.1. Dan.9.verf. 17. Luc.2.v.11. Iohan.13.verf.13.14. 1.Cor.8.v.6. c.15.v.47. Act.2.v.36. Iuda verf.14: herus, Iud.v.4: princeps, Ezech.37.verf.25. Apoc.1.v.5: dux, Dan.9.v.25: leo ille ex tribu Iudæ, Apoc.5.v.5.
units.tr: Because of this office Christ is called the king of God, Ps. 2:2; judge, and one who executes justice, and is ready for righteousness, Isa. 16:14; forerunner, Isa. 55:4; king of kings and lord of lords, Rev. 19:16; lord, Ps. 110:1; Dan. 9:17; Luke 2:11; John 13:13-14; 1 Cor. 8:6; 15:47; Acts 2:36; Jude 14; master, Judg. 4:4; prince, Ezek. 37:25; Rev. 1:5; leader, Dan. 9:25; the lion of the tribe of Judah, Rev. 5:5.

units.la: 8. Christus diuersimodè functus est triplici suo munere: puta in statu exinanitionis & exaltationis. Esa.53.v.7.8. Phil.2.
units.tr: 8. Christ discharged his threefold office in different ways, namely in the state of humiliation and in the state of exaltation. Isa. 53:7-8; Phil. 2.

units.la: In statu exinanitionis
units.tr: In the state of humiliation

units.la: a) conceptus est ex Spiritu sancto. b) natus est ex Mariâ virgine, Bethlehemi. c) octauo die à natiuitate est circumcisus, & Iesus appellatus. d) præcursorem habuit Iohannem Baptistam. e) donis paulatim profecit, atque ita ad munus suum fuit præparatus. f) anno ætatis duodecimo specimen quoddam muneris prophetici edidit in templo. g) anno ætatis trigesimo fuit baptizatus à Iohanne. h) post baptismum solemniter inchoavit munus propheticum. i) sacerdotale munus patiendo inchoatum videl. pauperè suâ nativitate, patiendo continuavit. k) regiam majestatem suam ad tempus occultavit. l) sacram cœnam instituit. m) ad magnam passionem se præparavit. n) tandem crucifixus est, mortuus, & sepultus. o) descenditque ad inferos.
units.tr: a) He was conceived of the Holy Spirit. b) He was born of the virgin Mary at Bethlehem. c) On the eighth day after his birth he was circumcised and called Jesus. d) He had John the Baptist as his forerunner. e) He advanced little by little in gifts, and so was prepared for his office. f) At the age of twelve he gave a certain specimen of the prophetic office in the temple. g) At the age of thirty he was baptized by John. h) After his baptism he solemnly began the prophetic office. i) He began the priestly office by suffering: poor in his birth, he continued it by suffering. k) For a time he hid his kingly majesty. l) He instituted the holy supper. m) He prepared himself for the great passion. n) At last he was crucified, died and was buried. o) He descended into hell.

units.la: Quantum ad statum exaltationis.
units.tr: As regards the state of exaltation

units.la: p) tertio die resurrexit à mortuis. q) postquam, quadraginta dies se vivum in terris exhibuisset, & ministerium novi testamenti constituisset, ascendit in cœlum: r) ubi sedet ad dextram Patris sui, regnans super omnia.
units.tr: p) He rose from the dead on the third day. q) After he had shown himself alive on earth for forty days and had established the ministry of the New Testament, he ascended into heaven; r) where he sits at the right hand of his Father, reigning over all things.

units.la: ∫) in die Pentecostes Spiritum sanctum effudit in discipulos.
units.tr: ∫) On the day of Pentecost he poured out the Holy Spirit upon the disciples.

units.la: t) in fine seculi redibit ad iudicandum vivos & mortuos.
units.tr: t) At the end of the age he will return to judge the living and the dead.

units.la: a) Luca 1. vers.34.35.
b) Matth.1.v.16.Luc.2.Mich.5.v.2.Matth.2.v.1.
units.tr: b) Matt. 1:16; Luke 2; Mic. 5:2; Matt. 2:1.

units.la: c) Luca 2.v.21. Ad nomen Iesus allusum est in V.T. per voces [?] & [?] Esa.12.v.3.4. c.46.v.13.c.49.v.6.c.62.v.13.Habac.3.v.13.
units.tr: c) Luke 2:21. The name Jesus is alluded to in the Old Testament by the words [?] and [?]. Isa. 12:3-4; 46:13; 49:6; 62:13; Hab. 3:13.
d) Isa. 40:1-4; Matt. 3; Mark 1.

units.la: g) Matth.3. Luca 3.verf.21.22.
units.tr: g) Matt. 3; Luke 3:21-22.

units.la: h) Matth. 4. verf.17.& seqq.
units.tr: h) Matt. 4:17 and following.

units.la: i) Luc.2. verf.7. Peperit igitur filium suum primogeniturn, & fasciis eum inuoluit, reclinauitq3 eum in præsepi: eo quod non erat eis locus in diuersorio.
units.tr: i) Luke 2:7. So she bore her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling cloths, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.

units.la: Matth.2. Christus expositus fuit insidiis Herodis, quas vt effugeret, in Ægyptum est transportatus.
units.tr: Matt. 2. Christ was exposed to the plots of Herod, and to escape them he was carried into Egypt.

units.la: Matth.8. v.20. Vulpes habent lustra, & volucres cœli nidos: filius autem hominis non habet, vbi caput reclinet. Confer Luc. 9.verf.58.
units.tr: Matt. 8:20. Foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests, but the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head. Compare Luke 9:58.

units.la: 2. Cor. 8. v.9. Nostis enim beneficentiam Domini nostri Iesu Christi, eum videlicet propter vos pauperem factum esse, cum esset diues: vt vos illius paupertate ditesceretis.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 8:9. For you know the generosity of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that by his poverty you might become rich.

units.la: k) Matth.20.v.28. Filius hominis non venit, vt sibi ministretur, sed vt ministret.
units.tr: k) Matt. 20:28. The Son of man came not to be served but to serve.

units.la: Phil.2,v.7.8. Ipse se inaniuit, forma serui acceptâ, similis hominibus factus: & habitu inuentus vt homo, ipse se submisit, factus obediens vsq3 ad mortem, mortem autem crucis.
units.tr: Phil. 2:7-8. He emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men; and being found in human form, he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even death on a cross.

units.la: Hebr.5.v.7.& deinceps. Christus in diebus carnis suæ, deprecationibus & supplicationibus oblatis cum clamore valido & lachrymis, &c.
units.tr: Heb. 5:7 and following. Christ, in the days of his flesh, offering up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears, etc.

units.la: l) Matth. 26.
units.tr: l) Matt. 26.

units.la: m) Matth.26. Luc.18.v.31. & seqq.Iohan.17.
units.tr: m) Matt. 26; Luke 18:31 and following; John 17.
n) Matt. 27; Luke 23; Acts 2:23; 4:10; 1 Cor. 1:13; 2:2; 7:8; 15:4 (references as printed).

units.la: o) Psal.16.v.10. Non es derelicturus animam meam in sepulchro: neq3 expositurus benignum tuum, vt videat corruptionem. Confer Act.2.v.30.31.
units.tr: o) Ps. 16:10. You will not leave my soul in the grave, nor let your holy one see corruption. Compare Acts 2:30-31.

units.la: Matth.12.v.40. Sicut fuit Ionas in ventre ceti tres dies & tres noctes: ita erit filius hominis in corde terræ tres dies & tres noctes.
units.tr: Matt. 12:40. For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the whale, so will the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

units.la: Eph.4. v.9. Caterum illud Ascendit, quid est nisi quod etiam descenderat prius in infimas partes terræ?
units.tr: Eph. 4:9. But this word "he ascended," what does it mean except that he had first descended into the lower parts of the earth?

units.tr: p) Matt. 28; Luke 24; 1 Cor. 15.

units.la: LOCUS XVIII. De ecclesia.
units.tr: LOCUS XVIII. Concerning the church.

units.la: 1. Vocabulo ecclesiae intelligitur
units.tr: 1. By the word "church" is understood:

units.la: a) interdum multitudo hominum electorum; & usitatè dicitur ecclesia catholica.
units.tr: a) sometimes the multitude of the elect, and this is commonly called the catholic church.

units.la: b) interdum coetus profitentium fidem Christi; & usitatè dicitur ecclesia particularis.
units.tr: b) sometimes the assembly of those who profess faith in Christ, and this is commonly called the particular church.

units.la: c) interdum conventus ecclesiasticus.
units.tr: c) sometimes an ecclesiastical assembly.

units.la: a) Matth.16.v.18. Super hanc petram ædificabo ecclesiam meam.
units.tr: a) Matt. 16:18. Upon this rock I will build my church.

units.la: Eph.5.v.23. Christus est caput ecclesia. Et vers.25. Christus dilexit ecclesiam, & semetipsum exposuit pro eâ.
units.tr: Eph. 5:23. Christ is the head of the church. And verse 25: Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her.

units.la: Act.20.v.28. Deus ecclesiam acquisivit proprio sanguine.
units.tr: Acts 20:28. God acquired the church with his own blood.

units.la: 1.Tim.3.v.11. Ecclesia Dei vivi est columna & stabilimentum veritatis.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 3:11. The church of the living God is the pillar and ground of the truth.

units.la: b) Sic ecclesia nominatur coetus credentium apud Corinthios, 1.Cor.1.v.2. 2.Cor.1.vers.1. item apud Galatas, Gal.1.v.2. item apud Thessalonicenses, 1.Thess.1.v.1. 2.Thess.1.v.1. Confer Apoc.1.v.20. item cap.2. & 3.
units.tr: b) So the assembly of believers is called church among the Corinthians, 1 Cor. 1:2; 2 Cor. 1:1; likewise among the Galatians, Gal. 1:2; likewise among the Thessalonians, 1 Thess. 1:1; 2 Thess. 1:1. Compare Rev. 1:20, and likewise chapters 2 and 3.

units.la: c) Matth.18.v.17. Dic ecclesiæ. Quòd si ecclesiam audire neglexerit, &c.
units.tr: c) Matt. 18:17. Tell it to the church. But if he refuse to hear the church, etc.

units.la: 2. Ecclesia ab externâ vocatione est & dicitur visibilis, ab interna, invisibilis.
units.tr: 2. The church is, from its external calling, visible, and is called visible; from its internal calling, invisible.

units.la: Rom.1.v.8. Primùm quidem gratias ago Deo meo per Iesum Christum, super omnibus vobis, quòd fides vestra annuntiatur in toto mundo.
units.tr: Rom. 1:8. First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.

units.la: Etc.2.v.28.29. Non enim qui est in propatulo Iudaeus, Iudaeus est: nec ea quae est in propatulo circumcisio, id est in carne, circumci-fio est: Sed qui in occulto Iudaeus est, & circumcisio cordis, id est, in spiritu, non litera: cuius Iudaei laus non est ex hominibus, sed ex Deo. Et cap.9.verf.3.4.5.6.7.8.& cap.11.v.1.2.3.4.17.19. 20.21 23.24.25.26.
units.tr: Rom. 2:28–29. For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, nor is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh. But he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men but of God. And ch. 9, vv. 3–8, and ch. 11, vv. 1–4, 17, 19–21, 23–26.

units.la: Ierem.7.v.4. Ne habetote fiduciam vestram in rebus falsis,dicendo:Templum Domini,templum Domini,templum Domini.
units.tr: Jer. 7:4. Trust not in lying words, saying: The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord.

units.la: Matth.23. v.2. In cathedra Mosis sedent Scribæ & Pharifæi.
units.tr: Matt. 23:2. The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat.

units.la: Confer cum num.praeced.1. Vide etiam Exod.16.v.3. & 9.Num.1. v. 2. vbi fit mentio ecclesiæ siue congregationis Israëlitarum.
units.tr: Compare the preceding number 1. See also Exod. 16:3 and 9; Num. 1:2, where mention is made of the church, or congregation, of the Israelites.

units.la: 3. Ecclesiæ pars in cœlis triumphat, pars in his terris in medio inimicorum belligerat adversus diabolum,mundum & carnem. Hinc diu ditur ecclesia in
units.tr: 3. Part of the church triumphs in heaven; part, here on earth, is at war in the midst of enemies against the devil, the world and the flesh. Hence the church is divided into

units.la: a) triumphantem, quæ in fine demum seculi tota triumphabit,cùm iam ex parte tantùm triumphet.
units.tr: a) the triumphant church, which will at the end of the age triumph wholly, since now it triumphs only in part.

units.la: b) militantem.
units.tr: b) the militant church.

units.la: De vtraque coniunctim vide
units.tr: On both together see:

units.la: Eph.1.v.10. Vt recolligeret omnia illa in Christo, tum quæ in cœlis sunt,tum quæ in terrâ.
units.tr: Eph. 1:10. That he might gather together in Christ all things, both which are in heaven and which are on earth.

units.la: Etc.3.v.15. Ex quo tota familia in cœlis, & in terrâ nominatur. Confer 1.Cor.13.v.9.&seqq.
units.tr: Eph. 3:15. From whom the whole family in heaven and on earth is named. Compare 1 Cor. 13:9 and following.

units.la: a) Hebr.12.v.22.23. Accessistis ad montem Sion,& ciuitatem Dei viui, Hierusalem cœlestem, & myriadas angelorum, Conuentum vniuersalem & concionem primogenitorum qui conscripti sunt in cœlis.
units.tr: a) Heb. 12:22–23. You have come to Mount Sion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels, to the universal assembly and congregation of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven.

units.la: Hæc ecclesia magnificè describitur Apoc.4.5.21.&22.
units.tr: This church is magnificently described in Rev. 4, 5, 21 and 22.

units.la: b) 2.Cor.5.verf.6.7.8.9. Dum commoramur in corpore, peregrè absumus à Domino. Per fidem enim incedimus, non per aspectum,&c.
units.tr: b) 2 Cor. 5:6–9. While we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord. For we walk by faith, not by sight, etc.

units.la: 1.Tim.3.v.15. Vt noris quomodo oporteat in domo Dei versari, quæ est ecclesia Dei.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 3:15. That you may know how one ought to conduct oneself in the house of God, which is the church of God.

units.la: Hæc vocatur nigra, Cant.1.v.5. & confertur lilio inter spinas,Cant.2.v.2. & myrteto in profundo,Zach.1.v.8.
units.tr: This church is called black, Song 1:5, and is compared to a lily among thorns, Song 2:2, and to a myrtle in the deep, Zech. 1:8.

units.la: 4. Ad ecclesiam catholicam & inuisibilem pertinent solì electi.
units.tr: 4. Only the elect belong to the catholic and invisible church.

units.la: Eph.5.v.25.26. Christus exposuit se pro ecclesiâ, vt eam sanctificaret,postquam eam purgasset lauacro aquæ per verbum: vt sisteret fieret eam sibi gloriosam: id est, ecclesiam non habentem maculam, aut rugam, aut quidquam eiusmodi: sed vt esset sancta & inculpata: scilicet partim per imputationem, partim per inhæsionem.
units.tr: Eph. 5:25–26. Christ gave himself up for the church, that he might sanctify her, having cleansed her by the washing of water through the word; that he might present her to himself glorious, that is, a church not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she might be holy and blameless, namely partly by imputation and partly by inherence.

units.la: Et c.4. v.12.15.16. Ad coagmentationem sanctorum, ad opus ministerij, ad aedificationem corporis Christi: Sincere nos gerentes in charitate, prorsus adolescamus in eum, qui est caput, nempe Christus. Ex quo totum corpus congruenter coagmentatum, & compactum per omnes suppeditatas commissuras, ex vi intus agente pro mensura vniuscuiusq; membri, incrementum capit corpori conueniens ad sui ipsius extractionem [?] per charitatem.
units.tr: And c. 4, vv. 12, 15, 16. For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ; speaking the truth in love, we may grow up in every way into him who is the head, namely Christ. From whom the whole body, fitly joined and knit together through every supplied joint, by the working of the inner force according to the measure of each member, receives growth suited to the body, to its own building up [?] through love.

units.la: Huc pertinent magnifici illi tituli ecclesiæ; puta sponsa, siue coniux, & filia regis tota honorata, Psalm. 45. v.10. & seqq. Sponsa Agni, Apoc.21. v.9. quies Christi, Esa.11. verf.10. peculium Domini, 1.Pet.5.v.3: corpus Christi, Ephes.4.v.16. c.5.v.23. Col.1.v.18.24: complementum Christi, Eph.1.v.vlt. electi, Matth.24.v.22.24. Marc.13.v.20.22.27. Luc.18.verf.7. Rom.8.v.33. Col.3.v.12. 2.Tim.2.v.10. Tit.1.v.1. 1.Petri 1.verf.1. Apoc.17. v.14: genus electum, 1.Petri 2.v.9 vocati; Hebr.9.v. 15. Iudae v.1. Apoc.17.v.14: sancti, Rom.8.v.27. cap.12. v.13: sanctum sacerdotium, 1.Petri 2.2.5. populus sanctus, 1.Petri 2. v.9. oues Christi, Iohan.10.v.15. c.21.v.17. filij Dei, Iohan.11.v.52. Rom.8.v.19.21.
units.tr: To this belong those magnificent titles of the church: namely the bride, or wife, and the daughter of the king, all glorious, Ps. 45:10 and following; the bride of the Lamb, Rev. 21:9; the rest of Christ, Isa. 11:10; the peculiar people of the Lord, 1 Pet. 2:9; the body of Christ, Eph. 4:16, 5:23, Col. 1:18, 24; the fullness of Christ, Eph. 1 (last verse); the elect, Matt. 24:22, 24; Mark 13:20, 22, 27; Luke 18:7; Rom. 8:33; Col. 3:12; 2 Tim. 2:10; Titus 1:1; 1 Pet. 1:1; Rev. 17:14; an elect race, 1 Pet. 2:9; the called, Heb. 9:15; Jude 1; Rev. 17:14; the saints, Rom. 8:27, 12:13; a holy priesthood, 1 Pet. 2:2, 5; a holy people, 1 Pet. 2:9; the sheep of Christ, John 10:15, 21:17; the sons of God, John 11:52; Rom. 8:19, 21.

units.la: Huic porro ecclesiæ conueniunt duratio perpetua, summa antiquitas, & similia.
units.tr: To this church, moreover, belong perpetual duration, the highest antiquity, and the like.

units.la: 5. Ecclesiæ particulari & inuisibili [?], hoc est, coetui profitentium fidem Christi, admixti sunt hypocritæ.
units.tr: 5. Hypocrites are mixed in with the particular and visible church, that is, the assembly of those professing faith in Christ.

units.la: Hoc docet Christus per parabolas: vt per parabolam de zizaniis natis inter triticum, Matth.13.v.25. Item per parabolam de sagena, quæ concludit tam putres quam bonos pisces, Matth.13.v.47. Item per parabolam vitis, in qua sunt palmites fructiferi & infrugiferi, Iohan.15.verf.1. & seqq.
units.tr: Christ teaches this by parables: by the parable of the tares sown among the wheat, Matt. 13:25; likewise by the parable of the net, which gathers both bad and good fish, Matt. 13:47; likewise by the parable of the vine, in which there are fruitful and unfruitful branches, John 15:1 and following.

units.la: Idem docet Iohannes Baptista per parabolam de palea admixta tritico, Matth.3.v.12. & Esaias per parabolam vineæ ferentis labruscas, Esa.5. Exempla vide in septem ecclesiis, Apoc.2. & 3. Huc pertinet, quòd atrium in templo Salomonis figurauit ecclesiam visibilem, sicut sanctum ecclesiam catholicam in his terris militantem, & sanctum sanctorum ecclesiam triumphantem in cœlis.
units.tr: John the Baptist teaches the same by the parable of the chaff mixed with the wheat, Matt. 3:12, and Isaiah by the parable of the vineyard bearing wild grapes, Isa. 5. Examples are seen in the seven churches, Rev. 2 and 3. To this belongs the fact that the court in Solomon's temple prefigured the visible church, just as the holy place prefigured the catholic church militant on earth, and the holy of holies the church triumphant in heaven.

units.la: 6. Notæ ecclesiæ inuisibilis sunt internæ, numero tres, videlicet fides, spes, & charitas.
units.tr: 6. The marks of the invisible church are internal, three in number, namely faith, hope and love.

units.la: 1.Cor.13. verf.13. Nunc autem manet fides, spes, charitas, tria haec.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 13:13. But now faith, hope and love remain, these three.

units.la: Rom. 1. v.17. Omnibus, qui Romæ estis, dilectis Dei, vocatis, sanctis.
units.tr: Rom. 1:7. To all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called, saints.

units.la: 1.Cor.1. verf.2. Ecclesiæ Dei, quæ est Corinthi, sanctificatis in Christo Iesu, vocatis, sanctis, cum omnibus, qui invocant nomen Domini nostri Iesu Christi, quouis loco.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 1:2. To the church of God which is at Corinth, sanctified in Christ Jesus, called saints, with all who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place.

units.la: 1.Thess.1. v.2.3. Gratias agimus Deo indesinenter, commemorantes efficacem vestram fidem, & laboriosam charitatem, & patientem illam expectationem in Domino nostro Iesu Christo coram Deo & Patre nostro.
units.tr: 1 Thess. 1:2–3. We give thanks to God without ceasing, remembering your effective faith, and your laborious love, and that patient expectation in our Lord Jesus Christ before God and our Father.

units.la: Et cap.5. verf.8. Nos qui sumus diei, sobrij simus, induti thorace fidei & charitatis: & pro galea, spe salutis. Confer Ephes.2. v. 15.16.17.18.19.
units.tr: And ch. 5, v. 8. Let us who are of the day be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet, the hope of salvation. Compare Eph. 2:15–19.

units.la: 7. Ecclesiæ visibilis nota princeps est integra & pura verbi Dei prædicatio & professio: hinc legitima sacramentorum administratio: cum quibus iungi debet honesta disciplina, illis consentiens.
units.tr: 7. The chief mark of the visible church is the entire and pure preaching and profession of the Word of God; hence the lawful administration of the sacraments; with which an honest discipline, agreeing with these, ought to be joined.

units.la: Tres hæ notæ coniunguntur Matth.28. v.19.20. Profecti ergo docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomen Patris, Filij, & Spiritus sancti. Docentes eos seruare omnia quæ mandaui vobis. Confer Act.2. v.36.37. 38.42.46. nominatim v.42. qui sic habet: Erant perdurantes in doctrinâ apostolorum, & communicatione, & fractione panis, & precibus.
units.tr: These three marks are joined together in Matt. 28:19–20. Go therefore and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit; teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you. Compare Acts 2:36–38, 42, 46; especially v. 42, which reads thus: They continued steadfastly in the doctrine of the apostles, and in fellowship, and in the breaking of bread, and in prayers.

units.la: De professione verbi vide Deut.4.v.8. Qua gens maxima futura est: cui sunt statuta & iudicia iusta, sicut est tota hæc lex, quam ego propono vobis hodie.
units.tr: On the profession of the Word, see Deut. 4:8. What great nation is there that has statutes and righteous judgments such as this whole law which I set before you today.

units.la: Ioh.8. v.31. Si vos manseritis in sermone meo, vere discipuli mei eritis.
units.tr: John 8:31. If you remain in my word, you will truly be my disciples.

units.la: Et verf.47. Qui est ex Deo, verba Dei audit.
units.tr: And v. 47. He who is of God hears the words of God.

units.la: Ioh.10. v. 27. Oues mea vocem meam audiunt, & ego agnosco eas, & sequuntur me.
units.tr: John 10:27. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.

units.la: Eph.2.v.20. Superstructi super fundamentum apostolorum & prophetarum, exsistente imo angulari lapide ipso Iesu Christo.
units.tr: Eph. 2:20. Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief cornerstone.

units.la: De administratione sacramentorum vide Genes.17.
units.tr: On the administration of the sacraments, see Gen. 17.

units.la: verf.11. Circumcidetis carnem praeputij vestri, vt sit signum foederis inter me & vos.
units.tr: v. 11. You shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, that it may be a sign of the covenant between me and you.

units.la: Exod.12.v.43. Nullus alienigena vescitor illo, paschate.
units.tr: Exod. 12:43. No foreigner shall eat of that Passover.

units.la: Marc.16.verf.16. Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, seruabitur.
units.tr: Mark 16:16. He who believes and is baptized will be saved.

units.la: 1.Cor 12.v.13. Per vnum spiritum nos omnes in vnum corpus baptizati sumus, & Iudai & Graeci, & serui & liberi, & omnespotati sumus in vnum Spiritum.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 12:13. For by one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free; and we were all given to drink of one Spirit.

units.la: Confer 1.Cor.10.verf.16.
units.tr: Compare 1 Cor. 10:16.

units.la: De disciplina ecclesiae vide 1.Cor.14.verf.vlt. Omnia decenter & ordine fiant.
units.tr: On the discipline of the Church see 1 Cor. 14, last verse: "Let all things be done decently and in order."

units.la: Iohan.13.verf.35. Ex hoc omnes cognoscent, vos esse discipulos meos, si charitatem habueritis alij in alios: nempe congruenter Christi legibus in veritate.
units.tr: John 13, verse 35: "By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another"; that is, love agreeing with the laws of Christ in truth.

units.la: 8. Antiquitas doctrinae quaerenda est in ecclesia, non antiquitas loci.
units.tr: 8. The antiquity of doctrine is to be sought in the Church, not the antiquity of place.

units.la: Matth.19.v.8. A principio non fuit ita.
units.tr: Matt. 19, verse 8: "From the beginning it was not so."

units.la: 1.Cor.11.verf.23. Ego enim accepi a Domino, quod & tradidi vobis.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 11, verse 23: "For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you."

units.la: Iudae v.3. Necesse habui vobis scribere, ad vos hortandos vt decertetis pro fide quae semel tradita est sanctis.
units.tr: Jude, verse 3: "It was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints."

units.la: 9. Disciplina ecclesiae certis constat gradibus, quos non oportet transilire.
units.tr: 9. The discipline of the Church consists of certain steps, which must not be skipped over.

units.la: Matth.18.v.15.& seqq. Si peccauerit in te frater tuus, veni & argue eum inter te & ipsum solum. Si te audierit, lucratus es fratrem tuum. Sin vero te non audierit, accipe tecum adhuc vnum aut duos: vt in ore duorum aut trium testium stabile sit omne verbum. Quod si neglexerit eos audire, dic ecclesiae. Quod si ecclesiam audire neglexerit, sit tibi velut quispiam ethnicus & quispiam publicanus.
units.tr: Matt. 18, verse 15 and following: "Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother. But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.
