And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the Church: but if he neglect to hear the Church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican."

units.la: His verbis constituuntur quatuor gradus disciplinæ ecclesiasticæ, hoc modo.
units.tr: By these words four steps of ecclesiastical discipline are laid down, in this manner.

units.la: 1. Qui vni alicui priuatim scandalum dat, priuatim ab illo solo est corripiendus.
units.tr: 1. He who gives offence to some one person privately is to be rebuked privately by that one alone.

units.la: 2. Qui solitariæ correptioni locum non dat, corripiendus est assumtis testibus.
units.tr: 2. He who does not heed the private rebuke is to be rebuked with witnesses taken along.

units.la: 3. Qui correptioni testium locum non dat, deferendus est ad ecclesiam, id est, ad presbyterium, & ab illo corripiendus est.
units.tr: 3. He who does not heed the witnesses is to be brought before the Church, that is, before the eldership, and is to be rebuked by it.

units.la: 4. Qui presbyterij correptioni locum non dat, excommunicandus est. Qui gradus etiam locum habet, vbi aliquis ecclesiam offendit atroci scelere, 1.Cor.5. Quòd si excommunicatus ostendat signa resipiscentiæ, in ecclesiam recipiendus est, 2.Cor.2. v.6.7.8.
units.tr: 4. He who does not heed the rebuke of the eldership is to be excommunicated. This step also applies where someone offends the Church by a heinous crime, 1 Cor. 5. But if the excommunicated person shows signs of repentance, he is to be received back into the Church, 2 Cor. 2, verses 6, 7, 8.

units.la: 10. Concilia ecclesiastica debent esse conformia quatuor conciliis apostolicis.
units.tr: 10. Ecclesiastical councils ought to conform to the four apostolic councils.

units.la: De his vide in Actis. In horum primo eligitur Matthias cap. 1. in secundo diaconi instituuntur, cap.6. in tertio Iudaica instituta antiquantur, cap.15. quartum elicitur ex historia cap.21. de Pauli aduentu Hierosolymam.
units.tr: On these see in Acts. In the first, Matthias is chosen, chap. 1; in the second, deacons are instituted, chap. 6; in the third, Jewish ordinances are abolished, chap. 15; the fourth is drawn from the history of Paul's coming to Jerusalem, chap. 21.

units.la: 11. Minisferium ecclesiæ durabit inde ab initio vsque ad finem seculi. Matth.16.v.18.c.28.verf.vlt.
units.tr: 11. The ministry of the Church will endure from the beginning to the end of the age. Matt. 16, verse 18; Matt. 28, last verse.

units.la: Quod attinet ad ministerium V.T. ibi hoc officio perfuncti sunt.
units.tr: As far as the ministry of the Old Testament is concerned, those who performed this office were these.

units.la: 1. Sancti patres: vt Adam instituens filios de sacrificiis, Gen.4. Noah similiter, Gen. 8. v. 20: Abrahamus sacrificia Deo offerens, & circumcisionem à Deo accipiens, Genes. 12.v.5.&c.17. Isaacus filius benedicens, Gen.27.v.3.&seqq. Iacobus filiis suis prædicens fata ipsorum, Genes.49. Iosephus fratres erudiens de introductione ipsorum in terram Canaan, Gen.vlt.v.24.
units.tr: 1. The holy fathers: as Adam, instructing his sons about sacrifices, Gen. 4; Noah likewise, Gen. 8, verse 20; Abraham, offering sacrifices to God and receiving circumcision from God, Gen. 12, verse 5, etc., and 17; Isaac, blessing his son, Gen. 27, verse 3 and following; Jacob, foretelling the fates of his sons, Gen. 49; Joseph, instructing his brothers about their going up into the land of Canaan, Gen. last chapter, verse 24.

units.la: 2. Sacerdotes & Levita. Vide in Exodo & Levitico; nominatim Exod.28. Levit.8. item 1.Chron.23.
units.tr: 2. Priests and Levites. See in Exodus and Leviticus; especially Exod. 28, Lev. 8; likewise 1 Chron. 23.

units.la: 3. Prophetæ: vt Esaias, Ieremias, &c. Vide infra Chronologiam. Quantum attinet ad ministerium N.T. ibi hoc munere partim functi sunt, partim adhuc funguntur.
units.tr: 3. Prophets: as Isaiah, Jeremiah, etc. See below in the Chronology. As far as the ministry of the New Testament is concerned, some have performed this office, and some still perform it.

units.la: 1. Johannes Baptista, praecursor Christi. Matth.3. Marc.1. Luc.3. Johan.1.
units.tr: 1. John the Baptist, the forerunner of Christ. Matt. 3; Mark 1; Luke 3; John 1.

units.la: 2. Apostoli. Matth.10.v.1.&seqq. Act.1.v.26.c.9.v.15.& seqq. Gal.1.v.1. Item LXX.discipuli Christi, Luc.10.v.1.
units.tr: 2. Apostles. Matt. 10, verse 1 and following; Acts 1, verse 26; Acts 9, verse 15 and following; Gal. 1, verse 1. Likewise the seventy disciples of Christ, Luke 10, verse 1.

units.la: 3. Euangelistae, id est, euangelij praecones.
units.tr: 3. Evangelists, that is, heralds of the gospel.

units.la: 4. Prophetae, id est, interpretes Scripturae.
units.tr: 4. Prophets, that is, interpreters of Scripture.

units.la: 5. Doctores, qui adhuc durant,
units.tr: 5. Teachers, who still endure.

units.la: 6. Pastores, qui etiam adhuc durant.
units.tr: 6. Ministers, who also still endure.

units.la: 7. Gubernatores disciplinae, siue seniores; qui & ipsi adhuc durant. Rom.12.v.8. Qui praeest[?], praesit cum diligentia. 1.Cor.12. v.28, Deus in ecclesia constituit gubernationes.
units.tr: 7. Governors of discipline, or elders; who likewise still endure. Rom. 12, verse 8: "He that ruleth, let him do it with diligence." 1 Cor. 12, verse 28: "God hath set some in the Church... governments."

units.la: 8. Diaconi, id est, curatores pauperum; qui ipsi quoq; adhuc durant. 1.Tim.3.v.8.&seqq. Act.6.
units.tr: 8. Deacons, that is, overseers of the poor; who likewise still endure. 1 Tim. 3, verse 8 and following; Acts 6.

units.la: 12. Ministri Ecclesiae legitimè sunt vocandi & ordinandi,
units.tr: 12. The ministers of the Church are to be lawfully called and ordained.

units.la: Quod attinet ad vocationem, quando ecclesia habet magistratum Christianum, ius vocandi ministros est penes illum, exemplo Mosis, Exod.21.v.1.&seqq.&c.20.v.16. Item Dauidis, 1.Chron.23.v.2.&seqq. Item Salomonis, 1.Reg.2.v.27. 2.Chron.8.v.16. Item Ezechiae, 2.Chron.23.v.25. Si vero ecclesia non habeat magistratum Christianum, ius vocandi ministros ad ipsam pertinet, exemplo ecclesiae apostolicae, Act.1.v.15.&seqq.&c.6.v.2.&seqq.&c.14.v.23.
units.tr: As far as calling is concerned: when the Church has a Christian magistrate, the right of calling ministers rests with him, after the example of Moses, Exod. 21, verse 1 and following, and 20, verse 16; likewise David, 1 Chron. 23, verse 2 and following; likewise Solomon, 1 Kings 2, verse 27, 2 Chron. 8, verse 16; likewise Hezekiah, 2 Chron. 23, verse 25. But if the Church does not have a Christian magistrate, the right of calling ministers belongs to the Church itself, after the example of the apostolic Church, Acts 1, verse 15 and following, and 6, verse 2 and following, and 14, verse 23.

units.la: Quantum attinet ad ordinationem, illa debet fieri in timore Dei, ordine, & solenniter. Act.1.v.15.&seqq. 1.Cor. 14.v.vlt. Act.13.v.3. 1.Tim.4.v.14. 2.Tim.1.v.6. Tribus vltimis locis fit mentio impositionis manuum, per quam ordinatio ministrorum ecclesiae tempore apostolorum est facta. Qui ritus est liberae obseruationis.
units.tr: As far as ordination is concerned, it ought to be done in the fear of God, in good order, and solemnly. Acts 1, verse 15 and following; 1 Cor. 14, last verse; Acts 13, verse 3; 1 Tim. 4, verse 14; 2 Tim. 1, verse 6. In the last three places mention is made of the laying on of hands, by which the ordination of the ministers of the Church was carried out in the time of the apostles. This rite is of free observance.

units.la: LOCVS XIX.
units.tr: LOCUS XIX.

units.la: De vocatione.
units.tr: Concerning vocation.

units.la: 1. Per vocationem Deus nos transfert ex mundo in ecclesiam, gratia sua praeueniente.
units.tr: 1. Through vocation God brings us out of the world into the Church, his grace going before.

units.la: Esa.9.v.2. Populus eius, qui ambulant in tenebris, videbunt lucem magnam: super confidentes in terra umbra lethalis lux splendebit. Confer Matth. 4.v.16.
units.tr: Isa. 9.2: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; upon those who dwelt in the land of the shadow of death, a light has shone. Compare Matt. 4.16.

units.la: Act.26.v.17.18. Eruens te ex hoc populo, & gentibus, ad quos te nunc mitto, ut aperias oculos eorum, & conuertas eos a tenebris ad lucem, & a potestate Satanae ad Deum, ut remissionem peccatorum & sortem inter sanctificatos accipiant per fidem quae est in me.
units.tr: Acts 26.17-18: Delivering you from this people and from the Gentiles, to whom I now send you, to open their eyes and turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified, through faith that is in me.

units.la: 1.Petri 2.v.9. Ut virtutes praedicetis illius, qui vos vocavit e tenebris in admirabilem suam lucem.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 2.9: That you may proclaim the virtues of him who called you out of darkness into his marvellous light.

units.la: Rom.9.verf.25.26. Ut etiam apud Hoseam dicit, Vocabo populum, qui meus non erat, populum meum: & eam quae dilecta non erat, dilectam. Et erit in loco vbi dictum fuerat eis, Non populus meus vos, illic vocabuntur filij viuentis Dei. Confer Hos.1.verf. 10. & c.2.v.25.
units.tr: Rom. 9.25-26: As he also says in Hosea: I will call those who were not my people, my people; and her who was not beloved, beloved. And it shall come to pass that in the place where it was said to them, You are not my people, there they shall be called the sons of the living God. Compare Hos. 1.10 and 2.25.

units.la: 2.Tim.1.v.9. Qui seruauit nos, & vocauit vocatione sancta: non ex operibus nostris, sed ex suo proposito, & gratia, quae data quidem est nobis in Christo Iesu ante tempora saeculorum: Sed patefacta nunc est, &c.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 1.9: Who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before the ages of time, but now has been made manifest, etc.

units.la: 2 Vocatio externa est, qua homo transfertur in ecclesiam visibilem, per concionem legis & euangelii, vel per beneficia & iudicia Dei.
units.tr: 2. External vocation is that by which a man is brought into the visible Church, through the preaching of law and gospel, or through the benefits and judgments of God.

units.la: Matth.20.v.16,&c.22.v.14. Multi enim sunt vocati, pauci vero electi.
units.tr: Matt. 20.16, etc., 22.14: For many are called, but few are chosen.

units.la: Et c.22.v.11.12. Ingressus autem rex ut spectaret conuiuas, vidit illic quendam non indutum veste nuptiali: Tunc dicit ei, Amice, quomodo huc introisti non habens vestem nuptialem?
units.tr: And 22.11-12: But when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man who was not wearing a wedding garment. Then he said to him, Friend, how did you come in here without a wedding garment?

units.la: Marc.1.v.2.3. Ecce ego mitto nuntium illum meum ante faciem tuam, qui parabit viam tuam coram te. Vox clamantis in deserto, Parate viam Domini, complanate semitas eius. Confer Matth.3.v.3. Iohan.1.v.23.
units.tr: Mark 1.2-3: Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you. The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, make straight his paths. Compare Matt. 3.3; John 1.23.

units.la: Ier.1.verf.9.10. Et extendens Iehoua manum suam tetigit os meum, dixitq; Iehoua mihi, ecce indo verba mea ori tuo. Vide, praeficio te hodierno die gentibus ipsis & regnis, ad exstirpandum, & ad demoliendum, & ad perdendum, & ad destruendum, ad aedificandum, & ad plantandum.
units.tr: Jer. 1.9-10: And the LORD stretched out his hand and touched my mouth, and the LORD said to me, Behold, I have put my words in your mouth. See, I set you this day over nations and kingdoms, to root out and to pull down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant.

units.la: Huc refer loca, quibus prophetae iubentur stillare, i. prophetare. Eze.20.v.46.c.21.v.2. Mich.2.v.6.11. Amos 7.v.16 Naam fuit vocatus per curationem lepræ, 2.Reg.5:centurio & turba, per miracula edita in morte Christi, Matth. 27. & Luc.23:multi spectatores, per miracula Christi & apostolorum, Iohan.2.v.11.23. Marci 16.verf.vlt.
units.tr: Here belong the passages in which the prophets are commanded to drip, that is, to prophesy: Ezek. 20.46, 21.2; Mic. 2.6, 11; Amos 7.16. Naaman was called through the healing of leprosy, 2 Kings 5; the centurion and the crowd through the miracles done at Christ's death, Matt. 27 and Luke 23; many spectators through the miracles of Christ and the apostles, John 2.11, 23; Mark 16, last verse.

units.la: 3. Vocationis externæ dispar est euentus quantum ad electos & reprobos.
units.tr: 3. The outcome of external vocation differs as regards the elect and the reprobate.

units.la: a) Quantum ad electos, vocatio externa comitem habet internam, cuius effecta sunt fides, spes, & charitas.
units.tr: a) As regards the elect, external vocation has as its companion internal vocation, whose effects are faith, hope, and charity.

units.la: Quantum ad reprobos
units.tr: As Regards the Reprobate

units.la: b) quidam repudiant vocationem externam.
units.tr: b) Some reject external vocation.

units.la: c) quidam per eam illuminantur, & donantur fide historicâ.
units.tr: c) Some are enlightened by it and endowed with historical faith.

units.la: d) quidam donantur fide temporariâ, ita vt perfundantur gaudio.
units.tr: d) Some are endowed with temporary faith, so that they are filled with joy.

units.la: e) quidam donantur fide miraculorum.
units.tr: e) Some are endowed with the faith of miracles.

units.la: f) quidam indurantur & excæcantur magis magisque.
units.tr: f) Some are hardened and blinded more and more.

units.la: a) Rom.10.v.17. Fides ex auditu est:auditus autem per verbum Dei.
units.tr: a) Rom. 10.17: Faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of God.

units.la: Esa.55.v.10.11. Cùm descenderit pluuia aut nix de cœlo, rursus illuc non reuertitur, sed inebriat terram, facitq; vt pariat ipsa & producat; vt edat semen satori, & panem comedenti: Sic erit verbum meum quod egressum fuerit ex ore meo, non reuertetur ad me vacuum; sed faciet id, quo delector, & prosperabitur id quod emisero.
units.tr: Isa. 55.10-11: For as rain or snow comes down from heaven and does not return there, but waters the earth and makes it bring forth and sprout, that it may give seed to the sower and bread to the eater, so shall my word be that goes out of my mouth: it shall not return to me empty, but shall do what I please and prosper in that for which I sent it.

units.la: Luc.8.v.10. Vobis datum est nosse mysteria regni Dei. Confer v.15.
units.tr: Luke 8.10: To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God. Compare v. 15.

units.la: Act.16.v.14. Quædam autem mulier nomine Lydia, quæpurpuram vendebat in vrbe Thyatirorum, Deum colens, nos audiuit: cuius Dominus adaperuit cor, vt attenderet ea, quæ dicebantur à Paulo. Confer 1.Cor.1.v.24.& 2.Cor.2.v.16.
units.tr: Acts 16.14: A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple in the city of Thyatira, who worshipped God, heard us; the Lord opened her heart to attend to the things that were said by Paul. Compare 1 Cor. 1.24 and 2 Cor. 2.16.

units.la: b) Luc.14. v. 18. & seqq. Omnes cœperunt vno ore se excusare, &c.
units.tr: b) Luke 14.18 and following: They all began with one voice to make excuse, etc.

units.la: Matth.22.v.5. Illi autem cum hoc neglexissent, abierunt: alius quidem in agrum suum, alius vero ad mercaturam suam.
units.tr: Matt. 22.5: But when they had neglected this, they went away: one to his farm, another to his trade.

units.la: c) Act.26.v.27. Paulus dicebat regi Agrippæ, Credis Rex Agrippa prophetis? Scio te credere.
units.tr: c) Acts 26.27: Paul said to King Agrippa, Do you believe the prophets, King Agrippa? I know that you believe.

units.la: Luc.8.v.12. Qui autem secundum viam semen excipiunt, ij sunt qui audiunt: deinde venit diabolus, & tollit sermonem e corde ipsorum, ne, postquam crediderunt, seruentur.
units.tr: Luke 8.12: Those by the wayside are those who hear; then comes the devil and takes the word out of their hearts, lest, having believed, they be saved.

units.la: Hebr.4.v.4. Nam fieri non potest, vt qui semel fuerunt illuminati, &c.
units.tr: Heb. 4.4: For it is impossible that those who were once enlightened, etc.

units.la: d) Matth.13.v.20.21. Qui in petrosa semen excepit, id est, qui sermonem audit, & eum statim cum gaudio accipit: non habet autem radicem in se, sed temporarius est. Confer Luc.8.v.13.
units.tr: d) Matt. 13.20-21: He who received the seed on stony ground, that is, he who hears the word and at once receives it with joy, but has no root in himself, but is temporary. Compare Luke 8.13.

units.la: Heb.6.v.4.5.6. Nam fieri non potest vt qui semel fuerint illuminati, gustauerintq3 donum illud coeleste, & participes facti fuerint Spiritus sancti, gustauerintq3 bonum Dei verbum, ac virtutes futuri seculi: Si prolabantur, denuo renouentur ad resipiscentiam.
units.tr: Heb. 6.4-6: For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit, and have tasted the good word of God and the powers of the age to come, if they fall away, to be renewed again to repentance.

units.la: e) Matth.17.v.20. Amen dico vobis: Si habeatis fidem, quantulum est granum sinapis, dicetis monti huic, Demigra hinc illuc, & demigrabit: & nihil erit impossibile vobis. Confer Matth.21. verf.21.
units.tr: e) Matt. 17.20: Truly I say to you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, Move from here to there, and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you. Compare Matt. 21.21.

units.la: f) Act.7.v.51. Duri ceruice, & incircumcisi corde & auribus, vos semper resistitis Spiritui sancto: quales fuerunt patres vestri, tales & vos estis.
units.tr: f) Acts 7.51: Stiff-necked, and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit: as your fathers did, so do you.

units.la: Psal.81.v.12.13. Sed non auscultauit populus meus voci meæ, & Israel non acquieuit mihi. Quapropter dimisi eos ambulaturos ex sententia animi sui, dicens, Abeant cum prauis consiliis suis.
units.tr: Ps. 81.12-13: But my people did not listen to my voice, and Israel would not submit to me. So I let them go their own way, according to the desires of their heart, saying, Let them go in their wicked counsels.

units.la: Esa.6.v.9.10. Tum dixit, I, vt dicas populo isti: Audite indefinenter, at ne intelligatis, & videte indesinenter, neq3 cognoscatis. Fac vt pinguescat cor populi istius, & aures eius ingrauescant, oculiq3 eius fac conniueant: ne videat oculis suis, & auribus suis audiat, & corde suo intelligat, seq3 conuertat, & sanitas obueniat ei.
units.tr: Isa. 6.9-10: Then he said, Go, and say to this people: Hear indeed, but do not understand; see indeed, but do not perceive. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn and be healed.

units.la: Esa.63.v.10. Ipsis rebellantibus, & dolore afficientibus spiritum sanctitatis eius.
units.tr: Isa. 63.10: But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit.

units.la: Jer.44.v.16.17. In verbo, quod indixisti nobis nomine Jehoua, minime sumus auscultaturi tibi: Sed omnino facturi quodcunque verbum prodierit ex ore nostro, &c.
units.tr: Jer. 44.16-17: As for the word that you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD, we will not listen to you; but we will certainly do whatever word goes out of our mouth, etc.

units.la: Johan.12.v.37. & deinceps. Cum autem tot signa coram eis edidisset, non credebant in eum: Ut sermo Esaia impleretur, quem dixit, Domine, quis credidit sermoni nostro, & brachium Domini cui retectum est: Propterea non poterant credere, quia iterum dixit Esaias: Excæcauit oculos eorum, & obdurauit corda eorum: ne videant oculis, & intelligant corde, & sese conuertant, & sanem eos.
units.tr: John 12.37 and following: But although he had done so many signs before them, they did not believe in him, so that the word of Isaiah might be fulfilled, which he spoke: Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? Therefore they could not believe, because Isaiah said again: He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, lest they see with their eyes and understand with their heart, and turn, and I heal them.

units.la: Luc.8.v.10. Vobis datum est nosse mysteria regni Dei: reliquis autem per parabolas loquor, ut videntes non videant, & audientes non intelligant.
units.tr: Luke 8.10: To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God; but to the rest I speak in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.

units.la: 2.Cor.3.v.14.15. Christi bona fragrantia sumus Deo, in iis qui seruantur, & in iis qui pereunt: His quidem odor mortis ad mortem: illis vero odor vitæ ad vitam.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 2.15-16: For we are to God the good fragrance of Christ, among those who are saved and among those who perish: to the one indeed the smell of death to death, but to the others the smell of life to life.

units.la: 4. Deus per vocationem internam homines transffert in ecclesiam invisibilé, & in iis gratia suâ operante creat pœnitentiam, fidem, & sanctitatem.
units.tr: 4. By internal vocation God brings men into the invisible Church, and in them, by his working grace, creates repentance, faith, and holiness.

units.la: Esa.29.verf.23. Cùm videbit natos suos, opificium manuum mearum.
units.tr: Isa. 29.23: When he sees his children, the work of my hands.

units.la: Ier.31.v 33. Hoc est illud fœdus, quod pangam cum domo Israelis post dies hos dictum Domini: Indam legem meam menti eorum, & cordi eorum inscribam eam; & ero eis Deus, & ipsi erunt mihi populus.
units.tr: Jer. 31.33: This is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

units.la: Ezech.36.v.25.& deinceps. Aspergens vos aquis mundis,ut mundemini, ab omnibus impuritatibus vestris, & ab omnibus stercoreis diis vestris mundabo vos: & dabo vobis cor nouum, & spiritum nouum ponam in medio vestri: & amouens cor lapideum è carne vestrâ, indam vobis cor carneum: spiritum meum ponam in medio vestri; quo faciam, ut in statutis meis ambuletis, & iura mea observetis, facientes ea. Confer Hebr.8.v.10.11.12.
units.tr: Ezek. 36.25, etc.: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, that you may be clean; from all your uncleannesses and from all your idols I will cleanse you. And I will give you a new heart, and put a new spirit within you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh and give you a heart of flesh; I will put my Spirit within you, so that you walk in my statutes and keep my judgments and do them. Compare Heb. 8.10-12.

units.la: Act.11. v.18. His auditis quieverunt Judæi, & glorificauerunt Deum, dicentes : Nempe etiam gentibus Deus resipiscentiam dedit ad vitam.
units.tr: Act.11. v.18. When they heard these things, they held their peace and glorified God, saying: "Then God has also granted repentance unto life to the Gentiles."

units.la: Et c.16.v.14. Cuius (Lydiæ) Dominus adaperuit cor, ut attenderet iis, quæ dicebantur à Paulo.
units.tr: Et c.16.v.14. "Whose heart the Lord opened, so that she attended to the things that were spoken by Paul."

units.la: 1.Cor. 2. v.5. Ne fides vestra consistat in sapientiâ hominum, sed in potentiâ Dei.
units.tr: 1.Cor. 2. v.5. "That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God."

units.la: 2. Cor.3.vers.3. Manifestum sit, vos esse epistolam Christi subministratam à nobis, inscriptam non atramento, sed Spiritu Dei viui[?]: non in tabulis lapideis, sed in carneis tabulis cordis.
units.tr: 2. Cor.3.vers.3. "It is plain that you are the letter of Christ, ministered by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on the fleshly tablets of the heart."

units.la: 2.Cor.4.v.6. Deus, qui dixit, vt è tenebris lux splendesceret, is est, qui splenduit in cordibus nostris ad lucem notitiæ gloriæ Dei in facie Iesu Christi.
units.tr: 2.Cor.4.v.6. "God, who said that light should shine out of darkness, is the one who has shone in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ."

units.la: Eph.2.v.5. Nos, cùm in peccatis mortui essemus, vnà vivificavit Deus cum Christo, cuius gratiâ estis seruati.
units.tr: Eph.2.v.5. "When we were dead in sins, God made us alive together with Christ; by his grace you have been saved."

units.la: Confer supra cum loc● 14. num.3.
units.tr: See above, with place 14, number 3.

units.la: Hinc patet, vocationem internam esse nouam creationem & generationem, siue regenerationem.
units.tr: From this it is plain that internal calling is a new creation and generation, or regeneration.

units.la: 5. Præcepta, quibus iubemur credere & sanctè vivere, sunt adminicula, quibus vocatio interna in nobis perficitur.
units.tr: 5. The precepts by which we are commanded to believe and to live holily are the aids by which internal calling is brought to completion in us.

units.la: 2.Chron.20.v 20. Firmè credite Domino Deo vestro, & confirmabimini: firmè credite prophetis, & prosperamini.
units.tr: 2.Chron.20.v 20. "Believe firmly in the Lord your God, and you shall be established; believe firmly his prophets, and you shall prosper."

units.la: Psal.34.v.10. Timete Deum sancti eius.
units.tr: Psal.34.v.10. "Fear the Lord, you his saints."

units.la: Psal.37.v.3.4.5. Confide in Domino, & fac bonum: inhabita terram, & pascere fide, & oblecta te in Domino, qui dabit tibi petitiones animi tui. Devolve super Dominum viam tuam & confide in eo. nam ipse efficiet.
units.tr: Psal.37.v.3.4.5. "Trust in the Lord and do good; dwell in the land and feed on faithfulness; delight yourself in the Lord, and he will give you the desires of your heart. Commit your way to the Lord and trust in him, for he will bring it about."

units.la: Indesinenter ambula coram me, & esto integer.
units.tr: "Walk continually before me, and be upright."

units.la: Deut.30.v.6. Circumcidet Dominus Deus tuus animum tuum, & animum seminis tui, ad diligendum Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, & ex tota anima tua, vt viuas.
units.tr: Deut.30.v.6. "The Lord your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed, to love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul, that you may live."

units.la: Et v.8. Tu conversus auscultabis voci Domini, & facies omnia præcepta eius, quæ ego præcipio tibi hodie.
units.tr: And v.8. "You shall return and hearken to the voice of the Lord, and do all his commandments which I command you this day."

units.la: Et c.19.v.20. Contestor hodie contra vos cœlum & terram, me vitam ac mortem proposuisse tibi, benedictionem & maledictionem. Quare vitam electurus es, vt viuas tu cum semine tuo, diligendo Dominum Deum tuum, auscultando voci eius, & adhærendo ei.
units.tr: And c.19.v.20. "I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing. Therefore choose life, that you and your seed may live, by loving the Lord your God, by hearkening to his voice, and by cleaving to him."

units.la: Nam ipse est vita tua, & longitudo dierum tuorum.
units.tr: "For he is your life and the length of your days."

units.la: Matth.5.v.16. Ita splendeat lux vestra coram hominibus, vt videant vestra bona opera.
units.tr: Matth.5.v.16. "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works."

units.la: 1.Cor.6.v.20. Emti estis pretio. Glorificate igitur Deum in corpore vestro, & in spiritu vestro, quæ sunt Dei.
units.tr: 1.Cor.6.v.20. "You were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God's."

units.la: Philip.4.v.8.9. Quæcunq; sunt vera, quæcunque venerancda, quæcunque iusta, quæcunque pura, quæcunque amabilia, quæcunq; boni nominis; si qua virtus, & si qua laus est, haec reputate. Qua & didicistis, & accepistis, & audivistis, & vidistis in me; haec, inquam, facite.
units.tr: Philip.4.v.8.9. "Whatever things are true, whatever things are honourable, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report; if there is any virtue and if there is any praise, think on these things. The things which you have both learned and received and heard and seen in me, these, I say, do."

units.la: 1.Joh.3. v. 11.18.24. Haec est denunciatio, quam audivistis a principio, ut diligamus alii alios. Filioli mei, ne diligamus verbo & lingua, sed facto & veritate. Hoc est eius praeceptum, ut credamus nomini Filii eius Jesu Christi, & diligamus alii alios, sicut praecepit nobis.
units.tr: 1.Joh.3. v. 11.18.24. "This is the message you heard from the beginning, that we should love one another. My little children, let us not love in word or in tongue, but in deed and in truth. And this is his commandment, that we should believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he commanded us."

units.la: Eadem est ratio interdictionum diuinarum.
units.tr: The same reasoning applies to the divine prohibitions.

units.la: Psal.32.verf.9. Ne essote[?], ut equus aut mulus, expertes intelligentia.
units.tr: Psal.32.verf.9. "Do not be as the horse or the mule, which lack understanding."

units.la: Esa.1. v.16. Lauate vos, purificate vos, amouete malignitatem actionum vestrarum ex adverso oculorum meorum; desinite malefacere.
units.tr: Esa.1. v.16. "Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes; cease to do evil."

units.la: 1.Cor.5.v.7. Expurgate vetus fermentum, ut sitis nova massa.
units.tr: 1.Cor.5.v.7. "Purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new lump."

units.la: 1.Thess.5.v.19.20 22. Spiritum ne extinguite, prophetias ne pro nihilo habete. Ab omni specie mali abstinete.
units.tr: 1.Thess.5.v.19.20 22. "Do not quench the Spirit. Do not despise prophesyings. Abstain from every appearance of evil."

units.la: 6. Promissiones evangelij sunt universales ratione electorum sive credentium, quorum universitas est quasi peculiaris mundus.
units.tr: 6. The promises of the gospel are universal with respect to the elect or believers, whose totality is, as it were, a peculiar world.

units.la: Joh.3.v.16. Ita enim Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum dederit, ut quisquis credit in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam aeternam.
units.tr: Joh.3.v.16. "For God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, so that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life."

units.la: Etc.6.v.51. Panis autem quem ego dabo, caro mea est, quam ego dabo pro mundi vita.
units.tr: Etc.6.v.51. "The bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world."

units.la: Matth.11.v.28. Venite ad me omnes, qui fatigati estis & onerati, & ego faciam ut requiescatis.
units.tr: Matth.11.v.28. "Come to me, all you who labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest."

units.la: Confer cum vers.25.& 29.in quorum illo promissionis huius analysis a priori, in hoc a posteriori traditur.
units.tr: Compare verses 25 and 29: in the former the analysis of this promise is given a priori, in the latter a posteriori.

units.la: 1.Johan.2.verf.2. Et ipse (Christus Jesus) est propitiatio pro nostris peccatis: nec pro nostris solum, sed etiam pro totius mundi peccatis.
units.tr: 1.Johan.2.verf.2. "And he himself (Christ Jesus) is the propitiation for our sins; and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world."

units.la: Marc.16.verf.16. Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, seruabitur.
units.tr: Marc.16.verf.16. "He who believes and is baptized will be saved."

units.la: Esa.53.v.11. Cognitione sui iustificabit iustus servus meus multos; quorum iniquitates ipse baiulaverit. Vide quoq loc.seq. n.2.
units.tr: Esa.53.v.11. "By the knowledge of himself shall my righteous servant justify many, for he shall bear their iniquities." See also the following place, n.2.

units.la: LOCUS XX. De Justificatione.
units.tr: LOCUS XX. On Justification.

units.la: I. Justificandi verbum in hoc doctrinæ loco
units.tr: I. The word "justify" in this locus of doctrine

units.la: a) interdum idem valet[?] quod iustum constituere, seu iustum censere reputareve.
units.tr: a) sometimes has the same meaning as to make someone righteous, or to deem and reckon them righteous.

units.la: b) interdum idem valet, quod iustum pronuntiare seu absoluere.
units.tr: b) sometimes has the same meaning as to pronounce or absolve someone as righteous.

units.la: a) Rom.5. v.19. Sicut per inobedientiam unius hominis peccatores constituti sunt multi: ita per unius obedientiam justi constituentur multi.
units.tr: a) Rom. 5. v. 19. For as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.

units.la: Et c.4. v.6. Dauid dicit beatificationem esse hominis, cui Deus imputat justitiam.
units.tr: And ch. 4. v. 6. David describes the blessedness of the man to whom God imputes righteousness.

units.la: b) Rom.8. v.33.34. Quis accusabit electos Dei? Deus est is qui justificat. Quis est qui condemnet?
units.tr: b) Rom. 8. v. 33, 34. Who shall lay anything to the charge of God's elect? It is God that justifieth. Who is he that condemneth?

units.la: 2. Justificatio est, quâ Deus gratiâ suâ gratum faciente, id est beneuolentiâ & fauore paterno, hominem fidelem in animo ipsius certum reddit, quòd eum, peccatis remissis, pro justo reputet, ob redemtionem seu satisfactionem & meritum Christi mediatoris. Itaque justificatio pendet
units.tr: 2. Justification is that by which God, through his grace which makes us acceptable (that is, through his fatherly goodwill and favour), assures the believer in his own mind that, with sins forgiven, he reckons him as righteous, on account of the redemption, or satisfaction, and merit of Christ the Mediator. Justification therefore depends

units.la: a) à gratiâ Dei tanquam causâ architectonicâ.
units.tr: a) on the grace of God as its architectonic cause.

units.la: b) à merito Christi tanquam fundamento.
units.tr: b) on the merit of Christ as its foundation.

units.la: c) à fide tanquam instrumento & manu.
units.tr: c) on faith as its instrument and hand.

units.la: De tribus hisce causis coniunctim vide Tit.3. vers. 4. & seqq.
units.tr: On these three causes taken together, see Tit. 3. vers. 4 and following.

units.la: a) Rom.3. v.23.24. Omnes peccauerunt ac deficiuntur gloria Dei, ut qui justificentur gratis, eius gratia.
units.tr: a) Rom. 3. v. 23, 24. For all have sinned and come short of the glory of God; being justified freely by his grace.

units.la: Et c.5. v.21. Ut quemadmodum regnauerat peccatum in mortem, ita etiam gratia regnaret per justitiam in vitam æternam, per Iesum Christum dominum nostrum.
units.tr: And ch. 5. v. 21. That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life, by Jesus Christ our Lord.

units.la: Ephes.2. v.8. Gratiâ seruati estis per fidem, idq; non ex vobis. Dei donum est.
units.tr: Eph. 2. v. 8. By grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God.

units.la: Rom.11.v.6. Quòd si per gratiam, non iam ex operibus. alioqui gratia iam non est gratia.
units.tr: Rom. 11. v. 6. And if by grace, then it is no more of works; otherwise grace is no more grace.

units.la: Esa.43.v.12. Ego, ego ipse deleo defectiones tuas propter me, & peccatorum tuorum non recordor.
units.tr: Isa. 43. v. 25. I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake, and will not remember thy sins.

units.la: Matth.9.v.6. Sciatis, potestatem habere filium hominis in terrā remittendi peccata.
units.tr: Matt. 9. v. 6. That ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins.

units.la: Gen.15.v.6. Credidit Abraham Domino, qui imputauit ei illud ad iustitiam.
units.tr: Gen. 15. v. 6. Abraham believed the Lord, and he counted it to him for righteousness.

units.la: Rom.4.v.6.& deinceps. Dauid declarat beatum eum hominem, cui Deus imputat iustitiam absq; operibus, dicens: Beati, quorum remissæ sunt iniquitates, & quorum obtecta sunt peccata. Beatus vir, cui non imputat Dominus peccatum.
units.tr: Rom. 4. v. 6 and following. David describes the blessedness of the man to whom God imputes righteousness without works, saying: Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.

units.la: b) Rom.5.v.15. At non ut offensa, ita etiam est quod Deus gratificatur (τὸ χάρισμα) nam si illius vnius offensâ multi mortui sunt, multò magis gratia Dei (ἡ χάρις τοῦ Θεοῦ) & donum per gratiam (ἡ δωρεὰ ἐν χάριτι) quae est vnius hominis Iesu Christi, in multos redundauit. Hic pulcherrimè gratia gratis data distinguitur à gratiâ gratis dante & gratiam faciente.
units.tr: b) Rom. 5. v. 15. But the gift is not like the offence. For if through the offence of one many died, much more has the grace of God, and the gift by the grace of the one man Jesus Christ, abounded unto many. Here the grace freely given (gratia gratis data) is admirably distinguished from the grace that freely gives and makes acceptable [τὸ χάρισμα; ἡ χάρις τοῦ Θεοῦ; ἡ δωρεὰ ἐν χάριτι].

units.la: Iohan.1.v.16.Et ex plenitudine ipsius (Christi)omnes accepimus, & gratiam pro gratiâ, (χάριν ἀντὶ χάριτος) id est, grariam supra gratiam, & gratiam propter gratiam, ita vt Christus sit vberrimus fons gratiarum, quae nobis conseruntur, Rom.3.v.23. Omnes peccauerunt & deficiuntur gloriâ Dei, vt qui iustificentur gratis, id est, eius gratiâ, per redemptionem factam in Iesu Christo.
units.tr: John 1. v. 16. And of his fullness (that is, of Christ) have all we received, and grace for grace [χάριν ἀντὶ χάριτος], that is, grace upon grace, and grace on account of grace, so that Christ is the most abundant fountain of the graces that are bestowed upon us. Rom. 3. v. 23. For all have sinned and come short of the glory of God; that they may be justified freely, that is, by his grace, through the redemption made in Jesus Christ.

units.la: Coloss.1.verf.14. In quo (Iesu Christo) habemus redemtionem (ἀπολύτρωσιν) per sanguinem ipsius, id est, remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: Col. 1. v. 14. In whom (Jesus Christ) we have redemption [ἀπολύτρωσιν] through his blood, that is, the forgiveness of sins.

units.la: Tit.2.v.13.14. Iesus Christus seruator noster dedit semetipsum pro nobis, vt redimeret (λυτρώσηται) nos ab omni iniquitate, & purificaret sibi populum peculiarem, accensum studio bonorum operum.
units.tr: Tit. 2. v. 13, 14. Jesus Christ our Saviour gave himself for us, that he might redeem [λυτρώσηται] us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.

units.la: 1.Petri 1.v.18.19. Non rebus corruptibilibus, argento vel auro, redemti estis (ἐλυτρώθητε) ex vana illa conuersatione à patribus traditâ, sed pretiosò sanguine, vtpote agni immaculati & incontaminati, Christi.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 1. v. 18, 19. Ye were not redeemed [ἐλυτρώθητε] with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot.

units.la: Gal.3.v.13. Christus nos redemit (ἐξηγόρασεν) ab execratione legis, dum pro nobis factus est execratio.
units.tr: Gal. 3. v. 13. Christ hath redeemed us [ἐξηγόρασεν] from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us.

units.la: Et cap.4. verf.5. Postquam venit plenum tempus, emisit Deus filium suum, factum ex muliere, factum sub lege, ut eos, qui sub lege erant, redimeret (ἐξαγοράσῃ) ut adoptionem acciperemus.
units.tr: And ch. 4. v. 4, 5. When the fullness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, to redeem [ἐξαγοράσῃ] them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption.

units.la: Apoc.5.v.9.10. Dignus es, qui accipias librum & aperias sigilla eius: quoniam mactatus es, & redemisti (ἠγόρασας)[?] nos Deo per sanguinem tuum, ex omni tribu, & lingua & populo & natione; & fecisti nos Deo reges & sacerdotes: & regnabimus in terra.
units.tr: Rev. 5. v. 9, 10. Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain, and hast redeemed [ἠγόρασας] us to God by thy blood, out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation; and hast made us unto our God kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth.

units.la: Coloss.1.v.13. Eruit (ἐῤῥύσατο) seu extraxit nos ex potestate tenebrarum.
units.tr: Col. 1. v. 13. He hath delivered [ἐῤῥύσατο] us, that is, rescued us, from the power of darkness.

units.la: Hebr.2.v.14.15. Ut per mortem aboleret eum, qui mortis habet imperium, hoc est, diabolum: Et liberos redderet, quotquot metu mortis per omnem vitam obnoxii erant servituti.
units.tr: Heb. 2. v. 14, 15. That through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil; and deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.

units.la: Hinc Christus appellatur vindex, Job.19.v.25: liberator, Job.8.v.38. Gal.5.v.1: salvator & servator, Luc.2.v.11. Joh.4.v. 42. Act.5.v.31. & 13.v.23. Phil.3.v.20. 2.Tim.1.v.10. Tit.1.v.10, 13. & 3.v.4.6. 2.Petri 1.v.1. & 2 v.20. & 3.v.2.18. 1.Joh.4.verf. 14. Jud.v.25.
units.tr: Hence Christ is called the avenger (Job 19. v. 25), the liberator (Job 8. v. 38; Gal. 5. v. 1), and the Saviour and Keeper (Luke 2. v. 11; John 4. v. 42; Acts 5. v. 31; 13. v. 23; Phil. 3. v. 20; 2 Tim. 1. v. 10; Tit. 1. v. 10, 13; 3. v. 4, 6; 2 Pet. 1. v. 1; 2. v. 20; 3. v. 2, 18; 1 John 4. v. 14; Jude v. 25).

units.la: Esa.53.v.10. Dominus delectatus conterere ipsum, morbo affecit, quandoquidem exponebat se ipse sacrificium pro reatu.
units.tr: Isa. 53. v. 10. The Lord was pleased to bruise him; he hath put him to grief, since he made himself an offering for sin.

units.la: Eph.5.v.2. Christus dilexit nos & tradidit semetipsum pro nobis oblationem ac victimam Deo, in odorem bonae fragrantiae.
units.tr: Eph. 5. v. 2. Christ loved us and gave himself for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God, for a sweet-smelling savour.

units.la: Hebr.9.v.14. Christus per spiritum æternum obtuli seipsum inculpatum Deo.
units.tr: Heb. 9. v. 14. Who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God.

units.la: 2.Cor.5.v.18. Deus reconciliavit nos sibi per Jesum Christum.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 5. v. 18. God hath reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ.

units.la: Hebræor.7. verf.22. Tanto melioris pacti sponsor factus est Jesus.
units.tr: Heb. 7. v. 22. By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better covenant.

units.la: 1.Cor.6.v.19.20. Non estis vestri juris. Nam pretio emti estis.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 6. v. 19, 20. You are not your own, for you were bought with a price.

units.la: Idem repetitur 1.Cor.7.v.23.
units.tr: The same is repeated in 1 Cor. 7. v. 23.

units.la: Matth.10.v.28. Filius hominis non venit, ut sibi ministretur, sed ut ministret, detq;[?] animam suam redemtionis pretium pro multis, λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.
units.tr: Matt. 10. v. 28. The Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many [λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν].

units.la: 1.Tim.2.v.6. Qui (Christus Jesus) sese ipse dedit redemtionis pretium pro omnibus, ἀντίλυτρον ὑπὲρ πάντων. Hoc pretium dicitur pretiosus sanguis agni inculpati & incontaminati Christi, 1.Petr.1.v.19.sanguis testamenti, Zach. 9.v.11:&pacti aeterni,Hebr.13.v.20.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 2. v. 6. Who gave himself a ransom for all [ἀντίλυτρον ὑπὲρ πάντων]. This price is called the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot (1 Pet. 1. v. 19), the blood of the testament (Zech. 9. v. 11), and the blood of the everlasting covenant (Heb. 13. v. 20).

units.la: Matth.26.v.28. Hoc poculum est sanguis meus noui fœderis, qui pro multis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum. Confer Luc.22.v.19.
units.tr: Matt. 26. v. 28. This is my blood of the new covenant, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. Compare Luke 22. v. 19.

units.la: Eph.2.v.13. Propinqui facti estis per sanguinem Christi.
units.tr: Eph. 2. v. 13. Ye who were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.

units.la: Colos.1.v.20. Pace per sanguinem crucis eius facta, per eum reconciliare sibi omnia, per eum, inquam, tum quæ in terrâ, tum quæ in cœlis.
units.tr: Col. 1. v. 20. Having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things to himself, by him, I say, whether things in earth, or things in heaven.

units.la: 1.Ioh.1.v.7. Sanguis Iesu Christi Filij eius purgat nos ab omni peccato.
units.tr: 1 John 1. v. 7. The blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.

units.la: Apoc.1.v.5.Lauit nos a peccatis per sanguinem suum.
units.tr: Rev. 1. v. 5. Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood.

units.la: Etc.7.v.14. Sancti laverunt stolas suas ac dealbarunt in sanguine Agni.
units.tr: Rev. 7. v. 14. They have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.

units.la: Rom.3.v.23.& deinceps. Omnes peccauerunt ac deficiuntur gloria Dei, ut qui iustificantur gratis, id est, eius gratia, per redemptionem factam in Iesu Christo, Quem proposuit Deus placamentum (ἱλαστήριον) per fidem in sanguine ipsius, ad demonstrationem iustitiae suae, propter dissimulationem peccatorum.
units.tr: Rom. 3. v. 23 and following. For all have sinned and come short of the glory of God; being justified freely, that is, by his grace, through the redemption made in Jesus Christ; whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation [ἱλαστήριον] through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness, for the remission of sins that are past.

units.la: Etc.5.v.10.Si, cum inimici essemus, reconciliati fumus Deoper mortem Filij eius, multo magis reconciliati servabimur per vitam ipsius.
units.tr: Rom. 5. v. 10. For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.

units.la: Hebr.2.v.17.Debuit per omnia fratribus similis fieri, ut misericors & fidelis pontifex in iis, quae apud Deum agenda erant ad expiandum peccata populi.
units.tr: Heb. 2. v. 17. He ought in all things to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.

units.la: 1.Ioh.2.v.2. Iesus Christus est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris, nec pro nostris solum, sed etiam totius mundi peccatis.
units.tr: 1 John 2. v. 2. Jesus Christ is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.

units.la: Etc.4.vers.10. In hoc est charitas, non quod nos dilexerimus Deum, sed quod ipse dilexerit nos, & miserit Filium suum, ut esset propitiatio pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: 1 John 4. v. 10. Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.

units.la: Porrò de redemtionis pretio & satisfactione Christi sunt elegantissimæ & significantissimæ phrases Scripturæ. Nominatur enim
units.tr: Moreover, the Scripture has very elegant and expressive phrases concerning the price of redemption and the satisfaction of Christ. For he is named:

units.la: Dominus ipse, qui se tradidit, obtulit & dedit pro nobis, Ephes. 5.vers.1. 1.Timoth.2.vers.5. Tit.2.vers.14. Hebr.7.v.26.27. c.9.vers.14.
units.tr: The Lord himself, who gave himself, offered and delivered up for us: Eph. 5. v. 1; 1 Tim. 2. v. 5; Tit. 2. v. 14; Heb. 7. v. 26, 27; ch. 9. v. 14.

units.la: Corpus eius quod pro nobis traditum est, 1.Corinth.II.v.24.
units.tr: His body, which was given for us: 1 Cor. 11. v. 24.

units.la: 1.Petri 2.v.24.
Caro ipsius, Eph 2.v.14.15. 1.Petri 4.v.1.
units.tr: His flesh: Eph. 2. v. 14, 15; 1 Pet. 4. v. 1.

units.la: Corpus carnis, Col.1.v.20.21.22.
units.tr: The body of his flesh: Col. 1. v. 20, 21, 22.

units.la: 5 Sanguis Dei, & Christi, Act.20.v.28. Eph.2.v.13. Coloff.1.
units.tr: 5 The blood of God and of Christ: Acts 20. v. 28; Eph. 2. v. 13; Col. 1.

units.la: Anima seu vita Christi, Esa.53.v.10. Matth.20.verf.28. Io-han.10.verf.15.
units.tr: The soul or life of Christ: Isa. 53. v. 10; Matt. 20. v. 28; John 10. v. 15.

units.la: Iustitia Christi, Rom.5.v.18.
units.tr: The righteousness of Christ: Rom. 5. v. 18.

units.la: 10 Obedientia, Rom.5.v.19.
units.tr: 10 Obedience: Rom. 5. v. 19.

units.la: Paupertas, 2.Cor.8.v.9.
units.tr: Poverty: 2 Cor. 8. v. 9.

units.la: Passio, Hebr.13.v.12.
units.tr: Passion, Hebr.13.v.12.

units.la: Vibices & liuor, seu tumex, Esa.53.v.5. 1.Petri 2.v.24.
units.tr: Stripes and bruise, or swelling, Esa.53.v.5. 1.Petri 2.v.24.

units.la: Attritio seu vulneratio, Esa.53.v.10.
units.tr: Bruising or wounding, Esa.53.v.10.

units.la: 15 Effusio sanguinis, Matth.26.v.28.
units.tr: 15 Effusion of blood, Matth.26.v.28.

units.la: Immolatio, Hebr.9.v.26. c.10.v.10.
units.tr: Offering up in sacrifice, Hebr.9.v.26. c.10.v.10.

units.la: Mactatio & sanguis, Apoc.5.v.9.
units.tr: Slaughter and blood, Apoc.5.v.9.

units.la: Mors, Rom.5.v.8. c.6.v.10. 1.Corinth.15.v.3. Gal.2.v.21.
units.tr: Death, Rom.5.v.8. c.6.v.10. 1.Corinth.15.v.3. Gal.2.v.21.

units.la: 20 Crucifixio, 1.Cor.1.v.23. c.2.v.22. 2.Cor.13.v.4.
units.tr: 20 Crucifixion, 1.Cor.1.v.23. c.2.v.22. 2.Cor.13.v.4.

units.la: Mors crucis, Phil.2.v.8.
units.tr: Death of the cross, Phil.2.v.8.

units.la: Sacrificium, Hebr.9.v.26. c.10.v.12.
units.tr: Sacrifice, Hebr.9.v.26. c.10.v.12.

units.la: Derelictio, Psal.22.v.2. Matth.27.v.46.
units.tr: Forsaking, Psal.22.v.2. Matth.27.v.46.

units.la: Maledictum, Gal.3.v.13.
units.tr: Curse, Gal.3.v.13.

units.la: 25 Condemnatio peccati, Rom.8.v.3.
units.tr: 25 Condemnation of sin, Rom.8.v.3.

units.la: Christus factus peccatum, id est, sacrificium pro peccato, 2.Cor.5.v.21.
units.tr: Christ made sin, that is, a sacrifice for sin, 2.Cor.5.v.21.

units.la: Profusio ipsius in mortem, Esa.53.v.12.
units.tr: Poured out to death, Esa.53.v.12.

units.la: Deletio chirographi, Coloff.2.v.14.
units.tr: Blotting out of the handwriting, Coloss.2.v.14.

units.la: 30 Baiulatio iniquitatum, Esa.53.v.11.
units.tr: 30 Bearing of iniquities, Esa.53.v.11.

units.la: Propitiatio, Rom.3.v.24. 1.Ioh.2.v.2.
units.tr: Propitiation, Rom.3.v.24. 1.Ioh.2.v.2.

units.la: Curatio, Malach.3.v.20.
units.tr: Healing, Malach.3.v.20.

units.la: c) Rom.3.verf.28. Colligimus igitur fide iustificari hominem
units.tr: c) Rom.3.verf.28. We conclude therefore that a man is justified by faith

units.la: absq; operibus legis.
units.tr: without the works of the law.

units.la: 35 Galat.2.verf.16. Scientes hominem non iustificari ex operibus legis, id est, nisi per fidem Iesu Christi: etiam nos in Christum Iesum credidimus, vt iustificaremur ex fide Christi, & non ex operibus legis.
units.tr: 35 Galat.2.verf.16. Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, that is, but by the faith of Jesus Christ: even we have believed in Christ Jesus, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law.

units.la: Phil.3.v.7.8.9. Quæ mihi erant lucra, ea duxi, propter Christum, damnum esse. Quinetiam certe duco, omnia damnum esse propter eminentiam notitiæ Christi Iesu Domini mei: propter quem omnibus istis me ipsum multauì, eaq; [?] duco pro stercoribus, vt Christum lucrifaciam: & comperiar in eo, non habens meam iustitiam, nempe, quæ est ex lege, sed eam, quæ est per fidem Christi, id est iustitiam, quæ est ex Deo per fidem.
units.tr: Phil.3.v.7.8.9. What things were gain to me, those I counted loss for Christ. Yes, doubtless, I count all things loss for the excellence of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and count them but dung, that I may gain Christ, and be found in him, not having my own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith.

units.la: Ioh. 3. v. 14. & deinceps. Prout Moses extulit serpentem in deserto, ita extolli oportet Filium hominis, vt, quisquis credit in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam.
units.tr: Ioh.3.v.14. and following. As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

units.la: Et v.36. Qui credit in Filium, habet vitam æternam.
units.tr: And v.36. He who believes in the Son has eternal life.

units.la: Cap.11.v.25.26. Ego sum resurrectio & vita. Qui credit in me, etiamsi mortuus fuerit, viuet: & quisquis viuit, & credit in me, non morietur in æternum.
units.tr: Cap.11.v.25.26. I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me, even if he is dead, shall live; and whoever lives and believes in me shall never die.

units.la: Et c.6.v.54. Qui edit carnem meam, & bibit sanguinem meum, habet vitam æternam.
units.tr: And c.6.v.54. He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life.

units.la: 3. Iustificari ex operibus & lege, est propria iustitia iustum esse: atex fide iustificari est iustum esse & absolui coram Deo ob alienam, nempe Christi, iustitiam, nobis imputatam, & vera fide acceptam, adeoq; appropriatam.
units.tr: 3. To be justified by works and the law is to be righteous by one's own righteousness; but to be justified by faith is to be righteous and absolved before God on account of another's righteousness, namely Christ's, imputed to us and received by true faith, and so made our own.

units.la: Phil.3. v.9. Non habens meam iustitiam, &c. Vide paulò ante, ad lit.c.
units.tr: Phil.3.v.9. Not having my own righteousness, etc. See a little above, at letter c.

units.la: Hab.2.v.4.Rom.1.v.17.Iustus ex fide viuet.
units.tr: Hab.2.v.4. Rom.1.v.17. The just shall live by faith.

units.la: Rom.3. verf.20.ad 29. Ex operibus legis nulla caro iustificabitur, &c.
units.tr: Rom.3.verf.20 to 29. By the works of the law no flesh shall be justified, etc.

units.la: Act.10.v.43. Huic (Iesu Nazareno) omnes prophetæ testimonium dant, remissionem peccatorum accepturum per nomen eius, qui crediderit in eum.
units.tr: Act.10.v.43. To him (Jesus of Nazareth) all the prophets give witness, that he will receive remission of sins through his name, who believes in him.

units.la: Rom.4.v.11. Abrahamus signum accepit circumcisionis, sigillum iustitiæ fidei.
units.tr: Rom.4.v.11. Abraham received the sign of circumcision, the seal of the righteousness of faith.

units.la: Et v.23.24. Non est scriptum propter eum solum, quòd hoc imputatum fuerit ei: sed etiam propter nos, quibus, futurum est, vt imputetur, iis nimirum, qui credunt in eum, &c. Rom.5.v.1. Iustificati ex fide pacem habemus apud Deum, per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum.
units.tr: And v.23.24. It was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him; but also for us, to whom it is to be imputed, namely those who believe in him, etc. Rom.5.v.1. Being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Gal.3. v.24. Lex paedagogus noster fuit in Christum, vt ex fide iustificaremur.
units.tr: Gal.3.v.24. The law was our schoolmaster to lead us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

units.la: 4. Fides, quâ iustificamur,
units.tr: 4. The faith by which we are justified

units.la: a) non est nuda & historica notitia;
units.tr: a) is not a bare and historical knowledge;

units.la: b) neque est temporale gaudium: sed est
units.tr: b) nor is it a temporary joy; but it is

units.la: c) notitia certa & firma, quâ non tantùm assentimur verbo Dei in genere, sed promissionem gratiæ in Christo, nobis, vt nostram peculiariter, adiudicamus.
units.tr: c) a certain and firm knowledge, by which we not only assent to the Word of God in general, but apply to ourselves, as our own in particular, the promise of grace in Christ.

units.la: d) cum quâ coniuncta est fiducia, in Deo acquiescens; & gaudium spirituale.
units.tr: d) joined with which is trust, resting in God, and spiritual joy.

units.la: e) quæ denique omnis generis opera, tanquam fructus, ex se producit, & ad finem vsq; perseuerat.
units.tr: e) which finally produces from itself all kinds of works, as fruits, and perseveres to the end.

units.la: a) Iac.2.v.17. Fides, si opera non habeat, mortua est.
units.tr: a) Jas.2.v.17. Faith, if it has no works, is dead.

units.la: Et v.19. Tu credis, Deum vnum esse. Recte facis. Etiam daemonia credunt; & horrescunt.
units.tr: And v.19. You believe that God is one. You do well. The devils also believe, and tremble.

units.la: Actor.26. verf.27. Credis rex Agrippa prophetis? Scio te credere.
units.tr: Act.26.verf.27. King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.

units.la: b) Matth.13.v.20.21. Qui in petrosa semen excepit, id est, qui sermonem audit, & eum statim cum gaudio accipit: non habet autem radicem in se.
units.tr: b) Matth.13.v.20.21. He who received the seed on stony ground, that is, who hears the word and at once receives it with joy, but has no root in himself.

units.la: c) Rom.4.verf.18. Qui (Abraham) contra spem sub spe credidit.
units.tr: c) Rom.4.verf.18. Who (Abraham) against hope believed in hope.

units.la: Et c.8.v.28.29. Mihi persuasum est, neq; mortem neq; vitam, neq; angelos neq; principatus, neq; potestates, neq; praesentia neque futura, neq; sublimitatem neq; profunditatem, neq; vllam rem aliam creatam nos posse separare à dilectione Dei, quæ est in Iesu Christo Domino nostro.
units.tr: And c.8.v.28.29. I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, can separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.la: 2.Tim.1.v.12. Non pudefio. Novi enim, cui crediderim; & mihi persuasum est, eum posse depositum meum in illum diem custodire.
units.tr: 2.Tim.1.v.12. I am not ashamed; for I know whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that he is able to keep what I have committed to him until that day.

units.la: Gal.2.v.20. Per fidem illam Filij Dei, qui dilexit me, & tradidit semetipsum pro me.
units.tr: Gal.2.v.20. By that faith of the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.

units.la: Iohan.3.verf.33. Qui recipit eius testimonium, is obsignauit Deum veracem esse.
units.tr: Iohan.3.verf.33. He who receives his testimony has certified that God is true.

units.la: Esa.26.v.3. Cogitationi innitenti custodis continuam pacem, cùm tibi confidit.
units.tr: Esa.26.v.3. You keep in continual peace the mind that rests on you, because it trusts in you.

units.la: Et cap.53.v.11. Cognitione sui iustificabit iustus seruus meus multos.
units.tr: Et cap.53.v.11. By his knowledge my righteous servant shall justify many.

units.la: 1.Cor.3.v.12. Vt sciamus, quia Deus est nobis gratificatus.
units.tr: 1.Cor.3.v.12. So that we may know that God has graciously bestowed on us

units.la: Iob.19.v.25. Noui redemtorem meum viuere.
units.tr: Iob.19.v.25. I know that my redeemer lives.

units.la: Huc pertinent magnifici illi tituli, quòd fides appellatur πληροφορίᾳ[?], πεποίθησις, ἔλεγχος, & ὑπόστασις: & quòd dicitur ex se parere παῤῥησίαν[?], libertatem ad Deum, & προσαγωγὴν[?], aditum ad Deum. Ephes.3.v.12. Rom.5.v.2.c.8. verf.38. 2.Cor.3.v.4. Hebr.11.v.1. item, quòd dicitur nostra victoria, 1.Iohan.5.v.4. scutum, Ephes.6.v.16. & arma militiæ nostræ, 2.Cor.10.v.4.5.
units.tr: To this belong those magnificent titles by which faith is called [πληροφορία] full assurance, [πεποίθησις] confidence, [ἔλεγχος] conviction, and [ὑπόστασις] substance; and by which it is said to produce of itself [παρρησία] boldness, freedom toward God, and [προσαγωγή] access to God. Ephes.3.v.12. Rom.5.v.2. c.8.verf.38. 2.Cor.3.v.4. Hebr.11.v.1. Likewise, it is called our victory, 1.Iohan.5.v.4; a shield, Ephes.6.v.16; and the weapons of our warfare, 2.Cor.10.v.4.5.

units.la: d) Ephes.3.v.12. In quo (Christo) habemus libertatem & aditum cum fiduciâ, per fidem ipsius.
units.tr: d) Ephes.3.v.12. In whom (Christ) we have freedom and access with confidence through his faith.

units.la: Iohan.8.verf.56. Abraham gestiuit, vt videret diem meum: & vidit, & gauisus est.
units.tr: Iohan.8.verf.56. Abraham rejoiced to see my day, and he saw it and was glad.

units.la: e) Iacob.2.verf.17. & seqq. Fides, si opera non habeat, mortua est per se, &c.
units.tr: e) Iacob.2.verf.17. and following. Faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself, etc.

units.la: Gal.5.v.6. In Christo Iesu neq; circumcisio quidquam valet, neque præputium, sed fides per charitatem efficax.
units.tr: Gal.5.v.6. In Christ Jesus neither circumcision avails anything, nor uncircumcision, but faith working through love.

units.la: Luc.22.v.32. Ego rogaui pro te, ne deficiat fides tua.
units.tr: Luc.22.v.32. I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail.

units.la: Ioh.10.v.28. Oues meas nemo rapiet ex manu mea.
units.tr: Ioh.10.v.28. No one shall snatch my sheep out of my hand.

units.la: 2.Tim.2.v.19. Solidum fundamentum Dei stat, habens sigillum hoc, Nouit Dominus qui sint sui.
units.tr: 2.Tim.2.v.19. The firm foundation of God stands, having this seal: The Lord knows those who are his.

units.la: 1.Petri 1.v.5. Virtute (ἐν δυνάμει[?]) Dei custodimini per fidem ad salutem.
units.tr: 1.Petri 1.v.5. By the power (ἐν δυνάμει) of God you are kept through faith unto salvation.

units.la: Et v.23. Renati estis ex semine incorruptibili.
units.tr: And v.23. You have been born again of incorruptible seed.

units.la: Esa.42.v.3. Matth.12.verf.20. Arundinem quassatam non frangets, & linum fumigans non extinguet.
units.tr: Esa.42.v.3. Matth.12.verf.20. A bruised reed he shall not break, and smoking flax he shall not quench.

units.la: Ier.32.v.40. Timorem meum indam cordi eorum, vt non recedant à me.
units.tr: Ier.32.v.40. I will put my fear in their hearts, so that they will not turn away from me.

units.la: Iohan.2.verf.27. Vnctio, quam vos accepistis ab eo, manet in vobis.
units.tr: Iohan.2.verf.27. The anointing which you have received from him abides in you.

units.la: 5. Iustificatio ex se parit a) unionem & communionem cum Deo. b) gloriam adoptionis. c) consolationem viuam. 5 d) bonam conscientiam. e) salutarem vsam[?] bonorum huius mundi. f) tolerantiam crucis. g) spem firmam. h) libertatem Christianam.
units.tr: 5. Justification of itself produces a) union and communion with God; b) the glory of adoption; c) living comfort; 5 d) a good conscience; e) a healthful use of the goods of this world; f) endurance of the cross; g) firm hope; h) Christian liberty.

units.la: 10 a) Esa.54.v.5. Coniux tuus erit opifex tuus, cuius nomen Dominus exercituum.
units.tr: 10 a) Esa.54.v.5. Your husband shall be your maker; the LORD of hosts is his name.

units.la: Hos.2.v.16.19.20. Eritq; die illo, dictum Iehoua, vt voces me, Vir mi. Et desponsabo te mihi in seculum: desponsabo te, inquam, mihi iustitia, iudicioq; & benignitate ac misericordia; & desponsabo te mihi fide, vt agnoscas Dominum.
units.tr: Hos.2.v.16.19.20. And it shall be in that day, says the LORD, that you will call me, My husband. And I will betroth you to me for ever: yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness, and in judgment, and in kindness and mercy; I will betroth you to me in faithfulness, that you may know the LORD.

units.la: Iohan.6.v.56. Qui edit carnem meam, & sanguinem meum bibit, in me manet, & ego in eo.
units.tr: Iohan.6.v.56. He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood abides in me, and I in him.

units.la: 1.Cor.7.v.17. Qui adhaeret Domino, vnus cum eo spiritus est.
units.tr: 1.Cor.7.v.17. He who is joined to the Lord is one spirit with him.

units.la: Eph.5.v.30. Membra sumus corporis eius (Christi) ex carne eius & ex ossibus eius.
units.tr: Eph.5.v.30. We are members of his body, of his flesh and of his bones.

units.la: 1.Cor.10.v.17. Vnus panis vnum corpus multi sumus.
units.tr: 1.Cor.10.v.17. We, being many, are one bread, one body.

units.la: 2.Cor.11.v.2. Aptaui vos, quos vni viro, vt virginem puram si-stam, nempe Christo.
units.tr: 2.Cor.11.v.2. I have betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.

units.la: Gal.3.v.28. Omnes vos vnus estis in Christo.
units.tr: Gal.3.v.28. You are all one in Christ Jesus.

units.la: 25 Coloss.3. v.15. Vocati estis in vnum corpus.
units.tr: 25 Coloss.3.v.15. You have been called into one body.

units.la: Iohan.6.verf.54. Qui edit carnem meam, & bibit sanguinem meum, habet vitam aeternam.
units.tr: Iohan.6.verf.54. He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life.

units.la: Ioh.15.v.4. & seqq. Manete in me, & ego in vobis manebo. sicut palmes non potest ferre fructum à semetipso, id est, nisi manserit in vite: ita nec vos, nisi in me manseritis, &c.
units.tr: John 15.4 and following: "Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine, so neither can ye, except ye abide in me, etc."

units.la: Rom.18.verf.17. Si filij, sumus etiam haeredes, haeredes quidem Dei, coharedes autem Christi.
units.tr: Rom. 18.17: "If we are children, then we are heirs also: heirs indeed of God, and joint-heirs with Christ."

units.la: Eph.4.v.3. & seqq. Studete conseruare vnitatem spiritus per vinculum pacis. Vnum est corpus, & vnus spiritus: sicut & vocati estis in vnam spem vocationis vestrae. Vnus Dominus, vna fides, &c.
units.tr: Eph. 4.3 and following: "Endeavour to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. There is one body and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling. One Lord, one faith, etc."

units.la: 1.Iohan. 1. v.5. & seqq. Hic est nuncius ille, quem audiuimus ex ipso, & renuntiamus vobis, Deum lucem esse, nec tenebras in eo vllas esse. Si dixerimus, nos communionem habere cum ipso, & in tenebris ambulamus, mentimur, nec sincere agimus. Quod si in luce ambulamus, sicut ipse est in luce, communionem habemus cum eo mutuam, & sanguis Filii eius purificat nos ab omni peccato.
units.tr: 1 John 1.5 and following: "This is the message which we have heard from him and declare to you: that God is light, and in him there is no darkness at all. If we say that we have fellowship with him and walk in darkness, we lie and do not practise the truth. But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of his Son cleanses us from all sin."

units.la: De hac vnione & communione vide Canticum canticorum.
units.tr: On this union and communion, see the Song of Songs.

units.la: b) Esa.43.v.17.& seqq. Sic ait Dominus, qui fecit te & formauit te ex vtero, adiuturus te: ne timeto. Nam effundam aquas super sitientem, & fluenta super aridam: effundam spiritum meum super semen tuum, & benedictionem meam super prognatos tuos. Et efflorescent velut inter gramen, velut salices secundum processus aquarum. Hic dicet, Domini sum, & iste vocabit se nomine Iacobi: ille vero scribet manu sua, sum Domini, & de nomine Israelis cognominabit.
units.tr: b) Isa. 43.17 and following: "Thus says the Lord, who made you and formed you from the womb, who will help you: fear not. For I will pour water on the thirsty and streams on the dry ground; I will pour out my Spirit on your seed and my blessing on your offspring. They shall spring up among the grass, like willows by the watercourses. One will say, I am the Lord's, and another will call himself by the name of Jacob; and another will write with his own hand, I am the Lord's, and will be surnamed by the name of Israel."

units.la: Et c.56.v.4.5. Qui observarint sabbata mea, & elegerint id quo delector, apprehenderint q3 [?] foedus meum: eis daturus sum in domo mea, & intra muros meos spatium & nomen melius, quam filiorum aut filiarum: nomen perpetuum daturus sum eorum cuique, quod non exscindetur.
units.tr: And ch. 56.4–5: "To those who keep my sabbaths, and choose what I delight in, and hold fast my covenant, to them I will give in my house and within my walls a place and a name better than sons and daughters. I will give each of them an everlasting name that shall not be cut off."

units.la: Et c.62.v.4. Indetur tibi nomen nouum, quod os Domini prafixerit.
units.tr: And ch. 62.2: "A new name shall be given you, which the mouth of the Lord shall name."

units.la: Hof.1.v.10. Erit pro eo, quod dicitur, non populus meus estis, vt dicatur, Filii Dei viuentis estis.
units.tr: Hos. 1.10: "In the place where it was said to them, You are not my people, it shall be said to them, You are the sons of the living God."

units.la: Matth.5.v.9. Beati, qui sunt pacifici: quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur.
units.tr: Matt. 5.9: "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the sons of God."

units.la: Et v.45. Estis filii patris illius vestri, qui est in coelis.
units.tr: And v. 45: "You are the children of your Father who is in heaven."

units.la: Et c.13.v.38. Bonum semen sunt filii regni.
units.tr: And ch. 13.38: "The good seed are the children of the kingdom."

units.la: Luc.6.v.35. Diligite inimicos vestros, &c. & erit merces vestra multa, ac filii eritis illius altissimi.
units.tr: Luke 6.35: "Love your enemies, etc., and your reward will be great, and you shall be sons of the Most High."

units.la: Iohan.1.v.12. Quotquot eum (Christum) exceperunt, dedit eis hoc ius, vt filii Dei fiant facti, nempe iis, qui credunt in nomen eius.
units.tr: John 1.12: "As many as received him (Christ), to them he gave the right to become the sons of God, namely to those who believe in his name."

units.la: Rom.8.v.14. & seqq. Quotquot spiritu Dei aguntur, hi sunt filii Dei: Non enim accepistis spiritum seruitutis rursum ad metum, sed accepistis spiritu adoptionis, per quem clamamus Abba, i.pater.
units.tr: Rom. 8.14 and following: "As many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are the sons of God. For you have not received the spirit of bondage to fear again, but you have received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, Abba, that is, Father."

units.la: 2.Cor.6.v.18. Ero vobis pro Patre, & vos eritis mihi pro[?]filiis & filiabus: dicit Dominus omnipotens.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 6.18: "I will be a Father to you, and you shall be my sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty."

units.la: Galat.3.verf.26. Omnes filij Dei estis per fidem in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: Gal. 3.26: "You are all the sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus."

units.la: Gal.4.v.5.6. Vt adoptionem acciperemus. Quoniam estis filij, emisit Deus spiritum Filij sui in corda vestra, clamantem Abba, id est, Pater.
units.tr: Gal. 4.5–6: "That we might receive adoption. And because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, that is, Father."

units.la: Eph.1.v.5. Quos adoptaret in filios per Iesum Christum.
units.tr: Eph. 1.5: "Whom he would adopt as sons through Jesus Christ."

units.la: Phil.2.v.15. Sitis integri & sine macula, tanquam filij Dei sinceri, qui habitant in generatione praua & peruersa.
units.tr: Phil. 2.15: "That you may be blameless and innocent, as sincere sons of God, living in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation."

units.la: 1.Iohan.3.v.2. Dilecti, nunc filij Dei sumus.
units.tr: 1 John 3.2: "Beloved, now we are the sons of God."

units.la: Et v.9.10. Quisquis natus est ex Deo, peccato non dat operam; quoniam semen ipsius in eo manet, nec potest peccare, quòd ex Deo natus est. Per hoc manifesti sunt filij Dei & filij diaboli.
units.tr: 1 John 3.9–10: "Whoever is born of God does not devote himself to sin, for his seed remains in him, and he cannot sin, because he is born of God. By this the sons of God and the sons of the devil are made manifest."

units.la: Apoc.2.v.17. Qui vicerit, ei tribuam, vt edat ex manna illo occulto, & dabo illi calculum album, & in calculo nomen nouum scriptum, quod nemo nouit, nisi qui accepit.
units.tr: Rev. 2.17: "To him who overcomes I will give to eat of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written, which no one knows except him who receives it."

units.la: Etc.21.v.9. Victor haereditario iure obtinebit omnia: & ero ipsi Deus, & ipse erit mihi filius.
units.tr: Rev. 21.7 (cited as "Etc.21.v.9"): "He who overcomes shall obtain all things by hereditary right, and I will be his God, and he shall be my son."

units.la: c) Psal.94.v.19. Cùm multae cogitationes sunt apud me, consolationes tuae oblectant animam meam.
units.tr: c) Ps. 94.19: "When there are many thoughts within me, your consolations delight my soul."

units.la: Esa.12.v.1. Dices tempore illo, Celebrabo te Domine, quia iratus fuisti mihi, sed auersa ira mea consolaris me.
units.tr: Isa. 12.1: "In that day you will say, I will praise you, O Lord, for though you were angry with me, your anger is turned away and you comfort me."

units.la: Etc.51.v.12. Ego ego sum consolator vester.
units.tr: Isa. 51.12: "I, I am your comforter."

units.la: Etc.61.v.1.2. Vnxit Dominus me, ad consolandum omnes lugentes.
units.tr: Isa. 61.1–2: "The Lord has anointed me to comfort all who mourn."

units.la: Etc.66.v.13. Vt aliquem consolatur mater sua, sic ego consolaturus sum vos.
units.tr: Isa. 66.13: "As a mother comforts someone, so will I comfort you."

units.la: 2.Corinth.1.v.3. & seqq. Benedictus Deus ac Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, pater ille miserationum, & Deus omnis consolationis, consolans nos in omni afflictione nostra: vt possimus in quauis afflictione positos consolari eâ ipsâ consolatione, quâ nos ipsos consolatur Deus. Nam sicut exundant perpessiones Christi in nobis: itaper Christum exundat etiam consolatio nostra.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 1.3 and following: "Blessed be God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort, who comforts us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction with the same comfort with which God himself comforts us. For as the sufferings of Christ overflow in us, so also our comfort overflows through Christ."

units.la: 2.Thess.2.v.16 17. Dominus noster Iesus Christus, & Deus ac pater noster, qui dilexit nos, & dedit consolationem aeternam · spem bonam per gratiam, consoletur corda vestra, & stabiliat vos in omni sermone & opere bono.
units.tr: 2 Thess. 2.16–17: "Our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who has loved us and given us eternal consolation and good hope through grace, comfort your hearts and establish you in every good word and work."

units.la: d) 2.Cor.1 v.11. Gloriatio nostra haec est, testimonium conscientiae nostrae, quod cum simplicitate & sinceritate Dei versati sumus in mundo.
units.tr: d) 2 Cor. 1.11: "Our boast is this: the testimony of our conscience, that we have conducted ourselves in the world in the simplicity and sincerity of God."

units.la: Hebr.13.v.18. Confidimus, nos bonam conscientiam habere, vt quiin omnibus studeamus bene versari.
units.tr: Heb. 13.18: "We trust that we have a good conscience, desiring in all things to live honourably."

units.la: Ioh.8.v.56. Abrahamus, pater ille vester, gestiuit videre diem istum meum, & vidit, ac gauisus est.
units.tr: John 8.56: "Abraham your father longed to see my day, and he saw it and rejoiced."

units.la: Rom.5.v.1. Iustificati ex fide, pacem habemus apud Deum per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum.
units.tr: Rom. 5.1: "Being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ."

units.la: 1.Petri 3.v.21. Baptismus nos seruat, non quo carnis sordes abiciuntur, sed stipulatio bona conscientiae apud Deum: id est, non baptismus externus, sed internus.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 3.21: "Baptism saves us, not by the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but by the answer of a good conscience towards God": that is, not external baptism but internal baptism.

units.la: e) 1.Timoth.4.v.3.4. Deus condidit cibos ad participandum cum gratiarum actione, fidelibus, & iis, qui nōrūt veritatem. Nam quidquid condidit Deus, bonum est: nec quidquam reiiciendum est, si cum gratiarum actione sumatur.
units.tr: e) 1 Tim. 4.3–4: "God created foods to be received with thanksgiving by the faithful and by those who know the truth. For whatever God has created is good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is taken with thanksgiving."

units.la: Deut.28.v.1. & seqq. Erit, si fideliter auscultaueris voci Domini Dei tui, &c. Benedictus eris in ciuitate, & benedictus eris [illegible, ~2 words] ruri, &c.
units.tr: Deut. 28.1 and following: "It shall be, if you diligently obey the voice of the Lord your God, etc. Blessed shall you be in the city, and blessed shall you be in the country, etc."

units.la: f) Iob.9.v.23. Adprobationem innocentium ridet.
units.tr: f) Job 9.23: "He mocks the trial of the innocent."

units.la: Psal.37. v.20. Multae sunt afflictiones iusti: sed ex omnibus illis eripit eum Dominus. Vide insignem similitudinem Esa.18. v.23. & deinceps.
units.tr: Ps. 37.20: "Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but out of them all the Lord delivers him." See the notable parallel at Isa. 18.23 and following.

units.la: Ier.46.v.28. Castigaturus sum te modice, non autem prorsus relicturus impunem.
units.tr: Jer. 46.28: "I will chastise you in measure, and will by no means leave you unpunished."

units.la: Rom.8.v.17. Si modo cum eo patimur, vt & cum eo glorificemur.
units.tr: Rom. 8.17: "If indeed we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified with him."

units.la: 1.Cor.11.v.32. Dum iudicamur, a Domino erudimur, ne cum mundo condemnemur.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 11.32: "When we are judged, we are chastened by the Lord, so that we may not be condemned with the world."

units.la: 2.Tim.3.v.12. Omnes, qui volunt pie viuere in Christo Iesu, persecutionem patientur.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 3.12: "All who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution."

units.la: Hebr.11.v.25[?].& seqq. Sanctorum alij distenti sunt, alij ludibria & flagella sunt experti,&c.
units.tr: Heb. 11.25 [?] and following: "Others of the saints were tortured, others experienced mockings and scourgings, etc."

units.la: Et c.12.v.5.6. Obliti estis[?] adhortationis, quae vobis tanquam fihis[?] loquitur : Fili mi, ne parui facito castigationem Domini, neque animo frangitor, cùm ab eo argueris. Quem enim diligit Dominus, castigat: flagellat autem, quemcunque filium agnoscit.
units.tr: And ch. 12.5–6: "You have forgotten the exhortation which speaks to you as to sons: My son, do not make light of the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when you are rebuked by him. For whom the Lord loves he chastens, and he scourges every son whom he receives."

units.la: Iacob. 1. v. 2. 3. Summo gaudio ducite, quoties in tentationes varias incideritis : scientes, explorationem fidei vestrae efficere tolerantiam.
units.tr: James 1.2–3: "Count it all joy when you fall into various temptations, knowing that the testing of your faith produces patience."

units.la: 1. Petr. 4. v. 17. Tempus est, vt incipiat iudicium à domo Dei.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 4.17: "It is time for judgment to begin at the house of God."

units.la: Apoc. 3. v. 19. Ego, quoscunque amo, arguo & castigo.
units.tr: Rev. 3.19: "Those whom I love, I rebuke and chasten."

units.la: g) Rom. 5. v. 5. Spes non pudefacit, eò quòd charitas Dei effusa est in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctum.
