units.tr: g) Rom. 5.5: "Hope does not put to shame, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit."

units.la: Et v. 2. Per quem (Iesum Christum) etiam fide adducti sumus in hanc gratiam per quam stamus, & gloriamur sub spe gloria Dei.
units.tr: And v. 2: "Through whom (Jesus Christ) we also have been brought by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we rejoice in hope of the glory of God."

units.la: Psal. 62. v. 8. Spes mea in Deo est.
units.tr: Psal. 62. v. 8. My hope is in God.

units.la: Et 142. v. 6. Dixi, Tu es spes mea.
units.tr: And Psal. 142. v. 6. I said, You are my hope.

units.la: Esa. 30. v. 15. In silentio & spe erit fortitudo vestra.
units.tr: Isa. 30. v. 15. In quietness and in hope shall be your strength.

units.la: Rom. 8. v. 24. Spe enim saluati sumus.
units.tr: Rom. 8. v. 24. For we are saved by hope.

units.la: 1. Thess. 5. v. 8. Induti thorace fidei & charitatis: & pro galea, spe salutis.
units.tr: 1. Thess. 5. v. 8. Having put on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet the hope of salvation.

units.la: Confer Rom. 12. v. 12. c. 15. v. 4. 2. Cor. 1. v. 7. c. 3. v. 12. Coloss. 1. v. 5. 1. Thess. 1. v. 3. Tit. 1. v. 2. Hebr. 3. v. 6. 1. Petri 1. v. 3.
b) libertas Christiana est in eo, quòd liberati sumus
units.tr: b) Christian liberty consists in this, that we are freed

units.la: i) à maledictione legis.
units.tr: i) from the curse of the law.

units.la: k) à rigidâ exactione legis.
units.tr: k) from the rigid exaction of the law.

units.la: l) à ceremoniis legis.
units.tr: l) from the ceremonies of the law.

units.la: m) à rerum adiaphorarum necessariâ obseruatione.
units.tr: m) from the necessary observance of indifferent things.

units.la: i) Gal. 3. v. 13. Christus nos redemit ab execratione legis, dum pro nobis factus est execratio.
units.tr: i) Gal. 3. v. 13. Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, becoming a curse for us.

units.la: Rom. 6. v. 14. Non estis sub lege, sed sub gratiâ.
units.tr: Rom. 6. v. 14. You are not under the law, but under grace.

units.la: k) Rom. 7. v. 22. Delector lege Dei, quod ad interiorem hominem.
units.tr: k) Rom. 7. v. 22. I delight in the law of God according to the inner man.

units.la: 1. Ioh. 5. v. 3. Mandata eius grauia non sunt.
units.tr: 1. John 5. v. 3. His commandments are not grievous.

units.la: l) Gal. 3. v. 24. Postquam venit fides, non amplius sub pædagogo sumus. Eph.2.v.14.15. Christus est pax nostra: qui utraq; fecit unum, & intergerini parietis septum soluit: inimicitias (id est, lege mandatorum quae in ritibus posita est) per carnem suam abolitis.
units.tr: l) Gal. 3. v. 24. After faith has come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster. Eph. 2. v. 14–15. Christ is our peace, who has made both one and has broken down the dividing wall of the fence, abolishing in his flesh the enmity (that is, the law of commandments, which lies in ritual observances).

units.la: Coloss.2.v.14. & deinceps. Christus delevit, quod adversus nos erat chirographum, quod erat nobis contrarium: ipse vero cruci affixum sustulit. Ne quis igitur nos damnet ob cibum vel potum, &c. Quae sunt umbra rerum futurarum: corpus autem est Christi.
units.tr: Col. 2. v. 14 and following. Christ blotted out the handwriting that was against us, which was contrary to us, and he took it away, nailing it to the cross. Let no one therefore condemn you in respect of food or drink, etc. These are a shadow of things to come, but the body is Christ's.

units.la: m) Gal.2.v.3. & deinceps. Sed neq; Titus, qui mecum erat, quamvis esset Graecus, coactus fuit circumcidi. Nempe propter irrepteptitios falsos fratres qui irrepserant, ad explorandum libertatem nostram quam habemus in Christo Iesu, ut nos in servitutem adigerent. Quibus ne ad momentum quidem nos subjiciendo cessimus; ut veritas evangelii permaneret apud vos.
units.tr: m) Gal. 2. v. 3 and following. But neither was Titus, who was with me, though he was a Greek, compelled to be circumcised. Indeed, it was because of false brethren secretly brought in, who had crept in to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage; to whom we did not yield in submission even for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel might remain among you.

units.la: LOCUS XXI.
units.tr: LOCUS XXI.

units.la: De bonis operibus.
units.tr: On Good Works.

units.la: 1. Sanctificatio est, qua Deus in iustificatis, gratia sua cooperante, sanctitatem gratia operante datam, dirigit ad bona opera facienda.
units.tr: 1. Sanctification is that by which God, cooperating with His grace in those who have been justified, directs them to perform good works, the holiness being given by grace and working through grace.

units.la: Exod.31.v.13. Ego Dominus sum, qui sanctifico vos.
units.tr: Exod. 31.13. I am the Lord who sanctifies you.

units.la: Ezech.20.v.12. Ego Dominus sanctifico vos.
units.tr: Ezek. 20.12. I the Lord sanctify you.

units.la: Et c.36.v.27. Spiritum meum ponam in medio vestri, quoafaciam ut in statutis meis ambuletis, & iura mea observetis, facientes ea.
units.tr: And ch. 36.27. I will put my Spirit in the midst of you, and I will cause you to walk in my statutes and to keep my judgments, doing them.

units.la: Et c.37.v.38. Cognoscant gentes, me Dominum sanctificare Israelem, cum erit sanctuarium meum in medio ipsorum.
units.tr: And ch. 37.28. The nations shall know that I the Lord sanctify Israel, when my sanctuary shall be in the midst of them.

units.la: Luc.11.v.13. Si vos, qui mali estis, nostis bona dare liberis vestris: quanto magis Pater vester caelestis dabit Spiritum sanctum, petentibus ab ipso.
units.tr: Luke 11.13. If you, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?

units.la: Ioh.17.v.17. Sanctifica, Pater, eos, tua veritate.
units.tr: John 17.17. Sanctify them, Father, in your truth.

units.la: 2.Cor.3.verf.5. Non sumus idonei per nos ipsos ad cogitandum quidquam, velut ex nobis ipsis: sed quod idonei sumus, idex Deo est.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 3.5. We are not sufficient of ourselves to think anything as of ourselves, but our sufficiency is of God.

units.la: Phil.4. v.13. Omnia valeo per eum, qui me corroborat, nempe Christum.
units.tr: Phil. 4.13. I can do all things through him who strengthens me, namely Christ.

units.la: Hebr.13. v.20.21. Deus pacis compingat vos ad omne opus bonum, adprastandam ipsius voluntatem, efficiens in vobis, quod gratum sit in conspectu suo.
units.tr: Heb. 13.20-21. May the God of peace make you complete in every good work, to do his will, working in you what is pleasing in his sight.

units.la: 2.Thess.1. v.18. Oramus semper pro vobis, ut vos dignetur ista vocatione Deus noster, & compleat omnem sua gratuita bonitatis beneuolentiam, & opus fidei potenter.
units.tr: 2 Thess. 1.11. We always pray for you, that our God would count you worthy of this calling and fulfil every desire of goodness and every work of faith with power.

units.la: Tit.2. v.14. Dedit semetipsum (Iesus Christus) pro nobis, ut redimeret nos ab omni iniquitate, & purificaret sibi ipsi populum peculiarem, accensum studio bonorum operum.
units.tr: Titus 2.14. He (Jesus Christ) gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and cleanse for himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.

units.la: Phil. 2. v.13. Deus is est, qui efficit in nobis, & ipsum velle, & ipsum agere, pro gratuita sua beneuolentia.
units.tr: Phil. 2.13. It is God who works in us both to will and to work, for his good pleasure.

units.la: 1.Cor.15. v.10. Gratia Dei sum id, quod sum: & gratia eius, quae in me collata est, non fuit inanis, sed amplius quam omnes laborau: non ego tamen, sed gratia Dei, quae mecum est.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 15.10. By the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace bestowed on me was not in vain, but I laboured more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which is with me.

units.la: Rom.6. v.22. Liberati a peccato, serui autem facti Deo, habetis fructum vestrum in sanctimoniam: finem autem vitam aeternam.
units.tr: Rom. 6.22. Being freed from sin and made servants of God, you have your fruit unto holiness, and the end eternal life.

units.la: Hinc est, quod sancti tum pro se, tum pro aliis orant, ut sancte incedant.
units.tr: Hence it is that the saints pray both for themselves and for others, that they may walk holily.

units.la: Psal.93. v.24. Deduc me, Deus, via perpetua.
units.tr: Ps. 139.24. Lead me, O God, in the everlasting way.

units.la: Et141. v.3.4. Compone, Domine, obserua os meum; custodiens moderare quidquid efferunt labia mea, ne fine inclinari animum meum ad rem malam, ad agitandum actiones per improbitatem cum viris operam dantibus iniquitati: etiam inescer rebus amoenis eorum.
units.tr: And Ps. 141.3-4. Set, O Lord, a watch before my mouth, and keep the door of my lips. Do not let my heart incline to an evil thing, to practise wicked deeds with men who work iniquity; and let me not eat of their delicacies.

units.la: Et143. v.10. Doce me facere placitum tuum, quia tu Deus meus es: tuo spiritu bono deduc me per terram planam.
units.tr: And Ps. 143.10. Teach me to do your will, for you are my God; let your good Spirit lead me into the land of uprightness.

units.la: Eph.3. v.14. & seqq. Huius rei gratia flecto genua mea ad Patrem domini nostri Iesu Christi, ex quo tota familia in coelis & in terra nominatur; ut det vobis pro diuite sua gloria, ut fortiter corroboremini per spiritum ipsius in interiore homine, & inhabitet Christus per fidem in cordibus vestris: ut in charitate radicati & fundati valeatis assequi cum omnibus sanctis, quae sit illa latitudo & longitudo, profunditas & sublimitas.
units.tr: Eph. 3.14 ff. For this cause I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, from whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named; that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might through his Spirit in the inner man, and that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith; that being rooted and grounded in love, you may be able to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth and length and depth and height.

units.la: 1.Petri 5.v.10.Deus omnis gratia, qui vocauit vos ad æternam suam gloriam in Christo Iesu, paulisper afflictos, is perficiat vos, stabiliat, roboret, fundet.
units.tr: 1 Peter 5.10. The God of all grace, who has called you to his eternal glory in Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, will himself perfect, establish, strengthen and settle you.

units.la: 2. Bona opera debent fieri ex fide, secundùm legem Dei, ad ipsius gloriam.
units.tr: 2. Good works ought to be done from faith, according to the law of God, and to the glory of God.

units.la: Rom.14.v.vlt. Quidquid vero ex fide non est, peccatum est.
units.tr: Rom. 14.23. Whatever is not of faith is sin.

units.la: Hebr.11.v.6. Fieri non potest, vt sine fide quisquam ei placeat.
units.tr: Heb. 11.6. It is impossible to please God without faith.

units.la: 1.Sam.15.v.22. At dixit Samuel, An delectatur Iehoua holocaustis & sacrificiis, vt cum auscultatur voci Iehoua? Ecce, auscultare est melius sacrificio; attendere, adipe arietum.
units.tr: 1 Sam. 15.22. But Samuel said: Does the Lord delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as much as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.

units.la: Eph.6.v.17. Galeam etiam salutis recipite, & gladium spiritus, hoc est, verbum Dei.
units.tr: Eph. 6.17. Take also the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.

units.la: Psal.119.v.105. Lucerna pedi meo verbum tuum est, lux itineri meo. Vide passim in hoc psalmo.
units.tr: Ps. 119.105. Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path. See throughout this psalm.

units.la: Deut.12.v.vlt. Vnamquamque rem, quam ego præcipio vobis, eam observantes facite:ne addito ei, neq[?] detrahito ex ea.
units.tr: Deut. 12.32. Whatever thing I command you, take care to observe it; you shall not add to it nor take away from it.

units.la: Esa.29.v.13. Dixit enim Dominus, propterea quòd appropinquans populus iste, ore suo & labiis suis honorant me, cor autem suum procul amouet à me: estq; reuerentia eorum erga me, quam præcepto hominum edocti sunt. Confer Matth.15.v.8.
units.tr: Isa. 29.13. For the Lord said: Because this people draws near with its mouth and honours me with its lips, but its heart is far from me, and their fear of me is taught by the precept of men. Compare Matt. 15.8.

units.la: Ezech.20.v.18.19. Edixi enim filiis illorum in deserto, In statutis patrum vestrorum ne ambuletis, & iura illorum ne observetis; neq[?] stercoreis diis illorum vos polluatis. Ego sum Iehoua Deus vester, in statutis meis ambulate, & iura mea observate, ac facite ea.
units.tr: Ezek. 20.18-19. For I said to their children in the wilderness: Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, nor keep their judgments, nor defile yourselves with their idols. I am the Lord your God; walk in my statutes, and keep my judgments and do them.

units.la: Matth.15.v.9. Frustra me colunt, docentes doctrinas, quæ sunt mandata hominum.
units.tr: Matt. 15.9. In vain do they worship me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.

units.la: 1.Cor.10.v.31. Omnia in Dei gloriam facite.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 10.31. Do all things to the glory of God.

units.la: Et c.6.v.20. Glorificate Deum in corpore vestro, & in spiritu vestro, quæ sunt Dei.
units.tr: And ch. 6.20. Glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God's.

units.la: 3. Bonorum operum cursus quotidie est instaurandus per pœnitentiam, hoc est, mortificationem veteris, & viuificationem noui hominis.
units.tr: 3. The course of good works must be renewed every day through repentance, that is, through the mortification of the old man and the quickening of the new man.

units.la: Matth.3.v.4. Ferte fructus resipiscentiâ dignos.
units.tr: Matt. 3.8. Bring forth fruits worthy of repentance.

units.la: Esa.1.v.16.17. Lauate vos, purificate vos, amouete maligni-tatem tatem actionum vestrarum ex adverso oculorum meorum; definite malefacere, discite benefacere.
units.tr: Isa. 1.16-17. Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean, put away the evil of your deeds from before my eyes; cease to do evil, learn to do good.

units.la: Amos 5.v.15. Odio habete malum, & amate bonum.
units.tr: Amos 5.15. Hate evil and love good.

units.la: Psal.34.v.15. Recede à malo, & fac bonum.
units.tr: Ps. 34.14. Depart from evil and do good.

units.la: Eph.4.v.21. & seqq. Per eum (Christum) edocti estis deponere, quod ad pristinam conversationem attinet, veterem illum hominem, qui de seductricibus cupiditatibus sese corrumpit: renovari vero spiritu mentis vestrae, & induere novum illum hominem, qui secundum Deum conditus est ad iustitiam & sanctimoniam veram.
units.tr: Eph. 4.21 ff. You have been taught by him (Christ) to put off, concerning your former way of life, the old man, who is corrupted by deceitful lusts; and to be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and to put on the new man, who after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.

units.la: Et c.3.v.8. Eratis olim tenebrae, nunc autem lux in Domino: ut filij lucis incedite.
units.tr: And ch. 5.8. You were once darkness, but now are light in the Lord; walk as children of light.

units.la: Tit.2.v.11.12. Illuxit gratia illa Dei salutifera omnibus hominibus, erudiens nos, ut, abnegatâ impietate & mundanis cupiditatibus, temperanter, & iuste, & pie vivamus in praesenti seculo.
units.tr: Titus 2.11-12. The saving grace of God has appeared to all men, teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously and godly in the present world.

units.la: 2.Cor.7.v.9.10. Nunc gaudeo, non quòd tristitiâ affecti sueritis, sed quòd tristitiâ affecti fueritis ad resipiscentiam. Nam tristitiâ fuistis affecti secundum Deum, &c. Nam qui secundum Deum dolor est, is resipiscentiam efficit ad salutem, cuius nunquam poeniteat: at mundi dolor mortem efficit.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 7.9-10. Now I rejoice, not that you were made sorry, but that you were made sorry unto repentance. For you were made sorry after a godly manner, etc. For the sorrow that is according to God produces repentance unto salvation, which is never regretted; but the sorrow of the world produces death.

units.la: 4. Deus remuneratur bona opera, praemiis temporalibus & aeternis, ex merâ gratiâ.
units.tr: 4. God rewards good works with temporal and eternal rewards, out of mere grace.

units.la: Luc.17.v.10. Vos, cùm feceritis omnia quae praecepta sunt vobis, dicite, serui inutiles sumus. nam quod debuimus facere, fe-cimus.
units.tr: Luke 17.10. When you have done all those things which are commanded you, say: We are unprofitable servants; for we have done what we ought to have done.

units.la: Matth.5.v.12. Gaudete & exultate: quoniam merces vestra multa est in coelis. Confer Luc.6.v.23.35. Apoc.21.v.12.
units.tr: Matt. 5.12. Rejoice and be exceedingly glad, for your reward is great in heaven. Compare Luke 6.23, 35; Rev. 21.12.

units.la: Matth.25.v.34. & seqq. Tunc dicet rex iis qui adsinistram ipsius erunt, Adeste benedicti Patris mei, possidete regnum paratum vobis à iacto mundi fundamento. Esuriui enim, & dedistis mihi, quo vescerer: sitiui, & dedistis mihi potum, &c.
units.tr: Matt. 25.34 ff. Then the king will say to those on his left: Come, blessed of my Father, possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave me food to eat; I was thirsty and you gave me drink, etc.

units.la: 1.Tim.4.v.8. Pietas ad omnia utilis est, ut quae promissionem habeat vitae praesentis ac futurae. Confer Deut.28.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 4.8. Godliness is profitable for all things, having the promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come. Compare Deut. 28.

units.la: 5. Opera primae tabulae praecipua, sunt
units.tr: 5. The chief works of the first table are these:

units.la: a) Dilectio Dei supra omnia, coniuncta cum timore filiali. b) Fiducia in Deo. c) Patientia erga Deum, coniuncta cum spe. d) Precatio. e) Confessio. f) Iuramentum. g) Votum. h) Religiositas.
units.tr: a) Love of God above all things, joined with filial fear. b) Trust in God. c) Patience towards God, joined with hope. d) Prayer. e) Confession. f) Oath. g) Vow. h) Religiousness.

units.la: a) Psal.18.v.2.3. Ex intimis visceribus meis diligam te, Domine firmitas mea; Domine petra mea, & propugnaculum meum, & liberator meus, Deus meus, rupes mea, ad quam recipiam me; clypeus meus, & cornu salutis mea, editus locus meus. Confer Matt. 22. verf.37.
units.tr: a) Ps. 18.1-2. I will love you from my inmost heart, O Lord my strength; O Lord my rock, my fortress and my deliverer, my God, my rock in whom I take refuge, my shield and the horn of my salvation, my high tower. Compare Matt. 22.37.

units.la: Deut.10.v.12. Quid Dominus tuus petit abs te (Israel) nisi ut timeas Dominum Deum tuum, ambules in omnibus viis eius, & diligas eum, & colas Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, & ex toto animo tuo?
units.tr: Deut. 10.12. What does the Lord your God require of you, Israel, but that you fear the Lord your God, walk in all his ways, love him, and serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul?

units.la: b) Esa.26.v.4. Confidite Domino vsq; in sempiternum. Nam in Domino Domino rupes seculorum est.
units.tr: b) Isa. 26:4. Trust in the LORD for ever, for in the LORD GOD is everlasting strength.

units.la: Psal.4.v.6. Fiduciam habete in Domino.
units.tr: Ps. 4:6. Put your trust in the LORD.

units.la: Psal.115.v.9. & deinceps. Israel confide Iehoua, auxilium horum & scutum horum est. Vos e familia Aaronis confidite Iehoua, auxilium horum, & scutum horum est. Timentes Iehouam confidite Iehoua, auxilium horum & scutum horum est.
units.tr: Ps. 115:9ff. O Israel, trust in the LORD: he is their help and their shield. O house of Aaron, trust in the LORD: he is their help and their shield. You who fear the LORD, trust in the LORD: he is their help and their shield.

units.la: c) Luc.8.v.15. Quod semen in bonam terram cecidit, ij sunt, qui corde honesto ac bono auditum sermonem retinent, & fructum afferunt in patientia.
units.tr: c) Luke 8:15. As for that which fell on the good ground, they are those who, having heard the word in an honest and good heart, keep it and bring forth fruit with patience.

units.la: Et c.21.v.19. Per tolerantiam vestram possidete animas vestras.
units.tr: And ch. 21:19. By your patience possess your souls.

units.la: Apoc.2.v.2. Noui opera tua, & laborem tuum, & tolerantiam tuam.
units.tr: Rev. 2:2. I know your works, and your labour, and your patience.

units.la: Iacob.5.v.8. Patiente animo estote, & stabilite corda vestra.
units.tr: Jas. 5:8. Be patient, and stablish your hearts.

units.la: Psal.103.v.7. Expectationem habeat Israel in Domino: quia apud Dominum est benignitas, & plurimū apud eum redemtionis.
units.tr: Ps. 130:7. Let Israel hope in the LORD, for with the LORD there is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption.

units.la: Hos.12.v.7. Tu (Israel) ad Deum tuum conuertere; benignitatem & iudicium obserua, & expectationem habe in Deo tuo iugiter. Pfal.22.v.5.Tibi confisi sunt maiores nostri:confisi sunt, & liberasti eos. Confer I.Petri i.v.13.21.1.Tim.4. v.10..
units.tr: Hos. 12:6. Turn you to your God: keep mercy and judgement, and wait on your God continually. Ps. 22:4. Our fathers trusted in you: they trusted, and you delivered them. Compare 1 Pet. 1:13, 21; 1 Tim. 4:10.

units.la: d) Pfal.50.v.15.Inuoca me in die angustia, eripiam te. Pfal.138.v.1. Celebrabo te ex toto animo meo.
units.tr: d) Ps. 50:15. Call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver you. Ps. 138:1. I will praise you with my whole heart.

units.la: 1.Thess 5.v.17.18.Indesinenter orate.In omnibus gratias agite. Hæc enim est voluntas Dei per Iesum Christum erga vos.
units.tr: 1 Thess. 5:17–18. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.

units.la: e) Rom.10.v.10. Corde enim creditur ad iustitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem.
units.tr: e) Rom. 10:10. For with the heart man believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.

units.la: Matth.10.v.32.33. Quisquis igitur agnoscet me coram hominibus, agnoscam & ego eū coram Patre meo qui est in cœlis: Quisquis autem abnegauerit me coram hominibus, abnegabo eum & ego coram Patre meo qui est in cœlis.
units.tr: Matt. 10:32–33. Whoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father who is in heaven. But whoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father who is in heaven.

units.la: f). Leuit.19.v.12. Neq; iurate per nomen meum ad fallaciam vllam: sic profanaueris nomen Dei tui, ego sum Iehoua.
units.tr: f) Lev. 19:12. And you shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shall you profane the name of your God: I am the LORD.

units.la: Matth.5.verf.33. Non peierabis, sed reddes Domino quæ iuraueris.
units.tr: Matt. 5:33. You shall not forswear yourself, but shall perform unto the Lord your oaths.

units.la: Ierem.4.v.2. Quin iures, viuit Iehoua, in veritate, iudicio, & iustitiâ.
units.tr: Jer. 4:2. And you shall swear, The LORD lives, in truth, in judgement, and in righteousness.

units.la: g) Pfal.50.v.14. Redde excelso vota tua.
units.tr: g) Ps. 50:14. Pay your vows to the Most High.

units.la: Et116.v.13.14. Quid responderem Domino? omnia beneficia eius superant me. Poculum omnis salutis acceptum exhibebo, & nomen Domini prædicabo: vota mea Domino rependens.
units.tr: And Ps. 116:12–14. What shall I render unto the LORD for all his benefits toward me? I will take the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the LORD, rendering my vows unto the LORD.

units.la: Eccles.5.v.5. Melius est, vt non voueas, quàm vt voueas ac non persoluas.
units.tr: Eccl. 5:4. It is better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay.

units.la: h) Pfal.50. Esa.1.v.11.& seqq. 1.Cor.11.verf.20.& seqq. Iacob.1.v.vlt. Religio pura & incontaminata apud Deum & Patrem hæc est, inuisere orphanos & viduas in afflictione ipsorum, & immaculatum se seruare à mundo.
units.tr: h) Ps. 50. Isa. 1:11ff. 1 Cor. 11:20ff. Jas. 1:27. Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unspotted from the world.

units.la: 6. Circa precationem attendenda sunt hæc tria:
units.tr: 6. Three things are to be considered concerning prayer:

units.la: a) Quid nos debeat mouere ad precandum: putà sensus nostræ necessitatis, mandatum Dei,& promissio exauditionis.
units.tr: a) What ought to move us to pray: namely, a sense of our need, the command of God, and the promise of being heard.

units.la: b) Quomodo fit precandum: videl reuerenter, ardenter, demissè, fiducialiter, piè & perseueranter.
units.tr: b) How prayer is to be made: namely, reverently, fervently, humbly, confidently, piously and perseveringly.

units.la: c) Quales circumstantiæ sint obseruandæ.
units.tr: c) What circumstances are to be observed.

units.la: a) Psal.50.v.15. Inuoca me in die angustiæ: eripiam te.
units.tr: a) Ps. 50:15. Call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver you.

units.la: Iohan.16.v.23.24. Petite, & accipietis. Amen amen dico vobis, Quæcunque petieritis à Patre meo in nomine meo, dabit vobis.
units.tr: John 16:23–24. Ask, and you shall receive. Verily, verily I say unto you, whatever you shall ask of my Father in my name, he will give it you.

units.la: Matth.7.v.7. Petite, & dabitur vobis.
units.tr: Matt. 7:7. Ask, and it shall be given you.

units.la: Etc.18.v.19. Si duo ex vobis consenserint in terra, quodcunque petierint, fiet eis à Patre meo qui est in cœlis.
units.tr: Matt. 18:19. If two of you shall agree on earth as touching anything that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father who is in heaven.

units.la: b) Vide exemplum Abrahami, Gen.18. v.24. & deinceps. Danielis, cap.9.v.3. & deinceps. publicani, Luc.18.v.13. & parabolam de vidua, Luc.18.v.1. & seqq.
units.tr: b) See the example of Abraham, Gen. 18:24ff.; of Daniel, ch. 9:3ff.; of the publican, Luke 18:13; and the parable of the widow, Luke 18:1ff.

units.la: Hebr.10.v.22. Cum habeamus libertatem ingrediendi sacrium per sanguinem Iesu: accedamus cum vero corde & certa perfuasione fidei.
units.tr: Heb. 10:22. Since we have boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, let us draw near with a true heart and in full assurance of faith.

units.la: Iac.1.v.6. Postulet cum fide.
units.tr: Jas. 1:6. Let him ask in faith.

units.la: Vide infrà Artem precandi.
units.tr: See below, the Art of Praying.

units.la: c) In N.T. non sumus astricti ad certum locum publicum, 1.Tim.2.v.8. Iohan.4. Matth.14.v.23. & c.6.v.6. & priuatis precibus non est præscriptum certum tempus, publicis verò præscriptus est dies Dominicus, Act.20.v.7. 1.Corinth.16.v.2. denique gestus varij possunt adhiberi, putà elevatio manuum, 1.Reg.8.v.22. flexio genuum, Act.20.v.36: elevatio oculorum versus cœlum, Ioh.11. v.41: capitis detectio, 1.Cor.11.v.4. &c.
units.tr: c) In the New Testament we are not bound to any fixed public place: 1 Tim. 2:8; John 4; Matt. 14:23; ch. 6:6. Nor is a fixed time prescribed for private prayers, but for public prayers the Lord's Day is prescribed: Acts 20:7; 1 Cor. 16:2. Finally, various gestures may be employed, for example lifting up the hands, 1 Kings 8:22; bowing the knees, Acts 20:36; lifting the eyes towards heaven, John 11:41; uncovering the head, 1 Cor. 11:4, etc.

units.la: 7. Circa votum hæc sunt obseruanda.
units.tr: 7. Concerning vows, the following are to be observed.

units.la: a) ne aliquid voueamus quod pugnet cum verbo Dei, vel cui præstando non simus pares, vel quod non conueniat nostræ vocationi.
units.tr: a) That we do not vow anything that conflicts with the word of God, or which we are not equal to performing, or which does not suit our calling.

units.la: b) vt per votum nostrum studeamus beneficium aliquod à Deo impetrare, non verò illud habeamus pro opere meritorio.
units.tr: b) That by our vow we should seek to obtain some benefit from God, and not regard it as a meritorious work.

units.la: c) vt per votum nos astringamus ad officium faciendum.
units.tr: c) That by a vow we bind ourselves to perform a duty.

units.la: a) Act.23. v.12. recitatur impium votum quadraginta virorum, qui voverant se non esuros neque bibituros, donec trucidassent Paulum.
units.tr: a) Acts 23:12 recounts the impious vow of forty men, who had vowed that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.

units.la: 1.Cor.7.v.9. Quod si se non continent, matrimonium contrahant. bant[?]. Itaque peccant, qui vouent cœlibatum, si non habeant donum continentiæ.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 7:9. But if they cannot contain, let them marry. Therefore those sin who vow celibacy if they do not have the gift of continence.

units.la: 1.Cor.7.v.4. Neuter (coniugum) habet potestatem proprij corporis. Peccaret igitur maritus, si voueret continentiam cum vxore; & vicissim.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 7:4. Neither (of the spouses) has power over their own body. Therefore a husband would sin if he vowed continence with his wife, and vice versa.

units.la: b) Tale fuit votum Iacobi, Gen.28.v.20: Iephthe, Iud.11. v.31.33: Hannæ, 1.Sam.1.v.11: Absalomi, 2.Sam.15.v.8.
units.tr: b) Such was the vow of Jacob, Gen. 28:20; of Jephthah, Judg. 11:31, 33; of Hannah, 1 Sam. 1:11; of Absalom, 2 Sam. 15:8.

units.la: c) Tale fuit votum Dauidis de inueniendo loco pro arca fœderis, Psal.132.v.2. & deinceps.
units.tr: c) Such was the vow of David to find a place for the ark of the covenant, Ps. 132:2ff.

units.la: 8. Præcipua opera secundæ tabulæ sunt,
units.tr: 8. The principal works of the second table are:

units.la: a) Dilectio proximi sincera & constans.
units.tr: a) Sincere and constant love of neighbour.

units.la: b) Eleemosyna.
units.tr: b) Almsgiving.

units.la: c) Euitatio scandali.
units.tr: c) Avoiding offence.

units.la: d) Ædificatio proximi.
units.tr: d) Edifying one's neighbour.

units.la: e) Legitimus vsus rerum indifferentium.
units.tr: e) The lawful use of indifferent things.

units.la: a) 1.Iohan.4.v.21. Hoc præceptum habemus ab eo, vt qui diligit Deum, diligat etiam fratrem suum.
units.tr: a) 1 John 4:21. And this commandment we have from him: that he who loves God should love his brother also.

units.la: Matth.5.v.44. Diligite inimicos vestros, benedicite iis qui deuouent vos, & precamini pro iis qui vobis infesti sunt, & prosequuntur vos. Confer Luc.6.v.27.& Matth.6.v.15.16.
units.tr: Matt. 5:44. Love your enemies, bless those who curse you, pray for those who hate you and persecute you. Compare Luke 6:27 and Matt. 6:15–16.

units.la: Rom.12.v.20. Si esurit inimicus tuus, ciba eum: si sitit, da ei potum. Hoc enim si feceris, carbones ignis coacervabis in caput eius.
units.tr: Rom. 12:20. If your enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink; for in so doing you shall heap coals of fire on his head.

units.la: b) Dan.4.v.27. Peccata tua iustitia abrumpe, & iniquitates tuas gratia erga afflictos.
units.tr: b) Dan. 4:27. Break off your sins by righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the afflicted.

units.la: Vide etiam Matth.6.v.1.& seqq.& c.25.v.34.& seqq.
units.tr: See also Matt. 6:1ff.; ch. 25:34ff.

units.la: c) Matth.18.v.6.& deinceps. Quisquis offenderit aliquem exparuis istis, qui in me credunt, præstiterit ei vt suspendatur mola asinaria in collo eius, ac demergatur in profundum maris. Vae mundo ab offendiculis. Hic tamen non debemus curare, si quis nostris rectè dictis aut factis offendatur, Matth.5.v.12. Iohan.6.verf.61.
units.tr: c) Matt. 18:6ff. Whoever shall offend one of these little ones who believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea. Woe to the world because of offences. Yet here we ought not to worry if someone is offended by our words or deeds that are rightly spoken or done: Matt. 5:12; John 6:61.

units.la: 1.Cor.10.v.32. Estote sine offendiculo, & Iudæis, & Græcis, & Ecclesiæ Dei.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 10:32. Be blameless both to the Jews, and to the Greeks, and to the Church of God.

units.la: d) Rom.15.v.2. Vnusquisq; proximo indulgeat ad bonum, ad ædificationem.
units.tr: d) Rom. 15:2. Let every one of us please his neighbour for his good, to edification.

units.la: 1.Corinth.10.verf.vlt. Sicut & ego per omnia omnibus placeo, non quarens meam ipsius vtilitatem, sed multorum, vt seruentur.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 10:33. Even as I please all men in all things, not seeking my own profit, but the profit of many, that they may be saved.

units.la: e) Rom.14.v.13. & seqq. Ne amplius igitur alij alios iudicemus: sed hoc iudicate potius, ne offendiculum ponatis fratri aut scandalum. Item: Si propter escam frater tuus tristitia afficitur, non iam secundum charitatem ambulas.
units.tr: e) Rom. 14:13ff. Let us not therefore judge one another any more, but judge this rather, that no man put a stumbling block or an occasion to fall in his brother's way. Likewise: If your brother is grieved because of your food, you are no longer walking in love.

units.la: 1.Cor.10.v.23. Omnia mihi licent: sed non omnia edificant.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 10:23. All things are lawful for me, but not all things edify.

units.la: Rom.15.v.1. Debemus autem nos qui firmi sumus, imbecillitates infirmorum portare, ac non indulgere nobis ipsis.
units.tr: Rom. 15:1. We then that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to please ourselves.

units.la: LOCVS XXII.
units.tr: Locus XXII.

units.la: De Sacramentis in genere.
units.tr: On the sacraments in general.

units.la: 1. Sacramenta sunt signa foederis gratuiti.
units.tr: 1. Sacraments are signs of a free covenant.

units.la: Gen.17.v.10.11. Hoc est foedus meum inter me & vos, & semen tuum post te, quod seruabitis: vt circumcidatur vobis omnis mas. Circumcidetis igitur carnem praeputij vestri, vt sit signum foederis inter me & vos.
units.tr: Gen. 17:10-11. This is my covenant between me and you, and your seed after you, which you shall keep: every male among you shall be circumcised. And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and you.

units.la: Rom.4.v.11. Accepit Abraham signum circumcisionis.
units.tr: Rom. 4:11. And he received the sign of circumcision.

units.la: Luc.22.v.20. Hoc poculum est nouum illud testamentum (seu foedus) per meum sanguinem.
units.tr: Luke 22:20. This cup is the new testament (or covenant) in my blood.

units.la: Exod.13.v.8.9. Et annuntiabis filio tuo die illo, dicendo: Propter hoc fecit ista Iehoua mihi, cum exirem ex Ægypto: Vt sit tibi in signum ad manum tuam, & in monimentum inter oculos tuos, vt sit doctrina Iehoua in ore tuo, quia manu forti eduxit te Iehoua ex Ægypto.
units.tr: Exod. 13:8-9. And thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the LORD did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt. And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the LORD's law may be in thy mouth: for with a strong hand the LORD hath brought thee out of Egypt.

units.la: 2. Sacramenta res significatas repræsentant similitudine suâ.
units.tr: 2. Sacraments represent the things signified by their likeness.

units.la: Deut.30.v.6. Iehoua circumcidet cor tuum. Sic Roman.2. verf.29.
units.tr: Deut. 30:6. The LORD thy God will circumcise thine heart. So also Rom. 2:29.

units.la: Exod.12.verf.46. Os ne confringatis in illo, agno paschali.
units.tr: Exod. 12:46. You shall not break a bone of it, of the paschal lamb.

units.la: Hoc præfigurauit fore vt Christo crucifixo non frangerentur crura, Iohan.19.v.33.36.
units.tr: This foreshadowed that the legs of Christ crucified would not be broken, John 19:33, 36.

units.la: 1.Cor.5.v.7. Pascha nostrum pro nobis sacrificatum est, nem-pe Christus. Act.22. v.16. Baptizare & ablue peccata tua.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 5:7. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. Acts 22:16. Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins.

units.la: i.Corinth.11. v.24. Hoc meum est corpus quodpro vobis frangitur.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 11:24. This is my body, which is broken for you.

units.la: Luc.22. v.20, Hoc poculum est nouum illud testamentum per meum sanguinem, qui pro vobis effunditur.
units.tr: Luke 22:20. This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.

units.la: 3. Sacramenta sunt signa a) significantia & docentia, siue picturæ. b) obsignantia & confirmantia, siue sigilla. c) exhibentia rem significatam in legitimo vsu. d) discernentia, siue indicantia Christianos. e) memorialia. f) prædicentia resurrectionem carnis, & vitam æternam. a) Vide num.2. b) Rom.4.verf.11.Et signum accepit circumcisionis,(Abraham)sigillum iustitiæ fidei.
units.tr: 3. Sacraments are signs: (a) signifying and teaching, or pictures; (b) sealing and confirming, or seals; (c) exhibiting the thing signified in lawful use; (d) distinguishing, or indicating Christians; (e) memorials; (f) foretelling the resurrection of the flesh and eternal life. a) See no. 2. b) Rom. 4:11. And he received the sign of circumcision, the seal of the righteousness of faith (Abraham).

units.la: c) Matth.26.v.26.27.28. Accipite, comedite:Hoc est corpus meum. Item: Bibite ex eo omnes. Hoc est enim sanguis meus noui fœderis, qui pro multis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: c) Matt. 26:26-28. Take, eat: this is my body. Likewise: Drink ye all of it. For this is my blood of the new covenant, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.

units.la: d) Gen.17. v.14. Præputiatus autem mas, qui non circumciderit carnem præputij sui, vtique exscindetur homo ille è populis suis.
units.tr: d) Gen. 17:14. And the uncircumcised male, who does not circumcise the flesh of his foreskin, that soul shall be cut off from his people.

units.la: Exod.12.v.43. Nullus alienigena vescitor illo.
units.tr: Exod. 12:43. No foreigner shall eat of it.

units.la: e) Exod.13. v.8.9. Vide num.1.
units.tr: e) Exod. 13:8-9. See no. 1.

units.la: 1.Cor.11.v 24.25. Hoc facite ad mei commemorationem.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 11:24-25. Do this in remembrance of me.

units.la: f) Rom. 6. v.4. Sepulti sumus igitur cum eo per baptismum in mortem : vt sicut suscitatus est Christus ex mortuis in gloriam Patris, ita & nos nouâ vitâ incedamus.
units.tr: f) Rom. 6:4. We are buried therefore with him by baptism into death, so that as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we also should walk in newness of life.

units.la: 4. In sacramentis vniuntur res terrestris & cœlestis vi promissionis Christi vera fide apprehensæ.
units.tr: 4. In the sacraments earthly and heavenly things are united by the power of Christ's promise, apprehended by true faith.

units.la: Matth.26.v.26. Hoc est corpus meum.
units.tr: Matt. 26:26. This is my body.

units.la: Et v.28. Hoc est sanguis meus. Sic Marcii14.v.22.24. Lucæ 22.v.19.20.1.Cor.10.v.4.&6.1.Cor.11.v.24.25.
units.tr: And v. 28. This is my blood. So Mark 14:22, 24; Luke 22:19, 20; 1 Cor. 10:4, 6; 1 Cor. 11:24, 25.

units.la: 5. Phrases sacramentales sacramentaliter sunt accipiendæ.
units.tr: 5. Sacramental phrases are to be understood sacramentally.

units.la: Gen.17.v.11. Fœdus meum erit in carne vestrâ.
units.tr: Gen. 17:11. My covenant shall be in your flesh.

units.la: Exod.12.v.11. Agnus est transitus Iehoua.
units.tr: Exod. 12:11. It is the Lord's passover.

units.la: Act.22.v.16. Bapti{z}are, & ablue peccata tua.
units.tr: Acts 22:16. Be baptized, and wash away your sins.

units.la: Vide etiam num.præced.4.
units.tr: See also the preceding no. 4.

units.la: In his locutionibus nomina rerum significatarum ipsis signis attribuuntur.
units.tr: In such expressions the names of the things signified are attributed to the signs themselves.

units.la: 6. Verbum & sacramenta
units.tr: 6. The Word and the sacraments

units.la: a) conueniunt nucleo, qui est Christus.
units.tr: a) agree in the kernel, which is Christ;

units.la: b) differunt modo docendi.
units.tr: b) differ in the mode of teaching.

units.la: a) 1. Iohan.1.v.7. Sanguis Iesu Christi Filij eius purgat nos ab omni peccato.
units.tr: a) 1 John 1:7. The blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.

units.la: Matth.26.v.26. Hoc est corpus meum. Et v.28. Hoc est sanguis meus.
units.tr: Matt. 26:26. This is my body. And v. 28. This is my blood.

units.la: b) Rom.10.v.17. Fides est ex auditu, auditus autem per verbum Dei.
units.tr: b) Rom. 10:17. Faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

units.la: Etc.4.vers.11. Signum accepit circumcisionis, sigillum iusti-tiafiaei[?].
units.tr: Gen. 4:11 [for Rom. 4:11]. He received the sign of circumcision, the seal of the righteousness of faith.

units.la: 7. Verbum in sacramentis est concionale, & proinde ratione credentium est practicum seu efficax, ratione incredulorum est inefficax.
units.tr: 7. The Word in the sacraments is preached, and therefore for believers it is practical or effective, while for unbelievers it is ineffective.

units.la: 2.Rom.2.v.25.& seqq. Circumcisio quidem prodest, si legem exequaris, &c. quòd si transgressor legis fueris, circumcisio tua fa-cta est præputium, &c.
units.tr: Rom. 2:25 and following. Circumcision indeed profits, if you keep the law, etc.; but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision, etc.

units.la: 1.Petri 3.v.21. Cui rei nunc correspondens exemplar baptismi nos quoque seruat (non quo carnis sordes abijciuntur, sed stipulatio bonæ conscientiæ apud Deum) per resurrectionem Iesu Christi.
units.tr: 1 Pet. 3:21. Corresponding to this, the pattern of baptism now saves us also (not by the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but by the answer of a good conscience toward God) through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

units.la: 2.Cor.2.v.15.16. Christi bona fragrantia sumus Deo, in iis qui seruantur, & in iis qui pereunt. His quidem odor mortis ad mortem: illis vero odor vitæ ad vitam. Confer 1.Cor.10.v.5. Sed plerosque illorum non approbauit Deus: eos videlicet qui escam spiritualem non rectè verâ fide sumserunt, &c.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 2:15-16. We are to God the good fragrance of Christ, among those who are saved and among those who perish. To the one we are the smell of death unto death; to the others the smell of life unto life. Compare 1 Cor. 10:5: But God was not pleased with most of them, namely those who did not rightly eat the spiritual food with true faith, etc.

units.la: 8. In sacramenti administratione sunt distinguenda ista sex: homo exterior dispensans & accipiens sacramentum, res terrestris, & actio circa rem terrestrem; quæ tria sunt externa: tum homo interior, res cœlestis seu tota Trinitas quæ ibi est præsens, & actio interior circa rem cœlestem.
units.tr: 8. In the administration of the sacrament six things are to be distinguished: the outward man dispensing and receiving the sacrament, the earthly thing, and the action concerning the earthly thing (these three are external); then the inward man, the heavenly thing (that is, the whole Trinity, who is present there), and the inward action concerning the heavenly thing.

units.la: Jer.4.v.4. Circumcidite vos Jehouæ, & amouete præputia animi vestri.
units.tr: Jer. 4:4. Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and take away the foreskins of your heart.

units.la: Matth.3.v.11. Ego quidem baptizo vos aquâ ad resipiscentiam: u[?] vero qui pone me venit, validior me est, &c. ipse vos baptizabit Spiritu sancto & igne. Confer Marc.1.v.8.Luc.3.verf.16.Johan.1.verf.26.
units.tr: Matt. 3:11. I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance; but he who comes after me is mightier than I, etc. He shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire. Compare Mark 1:8, Luke 3:16, John 1:26.

units.la: Marci 16.verf.16. Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, seruabitur.
units.tr: Mark 16:16. He who believes and is baptized shall be saved.

units.la: Matth. 28. v. 19. Baptizantes eos in nomen Patris, Filij, & Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: Matt. 28:19. Baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Coloss.2.v.11. In Christo circumcisi estis circumcisione quæ fit sine manibus.
units.tr: Col. 2:11. In Christ you were circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands.

units.la: Vide quoque i.Petri 3.v.21. ad num. præced.7.
units.tr: See also 1 Pet. 3:21 at the preceding no. 7.

units.la: LOCVS XXIII. De sacramentis vet. Testamenti,
units.tr: LOCUS XXIII. On the sacraments of the Old Testament,

units.la: I. Sacramenta V. & N. T. conueniunt reipsâ seu fundamento, nucleo & substantiâ; differunt gradu & modo claritatis, & facilitatis, itemq; largioris atque laxioris administrationis.
units.tr: I. The sacraments of the Old and New Testaments agree in the thing itself, that is, in foundation, kernel and substance; they differ in degree and mode of clarity and ease, and likewise in the fuller and less restricted manner of administration.

units.la: Vide supra loc.16. de evangelio.
units.tr: See above, locus 16, on the gospel.

units.la: Hoc ipsum patet ex collatione circumcisionis cum baptismo, & agni paschalis cum sacrâ cœnâ.
units.tr: This very thing is evident from the comparison of circumcision with baptism, and of the paschal lamb with the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Matth.28. v.19. Docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos.
units.tr: Matth.28. v.19. Teach all nations, baptizing them.

units.la: I.Cor.10.v.2.3.4. Et omnes in Mosen baptizatos esse nube & mari: Et omnes eandem escam spiritualem edisse: Et omnes eundem potum spiritualem bibisse. Bibebant enim ex sequente spirituali petra. Petra verò illa erat Christus.
units.tr: 1 Cor.10. v.2.3.4. And all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea; and all ate the same spiritual food; and all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them. Now that rock was Christ.

units.la: I.Cor.5.v.7. Pascha nostrum, pro nobis sacrificatum est, nempe Christus.
units.tr: 1 Cor.5. v.7. Our Passover has been sacrificed for us, namely Christ.

units.la: Coloss.2.v.11.12. In Christo circumcisi estis circumcisione quæ fine manibus, corpore peccatis carnis exuto per circumcisionem Christi, consepulti cum eo per baptismum, &c.
units.tr: Col.2. v.11.12. In Christ you were circumcised with a circumcision not made by hands, your body of the flesh being stripped off through the circumcision of Christ, buried with him through baptism, etc.

units.la: 2. Circumcisio ponebat populo Dei ob oculos naturam corruptam, & simul obsignabat, ipsos fœderi gratiæ esse insitos, & proinde in Christum venturum incorporatos.
units.tr: 2. Circumcision set before the eyes of God's people their corrupt nature, and at the same time sealed that they were engrafted into the covenant of grace and therefore incorporated in view of the Christ who was to come.

units.la: Gen.17.v.10.11. Hoc est fœdus inter me & vos, &c,
units.tr: Gen.17. v.10.11. This is the covenant between me and you, etc.

units.la: Vide loc.præced.num.1.
units.tr: See the preceding locus, number 1.

units.la: De interrupto & redintegrato circumcisionis usu vide lof.5.
units.tr: On the interrupted and restored use of circumcision, see locus 5.

units.la: Rom.4.v.11. Et signum circumcisionis accepit, sigillum iustitiæ fidei.
units.tr: Rom.4. v.11. And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of faith.

units.la: 3. Circumcisio externa, quæ erat signum communionis externæ, hypocritis etiam administrabatur: sed eadem coniuncta cum interna circumcisione cordis solis electis fuit propria.
units.tr: 3. External circumcision, which was a sign of external communion, was administered even to hypocrites; but the same, joined with the internal circumcision of the heart, belonged to the elect alone.

units.la: Rom.2.v.25. & deinceps usque ad finem: ubi, v.28.29[?]. apostolus ait: Nec ea, quæ est in propatulo circumcisio, id est, in carne, circumcisio est. Sed circumcisio cordis, id est, in Spiritu, non in litera.
units.tr: Rom.2. v.25 and following to the end, where at v.28.29[?] the apostle says: Nor is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh circumcision. But circumcision is of the heart, in the Spirit, not in the letter.

units.la: 4. Pascha populo Dei redigebat in memoriam liberationem ex Ægypto, & obsignabat spiritualem liberationem per sanguinem Christi.
units.tr: 4. The Passover reminded God's people of their liberation from Egypt, and sealed a spiritual liberation through the blood of Christ.

units.la: Exod.12.&13. collato cum 1.Cor.5.v.7.
units.tr: Exod.12.&13. compared with 1 Cor.5. v.7.

units.la: Sub liberatione ex Ægypto intelligere oportet conservationem a cæde primogenitorum, Exodi 12. verf.27. Victima paschatis est Domino, qui transiit præter domos filiorum Israëlis in Ægypto, cum caderet Ægyptios, familias nostras eripuit.
units.tr: By liberation from Egypt one must understand preservation from the slaughter of the firstborn, Exodus 12, verse 27: "It is the sacrifice of the Passover to the Lord, who passed over the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt, when he struck the Egyptians and saved our households."

units.la: Vide infra in Chronologia de quinque Paschatis, quæ Christus celebrauit, & supra in Computo de illa quæstione num Christus, iam iam adituru magnam & solennem suam passionem, anticipauerit Pascha.
units.tr: See below in the Chronology concerning the five Passovers which Christ celebrated, and above in the Computation on the question whether Christ, about to undergo his great and solemn passion, anticipated the Passover.

units.la: LOCUS XXIV. De baptismo.
units.tr: LOCUS XXIV. On baptism.

units.la: 1. Baptizandi sunt, tum adulti qui recens ad fidem Christianam conuersi sunt, tum infantes è Christianis parentibus nati.
units.tr: 1. Both adults who have recently been converted to the Christian faith and infants born of Christian parents are to be baptized.

units.la: Matth.28.v.19. Profecti docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomen Patris, & Filij, & Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: Matth. 28:19. Go therefore and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Hic obseruandum est in Graeco esse μαθητεύσατε[?], id est, discipulos facite. quasi dicat, discipulos factos baptizate, hoc est, congregatos in ecclesiam baptizate. Tales vero etiam sunt liberi Christianorum.
units.tr: Here it must be observed that the Greek is μαθητεύσατε [make disciples]. It is as if he said: baptize those who have been made disciples, that is, those gathered into the Church. Such indeed are the children of Christians.

units.la: Act.16.v.33. à Paulo & Silâ baptizatus est commentariensis Philippensis, & omnes domestici eius. Ibid. v.15. baptizata est Lydia & domus eius. Proinde & paruuli.
units.tr: Acts 16:33. The jailer of Philippi and all his household were baptized by Paul and Silas. Ibid. v. 15. Lydia and her household were baptized. Therefore infants too.

units.la: Coloff.2.v.11.12. Baptismus circumcisioni successit. At vero liberi Iudæorum sunt circumcisi octauo die, Genef. 17.v.12. Itaque & Christianorum liberi recens nati sunt baptizandi: quia non sunt deteriori conditione, quàm infantes in V.T.
units.tr: Col. 2:11, 12. Baptism succeeded circumcision. But the children of the Jews were circumcised on the eighth day, Gen. 17:12. Therefore the newly born children of Christians are also to be baptized, because they are not in a worse condition than the infants of the Old Testament.

units.la: I.Cor.7.v.14. Liberi vestri sancti sunt: quia scilicet comprehensi sunt in fœdere, de quo Gen.17.v.10. Hoc est fœdus meum inter me & vos, & semen tuum post te, quod seruabitis, &c.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 7:14. Your children are holy: clearly because they are included in the covenant concerning which Gen. 17:10 says: This is my covenant between me and you, and your seed after you, which you shall keep, etc.

units.la: Confer Matt.19.v.14.15. Iesus autem ait, Omittite istos pueros, & ne prohibete eos ad me venire. Talium est enim regnum cœlorum. Et cùm imposuisset eis manus, profectus est illinc. Sic Marc.10.v.13.& seqq. vbi v.16. dicitur: Et impositis manibus benedixit eis.
units.tr: Compare Matt. 19:14, 15: But Jesus said, Suffer the little children, and forbid them not to come unto me, for of such is the kingdom of heaven. And when he had laid his hands on them, he departed thence. So too Mark 10:13 and following, where at v. 16 it is said: And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them.

units.la: Act.2.v.38.39. Petrus autem dixit ad eos, Resipiscite, & baptizetur vnusquisque vestrùm in nomen Iesu Christi in remissionem peccatorum: & accipietis donum Spiritus sancti. Vobis enim facta est promissio, & liberis vestris, & omnibus longè post futuris, quoscunque videl. aduocauerit Dominus Deus noster.
units.tr: Acts 2:38, 39. Then Peter said to them, Repent, and let every one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is to you, and to your children, and to all who are afar off, whomsoever the Lord our God shall call.

units.la: 2. Administratio baptismi cohæret cum prædicatione verbi.
units.tr: 2. The administration of baptism is bound up with the preaching of the Word.

units.la: Matth. 28. verf. 19. Profecti docete omnes gentes, baptizan-tes eos.
units.tr: Matth. 28, v. 19. Go and teach all nations, baptizing them.

units.la: Itaque quia mulieri non licet docere, 1.Cor.14. verf.34. 1.Tim.2.v.12. neq; etiam licet baptizare.
units.tr: Therefore, since a woman is not permitted to teach (1 Cor. 14:34; 1 Tim. 2:12), neither is she permitted to baptize.

units.la: 3. Ritus baptizandi, qui fit per immersionem in aquam, significantius exprimit mortificationem veteris hominis, quàm ritus aspersionis.
units.tr: 3. The rite of baptism, which is performed by immersion in water, expresses more meaningfully the mortification of the old man than the rite of sprinkling does.

units.la: Rom.6.v.3.4. An ignoratis, nos quotquot baptizati sumus in Christum Iesum, in mortem eius esse baptizatos. Sepulti igitur sumus cum eo per baptismum in mortem,&c.
units.tr: Rom. 6:3, 4. Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death, etc.

units.la: Matth.3.v.16. Et baptizatus Iesus ascendit ex aqua.
units.tr: Matth. 3:16. And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water.

units.la: Act.8.v.38. Descenderunt ambo in illam aquam, Philippus simul & eunuchus: & ille baptizavit eum.
units.tr: Acts 8:38. They both went down into the water, Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.

units.la: 4. Per baptismum
units.tr: 4. Through baptism

units.la: a) omnes qui baptizantur, profitentur se esse Christianos.
units.tr: a) all who are baptized profess that they are Christians.

units.la: electi & credentes confirmantur
units.tr: the elect and believers are confirmed

units.la: b) in fide remissionis peccatorum.
units.tr: b) in faith in the remission of sins.

units.la: c) in fide & spe renouationis naturae nostrae.
units.tr: c) in faith and hope of the renewal of our nature.

units.la: d) in fide & spe vnionis cum Christo.
units.tr: d) in faith and hope of union with Christ.

units.la: a) Matth.28.verf.19. baptizari in nomen Patris,Filij, & Spiritus sancti, est per baptismum consecrari Deo.
units.tr: a) Matth. 28:19. To be baptized in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit is, through baptism, to be consecrated to God.

units.la: b) Act.2.v.38. Baptizetur vnusquisque vestrūm in nomen lesu Christi, in remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: b) Acts 2:38. Let every one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins.

units.la: c) Rom.6.v.3. & deinceps. Vide num.3.
units.tr: c) Rom. 6:3 and following. See no. 3.

units.la: Tit.3.v.5. Ex sua misericordia salvavit nos per lavacrum regenerationis & renovationis Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: Titus 3:5. According to his mercy he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: d) 1.Cor.12.v.13. Per unum spiritum nos omnes in unum corpus baptizati sumus.
units.tr: d) 1 Cor. 12:13. By one Spirit we were all baptized into one body.

units.la: 5. Baptismus integer constat actione corporali & spirituali, seu externa & interna.
units.tr: 5. Baptism as a whole consists of a bodily and a spiritual action, that is, of an external and an internal one.

units.la: Matt.3. v.11. Ego quidem baptizo vos aquâ ad resipiscentiam: is verò qui post me venit, validior me est, &c. ipse vos baptizabit Spiritu sancto & igne. Vide loc.22. num.8. & confer 1.Petri 3.verf.21.
units.tr: Matt. 3:11. I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance, but he who comes after me is mightier than I, etc. He shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire. See Loc. 22, no. 8, and compare 1 Pet. 3:21.

units.la: LOCUS XXV.
units.tr: LOCUS XXV.

units.la: De cœna Domini.
units.tr: On the Lord's Supper.

units.la: 1. Ad sacram cœnam nemo admittendus est nisi baptizatus & maturæ ætatis.
units.tr: 1. No one is to be admitted to the holy supper unless he is baptized and of mature age.

units.la: Exod.12. v. 48. non nisi circumcisi admittebantur ad agnum paschalem; in cuius locum successit cœna Domini.
units.tr: Exod. 12. 48. Only the circumcised were admitted to the paschal lamb, and the Lord's Supper has taken its place.

units.la: Matth.26. v.26. Edentibus autem eis (discipulis Christi) Iesus cum accepisset panem, &c.
units.tr: Matt. 26. 26. While they (the disciples of Christ) were eating, Jesus took bread, etc.

units.la: 2. Optima cœnæ administratio est, quæ cum institutione Christi per omnia convenit.
units.tr: 2. The best administration of the supper is the one that agrees in every respect with the institution of Christ.

units.la: Prout videl. illa describitur à tribus euangelistis, & apostolo Paulo. Matth.26. Marc.14. Luc.22.1. Cor.11.
units.tr: That is, as the institution is described by the three evangelists and by the apostle Paul. Matt. 26; Mark 14; Luke 22; 1 Cor. 11.

units.la: 3. Sacra cœna est administranda in conventu fidelium, eoq; ferme ordinario.
units.tr: 3. The holy supper is to be administered in the assembly of the faithful, and that ordinarily.

units.la: 1.Cor.11. v.20. Cum convenitis in unum, hoc non est Dominicam cœnam edere.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 11. 20. When you come together in one place, it is not to eat the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Act.20. v.7. Primo autem die hebdomadis, congregatis discipulis ad frangendum panem (id est, ad celebrandum cœnam Domini) Paulus differebat.
units.tr: Acts 20. 7. On the first day of the week, when the disciples had gathered to break bread (that is, to celebrate the Lord's Supper), Paul spoke at length.

units.la: 4. Panis sacræ cœnæ est corpus Christi, itemque vinum est sanguis Christi, sacramentaliter.
units.tr: 4. The bread of the holy supper is, sacramentally, the body of Christ, and likewise the wine is, sacramentally, the blood of Christ.

units.la: Vide supra loc.22. num.3.4.5. Idem iudicium est de illa phrasi, 1.Cor.10.v.16. Poculum benedictionis, cui benedicimus, nonne communio sanguinis Christi est? Panis quem frangimus, nonne communio corporis Christi est?
units.tr: See above, loc. 22, nn. 3, 4, 5. The same judgment applies to that phrase, 1 Cor. 10. 16: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?

units.la: 5. Sacra cœna est instituta
units.tr: 5. The holy supper was instituted

units.la: a) principaliter, ut commemoremus mortem Christi, idq; ex vera fide, adeoque communionem habeamus cum Christo & omnibus eius beneficiis morte ipsius partis.
units.tr: a) principally, that we might remember the death of Christ, and do so from true faith, and so have communion with Christ and all his benefits through his death.

units.la: b) secundario, ut nos ipsos Deo immolemus, & ad mutuam charitatem obligemus.
units.tr: b) secondarily, that we might offer ourselves to God and bind ourselves to mutual love.

units.la: a) 1.Corinth.11.v.24.25.26. Hoc facite ad mei recordationem,&c. Quotiescunq; enim ederitis panem hunc, & poculum hoc biberitis, mortem Domini annunciate,donec veniat. Annuntiatio ista non est nuda & historica, sed practica & coniunćta cum vera fide,quâ sola edimus carnem Christi,& bibimus sanguinem ipsius, Iohan. 6. verf.29. 35. 50. 53. 54. 55. 56. 63.
units.tr: a) 1 Cor. 11. 24, 25, 26. Do this in remembrance of me, etc. For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes. That proclamation is not bare and historical but practical and joined with true faith, by which alone we eat the flesh of Christ and drink his blood. John 6. 29, 35, 50, 53, 54, 55, 56, 63.

units.la: b) 1.Cor.5. verf.7 8. Pascha nostrum pro nobis sacrificatum est,nempe Christus. Itaq; festum agitemus, non fermento veteri,nec fermento malitiæ & nequitiæ, sed nonfermentatis panibus sinceritatis & veritatis.
units.tr: b) 1 Cor. 5. 7, 8. Our passover has been sacrificed for us, namely Christ. So let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

units.la: 1. Cor.10.v.17. Quoniam vnus est panis, vnum corpus nos illi multi fumus:nam omnes ex vno illo pane participamus.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 10. 17. Since there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of that one bread.

units.la: 6. Ad sacram cœnam nemo debet accedere,nisi qui recte fe præparauit.
units.tr: 6. No one ought to approach the holy supper unless he has prepared himself properly.

units.la: 1.Cor.11.v.28.& seqq. Probet quisque seipsum, & ita depane illo edat, & de poculo illo bibat. Nam qui edit & bibit indigne, damnationem sibi ipsi edit & bibit, non discernens corpus Domini.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 11. 28 ff. Let each one examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread and drink of that cup. For whoever eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgment on himself, not discerning the body of the Lord.

units.la: LOCVS XXVI.
units.tr: Topic XXVI.

units.la: De vltimo Christi aduentu.
units.tr: On the last coming of Christ.

units.la: 1. Christus è cœlo redibit ad iudicium, idq; subito, inopinato, & magnâ cum gloriâ.
units.tr: 1. Christ will return from heaven to judgment, and that suddenly, unexpectedly, and with great glory.

units.la: Matth.24.v.37. Sicut erant dies Noë, ita erit & aduentus filij hominis.
units.tr: Matt. 24.37. As the days of Noah were, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.

units.la: Et verf. 24. Vigilate ergo. nescitis enim, quâ horâ Dominus venturus sit.
units.tr: And v. 24. Watch therefore, for you know not at what hour the Lord will come.

units.la: 2.Petri 3.v.10. Veniet sicut fur in nocte dies ille Domini.
units.tr: 2 Pet. 3.10. The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night.

units.la: Confer Matth.24.v.43.&Luc.21.v.35.
units.tr: Compare Matt. 24.43 and Luke 21.35.

units.la: Matth.25.v.31. Cùm venerit filius hominis cum gloriâ suâ, & omnes sancti angeli cum eo, tunc sedebit in throno gloriæ suæ.
units.tr: Matt. 25.31. When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.

units.la: 1.Theff.4. v.16. Ipse Dominus cum hortationis clamore, cum voce archangeli, & cum Dei tuba descendet è cœlo.
units.tr: 1 Thess. 4.16. The Lord himself will descend from heaven with a shout of command, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet of God.

units.la: 1.Tim.6. v.14. Vsque ad illustrem illum aduentum Domini nostri Iesu Christi.
units.tr: 1 Tim. 6.14. Until the glorious appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Tit.2.v.13. Expectantes beatam illam spem, & illustrem illum aduentum gloriæ magni illius Dei ac seruatoris nostri Iesu Christi.
units.tr: Titus 2.13. Looking for that blessed hope and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ.

units.la: 2.Petri 3. v.10. Quo (scilicet die Dominus veniet) cœli cum stridore præteribunt, elementa vero æstuantia soluentur, terraq₃[?], & quæ in eâ sunt opera, exurentur.
units.tr: 2 Pet. 3.10. On that day (namely the day on which the Lord will come) the heavens will pass away with a roar, the elements will be dissolved by fire, and the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up.

units.la: Iud.v.14. Ecce venit Dominus cum sanctis millibus suis, ut ferat iudicium aduersus omnes.
units.tr: Jude 14. Behold, the Lord comes with ten thousands of his saints, to execute judgment upon all.

units.la: 2. Christus veniet ad iudicium, cùm impleta fuerint omnia vaticinia, è quibus tria restant
units.tr: 2. Christ will come to judgment when all the prophecies have been fulfilled, of which three remain:

units.la: a) prædicatio euangelij successiua per totum terrarum orbem.
units.tr: a) the successive preaching of the gospel throughout the whole world.

units.la: b) conuersio Iudæorum.
units.tr: b) the conversion of the Jews.

units.la: c) regnum Christi per mille annos in his terris.
units.tr: c) the reign of Christ for a thousand years on this earth.

units.la: a) Matth.24. v.14. Et prædicabitur istud euangelium regni in toto terrarum orbe, ut sit testimonio omnibus gentibus: & tunc veniet finis.
units.tr: a) Matt. 24.14. And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in the whole world, as a testimony to all nations; and then the end will come.

units.la: b) Rom.11. v.25. & seqq. Nolim enim vos ignorare, fratres, mysterium hoc, &c. obduratione ex parte Israeli obuenisse, tantisper dum plenitudo gentium introierit. Et ita totus Israel seruabitur: sicut scriptum est, Veniet ex Sion ille liberator, & auertet impietates Iacob. Et hoc illis à me fœdus, cùm abstulero peccata ipsorum.
units.tr: b) Rom. 11.25 and following. For I would not have you ignorant, brethren, of this mystery, that a hardening in part has come upon Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in. And so all Israel will be saved, as it is written: The Deliverer will come out of Zion, and will turn away ungodliness from Jacob. And this is my covenant with them, when I take away their sins.

units.la: Hos.3. vers.4.5. Nam diebus multis desidebunt Israelitæ, nullo rege, nullo⁊q; principe, & nullo sacrificio, ac nulla statua, nullo denique amiculo, aut imaginibus. Postea reuersi Israelitæ quærent Iehouam Deum suum, & Dauidem regem suum; & pauidi accedent ad Iehouam, & ad bonitatem eius, vltimis temporibus.
units.tr: Hos. 3.4-5. For many days the Israelites will sit without king, without prince, without sacrifice, without pillar, and without ephod or images. Afterwards the Israelites will return and seek Jehovah their God and David their king; and they will come trembling to Jehovah and to his goodness in the latter times.

units.la: c) Apoc.20.v.2. Qui (angelus) apprehendit draconem, serpentem illum antiquum, qui est diabolus & Satanas, & vinxit eum ad annos mille, &c. Vide totum caput.
units.tr: c) Rev. 20.2. He (the angel) laid hold of the dragon, that old serpent, who is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years, etc. See the whole chapter.

units.la: LOCVS XXVII. De resurrectione carnis.
units.tr: LOCUS XXVII. On the resurrection of the flesh.

units.la: 1. Sub vltimum Christi aduentum
units.tr: 1. Near the last coming of Christ:

units.la: a) omnes mortui resurgent. b) vivi demutabuntur in statum immortalem.
units.tr: a) all the dead will rise again; b) the living will be changed into an immortal state.

units.la: a) Dan.12.v.2.Tandem multi ex dormientibus in puluerulentâ terrâ expergiscentur.
units.tr: a) Dan. 12. v. 2. At last many of those who sleep in the dusty earth will awake.

units.la: Ioh.5. v. 28. Veniet hora, quâ omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem Filij Dei; & prodibunt.
units.tr: John 5. v. 28. The hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear the voice of the Son of God, and they will come forth.

units.la: Apoc.20.v.12.13. Vidi mortuos, magnos & pusillos, stantes in conspectu Dei. Et reddidit mare mortuos quos habebat. Mors quoq; & sepulchrum reddiderunt mortuos quos habebant.
units.tr: Rev. 20. v. 12, 13. I saw the dead, great and small, standing before God. And the sea gave up the dead which it held. Death also and the grave gave up the dead which they held.

units.la: b) 1.Cor.15.v.51. Ecce mysterium vobis dico: Non omnes quidem obdormiemus, sed omnes mutabimur, momento & iactu oculi ad ultimam tubam.
units.tr: b) 1 Cor. 15. v. 51. Behold, I tell you a mystery: we shall not indeed all sleep, but we shall all be changed, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet.

units.la: 1.Thess.4.v.15.& seqq. Hoc vobis dicimus verbis Domini, fore, ut nos vivi, qui reliqui erimus in aduentu Domini, non praeueniamus eos, qui obdormierint. Nam ipse Dominus cum hortatione clamore, cum voce archangeli, & cum Dei tubâ descendet è cœlo: & qui mortui fuerint in Christo, resurgent primùm: deinde nos vivi, qui reliqui erimus, rapiemur simul cum eis in nubes, in occursum Domini in aëra.
units.tr: 1 Thess. 4. v. 15 and following. We tell you this by the word of the Lord, that we who are alive and remain until the coming of the Lord will not precede those who have fallen asleep. For the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God; and the dead in Christ will rise first. Then we who are alive and remain will be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air.

units.la: 2. Idem numero corpus, quod hic gestamus, re-surget.
units.tr: 2. The same body that we now bear will rise again in number.

units.la: Iob.19.v.26.25. Et postquam vermes confoderint istud, euigilante me, tum carne meâ me visurum esse Deum, noui. Idem qui sum, ac non alienus visurus sum mihi, & oculi mei aspicient.
units.tr: Job 19. v. 26, 25. And after worms have consumed this, I know that in my flesh I shall see God when I awake. I myself, and not another, shall see him, and my eyes will behold him.

units.la: 1.Cor.15.v.42.43. Seritur corpus corruptioni obnoxium, suscitatur cum incorrupti naturâ: Seritur fœdum, suscitatur cum decore: seritur omnium virium expers, suscitatur potens: seritur corpus animale, suscitatur corpus spirituale.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 15. v. 42, 43. The body is sown subject to corruption; it is raised in incorruption. It is sown in dishonour; it is raised in glory. It is sown without strength; it is raised in power. It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body.

units.la: 3. Alij ad vitam æternam, alij ad mortem æternam resurgent.
units.tr: 3. Some will rise to eternal life, others to eternal death.

units.la: Dan.12. v.2. Tandem multi ex dormientibus in puluerulentâ terrâ expergiscentur; hi ad vitam æternam, illi ad opprobria & contemtum æternum.
units.tr: Dan. 12. v. 2. At last many of those who sleep in the dusty earth will awake: some to eternal life, others to everlasting shame and contempt.

units.la: Iohan.5.vers.28. Veniet hora, quâ omnes qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem Filij Dei: & prodibunt qui bona fecerunt, in resurrectionem vitæ: qui verò mala egerunt, in resurrectionem con- damnationis[?].
units.tr: John 5. v. 28. The hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear the voice of the Son of God, and they will come forth: those who have done good, to the resurrection of life; but those who have done evil, to the resurrection of condemnation.

units.la: Huc pertinet, quod Christus Iohan.6.verf.39.40.44.& 54. promittit, se electos & credentes suscitaturum ultimo die.
units.tr: To this belongs what Christ promises in John 6. v. 39, 40, 44 and 54: that he will raise up the elect and believers on the last day.

units.la: LOCUS XXVIII. De ultimo judicio.
units.tr: LOCUS XXVIII. On the Last Judgment.

units.la: 1. Christus in forma aspectabili exercebit hoc judicium erga omnes in universum homines.
units.tr: 1. Christ will exercise this judgment in visible form over all men in general.

units.la: Iohan.5.v.22. Nec enim Pater iudicat quenquam, sed omne iudicium dedit Filio.
units.tr: John 5:22. For the Father judges no one, but has committed all judgment to the Son.

units.la: Act.10.v.42. Praecepit autem nobis ut praedicemus populo, & cum testificatione denuntiemus, eum (Iesum Christum) esse qui definitus sit a Deo, iudex vivorum ac mortuorum.
units.tr: Acts 10:42. And he commanded us to preach to the people and solemnly declare that this (Jesus Christ) is the one appointed by God to be judge of the living and the dead.

units.la: Et c.17.v.31. Eo quod statuit diem, quo juste judicaturus est orbem terrarum, per eum virum, quem definit.
units.tr: And Acts 17:31. Because he has appointed a day on which he will judge the world in righteousness, by that man whom he has appointed.

units.la: Apocal.1.v.7. Ecce, venit cum nubibus, & videbit eum omnis oculus, etiam qui eum transfixerunt: & plangent coram eo omnes tribus terrae: etiam, Amen.
units.tr: Rev. 1:7. Behold, he comes with the clouds, and every eye will see him, even those who pierced him; and all the tribes of the earth will mourn over him. Even so, Amen.

units.la: Matth.25.v.32. Congregabunt (angeli) coram eo (Christo) omnes gentes, & separabit eos, alteros ab alteris, ut pastor separat oves ab hœdis.
units.tr: Matt. 25:32. (The angels) will gather before him (Christ) all the nations, and he will separate them one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.

units.la: Rom.14.v.11. Omnes enim sistemur apud tribunal Christi.
units.tr: Rom. 14:11. For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.

units.la: 1.Cor.5.v.10. Omnes nos manifestos fieri oportet coram tribunali Christi, ut unusquisq; reportet, quae in corpore fecerit, congruenter ad id, quod fecerit, sive bonum, sive malum.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 5:10. We must all be made manifest before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may receive what he has done in the body, whether good or evil, in accordance with what he has done.

units.la: Porro sancti homines approbabunt hoc judicium, Matth.19.v.28. 1.Cor.6.v.2.
units.tr: Moreover, holy men will approve this judgment: Matt. 19:28; 1 Cor. 6:2.

units.la: 2. In ultimo judicio tria ista fient,
units.tr: 2. In the last judgment these three things will take place:

units.la: a) omnium hominum convocatorum opera manifestabuntur.
units.tr: a) the works of all men who have been called together will be made manifest.

units.la: b) sententia feretur, absolvendo electos, & condemnando reprobos.
units.tr: b) sentence will be pronounced, acquitting the elect and condemning the reprobate.

units.la: c) sententia dicta quantocyus implebitur, seu executioni mandabitur, ita ut electi evehantur in cœlum, & reprobi detrudantur in infernum.
units.tr: c) the sentence once pronounced will be carried out at once, or put into execution, so that the elect are raised up into heaven and the reprobate are thrust down into hell.

units.la: a) Rom.2.v.12.16. Quicunque enim sine lege peccauerunt, sine lege quoq; peribunt; & quicunq; in lege peccauerunt, per legem damnabuntur, in die, quo iudicabit Dominus de rebus occultis hominum.
units.tr: a) Rom. 2:12, 16. For all who have sinned without law will also perish without law; and all who have sinned under law will be judged by law, on the day when God will judge the secrets of men.

units.la: Matth.12.v.36. Quodcunque verbum otiosum locuti fuerint homines, de eo reddent rationem in die iudicij. Vide quoque loc. seq.num.1. & Rom.2.v.6.7.
units.tr: Matt. 12:36. For every idle word that men speak, they will give an account of it on the day of judgment. See also the following topic, section 1, and Rom. 2:6–7.

units.la: 1.Cor.5.v.10. Vide num.praeced.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 5:10. See the preceding section.

units.la: Matth.25.v.35.36.42.43. Esuriui enim, & dedisti mihi quo vescerer, &c. Esuriui enim, & non dedisti mihi quo vescerer, &c. Vide etiam lit.seq.Iud.v.15.
units.tr: Matt. 25:35–36, 42–43. For I was hungry, and you gave me something to eat, etc. For I was hungry, and you gave me nothing to eat, etc. See also the following letter; Jude 15.

units.la: b) Matth.25.verf.34. Tunc dicet rex iis qui ad dextram ipsius erunt, Adeste benedicti Patris mei, possidete regnum paratum vobis a iacto mundi fundamento.
units.tr: b) Matt. 25:34. Then the king will say to those on his right hand, Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

units.la: Et v.41. Exsecrati, abite a me in ignem aeternum, qui paratus est diabolo & angelis eius.
units.tr: And v. 41. Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

units.la: Et c.7.v.23. Tunc autem profitebor eis, Certe nunquam noui vos. Discedite a me, qui operam datis transgressioni legis. Confer Luc.13.verf.27.
units.tr: And Matt. 7:23. And then I will declare to them, I never knew you; depart from me, you who work lawlessness. Compare Luke 13:27.

units.la: Iud. v.15. Feret iudicium aduersus omnes, & redarguet, quicunque ex ipsis sunt impij, de factis omnibus, quae impie patrarint, deq; omnibus duris, quae locuti fuerint aduersus ipsum peccatores impij.
units.tr: Jude 15. He will execute judgment upon all, and will convict all the ungodly of all the deeds of ungodliness that they have done, and of all the harsh things that ungodly sinners have spoken against him.

units.la: c) Matth.25.v.vlt. Et abibunt isti ad supplicium aeternum, iusti vero ad vitam aeternam.
units.tr: c) Matt. 25:46 (last verse). And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.

units.la: 3. In vltimo iudicij die Deus creabit cœlum nouum, & terram nouam.
units.tr: 3. On the last day of judgment God will create a new heaven and a new earth.

units.la: 2.Petri 3.v.13. & seqq. Cœlos nouos & terram nouam expectamus, in quibus iustitia inhabitat. Quapropter dilecti, cum haec expectetis, studete vt incontaminati & inculpati ab eo inueniamini cum pace; Domini nostri tarditatem ad vitam[?], salutem ducite.
units.tr: 2 Pet. 3:13 and following. But according to his promise we look for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells. Therefore, beloved, since you look for these things, be diligent to be found by him in peace, without spot and blameless; and count the patience of our Lord as salvation.

units.la: Et v.10. Veniet autem sicut fur in nocte dies ille Domini, quo cœli cum stridore praeteribunt, elementa vero astuantia soluentur, & terraq; & quae in ea sunt opera exurentur.
units.tr: And v. 10. But the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a roar, and the elements will be destroyed by fire, and the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up.

units.la: Rom. 8. v. 19. & seqq. Creatura quasi exserto capite observans, expectat revelationem filiorum Dei. Nam vanitati creatura est subiecta: non sua sponte, sed propter eum, qui subiecit eam isti vanitati: sub spe, quòd & ipsa creatura liberabitur ex seruitute corruptionis in libertatem gratiæ filiorum Dei. Scimus enim, omnem creaturam vnà suspirare & vnà parturire ad hoc vsq; tempus.
units.tr: Rom. 8:19 and following. The creation waits with eager longing for the revealing of the sons of God.
