For thus saith the LORD: after seventy years are accomplished at Babylon, I will visit you and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place. From these words it may be gathered that the Babylonian captivity must be dated from the deportation of Jechoniah, which fell in the year of the world 3350. Therefore there are 418 years from the foundation of the temple until the beginning of the Babylonian captivity. If you prefer, extend this interval to the destruction of the temple, which fell in the year 3360. In this way the interval is increased by ten years, so that it becomes 428 years.

units.la: Sextum interuallum est à captiuitate Babylonicâ, vsq; ad initium septimanarum Danielis, quæ incipiunt anno M. 3527. Itaque hoc interuallum est annorum 177. Si malis, duc hoc interuallum ab excidio templi vsq; ad ipsius instaurationem anno M.3531. Cæterum interuallum hoc ita probatur. Captiuitas Babylonica duravit annos 70. Proinde soluta est anno M.3419. definente, seu 3420. ineunte, anno primo Cyri. Esdr.1.v.1. Intelligeprimū ipsius annum per totam Asiam. Deinceps variè impedita fuit instauratio politiæ Iudaicæ, adeoque vrbis & templi, vsq; ad Darium Nothum, & quidem vsq; ad secundum ipsius annum, vt est Esdr.4.v.24. quo anno templum cœptum est ædificari, & absolutum anno eius sexto. Esdr.6.v.15. Concurrit autem annus Darij Nothi secundus cum anno M. 3527, sextus cum anno M. 3532.
units.tr: Sextum interuallum is from the Babylonian captivity until the beginning of Daniel's weeks, which begin in the year 3527. Therefore this interval is 177 years. If you prefer, reckon this interval from the destruction of the temple to its restoration in the year 3531. Moreover, this interval is proved as follows. The Babylonian captivity lasted seventy years. Accordingly it ended in the year 3419, or, at its beginning, in 3420, the first year of Cyrus. Esdr.1.v.1. The first year of it is to be understood throughout all Asia. Afterwards the restoration of the Jewish polity, and so of the city and temple, was variously hindered until Darius Nothus, and indeed until his second year, as is Esdr.4.v.24. In that year the temple was begun to be built, and completed in its sixth year. Esdr.6.v.15. Now the second year of Darius Nothus coincides with the year 3527, and his sixth year with the year 3532.

units.la: Septimum interuallum est annorum 490, ab inchoatâ instauratione templi ad excidium eiusdem per Romanos, anno M.4017.exeunte, seu 4018.ineunte,qui est annus Christi 69. Vide Dan.9.v.24. & seqq. vbi 70. septimanæ efficiunt annos 490.
units.tr: Septimum interuallum is 490 years, from the beginning of the restoration of the temple to its destruction by the Romans, at the end of the year 4017, or the beginning of 4018, which is the year of Christ 69. See Dan.9.v.24. & seqq. where the seventy weeks make 490 years.

units.la: Octauum interuallum est annorum 1290, ab excidio templi, siue ab anno Christi 69, vsque ad annum Christi 1359. Hoc interuallum exprimitur Dan.12.v.11. A tempore autem, quo ablatus fuerit iugis cultus, & posita abominatio desolans, dies erunt mille ducenti nonaginta. Hic intelligitur desolatio facta per Romanos, & dies sunt prophetici, qui constituunt totidem annos.
units.tr: Octauum interuallum is 1290 years, from the destruction of the temple, that is, from the year of Christ 69, until the year of Christ 1359. This interval is expressed in Dan.12.v.11. And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. Here the desolation made by the Romans is meant, and the days are prophetic, each standing for a year.

units.la: Nonum interuallum est annorum 335, ab anno Christi 1359 vsque ad an. 1694. Quod ita patet. Danielis 12.v.11. ita legimus: Beatus, qui praestolabitur & perueniet ad dies mille trecentos triginta quinque. Hi dies rursus sunt prophetici, & proinde totidem anni, quos si adieceris ad priorem summam praecedentis versus & interualli, habebis annos 2694. qui est terminus a Daniele praedictus. Ab hac summa subduc annos 1000, de quibus Apoc.20.verf.2: & relinquetur annus Christi 1694.
units.tr: Nonum interuallum is 335 years, from the year of Christ 1359 until the year 1694. This is evident as follows. We read in Daniel 12.11: Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and thirty-five days. These days again are prophetic, and therefore equal years. If you add them to the former sum of the preceding verse and interval, you will have the years 2694, which is the end foretold by Daniel. Subtract from this sum 1000 years, concerning which Apoc.20.verf.2: & relinquetur the year of Christ 1694 remains.

units.la: Decimum interuallum est 1000. annorum, inde ab anno Christi 1694 vsque ad bellum Gog & Magog, quo consecto erit finis seculi. Apoc.20.v.2. Qui (angelus è coelo descendens) apprehendit draconem, serpentem illum antiquum, qui est diabolus & Satanas, & vinxit eum ad mille annos. Ibid. verf.7.8. Cum vero expleti fuerint mille anni, soluetur Satanas è carcere suo: & exibit, vt seducat gentes, quæ sunt in quatuor angulis terræ, Gogum & Magogum, vt congreget eos in prælium.
units.tr: Decimum interuallum is 1000 years, from the year of Christ 1694 until the war of Gog and Magog, after which the end of the age will come. Apoc.20.v.2. He (the angel descending from heaven) laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years. Ibid. verf.7.8. And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, and shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle.

units.la: Atque hæc etiam sunt decem illa sacræ chronologiæ interualla, è quibus nouem priora explicare iam aggredimur in epitome historico-chronologicâ, decimum nonnisi obiter visuri.
units.tr: These are also the ten intervals of sacred chronology, of which we now proceed to explain the first nine in the historical-chronological epitome, the tenth to be treated only in passing.

units.la: LI. EPITOME Historiæ & Chronologiæ sacræ.
units.tr: LI. EPITOME of Sacred History and Chronology.

units.la: Primum interuallum, à creatione mundi ad diluuium.
units.tr: The first interval, from the creation of the world to the flood.

units.la: In principio temporis Deus creauit cœlum & terram, & vniuersum exercitū illorum. Gen. 1. & 2. Fuit autem istud principium veris: quia hæc est naturalissima & perfectissima anni ratio, ut incipiat à vere. Quæ etiam causa est, quòd Deus annum sacrum inchoauit à vere, politi-cum ab autumno. Sanè perfectissimam anni rationem in sacris obtinuisse nemini debet esse dubium. 130. | Adam genuit Seth. Gen.5.v.3. 235. | Enos nascitur ex Seth. Gen.5.v.6. 325. | Cainan, filius Enos, nascitur. Gen.5.v.9. 395. | Malaleel, filius Cainan, nascitur. Gen.5.v.12. 460. | Iared, filius Malaleel, nascitur. Gen.5.v.15. 622. | Enoch, filius Iared, nascitur. Gen.5.v.18. Hic fuit se-ptimus ab Adam. Iudæ v.14. 687. | Mathusalem, filius Enoch, nascitur. Gen.5.v.21. 874. | Lamech, filius Mathusalem, nascitur. Gen.5.v.25. 930. | Adam moritur. Gen.5.v.5. 987. | Enoch assumitur viuus in cœlum. Gen.5.v.24.25. 1042. | Seth moritur. Gen.5.v.8. 1056. | Noah, decimus ab Adam, nascitur ex Lamecho. Gen.5.v.28. 1140. | Enos moritur. Gen.5.v.11. 1235. | Kenan moritur. Gen.5.v.14. 1422. | Iared moritur. Gen.5.v.20.
units.tr: In the beginning of time God created heaven and earth, and all their host. Gen. 1. & 2. That beginning was in spring, because this is the most natural and most perfect reckoning of the year, that it begins in spring. This is also the reason why God began the sacred year in spring, but the civil year in autumn. Indeed, no one ought to doubt that the most perfect reckoning of the year held sway in the sacred books. 130. Adam begat Seth. Gen. 5. v. 3. 235. Enos is born of Seth. Gen. 5. v. 6. 325. Cainan, son of Enos, is born. Gen. 5. v. 9. 395. Mahalalel, son of Cainan, is born. Gen. 5. v. 12. 460. Jared, son of Mahalalel, is born. Gen. 5. v. 15. 622. Enoch, son of Jared, is born. Gen. 5. v. 18. He was the seventh from Adam. Jude v. 14. 687. Methuselah, son of Enoch, is born. Gen. 5. v. 21. 874. Lamech, son of Methuselah, is born. Gen. 5. v. 25. 930. Adam dies. Gen. 5. v. 5. 987. Enoch is taken up alive into heaven. Gen. 5. v. 24, 25. 1042. Seth dies. Gen. 5. v. 8. 1056. Noah, the tenth from Adam, is born of Lamech. Gen. 5. v. 28. 1140. Enos dies. Gen. 5. v. 11. 1235. Kenan dies. Gen. 5. v. 14. 1422. Jared dies. Gen. 5. v. 20.

units.la: Incipiunt 100. anni prædicationis pœnitentiæ.Gen.6.v.5.
units.tr: The 100 years of preaching repentance begin. Gen. 6. v. 5.

units.la: Sem nascitur. Gen.5.v.32.
units.tr: Shem is born. Gen. 5. v. 32.

units.la: Cham nascitur.Gen.5.v.32.
units.tr: Ham is born. Gen. 5. v. 32.

units.la: Iapheth nascitur.Gen.5.v.32.
units.tr: Japheth is born. Gen. 5. v. 32.

units.la: Hoc ordine procul dubio nati sunt filij Noë: quia passim ita commemorantur. Confer Gen.6. verf.10.c.9.v.18.c.10. v.1.
units.tr: Without doubt the sons of Noah were born in this order, because they are so mentioned everywhere. Compare Gen. 6. v. 10, ch. 9. v. 18, ch. 10. v. 1.

units.la: Lamech moritur. Gen.5.v.30.
units.tr: Lamech dies. Gen. 5. v. 30.

units.la: Mathusalem moritur paulò ante diluuium. Gen.5. verf.27. Vixit diutissimè omnium,annos 969. Non assecutus est millenarium: quia hic numerus est symbolum perfectionis æternæ.
units.tr: Methuselah dies shortly before the flood. Gen. 5. v. 27. He lived longer than all others, 969 years. He did not reach a thousand, because this number is the symbol of eternal perfection.

units.la: Diluuium incidit,& durat annum. Gen.7. & 8.
units.tr: The flood came upon the earth and lasted a year. Gen. 7. & 8.

units.la: Summa annorum à condito mundo vsq; addiluuium iuxta LXX. Interpretes est annorum 2242. nam illi in generatione primâ, secundâ, tertiâ & quartâ dissentiunt ab Hebraicâ veritate: quia in singulis hisce generationibus addiderunt 100. annos: in sextâ generatione vtrique codices consentiunt: in septimâ rursus addiderunt LXX. annos 100: in octauâ detraxerunt annos 20: in nonâ addiderunt sex annos: in decimâ conueniunt. In sex igitur generationibus LXX. addiderunt 600. annos, & in nonâ addiderunt sex. Et ita omnes anni sunt 606. Sed quoniam à generatione octauâ detraxerunt 20, fit vt omnes anni mundi conditi sint 586, qui simul iuncti cum annis 1656. efficiunt annos 2242. Nostrum est sequi Hebraicam veritatem. Sed obiicitur, Græcam computationem ideo esse amplectendam, quia in sexta synodo generali, actione 6. est approbata: vbi habetur, annos à mundo condito vsque ad Christum fluxisse 5508: deinde, quia editio LXX. Interpretum vsu totius ecclesiæ fuit olim per 500. annos approbata: vtpote cuius authoritate vsus est Christus, apostoli, & postea Græci, & Latini Patres ante Hieronymum. Resp. 1. Nullum concilium potest vel debet aliquid statuere contra Hebraicam veritatem. 2. Editio LXX. Interpretum ita est approbata ab ecclesiâ, vt tamen mendæ librariorum non sint canonizatæ. 3. Christus & apostoli sanctificarunt ista verba, quæ citarunt ex LXX. Interpretatione, non verò totum systema approbarunt. 4. Patres Græci & Latini, qui sequuntur chronologiam LXX. Interpretum, errant.
units.tr: According to the Seventy interpreters, the sum of years from the created world up to the flood is 2242. For they differ from Hebrew truth in the first, second, third and fourth generations, because in each of these generations they added 100 years; in the sixth generation both codices agree; in the seventh they again added 100 years; in the eighth they subtracted 20 years; in the ninth they added six years; in the tenth they agree. So in six generations the Seventy added 600 years, and in the ninth they added six. Thus all the years come to 606. But since they subtracted 20 from the eighth generation, it follows that all the years of the world since its creation are 586, which together with the 1656 make 2242. It is our task to follow Hebrew truth. But it is objected that the Greek computation is to be embraced, because it was approved in the sixth general council, action 6, where it is stated that the years from the created world to Christ amount to 5508; and secondly, because the edition of the Seventy interpreters was for 500 years approved by the use of the whole Church, since Christ, the apostles, and afterwards the Greek and Latin Fathers before Jerome made use of its authority. Answer: (1) No council can or should decide anything against Hebrew truth. (2) The edition of the Seventy has been approved by the Church in such a way that the errors of scribes were nonetheless not canonized. (3) Christ and the apostles sanctified those words which they quoted from the Septuagint translation, but they did not approve the whole system. (4) The Greek and Latin Fathers who follow the chronology of the Seventy are in error.

units.la: Secundum interuallum, à diluuio vsque ad promissionem Abrahamo factam.
units.tr: The second interval, from the flood to the promise made to Abraham.

units.la: 1656. | Mense primo huius anni Noah egressus est ex arca. Gen.8.v.13. 1658. | Arphaxad, filius Semi[?], nascitur. Gen.11.v.10. 1693. | Salah, filius Arphaxad, nascitur. Gen.11.v.13. 1723. | Heber, filius Salah, nascitur. Gen.11.v.14. 1757. | Peleg, filius Heber, nascitur. Gen.11.v.16. Hic nomen habuit à diuisione: quia diuisio linguarum Gen.11.v.7. sub illo contigit. 1787. | Regu, filius Peleg, nascitur. Gen.11.v.18. 1819. | Serug, filius Regu, nascitur. Gen.11.v.20. 1849. | Nahor, filius Serug, nascitur. Gen.11.v.22. 1878. | Tharah, filius Nahor, nascitur. Gen.11.v.24. 1948. | Abraham, filius Tharah, nascitur, anno 70[?]. Tharah. Gen.11.v.26. 1958. | Sara nascitur. Gen.17.v.17. 1996. | Peleg moritur. Gen.11.v.19. 1997. | Nahor moritur. Gen.11.v.24.25. 2005. | Noah moritur. Gen.9.v.28.29.
units.tr: 1656. In the first month of this year Noah went out of the ark. Gen. 8. v. 13. 1658. Arphaxad, son of Shem, is born. Gen. 11. v. 10. 1693. Salah, son of Arphaxad, is born. Gen. 11. v. 13. 1723. Eber, son of Salah, is born. Gen. 11. v. 14. 1757. Peleg, son of Eber, is born. Gen. 11. v. 16. He had his name from division, because the division of tongues Gen. 11. v. 7. happened in his time. 1787. Reu, son of Peleg, is born. Gen. 11. v. 18. 1819. Serug, son of Reu, is born. Gen. 11. v. 20. 1849. Nahor, son of Serug, is born. Gen. 11. v. 22. 1878. Terah, son of Nahor, is born. Gen. 11. v. 24. 1948. Abraham, son of Terah, is born, in the seventieth year[?] of Terah's life. Gen. 11. v. 26. 1958. Sarah is born. Gen. 17. v. 17. 1996. Peleg dies. Gen. 11. v. 19. 1997. Nahor dies. Gen. 11. v. 24, 25. 2005. Noah dies. Gen. 9. v. 28, 29.

units.la: In hoc interuallo rursus est discrepantia inter codicem authenticum, qui est veritatis Hebraicæ, & codices Græcos LXX. Interpretum. Nam in primâ generatione vtrique codices conueniunt, & in nonâ: at in 2.3.4.5.6.7. Interpretes LXX semper addiderunt 100 annos, & in octauâ addiderunt 50: denique inter Arphaxad & Salah posuerunt generationem Cainan, cui annos 130 tribuerunt. Sic enim legimus Gen. 11. in istâ versione: Arphaxad genuit Cainan anno ætatis 135 : Cainan genuit Sale anno ætatis 130. Hanc versionem sequitur Lucas cap.3. Qui fuit Sale, qui fuit Cainan. Sed sciendum est, LXX Interpretes hæc omnia de suo addidisse: & locum apud euangelistam Lucam à librariis, Hebraicæ literaturæ imperitis, ex LXX Interpretum versione esse transscriptum.
units.tr: In this interval there is again a discrepancy between the authentic codex, which is the Hebrew truth, and the Greek codices of the Seventy interpreters. For in the first generation both codices agree, and in the ninth; but in the second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth and seventh the Seventy interpreters always added 100 years, and in the eighth they added 50. Finally, between Arphaxad and Salah they placed a generation of Cainan, to whom they assigned 130 years. For so we read in Genesis 11 in that version: Arphaxad begat Cainan at the age of 135; Cainan begat Salah at the age of 130. Luke ch. 3 follows this version: "who was of Salah, who was of Cainan." But it must be known that the Seventy interpreters added all these things of their own, and that the passage in the evangelist Luke was copied by scribes, who were ignorant of Hebrew literature, from the Seventy's version.

units.la: Interuallum tertium, à promissione Abrahamo factâ vsq; ad exitum ex Æ- gypto.
units.tr: The third interval, from the promise made to Abraham to the exodus from Egypt.

units.la: Abraham, natus annos 75, migrat ex Haran, & accipit diuinam promissionem. Gen.12.v.1. Gal.3. v.17. Atque hic incipiunt anni 430 peregrinationis siue incolatus Israelitarum in Ægypto. Exod.12.
units.tr: Abraham, aged 75, migrates from Haran and receives the divine promise. Gen. 12 v. 1; Gal. 3 v. 17. And here begin the 430 years of the pilgrimage, or sojourning, of the Israelites in Egypt. Exod. 12.

units.la: Regu moritur. Gen.11.v.20.21.
units.tr: Reu dies. Gen. 11 v. 20, 21.

units.la: Abraham reportat victoriam aduersus reges Cananæos. Gen.14. Melchisedec ipsi occurrit. ibid.
units.tr: Abraham gains a victory over the Canaanite kings. Gen. 14. Melchizedek meets him. ibid.

units.la: Ifmael nascitur. Gen.16.v.3.
units.tr: Ishmael is born. Gen. 16 v. 3.

units.la: Loth, filius Haran fratris Abrahæ, separatur ab Abrahamo. Gen.13.
units.tr: Lot, son of Haran, Abraham's brother, is separated from Abraham. Gen. 13.

units.la: Circumcisio instituitur, anno 99 ætatis Abrahæ. Gen.17.
units.tr: Circumcision is instituted, in the 99th year of Abraham's age. Gen. 17.

units.la: Ifaac nascitur, anno 100 Abrahæ. Gen.21.v.5. Eodem anno nascuntur Moab & Ammon ex incestuoso concubitu Lothi & filiarum eius. Genef.19.v.37.38.
units.tr: Isaac is born, in Abraham's 100th year. Gen. 21 v. 5. In the same year Moab and Ammon are born from the incestuous intercourse of Lot with his daughters. Gen. 19 v. 37, 38.

units.la: Hagar ancilla pellitur è domo Abrahæ. Gen.21.
units.tr: Hagar, the maidservant, is driven out of Abraham's house. Gen. 21.

units.la: Ifaac circa hoc tempus, ut videtur, iussu diuino immolandus, in viuis seruatur. Gen.22. 2083. | Tharah moritur. Gen.11.v.32. 2085. | Sara moritur. Gen.23.v.1. 2088. | Isaac, natus annos 40, ducit Rebeccam, filiam Bathuelis, filij Nahor. Gen.25.v.20. 2097. | Arphaxad moritur. Gen.11.v.12.13. 5 2108. | Esau & Iacob nascuntur anno 60 Isaaci. Genef.25. verf.26. 2123. | Abraham moritur. Gen.25.v.7. 2126. | Salah moritur. Gen.11.v.14.15. 2129. | Isaac fame compulsus in Palaestinam, habitat in Gerar. Gen.26.v.1. 10 2148. | Esau quadragenarius ducit vxores gentiles. Gen.27.v.1. 2158. | Sem moritur, annorum 600. Gen.11.v.10.11. Hic est Melchisedec, rex ἀπάτωρ [?] ἀμήτωρ [?], ratione genealogiae regiae. Gen.14.Heb.5.&7. 15 2171. | Ishmael moritur. Gen.25.v.17. 2185. | Iacob proficiscitur ad Laban, & videt scalam in somnio. Gen.28. 2187. | Heber moritur. Gen.16.v.17. 20 2192. | Iacob accipit Leam in vxorem. Gen.29. & exacto conuiuio septemdiali nuptiarum, adiungit Rachelem. Gen.29.v.28. 2193. | Ruben nascitur 2194. | Simeon nascitur | Iacobo ex Lea. Genef.29.v.32.& seqq. 25 2195. | Leui nascitur 2196. | Iuda nascitur 2197. | Dan nascitur Iacobo ex Bilha ancilla. units.tr: Isaac, at about this time, as it seems, is to be sacrificed at the divine command, but is preserved alive. Gen. 22. 2083 | Terah dies. Gen. 11 v. 32. 2085 | Sarah dies. Gen. 23 v. 1. 2088 | Isaac, aged 40, marries Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel, son of Nahor. Gen. 25 v. 20. 2097 | Arphaxad dies. Gen. 11 v. 12, 13. 2108 | Esau and Jacob are born in Isaac's 60th year. Gen. 25 v. 26. 2123 | Abraham dies. Gen. 25 v. 7. 2126 | Salah dies. Gen. 11 v. 14, 15. 2129 | Isaac, compelled by famine, goes into Palestine and settles in Gerar. Gen. 26 v. 1. 2148 | Esau, at forty, marries Gentile wives. Gen. 27 v. 1. 2158 | Shem dies, aged 600. Gen. 11 v. 10, 11. This is Melchizedek, the king without father, without mother [ἀπάτωρ, ἀμήτωρ], with respect to the genealogy of kingship. Gen. 14; Heb. 5 and 7. 2171 | Ishmael dies. Gen. 25 v. 17. 2185 | Jacob sets out for Laban and sees the ladder in a dream. Gen. 28. 2187 | Eber dies. Gen. 11 v. 17. 2192 | Jacob takes Leah as his wife; and when the seven-day wedding feast is over, he takes Rachel also. Gen. 29 v. 28. 2193 | Reuben is born. 2194 | Simeon is born to Jacob by Leah. Gen. 29 v. 32 ff. 2195 | Levi is born. 2196 | Judah is born. 2197 | Dan is born to Jacob by Bilhah the maidservant. Gen. 30 v. 6. Naphtali is likewise born by Bilhah. Gen. 30 v. 8. 2196 | Gad is born to Jacob by Zilpah the maidservant. Gen. 30 v. 11. 2197 | Asher is likewise born by Zilpah. ibid. v. 11. And Issachar is born to Jacob by Leah. ibid. v. 18. 2198 | Zebulun is likewise born by Leah. ibid. v. 20. Dinah is born by Leah. ibid. v. 21. 2199 | Joseph is born by Rachel. ibid. v. 23, 24. He is born, I say, in the 14th year of servitude, in Jacob's 91st year. For Joseph was 39 years old when Jacob was 130. Gen. 41 v. 46; 45 v. 6; 47 v. 9.

units.la: Iacob clam [?] proficiscitur à Labane, & redit è Mesopotamiâ in Canaan, cùm uniuersâ familiâ. Gen.31.v.41.
units.tr: Jacob secretly departs from Laban and returns from Mesopotamia to Canaan with his whole household. Gen. 31 v. 41.

units.la: Dina putatur hoc tempore stuprata. Gen.34.
units.tr: Dinah is thought to have been violated about this time. Gen. 34.

units.la: Rahel obit. Gen.36.verf.16.
units.tr: Rachel dies. Gen. 35 v. 16.

units.la: Ioseph à fratribus venditur in Ægyptum. Gen.37. verf.27.
units.tr: Joseph is sold by his brothers into Egypt. Gen. 37 v. 27.

units.la: Ioseph in carcerem coniicitur. Gen.39.
units.tr: Joseph is thrown into prison. Gen. 39.

units.la: Ioseph exponit somnia. Gen.40.
units.tr: Joseph interprets dreams. Gen. 40.

units.la: Ifaac moritur. Gen.35.v.28.
units.tr: Isaac dies. Gen. 35 v. 28.

units.la: Ioseph exaltatur. Gen.41.v.40. Exaltatur,inquam, anno ætatis 30. Ita Christus expleto hoc anno manifestatur ber [?] baptismum & prædicationem suam. Cæterum Kahath eodem an.M.nascitur, anno Leui 34. Exod.6.v.18.
units.tr: Joseph is exalted. Gen. 41 v. 40. He is exalted, I say, in his 30th year of age. Thus Christ, when this year was complete, was manifested at [his] baptism and preaching. Meanwhile Kohath is born in the same year, in Levi's 34th year. Exod. 6 v. 18.

units.la: Anni septem sterilitatis, à Iosepho prædictæ, incipiunt. Gen.41.
units.tr: The seven years of famine, foretold by Joseph, begin. Gen. 41.

units.la: Anni septem fertilitatis incipiunt. ibid.
units.tr: The seven years of plenty begin. ibid.

units.la: Iacob cum uniuersâ familiâ descendit in Ægyptum,annorum 130. Gen.46.v.1.c.47.v.11. fecundo sterilitatis anno exeunte. Gen.45.v.11. Hic incipit secunda medietas annorum, quibus commorati sunt Israelitæ in Ægypto. Prima medietas est partim commorationis, partim peregrinatio-nis, secunda est commorationis tantum. Vide paulò ante an. M.2023.
units.tr: Jacob, aged 130, descends with his whole household into Egypt, as the second year of famine is ending. Gen. 46 v. 1; 47 v. 11; 45 v. 11. Here begins the second half of the years during which the Israelites dwelt in Egypt. The first half was partly sojourning and partly pilgrimage; the second is sojourning only. See a little earlier, in the year of the world 2023.

units.la: Iacob moritur, annorum 147. Gen.47.verf.28.
units.tr: Jacob dies, aged 147. Gen. 47 v. 28.

units.la: Post mortem eius contigit historia Gen.50.
units.tr: After his death the story of Gen. 50 takes place.

units.la: Amram nascitur, annis 65. à descensu Iacobi in Ægyptum. Vixit annos 137. Exod.6.v. 19.
units.tr: Amram is born, 65 years after Jacob's descent into Egypt. He lived 137 years. Exod. 6 v. 19.

units.la: Ioseph moritur. Genef.49.v.26.
units.tr: Joseph dies. Gen. 49 v. 26; 50 v. 26.

units.la: Leui moritur, annorum 137. Exod.6.v.16.
units.tr: Levi dies, aged 137. Exod. 6 v. 16.

units.la: Circa hæc tempora incipit pressura Israelitarum. Exod.1.
units.tr: About this time the oppression of the Israelites begins. Exod. 1.

units.la: Kahath moritur,annorum 133.Exod.6.v.18.
units.tr: Kohath dies, aged 133. Exod. 6 v. 18.

units.la: Aharon nascitur.Exod.7.v.10.
units.tr: Aaron is born. Exod. 7 v. 7.

units.la: Moses nascitur. ibidem. Historia natiuitatis est Exod. 2.
units.tr: Moses is born. ibid. The story of his birth is in Exod. 2.

units.la: Moses quadragenarius occidit Ægyptium.Exod.2. Act.7.v.23. Vita ipsius diuiditur in tres quadragenas. Sub finem primæ quadragenæ occidit Ægyptium: sub finem secundæ eduxit populum. Exod.12: sub finem tertiæ est mortuus. Deut.34. verf.7.
units.tr: Moses, at forty, kills an Egyptian. Exod. 2; Acts 7 v. 23. His life is divided into three forties. Near the end of the first forty he killed the Egyptian; near the end of the second he led the people out. Exod. 12; near the end of the third he died. Deut. 34 v. 7.

units.la: Iosua & Caleb nascuntur. Iof.14.v.7.10.
units.tr: Joshua and Caleb are born. Josh. 14 v. 7, 10.

units.la: Amram moritur.Exod.6.v.20.
units.tr: Amram dies. Exod. 6 v. 20.

units.la: Quartum interuallum ab exitu ex Ægypto ad templum Salomonis.
units.tr: The fourth interval, from the exodus from Egypt to the temple of Solomon.

units.la: Israelitæ exeunt ex Ægypto. Hoc anno & præcedenti contigerunt gesta Exod.3.&seqq.ad 36. Post 40.dies lex promulgatur in monte Sinai.
units.tr: The Israelites go out of Egypt. In this year and the preceding one took place the events of Exod. 3 ff., to 36. Forty days after this the law is proclaimed on Mount Sinai.

units.la: Tabernaculum incipit ædificari.Exod.36. Moses est dux populi per 40.annos in deserto, ab hoc anno 2454. vsq; ad an.M.2493, quo est mortuus. Hoc toto tempore contigerunt varia miracula diuina, multiplex rebellio populi aduersus Deū, & alia, quæ describuntur in Exodo, Leuitico, Numeris, & Deuteronomio.
units.tr: The tabernacle begins to be built. Exod. 36. Moses is leader of the people for 40 years in the wilderness, from this year 2454 to the year of the world 2493, in which he died. During this whole time various divine miracles occurred, and many rebellions of the people against God, and other things, which are described in Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy.

units.la: Iosua de tribu Ephraim, fit dux populi Dei, & ingressus in terram Canaan, primis sex annis debellat Cananæos.Iof.1.2.3.4.5.
units.tr: Joshua, of the tribe of Ephraim, becomes leader of God's people, and having entered the land of Canaan, in the first six years he subdues the Canaanites. Josh. 1–5.

units.la: Terra Canaan diuiditur per sortem, &primus iubilæus incipit.Iof.14.&seqq.
units.tr: The land of Canaan is divided by lot, and the first jubilee begins. Josh. 14 ff.

units.la: Othoniel, ex tribu Iuda, præest summæ rerum. Iudic.3. Hic quæritur,quomodo sint computandi anni, quibus Israelitæ seruierunt gentibus? Respondeo,eos,exceptis annis 18, esse numerandos partim in annis subsequentium, partim in annis præcedentium iudicum; non vero seorsim, vt quidam faciunt. Si enim interregna seorsim cōputentur, efficientur anni plures, quàm qui 1.Reg. 6.v.1. numerantur, quingeti nimirum, & eo plures. Quomodo autem sint computanda ista interregna, dicemus vbi ad singula peruentū fuerit. Sic primum interregnum, siue prima seruitus octennalis sub Chusan rege Mesopotamiæ, Iud.3. numerari debet in annis 40, de quibus Iud.3.v.11. hoc modo. Iosua præfuit populo Dei annis 25 incompletis: Othoniel 16 annis. Atq; ita habemus 40 annos Iud.3.verf.11. Sedecim annis Othonielis includendi sunt 8 anni primæ seruitutis.
units.tr: Othniel, of the tribe of Judah, presides over the public affairs. Judg. 3. Here it is asked how the years during which the Israelites served the nations are to be counted. I answer that, apart from the 18 years, they are to be counted partly within the years of the following judges and partly within those of the preceding judges, and not separately, as some do. For if the interregnums are counted separately, the years will amount to more than the number given in 1 Kings 6 v. 1, namely 500, and more besides. How these interregnums are to be counted we will say when we come to each one. So the first interregnum, or first servitude of eight years under Chushan, king of Mesopotamia, Judg. 3, must be counted among the 40 years mentioned in Judg. 3 v. 11, as follows. Joshua governed the people of God for 25 incomplete years; Othniel for 16 years. And so we have the 40 years of Judg. 3 v. 11. Within the sixteen years of Othniel are to be included the eight years of the first servitude.

units.la: Ehud, siue Aioth, ex tribu Beniamin, præfuit annis 8o Iud.3.v.30. In octoginta istis annis computandi sunt anni duodeviginti, quibus Hebræi serviérunt Elon regi Moabitarum. Iud.3.verf.14. Quidam existimant, Samgar successisse Ehudo in regimine. Sed recte sentiunt Iudæi, ipsum non fuisse iudicem, meminisse tamen eius Scripturam tanquam clarissimi viri, quippe qui multam hostium stragem ediderat extremis annis Ehudiudicis.Iud.3.vers.ult.
units.tr: Ehud, or Aioth, of the tribe of Benjamin, governed for 80 years. Judg. 3 v. 30. Within these eighty years are to be counted the eighteen years during which the Hebrews served Eglon, king of the Moabites. Judg. 3 v. 14. Some think that Shamgar succeeded Ehud in government. But the Jews rightly hold that he was not a judge, though Scripture remembers him as a most famous man, since he had inflicted a great slaughter of enemies in the last years of Ehud the judge. Judg. 3, last verse.

units.la: Debora, ex tribu Ephraim, adsciscit ducem belli Barachum, ex tribu Naphthali, & praefuit an.40. Iud.5.vers.31. Sub his annis 40 comprehenduntur anni 20, quibus seruierunt Hebraei tertiam seruitutem sub rege Cananaeorum Iabin.Iud.5.
units.tr: Deborah, of the tribe of Ephraim, enlists Barak, of the tribe of Naphtali, as leader in war, and governed for 40 years. Judg. 5 v. 31. Within these 40 years are comprehended the 20 years during which the Hebrews served a third servitude under Jabin, king of the Canaanites. Judg. 5.

units.la: Gedeon, alias Hierobaal, ex tribu Manasse, praefuit an. 40. quibus includi debent septem anni quartae seruitutis Israelitarum, quibus fuerunt sub potestate Midianitarum.Iud.6.v.1.c.8.v.28.
units.tr: Gideon, otherwise Jerubbaal, of the tribe of Manasseh, governed for 40 years, within which must be included the seven years of the fourth servitude of the Israelites, during which they were under the power of the Midianites. Judg. 6 v. 1; 8 v. 28.

units.la: Abimelech, spurius filius Gedeonis, praefuit an. 3.Iud.9.v.22.
units.tr: Abimelech, the illegitimate son of Gideon, governed for 3 years. Judg. 9 v. 22.

units.la: Thola, ex tribu Isachar, praefuit an. 23.Iud.10. verf.2.
units.tr: Tola, of the tribe of Issachar, governed for 23 years. Judg. 10 v. 2.

units.la: Iair, ex tribu Manasse, praefuit an. 22.Iud.10. v.3.
units.tr: Jair, of the tribe of Manasseh, governed for 22 years. Judg. 10 v. 3.

units.la: In his annis viginti duobus non numerari debent anni duodeviginti, quibus Israëlitæ subiecti fuerunt Ammonitis & Philistæis: sed sunt seorsim computandi, hoc modo,
units.tr: Of these twenty-two years the eighteen years during which the Israelites were subject to the Ammonites and Philistines should not be counted, but are to be reckoned separately, as follows.

units.la: Interregnum Philistæorum & Ammonitarum quintâ seruitute.Iud.10.v.8. fuit annorum 18. Atque hi sunt 18 anni, quos supraadan.M.2517.excepimus.
units.tr: The interregnum of the Philistines and Ammonites, the fifth servitude. Judg. 10 v. 8. It lasted 18 years. These are the 18 years which we excepted above, at the year of the world 2517.

units.la: Iephthe, ex tribu Manasse, an.6.Iud.12.v.7.
units.tr: Jephthah, of the tribe of Manasseh, 6 years. Judg. 12 v. 7.

units.la: Ebzan, ex tribu Iudâ, an.7.Iud.12.v.9.
units.tr: Ibzan, of the tribe of Judah, 7 years. Judg. 12 v. 9.

units.la: Elon, ex tribu Zabulon, annos 10.Iud.12.v.11.
units.tr: Elon, of the tribe of Zebulun, 10 years. Judg. 12 v. 11.

units.la: Abdon, ex tribu Ephraim, annos 8.Iud.12.v.14.
units.tr: Abdon, of the tribe of Ephraim, 8 years. Judg. 12 v. 14.

units.la: Samson, annos 20.Iud.16.v.31. Anni quadragintâ, quibus Israëlitæ Philistinis seruisse dicuntur, Iud.13. numerandi sunt hunc in modum. Integris 20 annis, quibus Samson iudicauit, seruierunt. Reliqui 20 anni pertinent ad tempora, quibus Eli populum gubernauit. Neque tamen est, quòd ideo Samsonem cū Andreâ Masio expungamus è numero Iudicum. Nam Scriptura non dicit de Samsone, quòd populum ab hostibus liberauerit, sicut de aliis iudicibus dicit: sed solùm, quòd praefuerit summæ rerum, in statu scilicet reipub. turbato.
units.tr: Samson, 20 years. Judg. 16 v. 31. The forty years during which the Israelites are said to have served the Philistines, Judg. 13, are to be counted in this way. For 20 full years they served while Samson judged. The remaining 20 years belong to the time when Eli governed the people. Nor is there any reason why we should therefore strike Samson from the number of the judges, with Andreas Masius. For Scripture does not say of Samson that he delivered the people from their enemies, as it says of the other judges; it says only that he presided over public affairs, in a state of the commonwealth that was troubled.

units.la: Eli, de tribu Leui, praefuit annos 40. 1.Sam.4. verf.18.
units.tr: Eli, of the tribe of Levi, governed for 40 years. 1 Sam. 4 v.18.

units.la: Samuel circa hoc tempus nascitur. Obit enim septuagenarius, anno M.2888.1.Sam.25.
units.tr: Samuel is born about this time. For he dies an old man of seventy, in the year M.2888. 1 Sam. 25.

units.la: Samuel duodecim annorum accipit diuinam vocationem.1.Sam.3.
units.tr: Samuel, at twelve years old, receives the divine calling. 1 Sam. 3.

units.la: Eli frangit ceruicem, accepto tristi nuntio de arcâ Domini captâ. 1.Sam.4.v.15.
units.tr: Eli breaks his neck when he hears the sad news that the ark of the Lord has been captured. 1 Sam. 4 v.15.

units.la: Samuel, è tribu Leui, praefuit annos 40. computatis annis regni Saulis. Actor.13.verf.21. Iosephus tribuit Samueli soli post obitum Eli annos 12, & ei vnà cum Saule annos 18, & Sauli post Samuemuclemannos 10. Etita omnesanni sunt 40.
units.tr: Samuel, of the tribe of Levi, governed for 40 years, counting the years of Saul's reign. Acts 13 v.21. Josephus assigns to Samuel alone, after the death of Eli, 12 years; to him together with Saul, 18 years; and to Saul alone, after Samuel, 10 years. So all the years come to 40.

units.la: Dauid nascitur. Est enim annorum 30, cùm in Hebron vnctus fuit. 2. Sam.5.v.4. Hâc in re fuit typus Christi, qui anno 30. completo baptizatus est.
units.tr: David is born. For he was thirty years old when he was anointed in Hebron. 2 Sam. 5 v.4. In this matter he was a type of Christ, who was baptized when he had completed his thirtieth year.

units.la: Samuel insignem victoriam reportat dePhiliftæis 1.Sam.7.v.1.
units.tr: Samuel wins a notable victory over the Philistines. 1 Sam. 7 v.1.

units.la: Saul,ē tribuBeniamin,vngitur in regem Israël. 1.Sam.13.v.1. Atq; hîc definit regimen iudicum, quod durauit annos 386. Perperam huc trahuntur 300. anni Iud.11.verf.28:quia illi incipiunt ab exitu ex Ægypto, vnde Iephthe narrationis suæ initium fecerat verf.18. Præcise autem numerat annos 300, numero rotundo siue completo.
units.tr: Saul, of the tribe of Benjamin, is anointed king over Israel. 1 Sam. 13 v.1. And here the rule of the judges ends, which lasted 386 years. The 300 years of Judg. 11 v.28 are wrongly drawn in here, because they begin from the exodus from Egypt, whence Jephthah began his narrative, v.18. But he counts exactly 300 years, a round or complete number.

units.la: Saul duobus annis exactis reiicitur, & Dauid inungitur. 1.Sam.13.v.1.&16.v.14.
units.tr: Saul, after two years have passed, is rejected, and David is anointed. 1 Sam. 13 v.1 and 16 v.14.

units.la: Dauid prosternit Goliathum. 1.Sam.17.
units.tr: David strikes down Goliath. 1 Sam. 17.

units.la: Saul Dauidem persequitur.
units.tr: Saul pursues David.

units.la: Saul perit, anno regni 10:cum quo concurrit quadragesimus Samuelis, qui ipse tum quoque obiit. 1.Sam.25.
units.tr: Saul perishes in the tenth year of his reign; at the same time falls the fortieth year of Samuel, who himself also died then. 1 Sam. 25.

units.la: Dauid,filius Isai, regnat annos 40. 2.Sam.5.v.4. Secundo vngitur Saule occiso,in Hebron,& tertio quoque. 2.Sam.2.v.4. In Hebron regnat annos 7.menf. 6. Hierosolymis,an.33. 2.Sam.1.
units.tr: David, son of Jesse, reigns 40 years. 2 Sam. 5 v.4. He is anointed a second time, after Saul's death, in Hebron, and a third time as well. 2 Sam. 2 v.4. In Hebron he reigns 7 years and 6 months; in Jerusalem, 33 years. 2 Sam. 1.

units.la: Dauid Philiftæos vincit, & arcam Domini reducit, quæ ad 50.annos fuerat in domo Aminadab.2.Sam.6.
units.tr: David defeats the Philistines and brings back the ark of the Lord, which had been for 50 years in the house of Abinadab. 2 Sam. 6.

units.la: Nathan promittit Dauidi Messiam. 2.Sam.7.
units.tr: Nathan promises David the Messiah. 2 Sam. 7.

units.la: Dauid est clarus togâ&sago. 2.Sam.8.9.10.
units.tr: David is famous both in peace and in war. 2 Sam. 8, 9, 10.

units.la: Dauid se polluit adulterio & homicidio: quâ de causâ reprehenditur à Nathane. 2.Sam.11.12.
units.tr: David defiles himself with adultery and murder, for which he is rebuked by Nathan. 2 Sam. 11, 12.

units.la: Salomon nascitur ex Bathsheba.2.Sam.12.
units.tr: Solomon is born of Bathsheba. 2 Sam. 12.

units.la: Thamar stupratur vi à fratre Amnone. 2.Samuelis13.
units.tr: Tamar is violated by force by her brother Amnon. 2 Sam. 13.

units.la: Amnon interficitur ab Absalomo, qui postea fugit. 2.Sam.13. Hoc tempore floruerunt Asaph, Ethan, & Heman, Psalmistae. 1.Chron.25.
units.tr: Amnon is killed by Absalom, who afterwards flees. 2 Sam. 13. At this time flourished the psalmists Asaph, Ethan and Heman. 1 Chron. 25.

units.la: Absolom tertio anno à cæde reuocatur operâ Ioabi. 2.Sam.14.
units.tr: Absalom is recalled three years after the killing, through the work of Joab. 2 Sam. 14.

units.la: Absolom eiicit patrem regno: sed vincitur & occiditur. 2.Sam.15.16.17.18.
units.tr: Absalom drives his father from the kingdom, but is defeated and killed. 2 Sam. 15, 16, 17, 18.

units.la: Mephibosteth restituitur. 2.Sam.19. Seba seditiosus plectitur. 2.Sam.20.
units.tr: Mephibosheth is restored. 2 Sam. 19. Sheba the seditious man is punished. 2 Sam. 20.

units.la: Fames triennis premit Israelem. 2.Sam.21.
units.tr: A three-year famine oppresses Israel. 2 Sam. 21.

units.la: Dauid ex [illegible, ~10 letters] numerat populum. 2.Sam.24.
units.tr: David [illegible] numbers the people. 2 Sam. 24.

units.la: Salomon adit regnum, idque administrat 40. annos, quamdiu pater regnauerat. 1.Reg.11.v.42. Petit & impetrat à Deo sapientiam. 1.Reg.3.v.6.
units.tr: Solomon comes to the kingdom and administers it for 40 years, as long as his father had reigned. 1 Kings 11 v.42. He asks for and obtains wisdom from God. 1 Kings 3 v.6.

units.la: Quintum intervallum, à fundatione templi Salomonis usq; ad captiuitatem Babylonicam.
units.tr: The fifth interval, from the foundation of Solomon's temple to the Babylonian captivity.

units.la: Templum Salomonis fundatur, anno 480. (ineunte) ab exitu. 1.Reg.4.v.1. mense secundo, siue Maio, anno 4. Salomonis, iuvante Hiramo rege Tyri. 1.Reg.5.v.3.
units.tr: Solomon's temple is founded in the 480th year from the exodus, at the beginning of the year. 1 Kings 4 v.1. In the second month, or May, in the fourth year of Solomon, with the help of Hiram, king of Tyre. 1 Kings 5 v.3.

units.la: Maiestas & sapientia Salomonis longè lateq; percrebescit. 1.Reg.3.4.10.
units.tr: The majesty and wisdom of Solomon spread far and wide. 1 Kings 3, 4, 10.

units.la: Templo septem annorum spatio absoluto, celebrantur eius encænia, anno ii. regni Salomonis. 1.Reg.6.
units.tr: When the temple had been finished over a span of seven years, its dedication is celebrated in the second year of Solomon's reign. 1 Kings 6.

units.la: Salomon componit varia cantica, & de variis rebus sapientissimè disserit. 1.Reg.4.v.32.33.
units.tr: Solomon composes various songs and discourses most wisely on various subjects. 1 Kings 4 v.32, 33.

units.la: Salomon constituit politiam sacram & ciuilem. 1.Reg.8.&9.
units.tr: Solomon establishes the sacred and civil polity. 1 Kings 8 and 9.

units.la: Regia Salomonis perficitur. 1.Reg.9.v.10. Regina Sabæ venit Hierosolymam. 1.Reg.10.
units.tr: Solomon's palace is completed. 1 Kings 9 v.10. The queen of Sheba comes to Jerusalem. 1 Kings 10.

units.la: Salomon corrumpitur à mulieribus. 1.Reg.11.
units.tr: Solomon is corrupted by women. 1 Kings 11.

units.la: Salomon moritur. ibid. Ipsi succedit Rehabeam filius, qui levitate & superbiâ à se abalienat subditos. Quâ occasione decem tribus deficiunt, & fit schisma regni, Ieroboamo obtinente regnum Israël.1.Reg.14.
units.tr: Solomon dies. Ibid. He is succeeded by his son Rehoboam, who by levity and pride alienates his subjects. On this occasion the ten tribes revolt and the kingdom is split in schism, Jeroboam obtaining the kingdom of Israel. 1 Kings 14.

units.la: Ahia, Iddo, & Semeia, prophetæ, florent. 2. Chron.9.1.Reg.12.Floret etiam propheta ἀνώνυμος[?], qui contra altare Bethel clamat, & exprimit nomen eucrsoris Iosiæ, annis 350 antequam fieret. 1.Reg.13.v.32.
units.tr: The prophets Ahijah, Iddo and Shemaiah flourish. 2 Chron. 9; 1 Kings 12. There also flourishes an unnamed prophet [anōnymos], who cries out against the altar at Bethel and names the future destroyer of Josiah, 350 years before he was born. 1 Kings 13 v.32.

units.la: Abia,rex Iuda, annos 2.regnat. 1.Reg.15.
units.tr: Abijah, king of Judah, reigns two years. 1 Kings 15.

units.la: Asa[?] fit rex Iuda:item Nadab, rex Israël.1.Reg.15.
units.tr: Asa becomes king of Judah; likewise Nadab, king of Israel. 1 Kings 15.

units.la: Baesa regnat in Israël. 2. Reg.16. Tempore Baesæ & Asæ florent Iehu, Hanani, & Asaria, prophetæ. 2.Paral.15.16.19.
units.tr: Baasha reigns in Israel. 2 Kings 16. In the time of Baasha and Asa the prophets Jehu, Hanani and Azariah flourish. 2 Chron. 15, 16, 19.

units.la: Medium mundi incidit in annum 13 Asæ.
units.tr: The middle of the world falls in the thirteenth year of Asa.

units.la: Asa ingenti prælio vincit regem Æthiopum Zaram. 2.Paral.14.& 15.
units.tr: Asa wins a great battle and defeats the king of the Ethiopians, Zerah. 2 Chron. 14 and 15.

units.la: Ela fit rex in Israël, an.2:& cum illo Zamri, dies 7. 1.Reg.16.
units.tr: Elah becomes king in Israel in the second year, and with him Zimri for seven days. 1 Kings 16.

units.la: Amri fit rex in Israël,an.12.e quibus duo includuntur annis Elæ. 1.Reg.16.
units.tr: Omri becomes king in Israel in the twelfth year, two years of which are included in Elah's. 1 Kings 16.

units.la: Achab regnat in Israël unà cum uxore suâ idololatricâ Iezebel. 1.Reg.16. Elias propheta hoc tempore claret. Eius discipulus fuit Elisæus. 1.Reg.17. 2.Reg.2.
units.tr: Ahab reigns in Israel together with his idolatrous wife Jezebel. 1 Kings 16. The prophet Elijah shines at this time. His disciple was Elisha. 1 Kings 17; 2 Kings 2.

units.la: Iosaphath fit rex Iuda.1.Reg.22.
units.tr: Jehoshaphat becomes king of Judah. 1 Kings 22.

units.la: Micha, propheta sub Ahabo, floret. 2.Reg.22.
units.tr: Micaiah, a prophet under Ahab, flourishes. 2 Kings 22.

units.la: Ochozias, seu Ahasia, regnat in Israël. 1.Reg.22.
units.tr: Ahaziah, also called Ochozias, reigns in Israel. 1 Kings 22.

units.la: Ioram succedit Ochoziæ. 2.Reg.3.
units.tr: Joram succeeds Ahaziah. 2 Kings 3.

units.la: Ioram, rex Iuda, succedit Iosaphatho.2.Reg.8.
units.tr: Joram, king of Judah, succeeds Jehoshaphat. 2 Kings 8.

units.la: Ochozias, rex Iuda, succedit Ioramo. 1.Reg.22.
units.tr: Ahaziah, king of Judah, succeeds Joram. 1 Kings 22.

units.la: Athalia, fœmina, capessit regnum Iuda. 2.Reg. 11.
units.tr: Athaliah, a woman, seizes the kingdom of Judah. 2 Kings 11.

units.la: Eodem anno Iehu fit rex in Israël. 1.Reg.10.
units.tr: In the same year Jehu becomes king in Israel. 1 Kings 10.

units.la: Ioas fit rex in Iudâ.2.Reg.11.
units.tr: Joash becomes king in Judah. 2 Kings 11.

units.la: Ioachas regnat in Israël. 2. Reg.13. Ioiada sacerdos, optimè de regno Iudâ meritus, circa hæc tempora obit, annorum 130. 2. Paral. 24.
units.tr: Jehoahaz reigns in Israel. 2 Kings 13. Jehoiada the priest, who deserved very well of the kingdom of Judah, dies about this time, aged 130. 2 Chron. 24.

units.la: Ioas fit rex in Israel. 2. Reg. 13.
units.tr: Joash becomes king in Israel. 2 Kings 13.

units.la: Amasia regnat in Iuda. 2. Reg. 14.
units.tr: Amaziah reigns in Judah. 2 Kings 14.

units.la: Ieroboam II fit rex in Israel. 2. Reg. 14. Sub hoc claruerunt Ionas, Hofeas, Ioel, & Amos. 2. Reg. 14. v.23.25. Hof.1.v.1. Ioel.1.v.15. Amos.1.v.1.
units.tr: Jeroboam II becomes king in Israel. 2 Kings 14. Under him flourished Jonah, Hosea, Joel and Amos. 2 Kings 14 v.23, 25; Hos. 1 v.1; Joel 1 v.15; Amos 1 v.1.

units.la: Azarias, qui & Ozia, & Vfias dicitur, regnat in Iuda. 2. Reg. 15. Sub hoc coepit vaticinari Esaias, & continuauit sub Iotham, Achas & Ezechia vsque ad Manassen. Esa. 1. Hoseas etiam floruit adhuc sub Ezechia.
units.tr: Azariah, who is also called Uzziah, reigns in Judah. 2 Kings 15. Under him Isaiah began to prophesy, and he continued under Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah down to Manasseh. Isa. 1. Hosea also flourished still under Hezekiah.

units.la: Zacharias regnat in Israel. 2. Reg. 14. Inter hunc & Ieroboamum II constituendum est interregnum 11 an.
units.tr: Zechariah reigns in Israel. 2 Kings 14. Between him and Jeroboam II an interregnum of eleven years must be placed.

units.la: Sellum fit rex Israelis. 2. Reg. 15.
units.tr: Shallum becomes king of Israel. 2 Kings 15.

units.la: Menahem regnat in Israel 2. Reg. 15.
units.tr: Menahem reigns in Israel. 2 Kings 15.

units.la: Pekaia fit rex Israelis. 2. Reg. 15.
units.tr: Pekahiah becomes king of Israel. 2 Kings 15.

units.la: Peka regnat in Israel 2. Reg. 15. Iotham, in Iuda, ibid. Sub Iotham, Achas, & Ezechia prophetat Micheas. Mich. 1.v.1.
units.tr: Pekah reigns in Israel. 2 Kings 15. Jotham in Judah, ibid. Under Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah the prophet Micah prophesies. Mic. 1 v.1.

units.la: Achaz fit rex Iuda. 2. Reg. 16.
units.tr: Ahaz becomes king of Judah. 2 Kings 16.

units.la: Hofea fit rex Israelis. 2. Reg. 15. 17. Sub hoc Samaria expugnatur, & decem tribus in perpetuam captiuitate abducuntur, in Colchos, Iberos, &c.
units.tr: Hoshea becomes king of Israel. 2 Kings 15, 17. Under him Samaria is taken, and the ten tribes are led away into perpetual captivity, into Colchis, Iberia, etc.

units.la: 2. Reg. 18. Atque hic definit regnum Israelis: vbi quaeritur, Quomodo summa annorum, quibus reges Israelis regnasse dicuntur in libris Regum, consentiat cum numero annorum regum Iuda, qui eodem tempore regnarunt? Resp. Aliquot fuerunt interregna in Israele, quae in Scripturis non indicantur. Nec mirum, interregna fuisse in regno impio, & quod ob factiones, bella ciuilia, & crebras familiarum vicissitudines, & mutationes, crebro perturbabatur. Alij existimant, omitti quosdam annos, quibus rex hic vel ille admodum male regnauit. e.g. Zacharias forte regnauit 2o annis, quia tamen sex mensibus bene vixit, dicitur in Scriptura regnasse tantum 6 mensibus. Sed prior sententia est magis probabilis.
units.tr: 2 Kings 18. And here the kingdom of Israel ends. Here it is asked: how does the sum of the years in which the kings of Israel are said in the books of Kings to have reigned agree with the number of years of the kings of Judah who reigned at the same time? Answer: there were several interregnums in Israel, which are not indicated in Scripture. Nor is this surprising, since there were interregnums in an impious kingdom, which was often disturbed by factions, civil wars and frequent changes and upheavals of families. Others think that some years are omitted, in which this or that king reigned very badly. For example, Zechariah perhaps reigned twenty years; but because he lived well for six months, he is said in Scripture to have reigned only six months. But the former opinion is more probable.

units.la: Ezechias regnat in Iudâ 2. Reg. 16. 18. 19. 20. Hoc tempore prophetasse putantur Habacuc & Nahum.
units.tr: Hezekiah reigns in Judah. 2 Kings 16, 18, 19, 20. At this time Habakkuk and Nahum are thought to have prophesied.

units.la: Senacherib, cæsis 185000 suis militibus, relinquit obsidionem Hierosolymorum. 2. Reg. 19. Esa.38.
units.tr: Sennacherib, after 185,000 of his soldiers were slain, abandons the siege of Jerusalem. 2 Kings 19; Isa. 38.

units.la: Manasses, filius Ezechiæ degener, succeditpatri. 2. Reg. 21.
units.tr: Manasseh, the degenerate son of Hezekiah, succeeds his father. 2 Kings 21.

units.la: Amon succedit. 2. Reg. 21.
units.tr: Amon succeeds. 2 Kings 21.

units.la: Iosias succedit. 2. Reg. 21. 22. 23. Sub hoc putatur prophetasse Sophoniam. Anno 13 Iosiæ incipit Ieremias. Ier. 1. v. 2.
units.tr: Josiah succeeds. 2 Kings 21, 22, 23. Under him Zephaniah is thought to have prophesied. In the thirteenth year of Josiah, Jeremiah begins. Jer. 1 v.2.

units.la: Ioachas succedit Iosiæ. 2. Reg. 23,
units.tr: Jehoahaz succeeds Josiah. 2 Kings 23.

units.la: Eliakim, seu Iojakim, succedit. 2. Reg. 23.24.
units.tr: Eliakim, or Jehoiakim, succeeds. 2 Kings 23, 24.

units.la: Iechonias succedit. 2. Reg. 24. Hic mense 3 abducitur Babylonem.
units.tr: Jehoiachin succeeds. 2 Kings 24. He is carried off to Babylon in the third month.

units.la: Sextum interuallum, à captiuitate Babylonicâ vsque ad initium septima- narum Danielis.
units.tr: The sixth interval, from the Babylonian captivity to the beginning of Daniel's seventy weeks.

units.la: Captiuitas Babylonica incipit. Quidam illam inchoant ab anno vltimo Zedekiæ, qui fuit annus vndecimus eius regni, & decimus nonus Nebucadnezaris, eamq; finiri aiunt anno secundo Darij Hystaspis. Hanc sententiam probant ex Ier. 25. vbi legimus, terram futuram in solitudinem, & in stuporem 7o annis. Sed non cœpit esse desertâ, nisi ab anno vltimo Zedekiæ, quo tempore Chaldæi templum & vrbem Hierosolymorum incenderunt, & reliquias Iudæorum transtulerunt. Et 2. Paral. vlt. legimus, terram Israëlis sabbatum egisse 7o. annis, id est, quieuisse, iam videl. in desertum & solitudinem redactam. At hoc non contigit nisi vltimo anno Zedekiæ. Sed sciendum est, hos non esse annos captiuitatis, sed solitudinis & desolationis. Nam anni captiuitatis initium sumunt ab eo anno, quo Iechonias vnà cum matre & popularibus captiuus abductus fuit Babylonem, qui fuit octauus annus regni Nebucadnezaris. Hi anni desinunt in primo anno monarchiæ Cyri, qui captiuitatem Babylonicam laxauit. Ier. 29. 2. Chron. 36. Esdr. 1. Huc accedit, quòd Matth. 1. distinguuntur quatuordecim generationes ante transmigrationem, ab aliis quatuordecim generationibus post transmigrationem, & numeratur transmigratio à prædicto Iechoniâ. Sic ig. habendum est. Captiuitas fuit diuisa in tres actus. Protasis contigit anno quarto Ioakimi, seu primo Nebucadnezaris 2. Chron. 36. v. 6. Epitasis incidit primo Iechoniæ, octauo Nebucadnezaris. 2. Reg. 24. v. 12. 2. Paral. 37. verf. 10. Catastrophe vndecimo Sedekiæ, 19 Nebucadnezaris. ibid. Iam verò epitasis est potior catastrophe. Sed hoc sit palmarium: Terminus à quo captiuitatis optimè colligitur ex termino ad quem. At is est primus annus Cyri, quo captiuitas est soluta.
units.tr: The Babylonian captivity begins. Some date its beginning from the last year of Zedekiah, which was his eleventh year and the nineteenth of Nebuchadnezzar, and they say it ended in the second year of Darius Hystaspis. They prove this opinion from Jer. 25, where we read that the land would become a desolation and an astonishment for seventy years. But it did not begin to be deserted until the last year of Zedekiah, when the Chaldeans burned the temple and city of Jerusalem and carried off the remnant of the Jews. And in 2. Paral. vlt. we read that the land of Israel kept its sabbath for seventy years, that is, rested, now reduced to a wilderness and solitude. But this did not happen until the last year of Zedekiah. However, it must be understood that these are not years of captivity but of solitude and desolation. For the years of captivity are reckoned from the year when Jeconiah, together with his mother and kinsmen, was led captive to Babylon, which was the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign. These years end in the first year of Cyrus's monarchy, who loosed the Babylonian captivity. Jer. 29; 2. Chron. 36; Ezra 1. Add to this that Matth. 1 distinguishes fourteen generations before the transmigration from fourteen generations after the transmigration, and reckons the transmigration from the aforesaid Jeconiah. So it must be held thus. The captivity was divided into three acts. The protasis fell in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, or the first of Nebuchadnezzar, 2. Chron. 36. v. 6. The epitasis fell in the first year of Jehoiachin, the eighth of Nebuchadnezzar, 2. Reg. 24. v. 12; 2. Paral. 37, verf. 10. The catastrophe came in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, the nineteenth of Nebuchadnezzar, ibid. Indeed the epitasis is more important than the catastrophe. But this is the chief point: the starting point of the captivity is best gathered from its end point. And that end point is the first year of Cyrus, when the captivity was loosed.

units.la: Ezechiel incipit vaticinari. cap. 8. & seqq.
units.tr: Ezekiel begins to prophesy. Ch. 8 and following.

units.la: Daniel anno 7 exilij Babylonici putatur interpretatus esse somnium Nebucadnezaris. Dan. 2.
units.tr: Daniel, in the seventh year of the Babylonian exile, is thought to have interpreted the dream of Nebuchadnezzar. Dan. 2.

units.la: Sedekias abducitur Babylonem, & Hierosolyma cum templo exciduntur. 2. Reg. 24. Ier. 52.
units.tr: Zedekiah is led away to Babylon, and Jerusalem with the temple is razed. 2. Reg. 24; Jer. 52.

units.la: Belsazer regnat in Babylonià. Eum regno exuit Darius Medus. Dan. 5. & 6.
units.tr: Belshazzar reigns in Babylon. Darius the Mede strips him of the kingdom. Dan. 5 and 6.

units.la: Cyri annus primus per Asiam cum hoc anno cohæret, ac proinde etiam solutio captiuitatis Babylonicæ, ac reditus populi duce Zorobabele anno primo (monarchiæ) Cyri. Esdr. 1. v. 1. Intelige annum M. 3419. completum, seu 3420. ineuntem. Ædificium templi & instauratio vrbis impeditur viuenteadhuc Cyro.Esdr.4.v.5. item sub Cambyse, & Dario Hyftaspide, ibid.v.6: item sub Xerxe, ibid. v.6: item sub Artaxerxe Longimano,ibid.v.7.18. &feqq. vsque ad annum secundum Darii Nothi. ibid.v.vlt.
units.tr: The first year of Cyrus through Asia coincides with this year, and therefore also with the release from the Babylonian captivity, and the return of the people under Zerubbabel in the first year of the monarchy of Cyrus, Ezra 1. v. 1. Understand the year 3419 of the world as completed, or the year 3420 as beginning. The building of the temple and the restoration of the city are hindered while Cyrus is still alive, Ezra 4. v. 5; likewise under Cambyses and Darius Hystaspis, ibid. v. 6; likewise under Xerxes, ibid. v. 6; likewise under Artaxerxes Longimanus, ibid. v. 7, 18 and following, down to the second year of Darius Nothus, ibid. last verse.

units.la: Assuerus, id est, Xerxes, ducit Estheram vxorem. Esth. 1.
units.tr: Assuerus, that is, Xerxes, takes Esther as his wife. Esth. 1.

units.la: Septimum interuallum, a templo se- cundo fundato vsq; ad eius excidium.
units.tr: The seventh interval, from the founding of the second temple to its destruction.

units.la: Anno secundo Darij Nothi inchoatur ædificatio templi.Esdr.4.v.vlt. Haggæus & Zacharias vaticinantur. Hic incipiunt 7 o septimanæ Dan.9.
units.tr: In the second year of Darius Nothus the building of the temple begins. Ezra 4, last verse. Haggai and Zechariah prophesy. Here the seventy weeks begin. Dan. 9.

units.la: Anno sexto Darij Nothi templum abfoluitur. Esdr.6.v.15.
units.tr: In the sixth year of Darius Nothus the temple is completed. Ezra 6. v. 15.

units.la: Anno septimo Artaxerxis Mnemonis Esdra proficiscitur Hierosolymam, magno instructus comitatu, & reformat ibi vtramque politiam,ecclesiasticam & ciuilem.Esdr.7.8.9.10.
units.tr: In the seventh year of Artaxerxes Mnemon, Ezra sets out for Jerusalem, equipped with a large retinue, and there reforms both polities, the ecclesiastical and the civil. Ezra 7, 8, 9, 10.

units.la: Nehemias, accepto nuntio de aduersis rebus in Iudæa, jejunat & orat.Nehem.1.
units.tr: Nehemiah, having received news of adversity in Judea, fasts and prays. Neh. 1.

units.la: Nehemias anno 2o Artaxerxis Mnemonis venit Hierosolymam permissu regis, & muros ciuitatis per annos 12. instaurat.Neh.2. &feqq.
units.tr: Nehemiah, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes Mnemon, comes to Jerusalem by the king's permission, and over twelve years restores the walls of the city. Neh. 2 and following.

units.la: Anno 31 Artaxerxis Mnemonis desinente muri Hierosolymæ sunt perfecti, annis 49, siue septem septimanis, à secundo anno Darij Nothi & initio hebdomadum Dan.9. Confer Esdr.6.v.14.
units.tr: In the thirty-first year of Artaxerxes Mnemon the walls of Jerusalem were finished, after forty-nine years, or seven weeks, counted from the second year of Darius Nothus and the beginning of the weeks, Dan. 9. Compare Ezra 6. v. 14.

units.la: Darius Codomannus vincitur ab Alexandro Magno. 1. Maccab. 1.v.1.
units.tr: Darius Codomannus is conquered by Alexander the Great. 1. Macc. 1. v. 1.

units.la: Alexandro Magno rebus humanis exemto, imperium eius cedit ducibus ipsius.1. Maccab. 1.v.6. &feqq.
units.tr: With Alexander the Great removed from human affairs, his empire passes to his commanders. 1. Macc. 1. v. 6 and following.

units.la: Antiochus Epiphanes Hierosolymam capit, & templum profanat. 2. Maccab.5.
units.tr: Antiochus Epiphanes captures Jerusalem and profanes the temple. 2. Macc. 5.

units.la: Iudas Maccabæus fortiter pugnat contra Antiochum. 1.Maccab. 3.
units.tr: Judas Maccabeus fights bravely against Antiochus. 1. Macc. 3.

units.la: Iohannes Baptista nascitur circa initium Aprilis. Conceptus enim fuit post 28 diem Iulij, quod ita demonstratur, ex 2. Paral. 24. & Luc. 1. v. 8. 9. 23. Dauid posteritatem Aharonis in 24 familias ita diuisit, vt singulae hebdomadam integram in templo operarentur. Quare singularum familiarum functio in orbem recurrebat per 168 dies. Hae 24 familiae ab encaeniis Iudae Maccabaei, ad excidium vsque templi, incolumes & imper mixta successione manserunt, teste Iosepho, qui, vtpote sacerdos, id ignorare non potuit. Principes harum familiarum in euangelio dicuntur ἀρχιερεῖς[?]. Istæ ig. 24 sacerdotum classes in templo operabantur, singulae hebdomadam suam. Vnde fiebat, vt vigesies quater septem, hoc est, 168, dies, singulae cessarent. Porro Iudas Maccabaeus erat sacerdos primae classis Ioiarib. Quare templum à Graecis pollutum expiaturus, 24 familijs sacerdotum conuocatis, quae per triennium & amplius cessauerant, pristinum earum ordinem instaurauit, vt in Encaeniis templi primae familiae ex prisco ordine primus locus daretur: cuius functio accidit 22 Nouembris, biduo ante Encaenia. Annus tum erat 3785. Classis autem Abiae, quae ordine octaua erat, sequenti anno, post dies 49 ministerium suum aggressa est sabbato, quod congruebat decimae diei Ianuarij: à quo ad sabbatum 21 Iulij anno M.3946 fluxerunt anni 160, dies 192. Itaque die 28 Iulij impleti fuerunt dies ministerij Zachariae, quo die reuersus est in montana patriae suae. Luc.1.v.23. Conceptio ig. Iohannis incidit in hebdomadam, quae secuta est proxime post 28 diem Iulij. Inter 21 autem & 28 Iulij contigit εὐαγγελισμὸς[?] Zachariae Luc. 1. v.11. & seqq. Itaque natalis Iohannis contigerit circiter initium Aprilis vel finem Martij anno Mundi 3947. ὅτι ἐδει δέ-ξαι.
units.tr: John the Baptist is born about the beginning of April. For he was conceived after the twenty-eighth day of July, as is shown from 2. Paral. 24 and & Luke 1. v. 8, 9, 23. David divided the posterity of Aaron into twenty-four families, so that each worked in the temple for a whole week. Hence the duty of the individual families came round in a cycle every 168 days. These twenty-four families, from the encaenia of Judas Maccabeus to the destruction of the temple, remained intact and in mixed succession, as Josephus testifies, who, being a priest himself, could not have been ignorant of it. The heads of these families are called in the Gospel chief priests [ἀρχιερεῖς]. For these twenty-four classes of priests served in the temple, each for its own week. Whence it came about that every twenty-four times seven, that is 168, days each class ceased. Moreover, Judas Maccabeus was priest of the first class, that of Joiarib. Therefore, about to cleanse the temple polluted by the Greeks, he summoned the twenty-four families of priests, who had ceased for three years and more, and restored their former order, so that at the encaenia of the temple the first family was given the first place according to the ancient order. Its duty fell on 22 November, two days before the Encaenia. The year was then 3785. The class of Abijah, which was eighth in order, began its ministry in the following year, after 49 days, on a Sabbath, which fell on the tenth day of January. From this to the Sabbath of 21 July in the year 3946 there passed 160 years and 192 days. Thus on 28 July the days of Zechariah's ministry were completed, the day on which he returned to the hill country of his homeland, Luke 1. v. 23. The conception of John therefore fell in the week immediately following 28 July. Between 21 and 28 July the annunciation [εὐαγγελισμός] to Zechariah took place, Luke 1. v. 11 and following. So John's birth came about the beginning of April or the end of March in the year of the world 3947, "because it was fitting to receive" [ὅτι ἔδει δέξασθαι].

units.la: Christus Iesus nascitur circa finem Sept. vel initium Octobr. Hoc ita demonstratur. Si coceptio Ioan. demonstrari possit, potest & natalis Dñi nostri Iesu Christi inuestigari. At prius potest. Ergo & posterius. Ratio consequentiæ est: quia à conceptione Ioannis ad conceptionem Domini menses sunt quinque absoluti. Luc. 1. v. 26. Ad assumptionem quod attinet, clarum est ex præcedenti commate, coceptionem Iohannis posse demonstrari, si tempus explorari possit, quo Zacharias incensum obtulit. Quare si Iohannes natus est circa initium Aprilis vel finem Martii, Christus natus fuerit circa initium Octobris vel finem Septembris. Diem enim definire non est possibile. Tempus autem, quod vero proximum est, designari potest. Deinde Christus ad baptismum accessit trigesimo anno completo, & trigesimo vno ineunte, vt paulò post demonstrabitur. Incidit autem is annus in decimumquintum Tiberii Luc. 3. vers. 1. hoc est, in annum vrbis Romæ 781, qui est mundi 3978. Deductis triginta annis solidis, relinquitur annus 3948, vindicandus natali Christi. Porrò Christus natus est sub Augusto Cæsare, cum Quirinius esset præses Syriæ. Luc. 2. v. 1. Anno, inquam, 42 Augusti. Nam is concurrit cum anno M.3948 siue anno vrbis 751, qui est primus Quirinii, quem historia Romana vocat P. Sulpicium Quirinium, de quo Iosephus lib. 18. scribit hac in sententiam: Venit Quirinius in Syriam, missus à Cæsare (Augusto) vt illi prouinciæ ius diceret, & fortunarum censum haberet. Cæterum æra Christi Dionysiana siue vulgaris, quæ apud astronomos etiam obtinet, sumit initium à tertio anno Christi, qui est mundi 3950, qui habuit Cosl. C. Iulium Cæsarem & L.Æmilium Paulum.
units.tr: Christ Jesus is born about the end of September or the beginning of October. This is shown thus. If the conception of John can be demonstrated, the nativity of our Lord Jesus Christ can also be investigated. But the former can be done. Therefore the latter can too. The reason for this inference is that five full months pass from the conception of John to the conception of the Lord. Luke 1. v. 26. As for the assumption, it is clear from the preceding verse that the conception of John can be demonstrated if the time can be ascertained when Zechariah offered incense. Therefore, if John was born about the beginning of April or the end of March, Christ was born about the beginning of October or the end of September. For the day cannot be fixed, but the time, which is very nearly true, can be designated. Next, Christ came to baptism when his thirtieth year was complete and in his thirty-first year was beginning, as will be shown shortly. That year fell in the fifteenth year of Tiberius, Luke 3. vers. 1, that is, in the year 781 of the city of Rome, which is the 3978th of the world. Subtracting thirty full years, there remains the year 3948, which is to be claimed for Christ's birth. Moreover, Christ was born under Caesar Augustus, when Quirinius was governor of Syria, Luke 2. v. 1. In the forty-second year of Augustus, I say. For this coincides with the year of the world 3948, or the year 751 of the city, which is the first of Quirinius, whom Roman history calls Publius Sulpicius Quirinius, of whom Josephus, book 18, writes to this effect: Quirinius came into Syria, sent by Caesar (Augustus), to administer justice in that province and to take a census of property. Moreover, the Dionysian or common era of Christ, which also prevails among the astronomers, takes its beginning from the third year of Christ, which is the 3950th of the world, which had as consuls C. Julius Caesar and L. Aemilius Paulus.

units.la: Magi venerunt ad Christum. Matth. 2. v. 1. Venerunt, inquam, τοῦ Ἰησοῦ γεννηθέντ@, h.e. paulò ante nato. Ea namque vis est vocis Græcæ & locutionis, vt erudite obseruat Casaubonus exerc. 2. sect. 10. his verbis: Participii aorisli ea vis est, vt simul denotet celeritatem aduentus. Et paulò post: Istud igitur primum obseruemus, dixisse euangelistam, γεννηθέντος, non γεγεννημένος: hoc de perfecta multò etiam ante actione rectè vsurpatur: illud de paullo ante perfecta, & quasi adhuc pendente. Huc accedit particula ἰδού, ecce. Hinc colligere licet, magos non longè post natiuitatem Christi aduenisse. Chrysostomus author est, illos aduenisse quadragesimo die; alii, decimo tertio; Epiphanius, exacto biennio, quæ sententia merito vapulat. Porro si Christus natus est ineunte Octobri, hoc quoque mense aduenerunt Magi. Sed quia vulgo natiuitas Christi cofertur in 25 Decembris, ex consuetudine ecclesiæ Latinæ, aduentus Magorum collocatur in Ianuarium.
units.tr: The Magi came to Christ. Matt. 2. v. 1. They came, I say, after Jesus had been born [γεννηθέντος], that is, shortly before. For this is the force of the Greek word and construction, as Casaubon learnedly observes in Exercit. 2, sect. 10, in these words: The aorist participle has this force, that it denotes at once the speed of the arrival. And a little later: Let us therefore observe this first, that the evangelist said γεννηθέντος, not γεγεννημένος: the latter is rightly used of an action completed long before, the former of one just completed and as it were still hanging. To this is added the particle ἰδού, behold. Hence we may gather that the Magi arrived not long after the birth of Christ. Chrysostom holds that they arrived on the fortieth day; others on the thirteenth; Epiphanius after two full years, a view that rightly gets a beating. Further, if Christ was born in early October, the Magi also arrived in this month. But since the birth of Christ is commonly placed on 25 December, following the custom of the Latin Church, the arrival of the Magi is placed in January.

units.la: Christus 12 annorum in templo disputat. Luc. 2.
units.tr: Christ, at twelve years of age, disputes in the temple. Luke 2.

units.la: Christus baptizatur, anno ætatis trigesimo completo. Luc. 3. v. 23. vbi sic legimus: καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα ἀρχόμενος: quæ vetus interpres plane κατὰ τὸ ἀρχόμενος, siue ad verbum, ita vertit: Et ipse Iesus erat incipiens, quasi annorum triginta. Hic locus cum sit insignis, totaq; annorum Christi ratio ex illius interpretatione pendeat, paulò penitius illum inspiciemus. Et primò quidem vsus loquendi, ἦν ἀρχόμενος ἐτῶν τριάκοντα, videtur innuere, Christum initisse tum annum trigesimum. Sed particula ὡσεὶ est attendenda. Cùm enim apud Iudæos ministerii sacerdotalis ætas le-gitigitima fuerit annus trigesimus exactus, admodum probabile est, Dominum nostrum administerii suifunctionem non prius accessisse, quàm illum annum implesset. Quare ὡσεὶ necessariò erit Caph veritatis, non deminutionis, vt erudite obseruat Casaubonus exerc. 13. f. 9. Et ideo Syrus ita expressit, quasi legisset, αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὢν ἦν ὡσεὶ τριάκοντα ἐτῶν, Ipse Iesus existens erat quasi triginta annorum. Deinde Lucas hoc ipso capite versu 1. & 2. admodum accuratè designat tempus, quo ministerium suum Christus inchoauit. Sic enim ait: Anno autem decimoquinto Tiberii Cæsaris, Pontio Pilato procurante Iudææ, tetrarchâ Galileæ Herode, Philippo autem ipsius fratre tetrarchâ Ituræae & Trachonitidis regionis, & Lysaniâ Abilenes tetrarchâ, sub Pontificibus maximis, Annâ & Caiaphâ & c. Nimirum Euangelista aggressus descriptionem earum rerum, quas Dominus noster toto ministerii sui tempore gessit, temporis circumstantiam, quæ erat omnium maximi momenti, accuratè sic designauit, vt parem diligentiam alibi Scripturarum non sit deprehendere. Primò Imperatoris nomen ponitur, cuius erat tum per orbem terrarum diffusa & cognita potestas: nec solùm nomen, sed etiam annus Imperij illius, Anno 15 imperij Tiberij Cæsaris. Additur statim nomen Procuratoris Cæsaris, Procurante Pontio Pilato. Fuit is annus tertius currens procurationis Pilati. Parum hoc Lucæ visum, nisi etiam potestatum aliarum nomina addidisset, quæ tunc in Iudæâ & finitimis regionibus eminebãt. Amplissimum Herodis Magni siue Ascalonitæ regnum, mutatâ formâ, diuisum fuit ab Augusto tribus filiis Herodis in Ethnarchias tres, quarum maximam & cæteris duabus parem Archelaus, & eo pulso Cæsaris Procurator obtinebat: reliquas duas Archelai fratres, Herodes Antipas, & Philippus. Unde apparet, quæ sit causa, cur Imperatori statim subiecerit Lucas Procuratorem Iudææ; huic Tetrarchas: Tetrarchâ Galilææ Herode (is est Antipas) Philippo autem fratre eius Tetrarchâ Ituræa & Trachonitidis regionis. Postremo loco addit, Et Lysaniâ tetrarchâ Abilenâ. In hac tetrarchiâ non pauci Iudæi habitabant, in finibus Decapoleos, quò venisse Christum, atq; euangelium ibi prædicasse, & Decapolitanos plures ad ipsum venitasse, eique μαθητευσαν[?], eius discipulos factos esse, tecantur euangelistæ. Matth.4.v.25. Marc.5.v.20.c. 7.v.31. Atque hæc causa est, quòd huius quoque Lysaniæ mentio sit facta. Sequitur apud euangelistam, sub Pontificibus maximis, Annâ & Caiaphâ.
units.tr: Christ is baptized, having completed the thirtieth year of his age. Luke 3. v. 23, where we read thus: καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα ἀρχόμενος [And Jesus himself was about thirty years old when he began]. The old translator rendered the words κατὰ τὸ ἀρχόμενος, that is, word for word, thus: And Jesus himself was beginning, as it were of thirty years. Since this passage is notable, and the whole chronology of Christ's years depends on its interpretation, we shall examine it a little more closely. First, the manner of speaking, ἦν ἀρχόμενος ἐτῶν τριάκοντα, seems to suggest that Christ had then entered his thirtieth year. But the particle ὡσεί must be noted. For since among the Jews the legitimate age for priestly ministry was the completed thirtieth year, it is very probable that our Lord did not take up his office until he had completed that year. Therefore ὡσεί must necessarily be a kaph veritatis, of truth, not of diminution, as Casaubon learnedly observes in Exercit. 13, f. 9. And so the Syriac translator expressed it as if he had read, αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὢν ἦν ὡσεὶ τριάκοντα ἐτῶν, Jesus himself, being, was as it were of thirty years. Next, Luke, in this same chapter, verses 1 and 2, marks very precisely the time when Christ began his ministry. For he says: Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being procurator of Judea, Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Iturea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene, under the high priests Annas and Caiaphas, etc. Clearly, in undertaking the description of the things which our Lord did during the whole time of his ministry, the evangelist has marked the circumstance of time, which was of the greatest importance of all, so accurately that one cannot find equal care elsewhere in the Scriptures. First the name of the Emperor is set down, whose power was then spread and known throughout the world: and not only his name but also the year of his reign, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar. The name of Caesar's procurator is added at once, Pontius Pilate being procurator. That was the third current year of Pilate's procuratorship. This seemed too little to Luke unless he had also added the names of the other powers which then held sway in Judea and the neighbouring regions. The very great kingdom of Herod the Great, or the Ascalonite, was, its form having been changed, divided by Augustus among three sons of Herod into three ethnarchies. The largest of these, and equal to the other two, Archelaus held, and when he had been removed, Caesar's procurator held it; the other two were held by Archelaus' brothers, Herod Antipas and Philip. From this it appears why Luke placed the procurator of Judea immediately after the Emperor, and then the tetrarchs: Herod being tetrarch of Galilee (this is Antipas), and his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Iturea and Trachonitis. Lastly he adds, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene. In this tetrarchy not a few Jews lived, on the borders of the Decapolis, and the evangelists relate that Christ came there and preached the gospel, and that many of the Decapolitans came to him and became his disciples [μαθητευσαν]. Matt. 4. v. 25; Mark 5. v. 20; c. 7. v. 31. And this is the reason why mention is also made of this Lysanias. There follows in the evangelist, under the high priests Annas and Caiaphas.

units.la: Hic quæritur, cùm certù sit, plures eodem tempore summos sacerdotes esse non potuisse, quomodo hæc verba sint accipienda? Resp. Caiaphas anno 15 Tiberij fuit Pontifex Maximus, & in eâ dignitate perseuerauit vsq; ad aduentum Vitellij in Syriam, ut author est Iosephus lib. 18.c. 3. Totos igitur septem annos fuit hic Pontifex maximus, & aliquantò ampliùs. Quod attinet ad Annam, is fuit vicarius summi Pontificis. Constat enim ex Scripturâ, Pontificem maximum habuisse suum vicarium. Ille appellatus fuit Pontifex primus, & magnus, hic, secundus. Vide 2.Reg.25.verf.18. & 1. Paral.24. vbi Nadab & Abiu, Eleazar & Ithamar, coniunguntur. Porrò per hæc tempora, & insecutos deinceps annos plures, inter omnes archiatricos ordinis Pontifices præstitit Annas: qui & funtus erat ipse iam illâ suprema dignitate, & postea tot filios suos in eandem vidit euectos. Nihil itaque mirum, quòd Lucas & hic & in Actis Caiaphæ præponit Annam. Præponitur enim, non solùm vt socer genero, verùm etiam, vt is penes quem erat summa potestas in populo Iudaico. co. Atque ita tenemus sensum verborum Lucæ. Vbi hoc unum addimus, baptismum Christi incidere in Septembrem vel Octobrem: quia nempe Christus baptizatus est anno trigesimo primo ineunte.
units.tr: Here it is asked, since it is certain that several men could not be high priests at the same time, how these words are to be understood? Answer: Caiaphas was high priest in the fifteenth year of Tiberius and persevered in that dignity until Vitellius came into Syria, as Josephus testifies, Book 18, c. 3. So this Caiaphas was high priest for the whole of seven years, and somewhat more. As for Annas, he was the deputy of the high priest. For it is clear from Scripture that the high priest had his own deputy. He was called the first and great priest, the other the second. See 2 Kings 25, verse 18, and 1 Chronicles 24, where Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar are joined together. Moreover, throughout these times and the many years that followed, Annas stood out among all the chief priests of the order: he had himself held that supreme dignity, and afterwards saw so many of his sons raised to the same. Nothing is therefore surprising in Luke placing Annas before Caiaphas both here and in Acts. For he is placed first not only as father-in-law before son-in-law, but also as the one in whose hands the supreme power over the Jewish people lay. And so we hold the sense of Luke's words. To this we add only one thing: the baptism of Christ fell in September or October, because Christ was baptized at the beginning of his thirty-first year.

units.la: Christus celebravit primum pascha 14 Nisan. Iohan. 2. verf. 13. Quid egerit ab hoc paschate usque ad secundum, cognosci debet ex harmonia euangelistarum. Vetustissima res est in ecclesiâ, genus illud scriptionis, & piæ meditationis, quæ multorum occupauit industriam, in redigedis quatuor euangelistarum libris ad formam unius, qui omnia contineat suis locis digesta. Duæ sunt eius propositi vtilitates praecipuae: nam & consensus euangelistarum hoc pacto melius intelligitur, & memoriae consulitur mirifice. Petantur itaque ex huiusmodi scriptis ea quae à Christo gesta sunt. Nobis satis est hoc loco interualla pafchatū, quae Dominus celebrauit, indicasse.
units.tr: Christ celebrated the first Passover on 14 Nisan. John 2. verse 13. What he did from this Passover until the second ought to be learned from a harmony of the evangelists. It is a very ancient practice in the Church, a kind of writing and pious meditation, which has occupied the diligence of many, to reduce the four books of the evangelists to the form of one book, containing all things arranged in their proper places. There are two chief advantages of this plan: for in this way the agreement of the evangelists is better understood, and the memory is marvellously assisted. Let the things done by Christ be sought from writings of this kind. For our purpose here it is enough to have indicated the intervals between the Passovers which the Lord celebrated.

units.la: Christus anno aetatis 32 celebrat fecundum pascha. Luc. 6. v. 1. Iohan. 4. v. 35. 45.
units.tr: Christ, in the thirty-second year of his age, celebrates the second Passover. Luke 6. v. 1; John 4. v. 35, 45.

units.la: Christus anno aetat. 33 celebrat tertium pascha. Iohan. 6. v. 4. Marc. 7. v. 1.
units.tr: Christ, in the thirty-third year of his age, celebrates the third Passover. John 6. v. 4; Mark 7. v. 1.

units.la: Christus celebrat quartum pascha, an. aet. 34. Iohan. 7. v. 2. Luc. 9. v. 51.
units.tr: Christ celebrates the fourth Passover, in the thirty-fourth year of his age. John 7. v. 2; Luke 9. v. 51.

units.la: Christus celebrat quintum pascha, an. aet. 35. Mat. 26. Ioh. 11. Celebrat, inquam, pascha eo die, quo lex Mosis iubebat: cùm Iudaei illud transtulissent in sabbatum. Itaque Christus passus est ante pascha Iudaicum, ipseque tanquam verum pascha immolatus est eo die, quo Deus praeceperat pascha mactari. Vide supra in Computo.
units.tr: Christ celebrates the fifth Passover, in the thirty-fifth year of his age. Matt. 26; John 11. He celebrates it, I say, on the day on which the law of Moses commanded, although the Jews had transferred it to the sabbath.
