So Christ suffered before the Jewish Passover, and he himself was sacrificed as the true Passover on the day on which God had commanded the Passover to be slain. See above, in the Computation.

units.la: Christo in coelum sublato vndecim apostoli complent numerum sui collegii. Act. 1. Ad hunc annum refer gesta Act. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7.
units.tr: After Christ was taken up into heaven, the eleven apostles complete the number of their college. Acts 1. To this year refer the events of Acts 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.

units.la: Eunuchus & Saulus conuertuntur. Act. 8. 9.
units.tr: The eunuch and Saul are converted. Acts 8, 9.

units.la: Paulus Damasco in Arabiam proficiscitur.Gal. 1.pòst redit Damascum. Act. 9. 2. Corint. 11. Gal. 1. ac triennio post conuersionem venit Hierosolymam ad Petrum. Gal. 1.
units.tr: Paul sets out from Damascus into Arabia. Gal. 1. Afterwards he returns to Damascus. Acts 9; 2 Cor. 11; Gal. 1. And three years after his conversion he comes to Jerusalem to Peter. Gal. 1.

units.la: Paulus fugiens Iudæos,venit Cæsaream Phœniciæ,inde Tarsum Ciliciæ. Act. 9.
units.tr: Paul, fleeing from the Jews, comes to Caesarea of Phoenicia, and thence to Tarsus in Cilicia. Acts 9.

units.la: Cornelius conuertitur. Act. 10.
units.tr: Cornelius is converted. Acts 10.

units.la: Ecclesia Antiochena plantatur, ibique discipuli primùm vocantur Christiani. Act. 11.
units.tr: The church at Antioch is planted, and there the disciples are first called Christians. Acts 11.

units.la: Herodes Agrippa ecclesias persequitur, incarcerat Petrum, & Iacobum gladio occidit. Act. 12. Paulus & Barnabas peragrat varias provincias, ibique ecclesias fundant. Postea redeunt Antiochiam. Act. 13. 14. Quæ omnia collocanda sunt in an. 45. 46. &seqq. vsque ad an. 50.
units.tr: Herod Agrippa persecutes the churches, imprisons Peter, and kills James with the sword. Acts 12. Paul and Barnabas travel through various provinces, founding churches there. Afterwards they return to Antioch. Acts 13, 14. All these things are to be placed in the years 45, 46 and following, down to the year 50.

units.la: Apostoli concilium habent Hierosolymis. Act. 15. Obseruant docti, quatuor conciliorum mentionem fieri in Actis: primi, in quo eligitur Matthias, cap. 1. secundi, in quo diaconi instituuntur, cap. 6. tertii, in quo Iudaica instituta antiquantur, c. 15. quartum eliciunt ex historiâc. 21. de Pauli aduentu Hierosolymam.
units.tr: The apostles hold a council at Jerusalem. Acts 15. The learned observe that four councils are mentioned in Acts: the first, in which Matthias is chosen, ch. 1; the second, in which the deacons are instituted, ch. 6; the third, in which the Jewish institutions are abolished, ch. 15; and they deduce a fourth from the history, ch. 21, concerning Paul's arrival at Jerusalem.

units.la: Paulus cum rescripto apostolico redit Antiochiam. Act. 15. Hic est annus 14 ab eâ profectione, quæ facta est post ipsius conuersionem an. Christi 37. Gal. 1.
units.tr: Paul returns to Antioch with the apostolic letter. Acts 15. This is the fourteenth year from that departure, which took place after his conversion, in the year of Christ 37. Gal. 1.

units.la: Deinceps in Actis describitur peregrinatio Pauli. Hic itaque apostoli Pauli itinerarium paucis trademus. Et primò quidé Paulus Antiochiæ docet: postea secessione Barnabæ factâ & allecto Silâ Syriam & Siciliam peragrat. c. 15. venit Derben & Lystram: Timotheum sibi adsciscit & circumcidit. c. 16. Peragrant Phrygiam, Galatiam, Mysiam. Veniunt Troadem. Inde Samothracem,ac post Neapolim,& Philippos,vbi Lydia conuersa. ibid. Paulus & Silas per Amphipolim & Apolloniam veniunt Theffalonicam,Beroeam & Athenas.Act.17.poft Corinthum.Act.18.Hoc tempore fcripfit Paulus utramque epiftolam ad Theffalonicenses.
units.tr: Next, Acts describes the journeys of Paul. Here, then, we shall set out briefly the itinerary of the apostle Paul. First, Paul teaches at Antioch; afterwards, after the separation from Barnabas, and with Silas chosen as companion, he travels through Syria and Cilicia. ch. 15. He comes to Derbe and Lystra, takes Timothy to himself and circumcises him. ch. 16. They travel through Phrygia, Galatia and Mysia. They come to Troas. From there to Samothrace, and afterwards to Neapolis and Philippi, where Lydia is converted. ibid. Paul and Silas, through Amphipolis and Apollonia, come to Thessalonica, Berea and Athens. Acts 17. After Corinth. Acts 18. At this time Paul wrote both letters to the Thessalonians.

units.la: Paulus Corintho difcedit,poftquam ibi manfiffet an. 1.menf. 6.Act.18. Venit Ephefum, inde Caefaream,Hierofolymam, Antiochiam ; poftad Galatas & Phryges.ibid. Paulus biennium manet Ephefi,& amplius.Act.19.ibi pugnat cum beftiis, 1.Cor.4.
units.tr: Paul leaves Corinth, after he had stayed there one year and six months. Acts 18. He comes to Ephesus, then to Caesarea, Jerusalem and Antioch; afterwards to the Galatians and Phrygians. ibid. Paul remains at Ephesus for two years and more. Acts 19. There he fights with beasts. 1 Cor. 4.

units.la: Ephefo proficifcitur in Macedoniam. Act.20. peragrat ecclesias Graeciae: fcribit utramque ad Corinthios,Philippis ; priorem ad Timotheum Laodicea,posteriorem ad Titum Nicopoli.Redit Corinthum,indeque fcribit epiftolam adRomanos, poftquam euangelio omnia impleffet inde ab Hierofolymis usque ad Illyricum. Rom. 15.
units.tr: From Ephesus he sets out for Macedonia. Acts 20. He travels through the churches of Greece; he writes both letters to the Corinthians from Philippi; the first to Timothy from Laodicea, the second to Titus from Nicopolis. He returns to Corinth, and from there writes the letter to the Romans, after he had fulfilled the gospel everywhere from Jerusalem as far as Illyricum. Rom. 15.

units.la: Paulus Affo vehitur Mitylenam, Chium, Samum,Miletum, Coum, Rhodum,Pataram,Tyrum,Ptolemaida, Caefaream, ac tandem Hierofolymam. Ibi captus vinctusque fidei fuae ratione reddit.Act.21,22,23.Ducitur Caefaream.Act.23,24. 25,26. inde nau[?] vehitur Sidone cum Ariftarcho & Luca.Act.27.Sublegunt Cyprum, ftringunt oram Ciliciae & Pamphiliae. Veniunt Myra urbemLyciae ,ibiq; cofcendunt nauim Alexandrinam, qua vehuntur Gnidum verfus, indeque profecti veniunt in Cretam,Claudam, Melitam. Poft tres menfes veniunt Syracufas, Rhegium, Puteolos, ac per forum Appii & tres Tabernas tandemRomam.Act.28.
units.tr: Paul is carried by ship from Assos to Mitylene, Chios, Samos, Miletus, Cos, Rhodes, Patara, Tyre, Ptolemais and Caesarea, and at last to Jerusalem. There, having been seized and bound, he gives an account of his faith. Acts 21, 22, 23. He is led to Caesarea. Acts 23, 24, 25, 26. From there he sails to Sidon with Aristarchus and Luke. Acts 27. They sail under Cyprus and skirt the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia. They come to Myra, a city of Lycia, and there they board an Alexandrian ship, in which they sail towards Cnidus, and from there, setting out, they come to Crete, Clauda and Melita. After three months they come to Syracuse, Rhegium, Puteoli, and by the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns at last to Rome. Acts 28.

units.la: Paulus Roma fcribit varias epiftolas; videl.ad Galatas,Ephefios,Philippenfes, Coloffenfes,pofteriorem ad Timotheum ; item ad Philemonem & Hebraeos Romae manet biennium, & ann.60 exeunte liberatur exore leonis. 2.Tim.4. Anno mundi 4018. incipiente, 7. Septembris Hierosolyma cum templo exciditur per Romanos. Anno 4017. 14 Aprilis fuit obsessa, & inde vsque ad 7. Septembris horrenda quaeque perpessa, iuxta vaticinium Danielis cap. 9. Confer cum Matth. 24. versi. 15. Marc. 13. vers.14. Luc. 21. v.20.
units.tr: Paul writes various letters from Rome, namely to the Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians, the later one to Timothy; likewise to Philemon and to the Hebrews. He remains at Rome for two years, and at the end of the year 60 he is freed from the mouth of the lion. 2 Tim. 4. In the year of the world 4018, at its beginning, on 7 September, Jerusalem with the temple is destroyed by the Romans. In the year 4017, on 14 April, it was besieged, and from then until 7 September it suffered every horror, according to the prophecy of Daniel, ch. 9. Compare Matt. 24, v. 15; Mark 13, v. 14; Luke 21, v. 20.

units.la: Octauum intervallum ab anno Chri- sti 69 vsque ad an. 1359.
units.tr: The eighth interval, from the year of Christ 69 to the year 1359.

units.la: Johannes euangelista scribit apocalypsin, & statum ecclesiarum septem in Asiâ depingit. Apoc. 1. 2. 3.
units.tr: The evangelist John writes the Apocalypse, and portrays the state of the seven churches in Asia. Rev. 1, 2, 3.

units.la: Septem sigilla figurant statum ecclesiae post Iohannis excelsum, vsque ad an. Chr. 606. hoc modo. Quatuor priora sigilla denotant praedicatione euangelii, bellum, famem, & pestem, inde a morte Iohannis vsque ad Constantinum Magnum, siue an. Chr. 307.
units.tr: The seven seals represent the state of the church after the death of John, down to the year of Christ 606, in this way. The first four seals denote, from the death of John down to Constantine the Great, or the year of Christ 307, the preaching of the gospel, war, famine and pestilence.

units.la: Quintum sigillum describit statum martyrum, & ipsorum preces, quarum effectum ecclesia sensit tempore Constantini Mag. qui religionem Christianam stabiliuit.
units.tr: The fifth seal describes the state of the martyrs and their prayers, the effect of which the church felt in the time of Constantine the Great, who established the Christian religion.

units.la: Sextum sigillum notat perturbationem ecclesiae & politiae post Constantini M. tempora, vsque ad ann. Chr. 606. Totum hoc tempus fuit bellorum & hæreseon [?] feracissimum. Nam in politiâ cælum terrae miscuerunt Persae, Hunni, Gothi, & aliae nationes. In ecclesiâ episcopi Romani, & alii doctores, abusi privilegiis a Constantino M. concessis, veluti stellae e cælo ceciderunt, & terram cum cælo, hoc est, secularem potestatem cum spiritualibus, & falsa veris permiscuerunt. Apoc.7.
units.tr: The sixth seal marks the disturbance of the church and the state after the time of Constantine the Great, down to the year of Christ 606. The whole of this time was most fertile of wars and heresies. For in the state the Persians, Huns, Goths and other nations shook heaven and earth. In the church the Roman bishops and other teachers, abusing the privileges granted by Constantine the Great, fell like stars from heaven, and mixed earth with heaven, that is, secular power with spiritual, and false things with true. Rev. 7.

units.la: Sigillum septimum aperitur, quod ex se parit septem tubas, quarum operatio est ab an. Chr. 606 ad an. 1517.
units.tr: The seventh seal is opened, which from itself brings forth seven trumpets, whose operation runs from the year of Christ 606 to the year 1517.

units.la: Primatuba produxit prodigiosam grandinem,
units.tr: The first trumpet brought forth a prodigious hail,

units.la: [Note: text ends at a full line; catchword "igni" stands below it.] igni & sanguine permixtam, h. e. turbulentum ingenium Phocæ, Papæ Bonifacii III. & Mahomedis, qui tres constituunt Cerberum tricipitem, ex quo aliquot flammæ noxiæ prosilierunt, ab anno 606 ad 650.
units.tr: mixed with fire and blood, that is, the turbulent disposition of Phocas, of Pope Boniface III, and of Mahomet, who together make up a three-headed Cerberus, from which several harmful flames leapt forth, from the year 606 to 650.

units.la: Secunda tuba corrupit mare, id est, doctrinam euangelii in oriente & occidente variis corruptelis infecit, ab an. 650 ad 730.
units.tr: The second trumpet corrupted the sea, that is, it infected the doctrine of the gospel in East and West with various corruptions, from the year 650 to 730.

units.la: Tertia tuba introduxit absinthium disputationum idololatricarum, ab anno 730 ad 800.
units.tr: The third trumpet introduced the wormwood of idolatrous disputations, from the year 730 to 800.

units.la: Quarta tuba peperit eclipsin solis, lunæ, & stellarum, i. e. donorum ecclesiasticorum.
units.tr: The fourth trumpet produced an eclipse of the sun, moon and stars, that is, of the ecclesiastical gifts.

units.la: Quinta tuba produxit locustas otiosas & inutiles, i. e. varios monachorum ordines.
units.tr: The fifth trumpet brought forth idle and useless locusts, that is, the various orders of monks.

units.la: Sexta tuba genuit equites, h. e. prælatos ecclesiasticos, qui secularibus delectantur, & sunt velut equites in regno antichristi. His adde Summistas, Scholasticos, & alios parasitos curiæ Romanæ.
units.tr: The sixth trumpet begot horsemen, that is, ecclesiastical prelates, who delight in secular things, and are like horsemen in the kingdom of antichrist. To these add the Summists, the Schoolmen, and other parasites of the Roman court.

units.la: Nonum interuallum, inde ab anno Christi 1359 ad an. 1694.
units.tr: Ninth interval, from the year of Christ 1359 to the year 1694.

units.la: Septima tuba sonuit tempore Petrarchæ, Wiclefi, Huffi, & aliorum, qui bestiæ cotradixerunt, ab an. 1359 ad an. 1517.
units.tr: The seventh trumpet sounded in the time of Petrarch, Wycliffe, Huss and others who opposed the beast, from the year 1359 to the year 1517.

units.la: Septem phialæ effunduntur: e quib. prima, circa an. Chr. 1517. super terram effudit ulcus malum & noxium: prædicatione euangelii excitando pessima animorum ulcera, iram, odium, livorem, surorem, in antichristi ministris, adversus euangelium, eiusque confessores, qui variis ulceribus, h. e. plagis sunt affecti ob constantem suam confessionem.
units.tr: The seven vials are poured out. Of these, the first, about the year of Christ 1517, poured out upon the earth a malignant and harmful ulcer: by the preaching of the gospel it stirs up the worst sores of minds, anger, hatred, envy and rage, against the ministers of antichrist, against the gospel and its confessors, who are afflicted with various ulcers, that is, with wounds, on account of their steadfast confession.

units.la: Secunda phiala effudit super mare, h. e. doctrinam euangelii, colluviem concil. Trid.
units.tr: The second vial poured out upon the sea, that is, upon the doctrine of the gospel, the filth of the Council of Trent.

units.la: Tertia phiala effundet in flumina & fontes aquarum, h. e. primipilares antichristi ministros, sanguinem siue bellum.
units.tr: The third vial will pour out into the rivers and springs of waters, that is, upon the chief ministers of antichrist, as blood or war.

units.la: Quarta phiala effundet super solum, h. e. euan-gelium Christi, clariorem lucem, quâ fiet, ut etjam Judaei conuertantur. Rom. 11.
units.tr: The fourth vial will pour out upon the sun, that is, upon the gospel of Christ, a clearer light, by which it will come about that even the Jews will be converted. Rom. 11.

units.la: Quinta phiala effundet super thronum bestiae tenebras, hoc est, obscurabit ipsius gloriam.
units.tr: The fifth vial will pour out darkness upon the throne of the beast, that is, it will obscure its glory.

units.la: Sextaphiala exsiccabit aquas Euphratis, h. e. animabit reges orientis, ut destruant Babylonem occidentis.
units.tr: The sixth vial will dry up the waters of the Euphrates, that is, it will stir up the kings of the east to destroy Babylon of the west.

units.la: Decimum interuallum, ab an. Christi 1694. usque ad bellum Gogicum.
units.tr: Tenth interval, from the year of Christ 1694 until the war of Gog.

units.la: Postquam sexta phiala erit effusa, incipient mille anni Apoc. 20. v. 2. & seqq.
units.tr: When the sixth vial has been poured out, the thousand years will begin. Apoc. 20. v. 2 and following.

units.la: Elapsis mille annis incipiet bellum Gog & Magog. Apoc. 20. v. 7. 8. 9.
units.tr: When the thousand years have elapsed, the war of Gog and Magog will begin. Apoc. 20. v. 7, 8, 9.

units.la: Septimaphiala effundetur in aerem, descendetque ignis e coelo, qui consumat Gog & Magog: & tunc erit acta mundi fabula. Apocal. 20. vers. 9. 10. & seqq.
units.tr: The seventh vial will be poured out into the air, and fire will come down from heaven, which will consume Gog and Magog; and then the play of the world will be finished. Apoc. 20. vers. 9, 10 and following.

units.la: LII.
units.tr: LII.

units.la: PROSOPOGRAPHIA SACRA.
units.tr: SACRED PROSOPOGRAPHY.

units.la: I. Prosopographia sacra est pars historiae sacrae de viris & foeminis illustrib. V.&N.T. Tres sunt veluti columnae historiarum, circumstantia videl. personarum, locorum, & temporum, quae totidem partibus explicantur, utputa prosopographia, topographia, & chronologia. Ex his ultimam vide paulo ante traditam: nunc primam persequemur, vel potius adumbrabimus, idque ex sacris literis. Ubi accusanda est impia ignauia illorum, qui malunt Themistoclis, Scipionis, Alexandri M. & aliorum ethnicorum, quàm Abrahami, Dauidis, Ezechiæ, & aliorum sanctorum pericula, sermones, victorias, errores, lapsus, facinora, cognoscere.
units.tr: I. Sacred prosopography is the part of sacred history concerning illustrious men and women of the Old and New Testaments. There are three pillars of histories, namely the circumstances of persons, places and times, which are explained in as many parts: prosopography, topography and chronology. Of these, the last was set out a little earlier; now we shall pursue, or rather sketch out, the first, and that from the sacred letters. Here we must censure the impious laziness of those who prefer to learn of the dangers, speeches, victories, errors, lapses and deeds of Themistocles, Scipio, Alexander the Great and other heathens, rather than those of Abraham, David, Hezekiah and other saints.

units.la: II. Prosopographia sacra diuidi potest in decem sectiones, hoc ordine.
units.tr: II. Sacred prosopography can be divided into ten sections, in this order.

units.la: Prima est libertatis ecclesiæ inuictæ: secunda, ecclesiæ per miseriam propagatæ: tertia, ecclesiæ à ducibus gubernatæ: quarta, regijecclesiæ imperii: quinta, regni Israëlitici, seu Samaritani: sexta, regni Iudaici, seu Hierosolymitani: septima, ecclesiæ in Babylone exulis, atque restitutæ: octaua, ecclesiæ à regibus Asiaticis vexatæ: nona, gentium ecclesiæ aduersantium: decima, ecclesiæ nascentis in N.T.
units.tr: The first concerns the invincible liberty of the Church; the second, the Church propagated through misery; the third, the Church governed by leaders; the fourth, the royal Church of the empire; the fifth, the kingdom of Israel, or Samaria; the sixth, the kingdom of Judah, or Jerusalem; the seventh, the Church exiled in Babylon and restored; the eighth, the Church harassed by the kings of Asia; the ninth, the Gentile churches opposing it; the tenth, the Church nascent in the New Testament.

units.la: III. Prosopographia tempore libertatis ec- clesiæ inuictæ sic habet ex Genesi.
units.tr: III. Prosopography in the time of the invincible liberty of the Church runs thus, from Genesis.

units.la: 1. Adam, homo protoplastus, decipitur fraude diaboli, sed à Deo accipit consolationem ipsius clementiâ plenam, & in ecclesiâ docet annis 930.
units.tr: 1. Adam, the first-formed man, is deceived by the fraud of the devil, but from God he receives a consolation full of his clemency, and he teaches in the Church for 930 years.

units.la: 2. Eua, ipso Deo authore & pronubo iunêta fuit Adamo, è quo sumta erat.
units.tr: 2. Eve, joined to Adam by God himself as author and giver in marriage, was taken from him.

units.la: 3. Cain, primus ex homine natus homo, singulare parentum gaudium, in adolescentiâ coepit agrum colere, tandem factus fratricida. Condidit primam vrbem, quâ vocauit de nomine filii sui Chanoc.
units.tr: 3. Cain, the first man born of man, a singular joy to his parents, began in youth to till the field, and at last became a fratricide. He founded the first city, which he called after the name of his son Enoch.

units.la: 4. Abel apud parentes minùs gratiosus, quàm Cain, respicitur & curatur à Deo.
units.tr: 4. Abel, less favoured by his parents than Cain, is regarded and cared for by God.

units.la: 5. Seth, tertius Adami filius, maximum parentis afflictissimi solatium fuit. Cùm enim alterum cæde, alterum fugâ amisset, huius ortu recreatus fuit mirificè. Hic patris disciplinâ sanctâ imbutus, promissionis defensoracerrimus, & caput ecclesiæ nascentis fuit annis 912.
units.tr: 5. Seth, the third son of Adam, was the greatest comfort of his most afflicted parent. For when he had lost one son by murder and the other by flight, he was wonderfully restored by this one's birth. Imbued with his father's holy discipline, a most staunch defender of the promise, and head of the nascent Church, he lived 912 years.

units.la: 6. Enos, filius Sethi, quæ de Deo ab auo atque patre intra priuatos parietes didicerat, extra domum extulit, & cum multis aliis publicè communicauit, maiculè se opponendo Cainicæ ecclesiæ, hypocriticæ illi & immane sobolescenti.
units.tr: 6. Enos, son of Seth, brought out of the house what he had learned of God from his grandfather and father within private walls, and publicly communicated it with many others, opposing himself strongly to the Cainite Church, hypocritical and growing monstrously.

units.la: 7. Enoch, trinepos Serhi, doctor ecclesiae verae, & propheta excellentissimus fuit. Per fidem translatus fuit ipso corpore ad vitae melioris gaudia: exemplo manifesto posteris ie isto[?], aliam superesse vitam.
units.tr: 7. Enoch, great-grandson of Seth, was a teacher of the true Church and a most excellent prophet. Through faith he was translated in body to the joys of a better life, a manifest example to posterity that another life remains.

units.la: 8. Lamechus impius, filius Methusaelis, de Caini stirpe, fuit membrum ecclesiae hypocriticae, & author digan[?]. Eius filius Iabal, fuit inventor tentoriorum & pecuariae; Iubal, organorum musicorum: Thubalcain, artis ferrariae.
units.tr: 8. Lamech the impious, son of Methuselah, of the stock of Cain, was a member of the hypocritical Church and the author of bigamy. His son Jabal was the inventor of tents and herding; Jubal, of musical instruments; Tubal-cain, of the art of the smith.

units.la: 9. Mathusalem fuit omnium mortalium μακροβιώτ[?]α-τ[?].
units.tr: 9. Methuselah was the longest-lived of all mortals [μακροβιώτατος].

units.la: 10. Lamechus pius, filius Mathusalae, trinepos Enochi, digna fuit virorum summorum proles, pater Noachi, & spiritu prophetico venerabilis.
units.tr: 10. Lamech the pious, son of Methuselah, great-grandson of Enoch, was a worthy offspring of the most eminent men, the father of Noah, and venerable for his prophetic spirit.

units.la: 11. Noa, Deo charus, mortalium miserrimus & felicissimus fuit. Nam ante diluvium conspexit maximum Dei contemtum: in diluvio videt iram Dei & omnium rerum interitum, ipse tamen cum suis salvus in arca: post diluvium est quasi alter Adam utpote seminarium alterum humani generis; perfert ludibrium Chami, plantat vineas, detestatur temeritatem ædificantium turrim.
units.tr: 11. Noah, dear to God, was the most wretched and the most fortunate of mortals. For before the flood he beheld the greatest contempt of God; in the flood he saw God's wrath and the destruction of all things, yet he himself was saved with his own family in the ark; after the flood he is almost a second Adam, a second seedbed of the human race; he endures the mockery of Ham, plants vineyards, and detests the rashness of those who built the tower.

units.la: 12. Cham, Noae filius natu minimus, fuit turpis apostata & homo facinorosus. Habitavit meridiem versus, & ab eo Æthiopes, Ægyptij, Numidae, Mauri, & omninò Afri deducti sunt.
units.tr: 12. Ham, the youngest son of Noah, was a foul apostate and a wicked man. He dwelt towards the south, and from him the Ethiopians, Egyptians, Numidians, Moors and, in general, the Africans are descended.

units.la: 13. Iapheth, Noae filius secundò genitus, locum in ecclesia Dei, & possessionem terrarum amplissimam accepit. Ab ipsius posteritate gentes hae bellicosae, Medi, Scythae, Sauromatae, Thraces, Germani, Itali & Iberi descendunt, qui sedes in occidente & septentrione potentissimas fixerunt.
units.tr: 13. Japheth, Noah's second-born son, received a place in the Church of God and a very ample possession of lands. From his posterity descend these warlike peoples: the Medes, Scythians, Sarmatians, Thracians, Germans, Italians and Iberians, who established the most powerful seats in the west and north.

units.la: 14. Sem, Noae filius natu maximus, hoc à Deo privilegium accepit, ut ecclesia apud ipsius posteritatem maneret, & ex ipso Messias nasceretur. Hic est Melchisedec, rex Salem. Ab illo populi orientales, homines sapientissimi, Chaldaei, Assyrij, Persae, Syri, Armenij, & Bactriani, ortum trahunt: inter quos ecclesia Dei longo tempore hospitium habuit. Videris hac de re Thesaurum chronologiæ nostræ.
units.tr: 14. Shem, Noah's eldest son, received from God this privilege, that the Church should remain among his posterity and that the Messiah should be born from him. This is Melchizedek, king of Salem. From him trace their origin the peoples of the east, most wise men: Chaldeans, Assyrians, Persians, Syrians, Armenians and Bactrians; among whom the Church of God had lodging for a long time. On this matter see our Thesaurus of Chronology.

units.la: 14. Nimrod, nepos Chami, vir audax & strenuus, initium dedit monarchiis, quas Deus texit, ut in iis maneret aliquis nidulus ecclesiæ.
units.tr: 14. Nimrod, grandson of Ham, a bold and vigorous man, gave a beginning to monarchies, which God wove so that in them some little nest of the Church might remain.

units.la: 15. Heber, pronepos Semi, suis maioribus non dissimilis, doctrinam de Deo & Messiâ pure casteque propagauit, & pro eâ propugnauit. Hinc, qui ad piam ecclesiam se aggregarunt, ab eius nomine, multis setulis Hebræi sunt denominati.
units.tr: 15. Eber, great-grandson of Shem, not unlike his ancestors, purely and chastely propagated the doctrine concerning God and the Messiah, and fought for it. Hence those who joined themselves to the pious Church were named Hebrews from his name, with many little bristles.

units.la: 16. Phaleg, filius Heberi, paternæ auitæque doctrinæ auditor & propagator, eo tempore natus est, & facto nomen eius conuenit, quo Deus, linguis confusis, dispersit agmen Nimrodicum, in turri Babylonicâ extruendâ occupatum. Maxima tum clades illata est ecclesiæ, & passim creuit superstitio multiplex. Quemadmodum autem homines, pœnâ confusionis linguarum in varias gentes, ex vnâ vibe distractifunt: ita dono intelligentiæ linguarum, omnes nationes & populi in vnam ciuitatem, quæ est ecclesia, rursus congregati sunt, Act. 2.
units.tr: 16. Peleg, son of Eber, a hearer and propagator of his father's and forefathers' doctrine, was born at the time, and his name fits, when God, having confused the languages, scattered the host of Nimrod, which was occupied in building the tower of Babel. Then the greatest disaster was inflicted on the Church, and everywhere manifold superstition grew. But just as men, by the punishment of the confusion of tongues, were scattered from one city into various nations, so by the gift of understanding tongues, all nations and peoples have been gathered again into one city, which is the Church. Acts 2.

units.la: 17. Thara, trinepos Heberi, pater Abrahami, habitauit in Vr Chaldæorum inter idololatras, & speciosâ illorum religione in errorem inductus fuit. E Chaldæâ migrauit cum filio, nuru, & nepote in Mesopotamiam, & in urbe Haran, quam posteri Carras nominarunt, mortuus est.
units.tr: 17. Terah, great-grandson of Eber, father of Abraham, dwelt in Ur of the Chaldeans among idolaters, and was led into error by their specious religion. He migrated from Chaldea with his son, daughter-in-law and grandson into Mesopotamia, and died in the city of Haran, which later generations called Carrhae.

units.la: 18. Nahor, filius Tharæ, mansit in Mesopotamiâ, & eruditus à fratre suo Abrahamo, retinuit aliquid de promisso Messiâ. Eius neptis fuit Rebecca. Bileam putatur fuisse ex eius progenie.
units.tr: 18. Nahor, son of Terah, remained in Mesopotamia, and, taught by his brother Abraham, retained something of the promised Messiah. Rebecca was his granddaughter. Balaam is thought to have come from his progeny.

units.la: 19. Abraham, ex idololatrâ fit pater credentium. Eius domus fuit velut hospitium angelorum. Fuit homo Deo quasi intimus, pater magnus plurimarum gentium, charus Melchisedeco.
units.tr: 19. Abraham, from an idolater, becomes the father of believers. His house was like a hospice of angels. He was a man almost intimate with God, the great father of very many nations, dear to Melchizedek.

units.la: 20. Sara, vxor Abrahami, virum sponte in exilium sequitur: propter eximiam formam bis rapta, semel in Ægypto, iterum in Palæstinâ, salua pudicitiâ semper restituitur. Decus matronarum, propter pietatem: & sexus sui ornamentum, propter mariti obseruantiam: ab apostolo Petro exemplum omnib. mulierib. proponitur.
units.tr: 20. Sarah, wife of Abraham, voluntarily follows her husband into exile; on account of her outstanding beauty she was twice carried off, once in Egypt and again in Palestine, and always restored with her chastity intact. An ornament of matrons on account of her piety, and the adornment of her sex on account of her obedience to her husband, she is set before all women as an example by the apostle Peter.

units.la: 21. Loth, Tharæ nepos, Saræ frater, patrui sui Abrahami comes indiuiduus, bona cum eo malaque tolerauit. Ab hoc Moabitæ & Ammonitæ, nominis Hebræi hostes sempiterni, sunt procreati.
units.tr: 21. Lot, son of Terah and brother of Sarah, was the inseparable companion of his uncle Abraham and shared with him both good and ill fortune. From him descended the Moabites and Ammonites, everlasting enemies of the Hebrew name.

units.la: 22. Hagar, Ægyptia, in domo Abrahami seruiuit seruitutem; iuncta thalamo domini sui, procreauit ei Ismaelem. In fugâ, consilium; in exilio, solatium & auxilium ab angelo accepit.
units.tr: 22. Hagar, the Egyptian, served as a slave in Abraham's house; joined to her master's bed, she bore him Ishmael. In her flight she received counsel, and in her exile comfort and help from an angel.

units.la: 23. Ifmaël, ex serua filius Abrahami, cum insolesceret, iniuste quæsita hæreditate excidit: aliis formidabilis, ipse nullius metuens vires aut potentiam, duodecim principes genuit. Ab illo Midianitæ & Arabes, & postea Saraceni, ducere se prosapiam gloriantur.
units.tr: 23. Ishmael, son of Abraham by a slave woman, grew arrogant and was cut off from the inheritance he had wrongly sought. He was feared by others, yet he himself feared the strength or power of no one, and he begot twelve princes. The Midianites and Arabs, and afterwards the Saracens, boast that they trace their descent from him.

units.la: 24. Abimelech, rex Palæstinorum in Gerar, primum vxorem Abrahami, deinde Isaaci, putans vtriusque sororem esse, in suam familiam transtulit: sed errore suo cognito, maritis sine infamiâ atque morâ, non tamen sine exprobratione simulationis & silentii noxii, eas reddidit. Tempore difficillimo famis, hospes & nutritor ecclesiæ fuit.
units.tr: 24. Abimelech, king of the Philistines in Gerar, took Abraham's wife, and later Isaac's, into his household, thinking that each woman was the sister of her husband. Once his error was recognised, he returned them to their husbands without dishonour and without delay, but not without rebuke for the pretence and the harmful silence. In the most difficult time of famine he was a host and nourisher of the Church.

units.la: 25. Mambres, & Ephron, pii hospites ecclesiæ Dei, & auditores ac socii Abrahami fuerunt.
units.tr: 25. Mamre and Ephron, pious hosts of the Church of God, were hearers and companions of Abraham.

units.la: 26. Eliezer, Damascenus, seruus atriensis & procurator domus Abrahami, primò propter sterile dominiconiugium putatus fuit hæres extraneus; siue non suus, vt ICtiloquuntur:postea legatus Abrahami factus, ad quærendam filio Isaaco vxorem, ea legatione perfunctus est singulari fide, pietate, industriâ.
units.tr: 26. Eliezer of Damascus, the steward and manager of Abraham's household, was at first thought to be the heir, because the marriage was childless; he was an outsider, not his own son, as the jurists put it. Afterwards he was made Abraham's envoy to seek a wife for his son Isaac, and he discharged that mission with singular faithfulness, piety and diligence.

units.la: 27. Bathuel, Syrus, filius Nachoris, Rebeccam filiam benè educatam, Isaaco absenti despondit, magnificè peractis sponsalibus.
units.tr: 27. Bethuel the Syrian, son of Nahor, betrothed his well-brought-up daughter Rebekah to the absent Isaac, and the betrothal was celebrated splendidly.

units.la: 28. Isaac, e corporis emortuis præter naturæ atque ætatis rationem & ordinem natus, patri suo Abrahamo vsque adiugulum pâret. Varias acerbitates expertus est. Nam Abimelech iplum expulit Gerare, importunus filius Efau priuatam quietem ipsi turbauit, caecitas ipsum in senectute afflixit, & sedes incerta in peregrinatione molestiam non exiguam creauit.
units.tr: 28. Isaac, born from bodies as good as dead, contrary to the order and reason of nature and of age, obeyed his father Abraham even to the point of being bound for sacrifice. He experienced various hardships. Abimelech drove him out of Gerar; the troublesome son of Esau disturbed his private peace; blindness afflicted him in old age; and an uncertain dwelling as a sojourner caused him no small distress.

units.la: 29. Rebecca, vxor Isaaci, fuit virgo multae virtutis & formae: iuncta viro, cum esset sterilis, mariti precibus & fide ardente prolem impetrauit, vnoque partu gemellos est enixa. Haec matrona virum senem & caecum curauit fideliter, filium periclitantem seruauit pie, nurus acerbas longo tempore tulit moderate, familiam copiosam gubernauit prudenter: suae domus columen, & ecclesiae lumen.
units.tr: 29. Rebekah, wife of Isaac, was a maiden of great virtue and beauty. Joined to her husband while she was barren, she obtained offspring through his prayers and her ardent faith, and at a single birth she bore twins. This matron faithfully cared for her old and blind husband, dutifully preserved her son when he was in danger, patiently bore her harsh daughters-in-law for a long time, and prudently governed a large household: the pillar of her house and the light of the Church.

units.la: 30. Esau, Isaaci filius, corpore pilosus & rufus (unde ipsi nomen Edom) moribus truculentus & vehemens, studiis venator & agricola, patri charissimus, excidit iure primogenitura, & fugatis Horræis montana Seiris vi occupauit. Ab ipso gens Idumæorum, populo Dei semper infesta, nomen atque opes comparauit.
units.tr: 30. Esau, son of Isaac, hairy in body and ruddy (whence his name Edom), fierce and violent in character, a hunter and farmer by pursuit and very dear to his father, lost the right of the firstborn. Having driven out the Horites, he seized the mountain of Seir by force. From him the nation of the Edomites, always hostile to the people of God, acquired its name and wealth.

units.la: 31. Iob, ex posteritate Nachoris, vel, vt aliis placet, Efaui, inter Idumæos infideles innocenter, inter Vsitas impios, sine reprehensione vixit. Omnibus suis bonis & liberis amissis, variisq; calamitatibus exercitus, tandem aerumnarum liber atque vacuus, ea bona, quae amiserat, dupliciter recepit, & sobole formosiore auctus fuit, non tamen, vt in caeteris bonis, duplicata, quia prior in Dei manibus adhuc viuebat, quamuis mundo extincta fuerat.
units.tr: 31. Job, of the posterity of Nahor or, as others prefer, of Esau, lived blamelessly among the faithless Idumeans and without reproach among the impious Uzites. Having lost all his goods and children and been tried by various calamities, at last he was freed from his miseries. He received back doubled the goods he had lost and was blessed with more beautiful offspring. Yet the children were not doubled as the goods were, because the earlier ones were still alive in God's hands, though they had been extinguished to the world.

units.la: 32. Laban, Syrus, Iacobi auunculus, homo turpis auaritia, calliditate, & perfidia, nullo lucro satiatur, nulla copia expletur, nullo beneficio mitigatur.
units.tr: 32. Laban, the Syrian, uncle of Jacob, a man foul with greed, cunning and treachery, is never satisfied by any gain, never filled by any abundance, and never softened by any kindness.

units.la: 33. Lea, Labanis filia, amitino suo Iacobo astute tradita, propter lippitudinem minus chara marito, propter fecunditatem sorori inuisa est. Ipsa vero contemtum & inuidiam ferre submisse. Mater Iudae fuit, a quo & tribus peculiaris, & tota gens Iudæa appellatur: & ex eius sanguine atque stirpe tandem Messias nascitur.
units.tr: 33. Leah, daughter of Laban, was cunningly given to her cousin Jacob. Because of her weak eyes she was less dear to her husband, and because of her fertility she was hated by her sister. She herself bore the contempt and envy meekly. She was the mother of Judah, from whom the tribe and the whole Jewish nation take their name, and from whose blood and stock the Messiah was at last born.

units.la: 34. Dina, Leæ filia, leuitate puellari seipsam pudicitiâ, multos mortales, putâ Sichemitas, vitâ spoliauit. Hanc suo agnato Iobo[?] datam postea coniugem Philo scribit.
units.tr: 34. Dina, daughter of Leah, by girlish levity deprived herself of chastity and many mortals, namely the Shechemites, of their lives. Philo writes that she was afterwards given as wife to her kinsman Jobo.

units.la: 35. Rachel, filia Labanis, primo aspectu fuit amata à Iacobo, qui pro ipsâ seruiuit annis quatuordecim.
units.tr: 35. Rachel, daughter of Laban, was loved by Jacob at first sight, and for her he served fourteen years.

units.la: IV. Prosopographia, tempore ecclesiæ per miseriam, in Ægypto & deserto, propagatæ, ex Genesi, Exodo, & reliquis libris Mosè, itemque ex libro Iosuæ, sic habet.
units.tr: IV. Prosopography, which was propagated in the time of the Church's distress, in Egypt and in the desert, drawn from Genesis, Exodus and the other books of Moses, and likewise from the book of Joshua, runs as follows.

units.la: 36. Iacob, Isaaci filius, homo placidus & prudens, à fratre securo ius primogenituræ emit, & benedictionem à patre consequitur astu matris. Fuit vir Deocharus[?] & prope familiaris, qui post varias calamitates tandem inedia coactus in Ægyptum venit: vnde post mortem fuit transportatus in terram Canaan, & ad avi patrisque monumenta tumulatus: cum quibus de nascituro[?] Messiâ ex ipsorum lumbis, promissiones lætas audiverat. Vnde Deus, cùm suam magnificentiam & veritatem fidelibus in V. T. voluit declarare, se Deum Abrahami, Isaaci, & Iacobi nominauit.
units.tr: 36. Jacob, son of Isaac, a calm and prudent man, bought the right of the firstborn from his unsuspecting brother and obtained the blessing from his father by his mother's craft. He was a man dear to God and almost a familiar friend. After various calamities, he was at last compelled by hunger to come into Egypt. After his death he was carried back into the land of Canaan and buried among the tombs of his grandfather and father, with whom he had heard joyful promises concerning the Messiah who was to be born from their loins. Hence God, when he wished to declare his magnificence and truth to the faithful in the Old Testament, named himself the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

units.la: 37. Ruben, primogenitus Iacobi filius, thoro patris inquinato, ius primogenituræ amisit, & pœnam incestus luit in totâ posteritate. Nam tribus illa numero semper exigua, & viribus minùs potens cæteris fuit. Nati sunt ex hac tribu propheta Ioel, & vidua Iudith.
units.tr: 37. Reuben, firstborn son of Jacob, defiled his father's bed and so lost the right of the firstborn, and he bore the penalty of incest throughout his whole posterity. For that tribe always remained small in number and less powerful in strength than the others. From this tribe were born the prophet Joel and the widow Judith.

units.la: 38. Simeon, & Leui, homines audacissimi, & patri suo improbè aduersi, nimiâ iracundiâ sororis stuprum crudeliùs vindicant, violato fœdere cum Sichemitis inito. In fratre Iosepho occidendo primas immanitatis partes ferunt. Eorum posteritas inops & vaga perpetuò fuit. Simeon partem possessionis in tribu Iudæ consecutus est: Leui proprium nihil omninò habuit, eique exautorato stirps Iosephi successit. Ex hac tamen tribu Leui despicatissima, Deus sibi ministros & sacerdotes legit. Post hos autem filios Iacobus pater nulli amplius filio imprecatur, quia misericordia Dei praeponderat iudicio. Ex tribu Leui nati sunt Moses, Samuel, Ieremias, Ezechiel, Zacharias, & Iohannes Baptista.
units.tr: 38. Simeon and Levi, most audacious men and wickedly opposed to their father, avenged their sister's rape with excessive cruelty, breaking the covenant they had made with the Shechemites. They bear the chief share of the savagery in the killing of their brother Joseph. Their posterity was always poor and wandering. Simeon obtained a portion of possession in the tribe of Judah. Levi had no property of its own at all, and when it was deprived of its place, the stock of Joseph succeeded it. Yet from this most despised tribe of Levi God chose for himself ministers and priests. After these sons, their father Jacob never again called down a curse on any son, because the mercy of God outweighed judgment. From the tribe of Levi were born Moses, Samuel, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Zechariah, and John the Baptist.

units.la: 39. Iudas, quartus Iacobi filius, fratrem Iosephum, ne occideretur, seruauit. Mortua uxore nurum suam Thamar insciens compressit. Huic amplissima precatus est pater moriturus, dignitatem inter fratres, victoriam de omnib. hostibus, primatum in ecclesia. Ab eius nomine populus vniuersus, Iudaei: pars Palaestinae nobilissima, Iudaea est appellata: & tribus Iudaicae excellentia vsque ad Christum durauit. Hinc appellatur tribus βασιλικὴ[?].
units.tr: 39. Judah, fourth son of Jacob, saved his brother Joseph from being killed. After his wife died, he unknowingly lay with his daughter-in-law Tamar. Their father, when dying, prayed for him the greatest blessings: dignity among his brothers, victory over all enemies, and primacy in the Church. From his name the whole people is called Jews, and the most noble part of Palestine was called Judea. The tribe of Judah kept its excellence until Christ, and for this reason the tribe is called royal [βασιλικὴ].

units.la: 40. Dan, habitauit in parte Beniaminis, iuxta mare. Posteritas eius felix & potens fuit. Ex hac tribu prodierunt fortissimi duces, Simson & Maccabaei. Hanc tribum omittit apostolus Apoc. 7. non quod Antichristus ex ea nasciturus esset, sed quod tribus Dan fecerit initium publicae defectionis, Iudic.17. v.18. atque ita figuraverit apostasiam Antichristi. Quae etiam causa est, quod Ephraim ab apostolo ibidē[?] praeteritur. Nam ex tribu Ephraim oriundus fuit Ieroboam, author defectionis in Israele. Omittuntur itaque Dan & Ephraim tanquam typi malitiae Antichristi, quam ille per bina sua brachia, seculare & spirituale, exercet. Tribus Dan brachium spirituale, Ephraim seculare notat. His substituuntur Leui, ordinarius templi minister, & Ioseph, dux populi Dei in Aegypto.
units.tr: 40. Dan dwelt in the part of Benjamin by the sea. Its posterity was fortunate and powerful, and from this tribe came the most valiant leaders, Samson and the Maccabees. The apostle omits this tribe in Apoc. 7, not because Antichrist was to be born from it, but because the tribe of Dan made the beginning of public defection, Judg. 17 v. 18, and so foreshadowed the apostasy of Antichrist. This is also the reason why Ephraim is passed over by the apostle in the same place, for Jeroboam, author of the defection in Israel, sprang from the tribe of Ephraim. Dan and Ephraim are therefore omitted as types of the malice of Antichrist, which he exercises through his two arms, the secular and the spiritual. The tribe of Dan signifies the spiritual arm, Ephraim the secular. In their place are substituted Levi, the ordinary minister of the temple, and Joseph, leader of God's people in Egypt.

units.la: 41. Naphthali accepit regnum Iabini, & Galilaeam superiorem, monti Libano & agro Damasceno contigua. Saepe a vicinis Syris haec tribus bello & incursionibus tentata, Dei beneficio euasit. Ex hac tribu prodierunt Debora & Tobias.
units.tr: 41. Naphtali received the kingdom of Jabin and Upper Galilee, bordering on Mount Lebanon and the Damascene countryside. Often attacked by the neighbouring Syrians in war and raids, this tribe escaped by God's favour. From this tribe came Deborah and Tobias.

units.la: 42. Gad, & Aser, procrearunt posteros magnanimos, de quibus nemo victorias deportauit laetas & incruentas. Possederunt solum terrae bonum atq; fertile. Extribu priore oriundus est Elias, è posteriore, Anna, quæ Messiam in templo est amplexata.
units.tr: 42. Gad and Asher produced magnanimous posterity, and none of them won victories that were happy and bloodless. They possessed only the good and fertile part of the land. From the former tribe was descended Elijah, and from the latter Anna, who embraced the Messiah in the temple.

units.la: 43. Ifaschar, & Zebulon, progenuerunt posteros inter sese plane dispares. Nam posteri Ifascharis reliquis tribubus quasi circumuallati, terramque amoenissimam possidentes, pacis studiosi erant: ideo quietis & tranquillitatis causa, seruitutem atque iugum non recusabant. Posteri autem Zebulonis, quia loca colebant maritima, otium desidiamque perosi, vacabant negotiationibus, & resistebant potentibus vicinis. Huius tribus alumnus fuit Ionas propheta.
units.tr: 43. Issachar and Zebulun produced posterity utterly unlike each other. The posterity of Issachar, hemmed in, as it were, by the other tribes and possessing a most pleasant land, was devoted to peace. Therefore, for the sake of quiet and tranquillity, they did not refuse servitude and the yoke. But the posterity of Zebulun, because they dwelt by the sea, hated idleness and sloth and gave themselves to trade, and they resisted powerful neighbours. The prophet Jonah came from this tribe.

units.la: 44. Iosephus, pietate, scientia diuinandi, fide, castitate, patientia, obedientia, imò & regiis virtutibus præditus, fuit verissimus vates, sanctissimus doctor, optimus princeps, suæ gentis ornamentum, alienæ firmamentum, Christi inter latrones imago in carcere, & mox in dignitate constitutus, eiusdem exaltati typus.
units.tr: 44. Joseph, endowed with piety, skill in interpreting dreams, faith, chastity, patience, obedience, and indeed with royal virtues, was a most truthful prophet, a most holy teacher, an excellent prince, the ornament of his own nation and the support of foreigners. He was an image of Christ, imprisoned among thieves, and soon afterwards, raised to dignity, a type of the same Christ exalted.

units.la: 45. Beniamin, minimus natu Iacobi filius, non in Syria, ut cæteri fratres, sed in Cananæa natus est. Posteri eius propter libidinem pene internecione delentur. In distractione regni hæc tribus adhæsit Iudæ. Ex illa nati sunt Ehud, Saul, Mardochæus, & Paulus, maximus inter apostolos.
units.tr: 45. Benjamin, the youngest son of Jacob, was born not in Syria, as his other brothers were, but in Canaan. His descendants were almost wiped out for their lust. When the kingdom was divided, this tribe adhered to Judah. From it were born Ehud, Saul, Mordecai, and Paul, the greatest of the apostles.

units.la: 46. Manasses, primogenitus Iosephi filius ex coniuge Ægyptia, adoptatus fuit ab auo in filiorum propriorum hæreditatem, exauthorato Leui. Multa felicitate & gloria honestati fuerunt posteri Manassis; qui cum propter nobilitatem, & opes ingentes superbirent, & cultum Dei sanctissimum nihil curarent, in seruitutem perpetuam rediguntur.
units.tr: 46. Manasseh, the firstborn son of Joseph by his Egyptian wife, was adopted by his grandfather into the inheritance of his own sons, Levi having been deposed. The descendants of Manasseh were honoured with much good fortune and glory; but because they grew proud of their nobility and their immense wealth, and cared nothing for the most holy worship of God, they were reduced to perpetual servitude.

units.la: 47. Ephraim, alter Iosephi filius, patre renitente, ius primogenituræ ab auo adipiscitur, & excepto Iuda, omnium est florentissimus. Eius posteri fuerunt ingenio feroci & tumultuoso.
units.tr: 47. Ephraim, the other son of Joseph, though his father opposed it, obtained the right of the firstborn from his grandfather, and, apart from Judah, was the most flourishing of all. His descendants were of a fierce and turbulent disposition.

units.la: 48. Thamar, Cananæa, inter mulieres exteras, prima Christi auia numeratur.
units.tr: 48. Tamar, a Canaanite woman, is counted as the first of Christ's grandmothers among the foreign women.

units.la: 49. Peres, Iudæ filius ex incestuoso coitu cum Thamare, tantâ fuit integritate & felicitate, vt posteri gratulaturi nouis coniugibus, domus Peres felicitatem optarent. Eius filius Efrom, nepos Aram, & pronepos Aminadab[?], in genealogiâ Dauidis & Christi collocantur.
units.tr: 49. Perez, son of Judah by his incestuous union with Tamar, was of such integrity and good fortune that, when newly married, the wives' families wished for the house of Perez to be happy. His son Hezron, grandson of Ram, and great-grandson of Amminadab[?], are placed in the genealogy of David and Christ.

units.la: 50. Potiphar, Pharaonis aulicus primarius, malè meretur de Iosepho, spectatæ fidelitatis seruo.
units.tr: 50. Potiphar, the chief courtier of Pharaoh, dealt badly with Joseph, a servant of proven fidelity.

units.la: 51. Pharao, cognomento Pius, item Amosis, siue Amos, fuit nutritius & hospes ecclesiæ liberalissimus, Iosepho & Iacobo familiariter vsus.
units.tr: 51. Pharaoh, surnamed the Pious, and likewise Amosis, or Amos, was a most generous nurturer and host of the Church, and had familiar dealings with Joseph and Jacob.

units.la: 52. Pharao, cognomento Impius, & Bufiris, est tyrannus infanticida. Huic geminus est Pharao Acherres, siue Cenchres, qui renuit dimittere populum Dei, eâque de causâ gratissimas pœnas dedit.
units.tr: 52. Pharaoh, surnamed the Impious, and Bufiris, is a tyrant and infanticide. His twin is Pharaoh Acherres, or Cenchres, who refused to let the people of God go, and for this reason received most grievous punishments.

units.la: 53. Siphra, & Pua: obstetrices optimæ, Pharaonis calliditatem prudenter deludunt, & à Deo ornantur præ-miis.
units.tr: 53. Shiphrah and Puah, excellent midwives, wisely outwitted the cunning of Pharaoh, and were rewarded with prizes by God.

units.la: 54. Amram, filius Caathi, nepos Leui, amitam suam Iochebedam vxorem ducit: ex quâ Aharonem & Mosen filios procreat tempore promulgati edicti de infanticidio.
units.tr: 54. Amram, son of Kohath, grandson of Levi, married his aunt Jochebed, by whom he begot Aaron and Moses as sons, at the time when the edict concerning infanticide was published.

units.la: 55. Aminadab, pronepos Peres, nobilitate domus Iudæ, & affinitate domus Leui, celebris fuit. Nam Aharoni filiam suam Elisebam in matrimonium collocauit.
units.tr: 55. Amminadab, great-grandson of Perez, was famous for the nobility of the house of Judah and for his kinship with the house of Levi, for he gave his daughter Elisheba in marriage to Aaron.

units.la: 56. Naasson, Aminadabi filius, Aharonis affinis, dux suæ tribus à Deo eligitur. In suo magistratu vir vtilis est ecclesiæ, annos duo-de-quadraginta. Verum in finibus regionis Moabiticæ ipse cum aliis, nec à gentilium sacris & fornicatione abstinuit, nec populum vt abstineret, authoritate suâ auertit. Quocirca cum vndecim reliquarum tribuum principibus, latâ àDeo sententiâ, in crucem agitur.
units.tr: 56. Nahshon, son of Amminadab, kinsman of Aaron, was chosen by God as leader of his tribe. In his office he was a man useful to the Church, aged forty-two years. Yet in the plains of Moab he himself, along with others, did not abstain from the sacrifices of the Gentiles and from fornication, nor did he, by his authority, turn the people away so that they might abstain. Wherefore, with the leaders of the eleven other tribes, sentence being pronounced by God, he was put to the cross.

units.la: 57. Iethro, alio nomine Hobab & Raguel, sacerdos idemque præses Midianitarum, Mosen exulem hospitio excepit, eique Zipporam filiam matrimonio iunxit, denique salutari consilio eum iuuit.
units.tr: 57. Jethro, also called Hobab and Reuel, priest and at the same time ruler of the Midianites, received Moses in exile as a guest, gave him his daughter Zipporah in marriage, and at last helped him with wholesome counsel.

units.la: 58. Zippora, Mosis uxor, filium, quem octauo die non permisit à marito circumcidi, tandè ipsa circumcidit. Sed propter legis sæuitiam marito conuitium faciens, eum deserit, & in domum patris repedat, vnde, authoritate patris, reducta, Mosi reconciliatur.
units.tr: 58. Zipporah, the wife of Moses, when her husband did not allow the son to be circumcised on the eighth day, circumcised him herself. But because of the severity of the law, she cast reproaches at her husband, deserted him, and returned to her father's house, whence, by her father's authority, she was brought back and was reconciled to Moses.

units.la: 59. Obabus, Iethronis filius, alio nomine dictus Cineus, cum Mose affine per desertum proficiscitur, eique, hominum ac locorum gnarus, non parum commodat in itinere difficili & longo. Eius posteritas, gens Cinæa, à Saule conseruatur, iussu Dei, cùm populum Amalekitarum deleturus esset.
units.tr: 59. Hobab, son of Jethro, also called Kenite, set out with Moses through the desert as a kinsman by marriage, and, knowing the men and places, gave him no little help on the difficult and long journey. His posterity, the Kenite people, was spared by Saul, by God's command, when he was about to destroy the nation of the Amalekites.

units.la: 60. Moses, miraculose conseruatus in infantiâ, regiè educatus in pueritiâ & adolescentiâ, gloriose vocatus à Deo in virili ætate, magnificè à Deo sepultus in extremâ senectâ, fuit propheta & dux insignis. In locum promissionis non venit, vti lex ad cælum non deducit. Vulgo appellatur cancellarius Dei.
units.tr: 60. Moses, miraculously preserved in infancy, royally educated in boyhood and youth, gloriously called by God in manhood, magnificently buried by God in extreme old age, was a prophet and an outstanding leader. He did not come into the promised land, just as the law does not lead up to heaven. He is commonly called the chancellor of God.

units.la: 61. Israelitæ, numero aucti in Ægypto, & ibi iugo intolerabili pressi, sed miraculose conseruati, & tandem inde per mare rubrum & desertum in terram Canaan deducti, sunt typus ecclesiæ militantis.
units.tr: 61. The Israelites, increased in number in Egypt and oppressed there under an intolerable yoke, yet miraculously preserved, and at last led out from there through the Red Sea and the desert into the land of Canaan, are a type of the militant Church.

units.la: 62. Maria, soror Mosis, spiritu prophetico prædita, contra fratrem insolenter locuta, & ideo scabroso lepræ morbo deformata, & ab eo precibus fratris à Deo sanata, est exemplum fœminæ heroinæ, & fœmineæ quoque infirmitatis atque inconstantiæ.
units.tr: 62. Miriam, sister of Moses, endowed with the prophetic Spirit, spoke insolently against her brother, and for this reason was disfigured by the foul disease of leprosy, and was healed by God at her brother's prayers. She is an example of a heroic woman, and also of female weakness and inconstancy.

units.la: 63. Aharon, frater Mosis, propter eloquentiam dictus fuit os fratris. Sacerdotium perpetuum cum suâ progenie obtinuit.
units.tr: 63. Aaron, brother of Moses, was called the mouth of his brother on account of his eloquence. He obtained the priesthood in perpetuity for himself and his posterity.

units.la: 64. Nadab, & Abihu, filii Aharonis natu maiores, patris boni mala & ambitiosa soboles, igne repentino cœlitus immissò, miserabiliter consumuntur, quòd vetitum ignem indeserto adolere aggressi fuissent.
units.tr: 64. Nadab and Abihu, the elder sons of Aaron, offspring of a good father but evil and ambitious, were miserably consumed by fire suddenly sent down from heaven, because they had undertaken to burn the forbidden fire in the wilderness.

units.la: 65. Eleazar, tertius Aharonis filius, ordinis sui decus ingens, princeps principum Leuitarum à Deo constitutus, à patruo consecratur. Cum Mose & Iosuâ res magnas &ecclesiæ salubberrimas gerit: custos doctrinæ cœlestis,&c legis avitæ defensor, & doctor populi vigilantissimus.
units.tr: 65. Eleazar, the third son of Aaron, a great ornament of his order, was appointed by God prince of the chief Levites, and was consecrated by his uncle. Together with Moses and Joshua he carried out great affairs, most salutary for the Church: he was a guardian of heavenly doctrine, a defender of the ancestral law, and a most watchful teacher of the people.

units.la: 66. Pinehas, Eleazaris filius, Aharonis nepos, patrisauique[?] imitator, zelo, fortitudine, prudentiâ, neminiinferior,vir malis timendus, bonis venerabilis.
units.tr: 66. Phinehas, son of Eleazar, grandson of Aaron, an imitator of his father and grandfather, second to no one in zeal, courage and prudence, a man to be feared by the wicked and revered by the good.

units.la: 67. Bileam,Syrus, è Nachoris posteritate, sacerdos & propheta celebris, vaticinatus est de Messiâ, & multorum populorum occasu. Tandem corruptus mercede, regem barbarum abdito consilio instruit, eâque de causâ, iusto Dei iudicio, in tumultu inter populum impium ferro occiditur, suæque avaritiæ præmium fert iustissimum.
units.tr: 67. Balaam, a Syrian, of the posterity of Nahor, a famous priest and prophet, prophesied concerning the Messiah and the downfall of many peoples. At last, corrupted by a bribe, he instructed the barbarian king with a secret plan, and for this reason, by the just judgment of God, he was killed with the sword in the tumult among the impious people, and bore the most righteous reward of his greed.

units.la: 68. Core, pronepos Leui, inuidia & ambitione perditus, & gratiæ alienæ captator fraudulentus, factionem excitat contra Mosen & Aharonem patrueles suos. Eam ob causam, fundamentis terræ dehiscentibus, vivus absumitur. Floruerunt è posteris eius viri lectissimi, quorum hymni inter Davidis carmina leguntur: magno solatio omnium, Deum esse clementem & propitium, si quiparentum malorum impia vestigia filii non sequantur.
units.tr: 68. Korah, great-grandson of Levi, ruined by envy and ambition, and a fraudulent seeker of another's favour, stirred up a faction against Moses and Aaron, his cousins. For this reason, the foundations of the earth opening, he was swallowed up alive. From his descendants there flourished men most select, whose hymns are read among the songs of David; a great comfort to all, that God is merciful and propitious, if the children of wicked parents do not follow their impious footsteps.

units.la: 69. Dathan, & Abiram, nepotes Rubenis, propter patris primogenita superbientes, contra Mosen conspirant cum Core: & eandem quoque luunt pœnam. In hac conspiratione fuerunt Mosis tribules ducenti & quinquaginta.
units.tr: 69. Dathan and Abiram, grandsons of Reuben, proud because of their father's firstborn status, conspired against Moses with Korah, and likewise paid the same penalty. In this conspiracy there were two hundred and fifty of Moses' own tribesmen.

units.la: 70. Selomithidis Hebræa filius, patre Ægyptio genitus, lapidatur, quòd blasphemasset nomen Dei. Maleficihiius nomen non est expressum: quia sanctissimum Dei nomen profanando meruit, ut suum nomen periret.
units.tr: 70. The son of the Israelite woman Shelomith, begotten by an Egyptian father, was stoned because he had blasphemed the name of God. The name of this evildoer is not expressed, because by profaning the most holy name of God he deserved that his own name should perish.

units.la: 71. Israelitæ in deserto, duci suo, id est Deo & Mosi, sapissimè fiunt contumaces propter impatientiam: ideò in multas ærumnas incidunt suo vitio. Deum tamen nunquam non præsentem & misericordem senserunt: quiva-riis miraculis se propitium declarauit. Ex illâ autem multitudine ingenti, sexcentis videl. millibus hominum qui ex Ægypto exierant, Caleb tantùm & Iosua Iordanem transeunt: reliqui omnes in deserto extinguuntur propter diffidentiam, & promissis beneficiis, eorum perfruuntur liberi.
units.tr: 71. The Israelites in the desert, though their leader, that is God and Moses, was present, very often became rebellious through impatience, and so through their own fault fell into many hardships. Yet they never failed to experience God as present and merciful, since by various miracles he showed himself favourable to them. Of that huge multitude, six hundred thousand men who had come out of Egypt, only Caleb and Joshua crossed the Jordan. All the rest were destroyed in the desert because of their unbelief, while their children enjoyed the promised blessings.

units.la: Achan cum filiis & filiabus lapidatur, quòd in direptioneHierichutis de anathemate sibi aliquid sumpserat, eoque facinore iram Dei aduersus totum populum, ab Haitis ideo fugatum, prouocauerat.
units.tr: Achan was stoned with his sons and daughters, because in the plunder of Jericho he had taken something for himself from what was devoted to God, and by this crime he had provoked the anger of God against the whole people, who for that reason had been put to flight by the men of Ai.

units.la: 73. Rahab, Hierichuntina, per fidem fuit benigna hospita ecclesiæ, quando abscondit duos exploratores Iosuæ. Hinc, urbe capta, seruatur cum sua propinquitate, & viri præstantis, Salmonis, potitur coniugio. In Christi genealogia, è mulierib. externis, loco secundo ponitur. nam regis Dauidis fuit tritauia.
units.tr: 73. Rahab of Jericho, through faith, was a kind hostess to the Church when she hid Joshua's two spies. Hence, when the city was taken, she was saved with her family, and she obtained in marriage the distinguished man Salmon. In the genealogy of Christ she is placed second among the foreign women, for she was the great-great-grandmother of King David.

units.la: 74. Gabaonitæ, stratagemate impetrant pacem à Iosuâ, qui eos in fidem semel susceptos defendit, mulctato nihilominus ipsorum dolo.
units.tr: 74. The Gibeonites, by a stratagem, obtained peace from Joshua, who defended them once received into his faith, though their deceit was nonetheless punished.

units.la: 75. Calebus, de tribu Iudâ, vir eximius, solus in terram promissam venit cum Iosua, ibique urbes gigantum expugnat & possidet: quòd gigantéam populi incredulitatem animosè redarguisset. Tam fuit vegetis viribus, utillæ ne senectute quidem diminutæ sint.
units.tr: 75. Caleb, of the tribe of Judah, an eminent man, alone came with Joshua into the promised land, and there he conquered and possessed the cities of the giants, because he had boldly refuted the unbelief of the people, which was giant-like. So vigorous were his strengths that they were not diminished even by old age.

units.la: V. Prosopographia, tempore ecclesiæ à du- cibus gubernatæ, ex libris Iosuæ, Iudicum, Ruth, & primo Samuelis, ita habet.
units.tr: V. Prosopography of the time when the Church was governed by leaders, drawn from the books of Joshua, Judges, Ruth, and 1 Samuel, as follows.

units.la: 76. Iosua, filius Nun, Ephraimites, minister Mosis, summo duce & propheta dignus discipulus, est speculum magnanimæ fidei in terrâ Canaan explorandâ, & fortitudinis inuictæ in eadem expugnandâ, iustitiæ deniq; & prudentiæ in rectâ ipsius diuisione. Mosis factus succesfor authoritate diuinâ, inauguratus est ab Eleazare. Ad preces eius steterunt Iordanes, sol, & luna. Triginta & vnum reges internecione deleuit. Fuit vir ingenti fide, præsentissimo animo, tolerantiâ maximâ spectatissimus, & typus Christi eminentissimus.
units.tr: 76. Joshua, son of Nun, an Ephraimite, minister of Moses, a disciple worthy of the supreme leader and prophet, is a mirror of great-hearted faith in spying out the land of Canaan, of unconquered courage in conquering it, and finally of justice and prudence in dividing it rightly. He succeeded Moses in office by divine authority and was inaugurated by Eleazar. At his prayer the Jordan, the sun, and the moon stood still. He destroyed thirty-one kings by slaughter. He was a man of immense faith, of ready courage, most renowned for endurance, and the most eminent type of Christ.

units.la: 77. Othoniel, fratris Calebi filius, de tribu Iudâ, Iosuæ successit in imperio, & expugnatâ Debirâ, belli mercede filiam Calebi accepit vxorem. Iugum externæ dominationis primum ipse primus à populi ceruicibus fortiter [?]uertit.
units.tr: 77. Othniel, son of Caleb's brother, of the tribe of Judah, succeeded Joshua in rule. After he captured Debir, he received Caleb's daughter as his wife as the reward of war. He himself was the first to bravely throw off the yoke of foreign domination from the necks of the people.

units.la: 78. Ehud, dux tertius, Eglonem Moabitarum regem fortiter obtruncat, decemque millia hominum {1}electo[?]rum occidit.
units.tr: 78. Ehud, the third leader, boldly struck down Eglon, king of the Moabites, and killed ten thousand of the chosen men.

units.la: 79. Samgar, in agro suo armenta ducens, & Philistinorum excursiones praedae causa reseifcens, solus, pedo pastorali, armis videl. pro tempore oblatis, latrones sexcentos, Dei auxilio prosternit.
units.tr: 79. Shamgar, while driving his herds in his own field and intercepting the raids of the Philistines for the sake of booty, alone, with an oxgoad, that is, with whatever weapons were at hand for the moment, struck down six hundred robbers with God's help.

units.la: 80. Debora, prophetissa & dux, tribulem suum Boracum belli ducem aduocat, populumque summa cum authoritate gubernat.
units.tr: 80. Deborah, prophetess and leader, summoned her fellow tribesman Barak as commander in war, and governed the people with the highest authority.

units.la: 81. Gideon, homo rusticanus, dum frumentum in horreo excutit, populi dux ab angelo designatur, & confirmatur caelitus miraculo. Initio imperii aram & lucum Baalis in domo patris euertit: unde Ierobael cognominatur. Stratagemate usus hoc consequitur, ut Midianitarum centum & triginta quinque millia oppetant. Regium nomen atque sceptrum ad se delatum sponte detrectat. Ex praeda autem hostili conflat idolum, idque in patria sua dedicat: quae profanatio diuini cultus, ipsi libertasque eius cessit in perniciem.
units.tr: 81. Gideon, a country man, while threshing wheat in the barn, was designated by an angel as leader of the people and was confirmed by a miracle from heaven. At the beginning of his rule he overthrew the altar and grove of Baal in his father's house, whence he was surnamed Jerubbaal. Using a stratagem, he brought it about that one hundred and thirty-five thousand Midianites perished. He voluntarily refused the royal name and sceptre when they were offered to him. From the hostile spoil, however, he made an idol and dedicated it in his own country; this profanation of divine worship turned to the ruin of him and of his liberty.

units.la: 82. Abimelechus, Gideonis e concubina Sichemensi filius, regnum a suis civibus versutia ebland itur. Tyrannidem exercuit annos tres, dedecus gentis & generis sui, homicida civium, parricida fratrum 69, euersor libertatis, patriae incendiarius.
units.tr: 82. Abimelech, son of Gideon by a concubine of Shechem, was flattered by his fellow citizens into seizing the kingship through cunning. He exercised tyranny for three years, a disgrace to his nation and his family, a murderer of his citizens, a parricide of sixty-nine brothers, an overthrower of liberty, and an incendiary of his country.

units.la: 83. Thola, patruelis Abimelechi, viro ambitioso & crudeli, ipse moderatus succedit. Eius temporibus pax undique tranquilla & iucunda floruit.
units.tr: 83. Tola, a cousin of Abimelech, succeeded him as a moderate ruler, after an ambitious and cruel man. In his times peace flourished calm and pleasant on every side.

units.la: 84. Iair, dux octauus, fuit filiorum triginta pater, quos ciuitatum totidem principes constituit, quae Iairis praesecturae longo tempore dictae sunt. Sub eo homines bono pacis abusi, a vera religione deficiunt, & multas hostilium vexationes ideo incurrunt.
units.tr: 84. Jair, the eighth leader, was the father of thirty sons, whom he appointed as the princes of as many cities, which for a long time were called the districts of Jair. Under him men, abusing the blessing of peace, fell away from true religion and therefore incurred many vexations from enemies.

units.la: 85. Iephtha, Iairis ciuis & tribulis, e matre natus infa-mi, mi, consuetudine latrociniorum, & robur militare, & nomen celebre comparat. Hinc ciuium suorum consensu dux belli creatur, & hostes vincit, viginti ciuitatibus subactis. Voto temerario filiam mactasse vulgo putatur. Sed ex circumstantiis patet, mactationem fuisse commutatam perpetuæ virginitatis cultu. Cum Ephraimitæ bellu ei non necessarium indicerent, duo & quadraginta ex iis prostrauit hominum millia.
units.tr: 85. Jephthah, a citizen and tribesman of Jair, born of an infamous mother, acquired, through the practice of robbery, military strength and a famous name. Hence, by the consent of his fellow citizens, he was created leader in war, and he defeated the enemies, subduing twenty cities. It is commonly thought that he sacrificed his daughter in fulfilment of a rash vow. But from the circumstances it is clear that the sacrifice was changed into the worship of perpetual virginity. When the Ephraimites declared war on him, which was unnecessary, he struck down forty-two thousand of them.

units.la: 86. Abesan, Elon, & Abdon, duces, fuerunt viri & honore publico, & obseruantiâ suorum inprimis nobiles & fortunati. Vixerunt enim cum liberis ac nepotibus suis, quos habuerunt bene multos (nam Abesan habuit triginta filios totidemque filias, & totidem generos in suâ domo aluit: Abdon filios quadraginta, & nepotes triginta numerauit) cum his, inquam, vixerunt in pace publicâ ætatem quietam & venerabilem.
units.tr: 86. Abesan, Elon, and Abdon, leaders, were men of public honour and, above all, noble and fortunate in the regard of their people. For they lived with their children and grandchildren, whom they had in great number (for Abesan had thirty sons and as many daughters, and maintained as many sons-in-law in his house; Abdon counted forty sons and thirty grandsons), and with these, I say, they lived in public peace, a quiet and venerable old age.

units.la: 87. Simson, alio nomine Bedan appellatus à tribu, robore gigantéo fuit. Philistæis plurima intulit damna in vitâ & in morte suâ. Qui ab hostibus capi non potuit, à fœminâ captus miserè periit.
units.tr: 87. Samson, otherwise called Bedan after his tribe, had gigantic strength. He inflicted very many losses on the Philistines both in his life and in his death. He who could not be captured by his enemies was taken by a woman and perished wretchedly.

units.la: 88. Eli, de stirpe Ithamaris, quarti filii Aharonis, functus est officio sacerdotis & ducis. Confectus senio, ecclesiam commisit filiis, turpibus & nefariis adolescen-tibus: quorum flagitia ipse suâ indulgentiâ fouit. Inde fa-ctum, ut sterilitas & inedia populum incesseret, filii eius in bello perirent cæsis de populo triginta hominum millibus, ipse de sellâ decidens ceruicem frangeret. Durauit pœna diu in eius familiâ. Nam Achitob nepos partu immaturo editur, pronepos Achimelech trucidatur temporibus Saulis; abnepos Abiathar, à dignitate remouetur tempore Salomonis.
units.tr: 88. Eli, of the line of Ithamar, the fourth son of Aaron, held the office of priest and leader. Worn out with age, he entrusted the Church to his sons, shameful and wicked young men, whose disgraceful deeds he himself indulged by his leniency. Hence it came about that famine and hunger attacked the people, his sons perished in battle, thirty thousand men of the people being slain, and he himself, falling from his seat, broke his neck. The punishment lasted long in his family. For Ahitub, his grandson, was born prematurely by a birth; his great-grandson Ahimelech was slaughtered in the time of Saul; his great-great-grandson Abiathar was removed from his dignity in the time of Solomon.

units.la: 89. Samuel, precibus à Deo impetratus, & Deo à pueritiâ dicatus, ab Eli sacerdote instituitur. Propheta primarius & fidelis, & Deo ita charus, ut ab eo frustrà nihil unquam petierit. A populo exauthoratus non tumultuatur:quin potius reges in gente sua unxit. Ab hoc Petrus Apostolus, prophetarum ducit initium.
units.tr: 89. Samuel, obtained from God by prayer and dedicated to God from boyhood, was trained by the priest Eli. He was the chief and faithful prophet, and so dear to God that he never asked anything of him in vain. Though deposed by the people, he did not riot; rather, he anointed kings among his own nation. From him the Apostle Peter derives the beginning of the prophets.

units.la: 90. Iotham, filius Gideonis natu minimus, stultitiam & sæuitiam Sichemitis exprobrat, & de futuro urbis excidio vaticinatur.
units.tr: 90. Jotham, the youngest son of Gideon, reproaches the Shechemites for their folly and cruelty, and prophesies the future destruction of the city.

units.la: 91. Noemi, cum marito Elimelech & duobus filiis, ad alendam se atque familiam, penuriæ tempore, è Iudæa in terram Moabitarum se confert.Marito ibidem defuncto, filiis puellas exteras despondet.Filiis quoque defunctis, ipsa redit in patriam, Bethlehemum, comitante Ruthâ nuru.
units.tr: 91. Naomi, with her husband Elimelech and two sons, in a time of famine, went from Judah into the land of the Moabites, to support herself and her family. When her husband died there, she betrothed her sons to foreign girls. When her sons also died, she herself returned to her homeland, Bethlehem, accompanied by her daughter-in-law Ruth.

units.la: 92. Ruth, Moabitis, orba marito & pauperⅽula, socrū Noëmim[?] loco matris honorat, eique senectutem & orbitatem suâ pietate & obseruantia leniorem efficit. Viro autem nobili & locupleti Booz iuncta connubio, fructus suæ pietatis magnos & insperatos percipit. Facta enim regis Dauidis auia est, & tertia è mulieribus peregrinis in genealogia Christi ponitur.
units.tr: 92. Ruth, a Moabitess, bereft of her husband and very poor, honoured her mother-in-law Naomi in place of a mother, and by her piety and devotion made old age and childlessness easier for her. But when she was joined in marriage to the noble and wealthy Boaz, she received great and unhoped-for fruits of her piety. For she became the great-grandmother of King David, and she is placed as the third of the foreign women in the genealogy of Christ.

units.la: 93. Booz[?], Salmonis filius, homo potens & magnâ in re Rutham sibi despondet, & ex eâ suscipit Obedum, avum Dauidis.
units.tr: 93. Boaz, son of Salmon, a powerful man, betrothed Ruth to himself with great ceremony, and by her he begot Obed, the grandfather of David.

units.la: 94. Helcanas, pater Samuelis, fuit bonus pater, quia filiis exemplum pietatis extitit: & commodus maritus, quia vxoris alt:rius[?] morositatem, alterius sterilitatem patienter tulit.
units.tr: 94. Elkanah, the father of Samuel, was a good father, because he set an example of piety to his sons; and a fitting husband, because he patiently bore the peevishness of one wife and the barrenness of the other.

units.la: 95. Penina, vxor Helcanæ, mulier superba, Annam quia sterilis esset, exagitat.
units.tr: 95. Peninnah, the wife of Elkanah, a proud woman, harassed Hannah because she was barren.

units.la: 96. Anna, mater Samuelis, matrona pia & patiens, multos annos degit sterilis.
units.tr: 96. Hannah, the mother of Samuel, a pious and patient matron, spent many years barren.

units.la: 97. Ophni, & Pinehas, filii Heli, summâ dignitate praediti, nihil honori sacerdotum egerunt conueniens, profani, indocti, indiligentes, auari, libidinosi, vecordes, impii. Ob quæ scelera graviter fuerunt à Deo puniti. Vide paulo ante n. 88.
units.tr: 97. Hophni and Phinehas, sons of Eli, endowed with the highest dignity, did nothing fitting the honour of the priests: they were profane, unlearned, careless, greedy, lustful, mad, and impious. For these crimes they were severely punished by God. See above, n. 88.

units.la: 98. Aminadab, homo integerrimus, arcam Dei, à Philistæis remissam hospitio accipit: quæ ibi mansit usque ad Dauidis tempora.
units.tr: 98. Aminadab, a most upright man, received into his house the ark of God, which had been sent back by the Philistines; it remained there until the time of David.

units.la: 99. Iohel, & Abias, filii Samuelis, à patre iam ætate consecto principes constituuntur: sed à paterna integritate & sanctimonia longè degenerant: contumaces, avari, insatiabiles, iniusti. Quamobrem, cùm neque domi neque foris essent ferendi, nouæ mutationis causa exiterunt turpissima, populo regem sibi petente.
units.tr: 99. Joel and Abijah, sons of Samuel, were appointed leaders by their father, now worn out with age; but they degenerated far from their father's integrity and holiness: obstinate, greedy, insatiable, unjust. Therefore, since they could be endured neither at home nor abroad, they became, for the sake of a new change, the most shameful cause for the people, who asked for a king.

units.la: VI. Profopographia, tempore regij ecclesiæ imperij, ex libris Samuelis, Regū, & Chro- nicorum, sic habet.
units.tr: VI. Prosopography of the kingdom of the Israelites during the time of the judges and kings, from the books of Samuel, Kings and Chronicles, is as follows.

units.la: 100. Saul, filius Cis, è tribu Beniamin, viribus & dignitate corporis homo eminentissimus, è clitellario in regem euehitur: regnum humilis accipit, sed integer non manet vltra biennium. Obiurgatus verbo Dei, seipsum semper defendit pertinacissimè, magis suæ laudis, quàm gloriæ Dei appetens. In præliis satis fuit felix, sed vti victoriā ad gloriam Dei, etiam admonitus, noluit. Non curat Samuelem, Dauidem armis, Ionathanem odio prosequitur, sacerdotes & infantes occidit, & pellit familias in exilium. Vsus autem hominum malorum consiliis, in exitium coniicitur, quemq; non audierat viuentem Samuelem, eundem mortuum per Pythonissam è tumulo euocare studet. Victus à Philistæis, sibi manum infert.
units.tr: 100. Saul, son of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin, a man most outstanding in strength and bodily stature, was raised from the donkey-pens to be king. He received the kingdom in humility, but did not remain upright for more than two years. Rebuked by the word of God, he always defended himself most stubbornly, seeking his own praise rather than the glory of God. He was fortunate enough in battles, but even when admonished he would not use victory for the glory of God. He did not care for Samuel, pursued David with arms, hated Jonathan, killed priests and infants, and drove families into exile. Using the counsel of wicked men, he was thrust into ruin. He tried to summon up from the grave, through a medium, the dead Samuel, whom he had not listened to while Samuel was alive. Defeated by the Philistines, he fell on his own sword.

units.la: 101. Naas, Ammonitarum rex, Saulo primus bellum infert, tanquam regi nouo & ignobili, sed infeliciter.
