units.tr: 101. Naas, king of the Ammonites, was the first to make war on Saul, treating him as a new and base king, but he fared unhappily.

units.la: 102. Ionathan, Saulis filius, pietate, fide, magnanimitate iuuenis insignis, amicitiam cum Dauide colit integerrimam. Hinc Ionathan & Dauid sunt par amicorum nobile.
units.tr: 102. Jonathan, son of Saul, was remarkable as a young man for his piety, faithfulness and magnanimity, and cultivated the most upright friendship with David. Hence Jonathan and David are a noble pair of friends.

units.la: 103. Isboseth, Saulis filius, patre defuncto, duos annos regnat, beneficio Abneris. Sed ab illo desertus, eò angustiarum redigitur, vt solam ancillam habeat corporis sui custodem, & tandem à duobus tribulibus, in conclaui suo dormiens, interimitur.
units.tr: 103. Ishbosheth, son of Saul, reigned for two years after his father's death, by the favour of Abner. But when Abner deserted him, he was reduced to such straits that he had only a single maidservant to guard his person, and at last he was killed by two men of his tribe, while sleeping in his chamber.

units.la: 104. Mephibosetħ, filius Ionathæ loripes, à Dauide honorificè habetur; sed falso crimine apud ipsum à Sibâ accusatus, bona omnia amittit. Restitutus in gratiam, partem eorum dimidiam recipit.
units.tr: 104. Mephibosheth, son of Jonathan, lame in both feet, was treated with honour by David; but, accused before him falsely by Ziba, he lost all his goods. Restored to favour, he received back half of them.

units.la: 105. Abner, Saulis patruus, & eius copiarum dux, rege peremto, Isbosethum eius filium in solium collocat, anniseque duobus fortiter defendit. Armis intestinis saeuientibus, alienatus a domino suo, mulierculae causa, transit ad Dauidem, a quo cum beneuolentia suscipitur: a Ioabo autem, aemulo suo, fratris necem ulturo, specie amicitiae & colloquii insidiose telo transfigitur.
units.tr: 105. Abner, uncle of Saul and commander of his forces, after the king was killed, set Ishbosheth, his son, on the throne and defended him bravely for two years. When civil wars were raging, he became estranged from his master on account of a woman, and passed over to David, by whom he was received kindly. But Joab, his rival, who was going to avenge his brother's death, ran him through treacherously with a spear, under the pretext of friendship and a private conversation.

units.la: 106. Doeg, Idumaeus, in aula Saulis vir magnus, accusat Achimelechum sacerdotem Nobensem familiarem suum, quod Dauidi, & commeatum & gladium dederit. Rex illud factum animo ita iracundo tulit, ut in omnes eius ecclesiae sacerdotes capitalem ferret sententiam: qua cum nemo militum aut satellitum exequi vellet, solus hic Idumaeus inuentus est, qui sanguinem innoxium sua manu funderet: neque contentus supplicio sacerdotum, infantes, mulieres, cives denique omnes, nullius ordinis, sexus, aetatis respectu, tolleret.
units.tr: 106. Doeg the Edomite, a great man at Saul's court, accused Ahimelech the priest of Nob, his acquaintance, because he had given David both provisions and a sword. The king took the deed so angrily that he pronounced a capital sentence against all the priests of that congregation. When no soldier or guard was willing to carry it out, this Edomite alone was found to shed innocent blood with his own hand. And not content with the punishment of the priests, he destroyed infants, women and, in short, all the citizens, without regard to rank, sex or age.

units.la: 107. Achimelech, Heli pronepos, vir integer & hospitalis, Dauidi, exuli a se petenti, panes & gladium praebet. Eam ob causam a Doego coniurationis accusatus, & in aulam accersitus, inscientem se peccasse restatur[?], & veniam erroris atque delicti petit. Verum excusationi eius & precibus locus ignoscentiae non fuit. Nam iussu regis cum sacerdotibus quinque & octoginta crudeliter iugulatur: & ecclesiae Nobensis domicilium, & virorum optimorum collegium, iussu Saulis, & malitia Doegi, delctur[?] miserrime.
units.tr: 107. Ahimelech, great-grandson of Eli, a man of integrity and hospitality, gave bread and a sword to David, an exile who asked him for them. For this reason he was accused of conspiracy by Doeg, summoned to the court, and, protesting that he had sinned unknowingly, he asked for pardon of the error and the offence. But his excuse and his prayers found no place for forgiveness. For by the king's command he was cruelly slaughtered together with eighty-five priests; and the dwelling of the congregation of Nob, and the company of the best men, were most wretchedly destroyed, by Saul's command and Doeg's malice.

units.la: 108. Rispa, concubina Saulis, corpora duorum filiorum, cum quinque filiis Michalis, a Gabaonitis suspensa, pallio suo tegens custodiuit, necab eis auelli potuit. Eius sedulam pietatem Dauid est remuneratus.
units.tr: 108. Rizpah, concubine of Saul, covered with her cloth the bodies of two sons of hers, together with five sons of Michal, who had been hanged by the Gibeonites, and guarded them; she could not be parted from them by these men. David rewarded her diligent devotion.

units.la: 109. Isai, filius Obedi, Bethlehemites, fuit filiorum octo pater, e quibus Dauid, natu minimus, pastor erat, reliquorum contemtissimus. Hunc tamen Samuel iussu Dei regem designauit. Quâ de causâ Saul Isaium cum omni familiâ odisse coepit, & in exilium pepulit, cui rex Moabitarum immunitatem dedit & hospitium.
units.tr: 109. Jesse, son of Obed, of Bethlehem, was the father of eight sons, of whom David, the youngest, was a shepherd, the most despised of the rest. Yet Samuel designated this man king by God's command. For this reason Saul began to hate Jesse and his whole family, and drove them into exile, and the king of Moab gave them immunity and hospitality.

units.la: 110. Dauid, adolescens cum leonibus lusit & ursis: anno ætatis vigesimo ad regnum accersitur, populi suffragiis trigesimo demum confirmatur. Fuit sanctissimus propheta, potentissimus rex, felicissimus bellator, doctissimus musicus, exercitatissimus scriptor.
units.tr: 110. David, as a youth, played with lions and bears. In his twentieth year he was called to the kingdom, and only at thirty was he confirmed by the votes of the people. He was a most holy prophet, a most powerful king, a most fortunate warrior, a most learned musician and a most practised writer.

units.la: 111. Goliath, viribus & vastitate corporis confidens, necvisu facilis, nec dictu affabilis ulli, à Dauide adolescente prostratus est lapilli ictu.
units.tr: 111. Goliath, trusting in his strength and bulk of body, neither easy to look upon nor affable to anyone to speak with, was struck down by the young David with a stone from a sling.

units.la: 112. Nabal, è virorum clarissimorum, Calebi & Othonielis, posteritate, magni vir nominis atque locuples, sed tenax, crudelis, & sordidus, soli sibi vivere, benefaccrenemini solebat.
units.tr: 112. Nabal, of the posterity of the most distinguished men, Caleb and Othniel, was a man of great name and wealth, but tight-fisted, cruel and mean; he used to say that he lived for himself alone and did good to no one.

units.la: 113. Ioab, Dauidis auunculus, & summus copiarum ipsius[?] dux, vir animo ferox, ingenio callidus, & vindictæ cupidus, omnibus bellis proDauide gestis victor fuit. Sed crudelitate suâ, quâ Abnerem, Amasam, & Absolomuminterfecit, animum Dauidis ita abalienauit, ut præ ægritudine verbis illum tristissimis devoueret. Cum Adoniâ tumultuante conspirans, mandato Salomonis, in ipso sacrario, ad quod confugerat, interficitur.
units.tr: 113. Joab, David's nephew and chief commander of his forces, a man fierce in spirit, clever in mind and eager for revenge, was victorious in all the wars waged for David. But by his cruelty, with which he killed Abner, Amasa and Absalom, he so alienated David's mind that, in his grief, he cursed him with most bitter words. Conspiring with the rebel Adonijah, he was killed by Solomon's command, in the very sanctuary to which he had fled for refuge.

units.la: 114. Abisai, auunculi sui Dauidis defensor constantissimus, tanto animi corporisque robore fuit, ut cum trecentis dimicare non vereretur, & pugnando solus victoriam de illis obtineret.
units.tr: 114. Abishai, the most steadfast defender of his uncle David, had such strength of mind and body that he did not hesitate to fight against three hundred, and by fighting alone he won the victory over them.

units.la: 115. Asabel, cursor & bellator sui temporis celeberrimus, in floreadolescentiæ, suâ temeritate periit.
units.tr: 115. Asahel, the most famous runner and warrior of his time, perished in the flower of his youth through his own rashness.

units.la: 116. Amasa, Dauidis auunculus, dux copiarum Absolomi creatur. Prælio victus cum rege suo factioso, à Dauide propter virtutem & cognationem veniam impetrat, & belli præfectura loco Ioabi ipsi traditur. Ioabus inuidiâ & iracundiâ flagrans, ipsum fraterne sevocat colloquiicausâ, sed inter amplexus sica ipsum traiicit. Amasæ interitum duplici nomine luget Dauid, & quòd duce altero priuatus effet, & quòd alterum ducem contaminatum videret maximo facinore.
units.tr: 116. Amasa, David's nephew, was made commander of Absalom's forces. Defeated in battle with his factious king, he obtained pardon from David on account of his valour and kinship, and was given the command of the army in place of Joab. Joab, burning with envy and anger, called him aside treacherously on the pretext of a private conversation, but, in the midst of an embrace, ran him through with a dagger. David mourned Amasa's death on two counts: because he was deprived of one commander, and because he saw the other commander stained by a most heinous crime.

units.la: 117. Michal, Saulis filia, Dauidi in matrimonium collocata, egregiè suam fidelitatem marito probauit. Tandem tamen paternâ dignitate superbiens, maritum despexit, cum ante arcam Domini gestiens & exultans incederet.
units.tr: 117. Michal, daughter of Saul, given in marriage to David, proved her loyalty to her husband with distinction. Yet at last, proud of her father's dignity, she despised her husband, when she came dancing and exulting before the ark of the Lord.

units.la: 118. Abigail, vxor Nabalis, prudentiâ & modestiâ suâ maritum stultum liberauit è manibus Dauidis, qui eam, post obitum mariti, duxit vxorem, & habuit exili j sui comitem & sociam.
units.tr: 118. Abigail, wife of Nabal, by her prudence and modesty rescued her foolish husband from the hands of David; David afterwards took her as his wife after her husband's death, and had her as the companion and partner of his exile.

units.la: 119. Bathseba, insigni venustate mulier, in nymphaeo domi lauans, à rege conspicitur, qui eius impotente amore captus, marito ipsius Uriâ nefariè interfecto, eam duxit vxorem, & ex eâ sustulit Salomonem.
units.tr: 119. Bathsheba, a woman of remarkable beauty, was seen by the king bathing at home in a fountain-house. Seized by an uncontrollable passion for her, he wickedly had her husband Uriah killed, took her as his wife, and by her begot Solomon.

units.la: 120. Ammon, primogenitus Dauidis filius, amore surioso, Thamarem sororem ex aliâ matre, perdite deperit, eamque lenocinio ad se pelleƈtam per vim comprimit, & dehonestatam domo expellit. Absalom sororis ignominiâ motus, cùm nec Amnonem facti nefariipœniteret, nec à patre rege castigaretur, tacitè secum de vindictâ cogitat, & demum post biennium, inter vina Amnonem incautum obtruncat.
units.tr: 120. Ammon, the firstborn son of David, was madly in love, with a frenzied passion, with Tamar, his sister by another mother. By a trick he got her to come to him, forced her, and after dishonouring her he drove her from the house. Absalom, moved by his sister's disgrace, when Ammon did not repent of his wicked deed and was not punished by his father the king, brooded in silence on revenge, and at last, after two years, while Ammon was off his guard over his wine, he struck him down.

units.la: 121. Absalom, tertius Dauidis filius, nullâ animi dote, corporisque dignitate caruit. Sed patri suo unam molestiam ex aliâ facessit, donec tandem in fugâ inuolueretur cæsarie ramis quercus, & ita pendens à Ioabo tribus hastilibus percuteretur.
units.tr: 121. Absalom, third son of David, lacked every endowment of mind and every distinction of body. Yet he caused his father one trouble after another, until at last, in flight, he was caught by his hair in the branches of an oak, and, hanging there, was pierced through with three spears by Joab.

units.la: 122. Adonias, quartus Dauidis filius, cum Ioabo & Abiatharo stultè conspirat aduersus patrem. Quod ipsum cùm tentaret aduersus Salomonem, iussu eius interfectus est.
units.tr: 122. Adonijah, fourth son of David, foolishly conspired with Joab and Abiathar against his father. When he attempted the same against Solomon, he was put to death by Solomon's command.

units.la: 123. Nathan, ex Bathsebâ Dauidis filius, post Salomonem fuit natus, etsi 1. Chron. 3. v. 5. & c. 14. v. 4. ante Salomonem collocatur. Ex huius posteritate quidam putant Christum esse natum, quòd Salomonis posteritas in Ochozia defecerit. Sed hoc falsum esse liquebit infra exfectione 10. num.345. ubi disputatur de genealogia Christi.
units.tr: 123. Nathan, son of David by Bathsheba, was born after Solomon, although in 1 Chron. 3:5 and 14:4 he is placed before Solomon. Some think that Christ was born of his posterity, because the line of Solomon failed in Ahaziah. But this will be shown to be false below, in section 10, no. 345, where the genealogy of Christ is discussed.

units.la: 124. Gad, propheta, Dauidem exulem è terrâ Moabitarum reuocat. Idem, cùm populum numerari & censeri rex iussisset, è tribus poenis inediae, exilii, morbi, optionem unius proponit.
units.tr: 124. Gad, the prophet, recalled David, an exile, from the land of Moab. The same man, when the king had ordered the people to be numbered and counted, offered him a choice of one of three punishments: famine, exile or pestilence.

units.la: 125. Nathan, propheta, Dauidem adulterii reum, rectè quidem, sed liberè obiurgat. Idem optata loquitur eidem de regni perpetuitate. In errore magno versatur, dum iubet Dauidem Deo extruere templum. Factus adolescentis Salomonis praeceptor, omni eum pietate doctrinâq;, tali adolescente digna, instituit. Adonia tumultuante, causam Salomonis tuendam, bonis & honestis rationibus suscipit. Tandem iussu Dauidis Salomonem inungens, diadema suo discipulo imponit, & ipsum populo meritis laudibus commendat.
units.tr: 125. Nathan, the prophet, rightly but freely rebuked David as guilty of adultery. The same man spoke to him of the perpetuity of the kingdom, as he had desired. He was greatly mistaken when he bade David build a temple for God. Having become tutor to the young Solomon, he trained him in all piety and learning, worthy of such a young man. When Adonijah was stirring up tumult, he undertook the defence of Solomon's cause on good and honourable grounds. At last, by David's command, he anointed Solomon, placed the crown on his pupil, and commended him to the people with well-deserved praise.

units.la: 126. Abiathar, sacerdos, filius interfecti à Saule Achimelechi, temporibus Saulis ad Dauidem se confert, & ab ipso ornatur dignitate summi sacerdotii. Sed oblitus meritorum, cum Adonia conspirat: quâ de causâ relegatus à Salomone, vitam priuatus finit. Honor sacerdotii in posteritate Ithamaris, in quâ ab Eli, usque ad hunc eius abnepotem, annos circiter nonaginta durauerat, rursus in familiam Eleazaris transfertur.
units.tr: 126. Abiathar, a priest, son of Ahimelech, who was killed by Saul, went over to David in Saul's time, and David honoured him with the dignity of the high priesthood. But forgetting his merits, he conspired with Adonijah. For this reason Solomon banished him, and he ended his life deprived of his office. The honour of the priesthood, which had remained in the posterity of Ithamar from Eli down to this great-grandson of his for about ninety years, was again transferred to the family of Eleazar.

units.la: 127. Zadoc, sacerdos, filius Achitobi, de stirpe Eleazaris, Dauidi exulanti, quae cauenda forent, per filium suum tacitè nuntiari, fideliter curauit. Hunc substituit Salomon in locum Abiatharis seditiosi.
units.tr: 127. Zadok, a priest, son of Ahitub, of the stock of Eleazar, faithfully took care that what was to be avoided was secretly reported to David in exile, through his son. Solomon put him in the place of the seditious Abiathar.

units.la: 128. Ionathan, Abiatharis, & Achimaaz, Zadoci filius, fratres patrueles, ambo sacerdotes, Dauidi fuerunt admodum fideles.
units.tr: 128. Jonathan, son of Abiathar, and Ahimaaz, son of Zadok, cousins and both priests, were very loyal to David.

units.la: 129. Oza, filius Aminadabi, cùm arcam Domini bonâ intentione sustinere vellet, manuque tangeret, ob id factum mortuus subitò concidit. Nimirum alieni muneris usurpatio ipsi mortem repentinam attulit.
units.tr: 129. Uzzah, son of Abinadab, when he wished to steady the ark of the Lord with good intentions and touched it with his hand, fell dead suddenly for this deed. Clearly, presuming to perform another's office brought him a sudden death.

units.la: 130. Vrias, vir strenuus, à Dauide perfidè fuit obiectus præsentissimo mortis periculo.
units.tr: 130. Uriah, a valiant man, was treacherously exposed by David to the most imminent danger of death.

units.la: 131. Ethaius, proselytus, ad populum Dei à Philistæis se aggregauerat. Fidus regis amicus atque socius nunquam non fuit.
units.tr: 131. Ittai, a proselyte, had joined the people of God from the Philistines. He was always the faithful friend and companion of the king.

units.la: 132. Chufai, abundans animo & consilio, impedit cõsilium Achitophelis deperseqUendo Dauidem ex itinere fessum.
units.tr: 132. Hushai, abounding in spirit and counsel, thwarted the counsel of Ahithophel by pursuing David when he was weary from the journey.

units.la: 133. Barsillai, vir dines & copiosus, Dauidi maximè egenti, maximè munificum se præbet. Quod beneficium ita opportunum gratumque Dauidi accidit, vt eum in aulam suam vocaret pollicitationibus & honoribus. Verùm senectutem suam & vitæ consuetudinem excusans, agere ruri & mori in patria præoptauit.
units.tr: 133. Barzillai, a rich and wealthy man, showed himself most generous to David when he was in great need. This kindness came so timely and welcome to David that he called him to his court with promises and honours. But excusing his old age and habits of life, Barzillai preferred to live in the country and die in his homeland.

units.la: 134. Siba[?], quæstor Mephibosethi, Dauidem ab impio filio pulsum commeatu iuuat, sed falso crimine suum herum accusat: cuius delationis gratiâ herilium bonorum potitur semisse[?]. Post partam de Absolomo victoriam, cũ filiis quindecim & vernis viginti, Dauidi rursus occurrit, eique vadum Iordanis aperit. Propter eiusmodi beneficij constantiam, data prioris cupiditatis veniâ, partem bonorum heri sui adhuc obtinet dimidiam.
units.tr: 134. Ziba [?], steward of Mephibosheth, helped David with supplies when he had been driven out by his impious son, but falsely accused his master. By the reward of this accusation he gained possession of his master's goods, half of them [semisse?]. After the victory over Absalom had been won, he came out to meet David again with fifteen sons and twenty servants, and showed him the ford of the Jordan. Because of the steadfastness of such a service, his former greed was pardoned, and he still keeps half of his master's goods.

units.la: 135. Simei, Saulis agnatus, Dauidis æmulus, huncfugientem, maledictis & lapidibus insectatur. Audito Absolomi interitu, supplex ad Dauidem primus accedit,& trans Iordanem cum suis seruitiis traducit, veniamque procacitatis merito recenti impetrat. Salomon pœnâ capitali ei interdixit, ne extra vrbem regiam exiret: quod cùm ille facerer, seruos quosdam fugitiuos insequens,capitis supplicium incurrit.
units.tr: 135. Shimei, a kinsman of Saul and a rival of David, pursued him with curses and stones as he fled. On hearing of Absalom's death, he was the first to come as a suppliant to David, brought his servants across the Jordan with him, and obtained pardon for his insolence on account of his recent service. Solomon forbade him, on pain of death, to leave the royal city. When he did so, pursuing some runaway slaves, he incurred the penalty of death.

units.la: 136. Achitophel tantâ apud Dauidem æstimatione fuit habitus, vt quidquid diceret, de cœlo prolatum ducerètur. Defectione eius tantoperè Dauid consternatus est, vt nullo vnquam periculo magis. Tandem præ impotentiâ laqueo sibi fauces interclusit.
units.tr: 136. Ahithophel was held in such esteem by David that whatever he said was taken as if it had come down from heaven. David was so dismayed by his defection that he was never in greater danger. At last, in his helplessness, he choked himself with a noose.

units.la: 137. Seba, iuuenis audax & inquietus, vix sedato Absolomitumultu[?], nouos terrores ciet. Sed obsessus à ducibus Dauidis, capite truncatur à ciuibus Abelensibus.
units.tr: 137. Sheba, a bold and restless young man, scarcely after the tumult of the Absalomites had been quelled, stirred up new alarms. But besieged by David's commanders, he was beheaded by the citizens of Abel.

units.la: 138. Iasabeam, Dauidi coniunctissimus, uno praelio trecentos Philistinos, ipse solus prostrauit.
units.tr: 138. Jashobeam, most closely attached to David, struck down three hundred Philistines in a single battle, all by himself.

units.la: 139. Eleazar, inter heroas Dauidis locum secundum obtinuit; Samma, tertium.
units.tr: 139. Eleazar held second place among David's heroes; Shammah, third.

units.la: 140. Bananias leonem in cisternam lapsum finearmis aggressus strangulat, & prouocatorem Aegyptium, altum cubitos quinque, dignum videl. (spectaculo hominem, pedo aggreditur, & suo ipsum telo superat. Hunc Dauid sibi adhibuit, ut a secretis esset, eumque regiarum copiarum ductorem effecit.
units.tr: 140. Benaiah, when a lion had fallen into a cistern, attacked it with his bare arms and strangled it. He also attacked an Egyptian challenger, five cubits tall and worthy, one might say, of a spectacle, on foot, and overcame him with his own spear. David attached him to himself so that he was among his confidants, and made him commander of the royal forces.

units.la: 141. Hadadezer, rex Sobae, bis a Dauide superatus, pacem cum ipso init, eique fit tributarius.
units.tr: 141. Hadadezer, king of Zobah, twice defeated by David, made peace with him and became his tributary.

units.la: 142. Hiramus, Tyri rex, cum Dauide & Salomone propter virtutem & sapientiam ut utriusque[?] foedus multorum annorum habuit, nominis Iudaici, & regum sapientissimorum socius & amicus, totius vitae tempore fidelissimus.
units.tr: 142. Hiram, king of Tyre, had a covenant of many years, on account of their virtue and wisdom, with David and with Solomon alike, as with each of them. He was the companion and friend of the name of Judah and of the most wise kings, and most faithful all his life.

units.la: 143. Salomon, qui & Iedidiah, & Lemuel, Dauidis filius, florente aetate sapientiam a Deo petiit & impetrauit, templum Domini sumtuose, regiam magnifice extruxit; politiam & ecclesiam bene constituit: procedente aetate mulierum externarum insanis amoribus correptus, & ab illis seductus deos gentiles adorauit: appetente fine vitae resipuit, ut ex ecclesiaste ipsius patet. Salomoni σύγχρονῷ[?] videtur fuisse Agur, cuius mentio fit Prouerb.30.
units.tr: 143. Solomon, who is also Jedidiah and Lemuel, son of David, in his flourishing youth asked wisdom from God and obtained it. He built the temple of the Lord sumptuously and the palace magnificently, and he established the polity and the Church well. But as he advanced in years, he was seized by insane love for foreign women, was seduced by them, and worshipped pagan gods. As his end approached he repented, as is clear from his Ecclesiastes. Agur seems to have been contemporary [synchronos] with Solomon; he is mentioned in Proverbs 30.

units.la: 144. Arabiae regina, è Sabâ Hierosolymam venit, excita rumoribus de sapientiâ Salomonis. Thesauros multos dedit & accepit. Nomen Dei, sapientiam regis, splendorem populi, felicitatem gentis totius neque admirari, neque extollere satis ipsa potuit.
units.tr: 144. The queen of Arabia came from Sheba to Jerusalem, roused by reports of Solomon's wisdom. She gave and received many treasures. She could neither admire nor extol enough the name of God, the king's wisdom, the splendour of the people, and the happiness of the whole nation.

units.la: 145. Adad, & Rezon, Salomonis, qui regum vicinorum terror erat, potentiam sustinuerunt, adeo ut ex ipsius prouinciis praedas hinc inde agerent, nemine prohibente. Hoc Salomoni accidit propter furores ipsius, & cultum idolorum.
units.tr: 145. Hadad and Rezon, enemies of Solomon, who was the terror of the neighbouring kings, maintained their power, so that they carried off booty here and there from his provinces, and no one prevented them. This happened to Solomon on account of his frenzies and his worship of idols.

units.la: 146. Hiramus, artifex, regibus Tyri charus fuit, excellentia artis & ingenij. Ad Salomonem missus, templum Dei, & arcem regis extruit, tantâ peritiâ, tantoque artificio, vt similes ædes opere, magnificentiâ, sumtu, ornamentis, terrarum orbis nullibi habuerit.
units.tr: 146. Hiram, the craftsman, was dear to the kings of Tyre on account of his excellence in skill and talent. Sent to Solomon, he built the temple of God and the royal citadel with such skill and such craftsmanship that the world nowhere had buildings like them in workmanship, magnificence, cost and ornament.

units.la: 147. Adoniram, fuit spectatæ vir diligentiæ, præfectus Salomonis ad inspiciendum labores & operas fabrorum trium millium & trecentorum, qui architectones essent: baiulorum septuaginta millium, qui onera portarent: lapicidarum octoginta millium, qui saxa & marmora foderent.
units.tr: 147. Adoniram was a man of proven diligence, appointed by Solomon to oversee the labours and works of the three thousand three hundred workmen who were the overseers; of the seventy thousand bearers who carried the burdens; and of the eighty thousand stonecutters who quarried the rocks and marble.

units.la: VII. Profopographia, tempore regni Israe- litici, seu Samaritani, talis est, ex libris Regum & Chronicorum.
units.tr: VII. Prosopography of the time of the kingdom of Israel, or of Samaria, taken from the books of Kings and Chronicles.

units.la: 148. Abias, propheta Silonites, temporibus Salomonis floruit, & regni à stirpe ipsius alienationem prædixit, atque Ieroboamo dominatus amplissimi spem indubitatam certo signo fecit.
units.tr: 148. Abias, the prophet of Shiloh, flourished in the days of Solomon. He foretold that the kingdom would be torn from his line and gave Jeroboam an unmistakable sign of the sure hope of a wide dominion.

units.la: 149. Ieroboam, satrapa Salomonis fortis & industrius, decem tribuum rex ab Abiâ designatus, eâ famâ peruulgatâ, profugit in Ægyptum pauore. Post Salomonis mortem reuersus in patriam, rex proclamatur publicis comitiis. Hic est, qui Israelem peccare fecit, mutando cultum diuinitùs præscriptum. Sæpiùs accusatus ab Abiâ, nihilo fit melior. Unde quoties literæ sacræ regem impium appellant, Ieroboami dicunt secutum vestigia.
units.tr: 149. Jeroboam, Solomon's brave and diligent governor, was designated by Ahijah as king of the ten tribes. When this report spread widely, he fled in terror into Egypt. After Solomon's death he returned to his country and was proclaimed king by a public assembly. He is the one who made Israel sin by changing the worship prescribed by God. Though often rebuked by Ahijah, he never got better. So whenever the sacred writings call a king impious, they say he followed in the footsteps of Jeroboam.

units.la: 150. Propheta anonymus, è Iudæâ missus ad Ieroboamum, vaticinatur de eversione altaris in Bethel, & nomen eversoris futuri nominat Iosiam. Iussus iter suum ieiunus conficere, non paret mandato Dei, & ideò à leone dilaniatur.
units.tr: 150. An anonymous prophet, sent from Judah to Jeroboam, prophesied the overthrow of the altar at Bethel and named the future destroyer, Josiah. Ordered to make his journey fasting, he did not obey God's command, and for this reason he was torn apart by a lion.

units.la: 151. Nadab, rex secundus, Ieroboami filius, anno regni secundo tollitur è vitâ miserrimè, inque ipso stirps & regnum Ieroboami deficit, quemadmodum Deus per Ahiam fuerat Ieroboamo minatus.
units.tr: 151. Nadab, the second king, son of Jeroboam, was taken miserably from life in the second year of his reign. With him the line and kingdom of Jeroboam came to an end, just as God had threatened Jeroboam through Ahijah.

units.la: 152. Baesa, rex tertius, ad regnum scelere peruenit. Fuit similis Jeroboamo, ne quicquam proficiente propheta Jehu, quem Ella interfecit.
units.tr: 152. Baasha, the third king, reached the throne by crime. He was like Jeroboam, and when the prophet Jehu achieved nothing, Elah had him killed.

units.la: 153. Ella, rex quartus, Baësæ filius, fatuus & temulentus, à Zamrio magistro equitum inter vina opprimitur.
units.tr: 153. Elah, the fourth king, son of Baasha, foolish and drunken, was overpowered during a drinking bout by Zimri, the commander of half his chariots.

units.la: 154. Zamri, rex quintus, interfecto Ellâ, sedem regiam occupat, & diadema insciente populo sibi rapit. Populus ducem militiæ Amri, regem creant, & ad Tharsam[?], sedem regiam, copias suas omnes adducunt. Zamri conscientiâ facinoris & periculi præsentiâ amens, regiam clausam incendit, & cum scelerum sociis se cremat.
units.tr: 154. Zimri, the fifth king, after killing Elah, seized the royal seat and snatched the crown without the people's knowledge. The people made Omri, the commander of the army, king, and they all marched to Tirzah[?], the royal seat. Zimri, out of his mind from the awareness of his crime and the nearness of danger, set fire to the closed palace and burned himself with the partners in his crimes.

units.la: 155. Amri, rex sextus, per tumultum adipiscitur regnum. Diviso enim post Tharsam occupatam in duas factiones populo, à nonnullis eligitur Thibni, sed Amri fautores prævaluerunt: rege autem alterius factionis in ipsâ contentione mortuo, communi consensu rex salutatur Amri. Qui ædificauit Samariam, & propter loci opportunitatem in eam transtulit regiam.
units.tr: 155. Omri, the sixth king, gained the kingdom through turmoil. After Tirzah had been taken, the people split into two factions. Some chose Tibni, but Omri's supporters prevailed. When the king of the other faction died during the very struggle, Omri was hailed as king by common consent. He built Samaria and moved the royal seat there because of the suitability of the place.

units.la: 156. Achab, rex septimus, filius Amri, regum omnium impiissimus, author fuit fœdissimarum superstitionum, & crudeliter persecutus est prophetas. Eius uxor Jefabel, Sidonia, regis filia, regum duorum mater, mulier importuna, iracunda, superba, ecclesiasticis & politicis negotiis sese impotenter ingerens, tandem de fenestrâ præcipitata periit.
units.tr: 156. Ahab, the seventh king, son of Omri, the most impious of all kings, was the author of the most foul superstitions, and he cruelly persecuted the prophets. His wife Jezebel, a Sidonian, daughter of a king and mother of two kings, was a troublesome, angry, proud woman who meddled without restraint in church and state affairs. At last she was thrown from a window and perished.

units.la: 157. Elias, Thesbites, fuit propheta magni zeli, miraculis clarus, quadrigis igneis in cœlum raptus. Post concilium Carmelitanum sacerdotes Baaliticos octingentos & quinquaginta ferro iussit interfici.
units.tr: 157. Elijah, the Tishbite, was a prophet of great zeal, famous for his miracles, who was taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire. After the council on Carmel he ordered eight hundred and fifty priests of Baal to be slain with the sword.

units.la: 158. Vidua Sareptana, Eliæ parat cibum tempore famis. Ideo urnulæ ipsius nunquam farina, aut gutto oleum deerat, totâ illâ tempestate difficillimâ. Filium eius è morte excitauit Elias.
units.tr: 158. The widow of Zarephath prepared food for Elijah in time of famine. So her little jar never lacked flour, nor her jug oil, throughout that most difficult season. Elijah raised her son from death.

units.la: 159. Abdias, aulæ Achabi præfectus, fuit fidus ecclesiæ hospes, sed tectus & timidus.
units.tr: 159. Obadiah, the steward of Ahab's household, was a faithful host to the Church, but he was secretive and fearful.

units.la: 160. Nabothus, falsò accusatus læsæ maiestatis, quòd
units.tr: 160. Naboth, falsely accused of treason because

units.la: Achabo vinetum paternum prope regis palatium vendere nollet, testibus conductis damnatur, & lapidatur.
units.tr: he refused to sell his father's vineyard, near the royal palace, to Ahab, was condemned by hired witnesses and stoned.

units.la: 161. Propheta anonymus, mittitur ad Achabum, qui ipsum consilio instruat, quo Syriæ regem Bendadum aggrediatur & vincat. Achab victoriâ potitus, non sequitur præceptum prophetæ de occidendo hoste. Ob quam leniitem propheta regem increpat, & iram Dei iamiam arsuram in populum denuntiat.
units.tr: 161. An anonymous prophet was sent to Ahab, to advise him how to attack and defeat Ben-hadad, king of Syria. Ahab gained the victory but did not follow the prophet's command to kill the enemy. For this leniency the prophet rebuked the king and announced that the wrath of God was about to fall upon the people.

units.la: 162. Benhadad, I, Syrus, rex sui seculi potentissimus, cum duobus regibus Iudæ, Abiâ & Asâ, confœderatus fuit: cum tribus regibus Israëlis, Baësâ, Achabo, & Ioramo, ferro dimicavit. Baëlam vicit vnâ incursione, cum Achabo tria bella gessit. Primo secum educit reges duos & triginta, sed in fugam coniicitur: altero centum millia peditum amittit, qui gladio occubuerunt; septem & viginti millia, qui ruinâ urbis cuiusdam interierunt: tertio demum victor fuit, quo & rex Iosaphat fugatus, & Achab traiectus est. Ioramo temporibus Samariam obsidione & fame presslit: à quâ Deus mirabiliter exercitum ipsius depulit.
units.tr: 162. Ben-hadad I, the Syrian, the most powerful king of his age, was allied with two kings of Judah, Abijah and Asa. He fought with three kings of Israel: Baasha, Ahab and Joram. He defeated Baelam in a single attack, and he waged three wars against Ahab. In the first he led out thirty-two kings with him, but he was put to flight. In the second he lost a hundred thousand foot soldiers, who fell by the sword, and twenty-seven thousand who perished when a certain city collapsed. In the third he was at last victorious, when King Jehoshaphat was put to flight and Ahab was pierced. In Joram's time he pressed Samaria with siege and famine, but God miraculously drove his army away.

units.la: 163. Fœmina Sunamitis, Elisæo hospitium subinde concedit, & ab illo variis beneficiis ornatur.
units.tr: 163. The Shunammite woman repeatedly offered Elisha lodging, and he honoured her with various kindnesses.

units.la: 164. Elisæus, ex agricolâ fit propheta, Eliâ dignus discipulis, oraculis & miraculis clarus.
units.tr: 164. Elisha, from a farmer became a prophet, worthy of Elijah as his teacher, famous for his oracles and miracles.

units.la: 165. Gehazi, fuit famulus Elisæi primò fidelis, postea corruptus avaritiâ: quam ob causam lepra inficitur, quæ ad eius quoque posteros vulgata est.
units.tr: 165. Gehazi, at first a faithful servant of Elisha, was afterwards corrupted by greed. For this reason he was struck with leprosy, which also spread to his descendants.

units.la: 166. Pueri Bethelenses, improbitatis & proteruiæ suæ pœnas dant, quòd Elisæum canitie venerabilem subsannarent.
units.tr: 166. The boys of Bethel paid the penalty for their wickedness and impudence, because they mocked Elisha, a man venerable for his grey hair.

units.la: 167. Naaman, regi Syriæ acceptissimus vir, à lepra sanatur per Elisæum, & hoc beneficio allicitur ad cultum Dei.
units.tr: 167. Naaman, a man most acceptable to the king of Syria, was cured of leprosy by Elisha, and through this benefit he was drawn to the worship of God.

units.la: 168. Discipuli Elisæi, victu tenui alebantur: qui, cum per imprudentiam alicuius è medio ipsorum esset venenata quadam herbâ infectus, ab Elisæo corrigitur.
units.tr: 168. The disciples of Elisha were fed on meagre fare. When one of them, through someone's carelessness, was infected by a poisonous herb in the pot, he was set right by Elisha.

units.la: 169. Micheas vaticinando dicit quod res est, & ideo multatur colapho & custodiâ.
units.tr: 169. Micaiah speaks the truth in prophesying, and for this reason he is punished with a blow and imprisonment.

units.la: 170. Sedechias, propheta mendax, superbus & percussor, habuit asseclas fere quadringentos. Decepit Iosephatum & Achabum. Tandem cum suis conuincitur vanitatis & audaciae: & regum, qui ipsi crediderant, alter interficitur, alter vulneratur.
units.tr: 170. Zedekiah, a lying prophet, proud and violent, had about four hundred followers. He deceived Jehoshaphat and Ahab. At last he and his men were proved vain and rash, and one of the kings who had trusted them was killed, the other wounded.

units.la: 171. Ochozias, rex octauus, Achabi filius, parentibus pessimis simillimus & infelix.
units.tr: 171. Ahaziah, the eighth king, son of Ahab, was very like his wicked parents and unfortunate.

units.la: 172. Ioram, rex nonus, auum, patrem, fratrem habuit reges. Ipse in stirpe suâ postremus fuit: vir impius & infelix; in tumultu obtruncatus à Iehu tribuno.
units.tr: 172. Joram, the ninth king, had kings for his grandfather, his father and his brother. He was the last of his line: an impious and unfortunate man, cut down in a riot by the captain Jehu.

units.la: 173. Iehu, rex decimus, fuit inter viros robustos Iorami fortissimus, & inter duces eius st[?] enuos celerrimus. Ab Elisaei discipulo rex unguitur. Usus est Elisaei consilio, & vaticinia Eliae non ignorauit, eaque summis viribus est executus. Nam reges Israelis & Iudae, Ioramum & Ochoziam, de vita sustulit: Iezabelem reginam de fenestra praecipitauit: de regia stirpe homines centum & duodecim iugulari praecepit; filios vidit. Achabi 170, & fratres regis Ochoziae 42; itemque consiliariorum & sacerdotum Achabi magnum numerum. Conuentu Samariam indicto, Baalis sacerdotes, insidiis & simulatione in unum collectos, interficit vniuersos, & è templo eius cloacam publicam facit: vitulos tamen aureos non sustulit. Posteritas eius durauit ad quartam vsque sobolem.
units.tr: 173. Jehu, the tenth king, was the bravest of Joram's sturdy men and the swiftest of his fierce commanders. He was anointed king by a disciple of Elisha. He used Elisha's counsel, did not ignore the prophecies of Elijah, and carried them out with all his might. For he removed from life the kings of Israel and Judah, Joram and Ahaziah. He threw Queen Jezebel from a window. He ordered a hundred and twelve men of the royal line to be slaughtered, and he saw the sons of Ahab, one hundred and seventy, and the brothers of King Ahaziah, forty-two, put to death; likewise a great number of Ahab's counsellors and priests. He called an assembly at Samaria, and by stratagem and pretence gathered the priests of Baal together and killed them all. He made a public sewer of their temple. Yet he did not remove the golden calves. His posterity lasted to the fourth generation.

units.la: 174. Ioachas, Iehu filius, rex vndecimus, fuit regum ante se omnium infelicissimus. Nam armis Syriacis ita est attritus, vt paucas ad corporis custodiam equitum turmas haberet: & ex omni flore iuuentutis, ac populo potentissimo, vltra decem peditum millia non posset armare amplius.
units.tr: 174. Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, the eleventh king, was the most unfortunate of all the kings before him. For he was so worn down by the Syrian armies that he had only a few squadrons of horsemen to guard his person, and from the whole flower of his youth and a powerful people he could not muster more than ten thousand foot soldiers.

units.la: 175. Ioas, rex duodecimus, Ioachae filius, aui sui Iehu successibus fuit usus. Ideo seruator populi cognominatus est, & regnauit cum dignitate, & finitimorum terrore.
units.tr: 175. Joash, the twelfth king, son of Jehoahaz, enjoyed the successes of his grandfather Jehu. For this reason he was surnamed the saviour of the people, and he reigned with dignity and to the terror of his neighbours.

units.la: 176. Azahel, Benhadi I. praefectus, in regem Syriae vngitur ab Elia, confirmatur ab Elisaeo. Vtrumque regnum, Iudae & Israelis, hoc tamen potius quam illud, valde attriuit.
units.tr: 176. Hazael, an officer of Ben-hadad I, was anointed king of Syria by Elijah and confirmed by Elisha. He sorely wore down both kingdoms, Judah and Israel, yet Israel more than the other.

units.la: 177. Benhadad II, regis Azahelis filius, non minore odio quàm pater, sed minore successu pugnauit in Israelem.
units.tr: 177. Ben-hadad II, son of King Hazael, fought against Israel with no less hatred than his father, but with less success.

units.la: 178. Ieroboam II, rex decimus tertius, Ioae filius, animo & felicitate patre non fuit inferior. Multis modis crudelitatem & superbiam Syrorum est vltus. Aures autem praebens hypocritis, Deum ex animo secutus non est.
units.tr: 178. Jeroboam II, the thirteenth king, son of Joash, was not inferior to his father in spirit or in good fortune. In many ways he avenged the cruelty and pride of the Syrians. Yet, lending his ears to hypocrites, he did not follow God wholeheartedly.

units.la: 179. Amos, propheta factus ex bubulco, gnauiter & grauiter suo fungitur officio, nihil territus aduersitatibꝰ[?], quas expertus est, inprimis ab Amasiâ, parasito Ieroboami. Amos[?] contemporaneus fuit Ioel.
units.tr: 179. Amos, a prophet made from a herdsman, performed his office vigorously and seriously, not frightened by the hardships he suffered, above all from Amaziah, the flatterer of Jeroboam. Amos was a contemporary of Joel.

units.la: 180. Ionas, non modo sui populi, sed etiam gentium, puta Assyriorum, doctor, Ieroboamo regi addit animum contra Syros. Crinibus veluti fuit tractus ad obediendum Deo in legatione ad Nineuitas.
units.tr: 180. Jonah, teacher not only of his own people but also of the nations, namely the Assyrians, encourages King Jeroboam against the Syrians. He was, as it were, dragged by the hair to obey God in his mission to the Ninevites.

units.la: 181. Zacharias, Ieroboami filius, rex decimus quartus, propter actam impie vitam, omnem gloriam paternam una cum vita & regno amittit, obtruncatus à Sallum seditioso. In hoc rege, abnepote Iehu, maiorum familia, & regni dignitas concidit: ita uti Deus minatus fuerat. Causae ig.interitus familiarum sunt idololatria & superbia.
units.tr: 181. Zechariah, son of Jeroboam, the fourteenth king, on account of his impious life, loses all his father's glory together with his life and kingdom, cut down by the seditious Shallum. With this king, great-grandson of Jehu, the house of his forebears and the dignity of the kingdom fell, just as God had threatened. The causes of the ruin of dynasties are idolatry and pride.

units.la: 182. Sallum, rex decimus quintus, crudelis sicarius & parricida, regnum caede partum caede amisit.
units.tr: 182. Shallum, the fifteenth king, a cruel assassin and parricide, lost by murder the kingdom he had won by murder.

units.la: 183. Manahom, rex XVI. Sallunum tyrannū occidit, & regnum sibi vendicat, illudque administrat auare & immaniter. Sub hoc rege Phul Assyrius infestat Israelem.
units.tr: 183. Menahem, the sixteenth king, killed the tyrant Shallum and claimed the kingdom for himself, administering it greedily and savagely. Under this king Phul the Assyrian attacks Israel.

units.la: 184. Phaceia, rex decimus septimus, Menahemi F.malo ingenio, & moribus sceleratis regnauit petulanter. Huius petulantiae praemium consecutus est dignissimum:en. Se videlic. traiectus à Pecâ, vno ex optimatibus, qui à rege tertius censebatur.
units.tr: 184. Pekahiah, the seventeenth king, son of Menahem, of wicked nature and criminal morals, reigned wantonly. He obtained the most fitting reward for his wantonness: namely, he was run through by Pekah, one of the nobles, who was reckoned third after the king.

units.la: 185. Peca, siue Phacea, rex decimus octauus, regis sui parriparricida, cum audacia coniunctos successus habuit. Centum & viginti millia hominum occidit in bello, quod Iothamo regi Iudae intulit. Sed a rege Assyriorum Tiglatphilassare vincitur, & ab Hosea comprehensus per insidias, de vita tollitur.
units.tr: 185. Pekah, the eighteenth king, a parricide of his own king, had successes joined with audacity. He killed one hundred and twenty thousand men in the war he waged against Jotham, king of Judah. But he is conquered by the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser, and, seized by treachery by Hoshea, is taken from life.

units.la: 186. Obed, propheta, clade Iudaeorum intellecta, exercitui Pecę triumphanti obviam progreditur, & suadet, ut matronas imbelles, & aetatis tenerae multitudo, incolumes dimittantur; idque impetrat.
units.tr: 186. Obed, a prophet, having perceived the slaughter of the Jews, goes out to meet the army of Pekah in its triumph, and persuades them to let the unwarlike matrons and the multitude of tender age go unharmed; and he obtains this.

units.la: 187. Hosea, rex ultimus, potentiam violenter comparat, & violenter amittit. Regi Assyriorum Salmanassari factus tributarius, cum Ægyptio de rebellione cogitat. Proditis eius consiliis, ab Assyrio captus, in vincula detruditur, & Samaria tribus annis obsessa expugnatur. Rege vincto, & capta gentis metropoli, populus Israëliticus in perpetuam captivitatem abducitur. Quarum aerumnarum causa fuit Dei, & verbi eius contemtio. Durauit hoc regnum an. 258.
units.tr: 187. Hosea, the last king, violently acquires power and violently loses it. Made tributary to the Assyrian king Shalmaneser, he plots rebellion with the Egyptian. When his plans are betrayed, he is captured by the Assyrian and thrust into chains, and Samaria, besieged for three years, is taken. The king being bound and the capital of the nation taken, the Israelite people are led away into perpetual captivity. The cause of these miseries was contempt of God and of his word. This kingdom lasted 258 years.

units.la: VIII. Prosopographia, tempore regni Iu- daici, seu Hierosolymitani, ex libris Regum & Chronicorum, est eiusmodi.
units.tr: VIII. Prosopography of the time of the kingdom of Judah, or of Jerusalem, from the books of Kings and Chronicles, is as follows.

units.la: 189. Rehabeam, siue Roboam, rex primus, Salomonis F, puerili animo atque consilio, cum adolescentibus stultis perverse deliberans, populum alienat levitate & superbia. Ideo tribus ab eo decem ad Ieroboamum defecerunt: ipse tribus duas, Iudae & Beniaminis, tantum retinet. Primo triennio bene se gessit, ut Nero primo quinquennio. Postea nec ipse Dei cultum sincerum curavit, nec aliis conseruavit pristinum beneficium. A' Sesaco igitur rege Ægyptiorum affligitur, urbe Hierosolyma direptâ, & regiâ atque aerario spoliato.
units.tr: 189. Rehoboam, or Roboam, the first king, son of Solomon, with a childish mind and counsel, deliberating perversely with foolish young men, alienates the people by levity and pride. Therefore ten tribes defected from him to Jeroboam; he himself retains only two tribes, Judah and Benjamin. He conducted himself well in the first three years, as Nero did in the first five. Afterwards he neither looked after pure worship of God himself, nor preserved for others the former benefit. Therefore he is afflicted by Shishak, king of the Egyptians, the city of Jerusalem is plundered, and the royal house and treasury are stripped.

units.la: 190. Semeias, propheta, exercitum Roboami contra regem Israëlis paratum, sua authoritate revocat, & arma regi animoso excutit. Idem post vastatam provinciam, & captam urbem sacram ab Ægyptiis, regem & principes consolatur.
units.tr: 190. Shemaiah, the prophet, by his authority calls back the army of Rehoboam prepared against the king of Israel, and wrests the arms from the spirited king. The same man, after the province was laid waste and the holy city taken by the Egyptians, consoles the king and princes.

units.la: 191. Abia, rex secundus, filius Roboami, patre quidè sapientior & fortior, sed non minùs temerarius atq; impius fuit. Ieroboamum, qui duplò maiore exercitu ipsum intercluserat, fugauit.
units.tr: 191. Abijah, the second king, son of Rehoboam, indeed wiser and stronger than his father, but no less rash and impious. He put to flight Jeroboam, who had surrounded him with an army twice as large.

units.la: 192. Asa, rex tertius, Abiae F, pietate & iustitiâ celebris, tranquillè regnat primis annis decem: quo tempore idola confringit, lucos incendit, homines impuros exilio mulctat, collapsam disciplinam instaurat, religionis veritatem revocat, denique matri peruicaci & superstitiosae, & nomen Augustae seu antistitae, & potestatem reginae ad. imit. Cum rege Aethiopum Zarâ, primùm praelio congrediens decies centena millia hominum internecione delet. Iterum cum rege Israelis Baesâ, auxiliis Benhadadi Syri, pugnans, tribum Naphthali occupat. Fossam ingentem, ad arcendas Israelis incursiones, impensis magnis ducit. Aetate extremâ laborauit podagrâ.
units.tr: 192. Asa, the third king, son of Abijah, celebrated for piety and justice, reigns peacefully in the first ten years; in which time he breaks the idols, burns the groves, punishes impure men with exile, restores the fallen discipline, revives the truth of religion, and deprives his stubborn and superstitious mother of the title of Augusta, or abbess, and of the power of queen. Engaging first in battle with Zerah, king of the Ethiopians, he destroys a million men by slaughter. Again fighting with Baasha, king of Israel, with the aid of Ben-hadad of Syria, he occupies the tribe of Naphtali. At great expense he builds a huge trench to keep off the incursions of Israel. In his last years he suffered from gout.

units.la: 193. Azarias, propheta, regi Asae gratulatur de victoriâ contra Aegyptios, & ipsum seueritate orationis ita impellit, vt idola euerteret, sedemque & domicilium hospitibus piis concederet. Hic propheta fuit quasi consiliarius ecclesiasticus Asae.
units.tr: 193. Azariah, the prophet, congratulates King Asa on his victory over the Egyptians, and by the severity of his speech impels him to overthrow the idols and to give a home and dwelling to pious strangers. This prophet was, as it were, the ecclesiastical counsellor of Asa.

units.la: 194. Hanan, propheta, regem Asam grauiter obiurgat, quòd amicitiam cum Benhadado Syro iunxerat, & auxilium hominis, auxilio Dei omnipotentis antepofuerat. Quâ accusatione, rex alioquin minimè malus, ita excanduit, vt habenas irae nimium laxaret, & prophetam in vincula coniiceret.
units.tr: 194. Hanani, the prophet, sharply rebukes King Asa because he had joined friendship with Ben-hadad of Syria and had preferred the help of man to the help of almighty God. By this accusation the king, otherwise by no means wicked, was so inflamed that he let the reins of his anger loose too far, and cast the prophet into chains.

units.la: 195. Iosaphat, rex quartus, Asae F. fuit iustissimus atque optimus: nisi quòd cum regibus Israelis, Achabo & Ochoziâ, affinitatem & societatem iniit: quae & prophetis displicuit, & ipsi eiusque regno penè exitio fuit.
units.tr: 195. Jehoshaphat, the fourth king, son of Asa, was most just and excellent, except that he entered into marriage alliance and partnership with the kings of Israel, Ahab and Ahaziah; which displeased the prophets, and nearly brought ruin upon him and his kingdom.

units.la: 196. Amarias, sacerdos, constitutus à Iosaphato pontisex, nihil praetermisit, quod ad viri sapientis & sedulimu[?] nus atque dignitatem pertineret. Idem fecit Zabadias in rebus ciuilibus. Vtriq; non defuit studium & opera regis laudatissimi.
units.tr: 196. Amariah, a priest, appointed high priest by Jehoshaphat, omitted nothing that pertained to the duty and dignity of a wise and diligent man. Zebadiah did the same in civil affairs. To both the zeal and labour of the most praiseworthy king were not wanting.

units.la: 197. Iehu, propheta, Hananis F, Iosaphatum è bello Syriaco faucium reuertentem, animo forti increpat, regemque habet docilem & obsequentem.
units.tr: 197. Jehu, the prophet, son of Hanani, rebukes with courage Jehoshaphat returning from the Syrian war, and finds the king teachable and obedient.

units.la: 198. Iehafiel, propheta, idemq; Leuita & musicus, prædicit Iosaphato victoriam, & viam ad victoriam ostendit, nempe fiduciam in Deum.
units.tr: 198. Jahaziel, the prophet, who was also a Levite and musician, foretells victory to Jehoshaphat, and shows him the way to victory, namely trust in God.

units.la: 199. Elieʒer, propheta, Iosaphatum obiurgat, quòd affinitati regum Israëlis plus tribuat & deferat honoris, quàm Dei verbo & virtuti.
units.tr: 199. Eliezer, the prophet, rebukes Jehoshaphat because he gives more weight and honour to his marriage alliance with the kings of Israel than to the word and power of God.

units.la: 200. Ioram, rex V, Iosaphati filius primogenitus, fuit degener, impius, & infelix. Vxor ipsius Athalia, filia Achabi, fuit fœmina supra sexum crudelis & furiosa[?]. Ioram laborauit alui profluuio per biennium, donec intestina defluerent, & ipse tabe conficeretur.
units.tr: 200. Joram, the fifth king, the firstborn son of Jehoshaphat, was degenerate, impious and unhappy. His wife, Athaliah, daughter of Ahab, was a woman cruel and frenzied beyond her sex. Joram suffered from a flux of the bowels for two years, until his intestines poured out and he was wasted by putrefaction.

units.la: 201. Ochozias, rex sextus, natu minimus Iorami F, remansit solus superstes è fratribus, qui ab Arabibus occisi erant. Huic causa exitii & interitus fuerunt, mater scelerata, & consiliarii improbi.
units.tr: 201. Ahaziah, the sixth king, youngest son of Joram, remained the only survivor of the brothers who had been killed by the Arabs. The causes of his ruin and death were his wicked mother and wicked counsellors.

units.la: 202. Athalia, septimum locum obtinet inter reges Iudæ. Fuit furiæ, quàm reginæ similior. Filio Ochoziæ defuncto tyrannidem arripit: templum Dei demolitur, Baalis erigit atque ditat: omnium piorum atrox aduersaria. Regiam quoque stirpem Dauidis, parricidio extinguit, uno infante Ioâ excepto. Fuit ergo quasi mater Antichristi; utpote quæ semen benedictum perdere & extirpare voluit. Ioiada sacerdos ipsam è templo extractam, obtruncat, quòd cum Ioâ facere recusaret.
units.tr: 202. Athaliah holds the seventh place among the kings of Judah. She was more like a fury than a queen. On the death of Ahaziah's son she seizes the tyranny: she demolishes the temple of God, and erects and enriches Baal; she is a savage enemy of all the pious. She also destroys the royal line of David by parricide, one infant, Joash, excepted. She was therefore, as it were, the mother of Antichrist, since she wished to destroy and root out the blessed seed. The priest Jehoiada drags her out of the temple and kills her, because she refused to go along with Joash.

units.la: 203. Ioas, rex octauus, anno ætatis septimo consecratur oleo à Ioiadâ, magnâ spe indolis sapientis & religiosæ. Facit ab initio omnia regis sancti officia: nisi quòd Ioiadâ defuncto, eius filium Zachariam, sacerdotem excellentem, lapidibus obrui finit: oblitus omnium beneficiorum, quæ acceperat: nec ullâ post id facinus felicitate domi aut foris usus.
units.tr: 203. Joash, the eighth king, in the seventh year of his age is anointed with oil by Jehoiada, with great hope of a wise and religious disposition. From the beginning he performs all the duties of a holy king, except that, after Jehoiada's death, he allows Jehoiada's son Zechariah, an excellent priest, to be stoned to death, forgetful of all the benefits he had received; and after that crime he enjoyed no prosperity at home or abroad.

units.la: 204. Ioiada, sacerdos, cognomento Barachias, Ioam è manibus Athaliæ clam ereptum populo producit, & regem proclamat. Templum, aram, statuam Baalis confringit: Matthanem, summum sacerdotem, ad aram mactat. Quamdiu regi à sacris & consiliis fuit, omnia in templo & repub. bene se habuerunt. Sed cùm è viuis excessisset, aulicorum Ioæ indulgentia & obsequium effecit, vt rex adolescens corruptus, & idololatra & tyrannus fieret.
units.tr: 204. Jehoiada, the priest, surnamed Barachias, secretly snatches Joash from the hands of Athaliah, presents him to the people, and proclaims him king. He smashes the temple, the altar and the statue of Baal; he slaughters Mattan, the high priest, at the altar. As long as he presided over the sacred and public counsels, all went well in the temple and the commonwealth. But when he had departed from the living, the indulgence and compliance of the courtiers of Joash made the young king corrupt, and he became an idolater and tyrant.

units.la: 205. Zacharias, Ioiadæ F. integritatis & libertatis paternæ imitator, aulicos Ioæ superstitiosos & effrænes, & regis imperiti animum ad insaniam similem trahentes, magnâ authoritate increpuit. Quod cùm illi ægrè ferrent, in vestibulo templi, rege connivente, lapidib. ipsum obruunt. Vindictam diuinam, & regi & aulicis, in ipsâ morte denunciat, nec fefellit vaticinium. Nam spatio an. ni nondum exacto, violentâ & malâ morte perierunt universi. Apud Matthæum Christus cum Abele coniungit hunc Zachariam. Ita primus martyr V.T. est Abel, postremus Zacharias: de quo nempe sacræ literæ expresse testantur.
units.tr: 205. Zechariah, son of Jehoiada, imitator of his father's integrity and freedom, rebukes with great authority the superstitious and unbridled courtiers of Joash, who were drawing the mind of the inexperienced king towards a similar madness. When they took this ill, they stoned him to death in the vestibule of the temple, the king conniving. In his very death he announces divine vengeance upon both the king and the courtiers, and the prophecy did not fail. For before the year was out, all of them perished by violent and evil death. In Matthew, Christ joins this Zechariah with Abel. Thus Abel is the first martyr of the Old Testament, and Zechariah the last: concerning whom the sacred letters expressly bear witness.

units.la: 206. Amasias, rex nonus, Ioæ F, patris necem sine crudelitate vindicat. Homicidas enim perimit, liberis eorum innocentibus parcit. Sub initium fuit felix.
units.tr: 206. Amaziah, the ninth king, son of Joash, avenged his father's death without cruelty. He put the murderers to death but spared their innocent children. At the beginning of his reign he was prosperous.

units.la: 207. Propheta anonymus, bis mittitur ad Amasiam, qui priorem admonitionem æquo, posteriorem iniquo fert animo.
units.tr: 207. An anonymous prophet was sent twice to Amaziah. He took the first warning calmly and the second with ill temper.

units.la: 208. Ozias, alio nomine Azarias, Amasiæ F, rex X, fuit bonus paterfamilias, fortissimus vir, & prudentissimus gubernator. In magnâ felicitate eò dementiæ peruenit, vt sacerdotis munus exequi aggrederetur. Quæ ipsius πολυπραγμοσύνῃ[?] fuit punita lepra incurabili.
units.tr: 208. Uzziah, also called Azariah, son of Amaziah, the tenth king, was a good head of his household, a very brave man and a most prudent governor. In his great prosperity he fell into such madness that he undertook to perform the office of priest. For this meddling [πολυπραγμοσύνη] he was punished with incurable leprosy.

units.la: 209. Azarias, sacerdos maximi animi, & legis antiquæ defensor, regem Oziam adolescentem incensum prohibet: cui assensi sunt octoginta alii sacerdotes.
units.tr: 209. Azariah, a priest of great courage and a defender of the ancient law, forbade King Uzziah, who was inflamed with anger. Eighty other priests agreed with him.

units.la: 210. Iotham, rex vndecimus, Oziæ F, patre suo propter morbum tetrum, à multitudine segregato, regni habenas tenuit, non sine laude pietatis & magnificen-tiæ.
units.tr: 210. Jotham, the eleventh king, son of Uzziah, held the reins of the kingdom while his father was kept apart from the people by a foul disease. He did this not without praise for his piety and generosity.

units.la: 211. Achas, rex XII. Iothami F, fuit omnium religionū & cultuum externorum insipiens imitator: homo pessimus, & infelicissimus.
units.tr: 211. Ahaz, the twelfth king, son of Jotham, was a foolish imitator of all the religions and foreign cults. He was a most wicked and most unhappy man.

units.la: 212. Vrias, sacerdos hypocrita, regis Achae impiis suroribus, non modò non resistit, sed omnia eius iussa execranda scelerate comprobat & exequitur.
units.tr: 212. Uriah, a hypocritical priest, did not merely fail to resist the impious rages of King Ahaz; he also approved and carried out, in a wicked manner, all his detestable commands.

units.la: 213. Ezechias, rex XIII, patris pessimi, filius praestantissimus, fuit Dei amans, & religionis verae instaurator pius, & felix.
units.tr: 213. Hezekiah, the thirteenth king, was the most outstanding son of a most wicked father. He loved God, was a pious restorer of the true religion, and was prosperous.

units.la: 214. Salmanassar, Assyriorum imperator, capit Samariam, Hoseam regem abducit, & populum in exteras colonias distribuit, gentesq; Persicas in Iudaeam mittit. Cùm autem agros Samariae leones vastarent, & colonos ipsos laniarent, eis sacerdotem Israëliticum praefecit, qui populum expiaret, rectèque instrueret. Igitur religio Iudaica iam ante in Samaria corrupta, cum gentili fuit commixta. Unde Samaritani pessimè apud Iudaeos audiuerunt, & convitium est in historiâ evangelicâ, Samaritanum appellari.
units.tr: 214. Shalmaneser, emperor of the Assyrians, took Samaria, carried King Hoshea away, and distributed the people among foreign colonies. He sent Persian peoples into Judaea. But when lions began to lay waste the fields of Samaria and tear the settlers themselves, he set over them an Israelite priest to purify the people and instruct them properly. Thus the Jewish religion, already corrupted in Samaria, was mixed with paganism. For this reason the Samaritans were very badly regarded by the Jews, and in the gospel story to be called a Samaritan is an insult.

units.la: 215. Sanherib, sive Sennacherib, aliàs Sargon, filius Salmanassaris, aegrè facit Ezechiae, qui frustrà ipsum conciliare studet muneribus. Exercitu eius ad Hierosolymam deletoab angelo, ipse domum reversus à duobus filiis natu maioribus ferro transfoditur inter sacra immanissima, quibus duos filios natu minores immolabat ad reparandum deorum favorem.
units.tr: 215. Sennacherib, also called Sargon, son of Shalmaneser, was hostile to Hezekiah, who tried in vain to win him over with gifts. When his army was destroyed before Jerusalem by an angel, he returned home and was stabbed with a sword by his two elder sons, while he was in the midst of a most savage sacrifice, in which he offered his two younger sons to restore the favour of the gods.

units.la: 216. Tobias, senior, ductus in Assyriam, à Salmanassare opes & praefecturam accipit, à Sanheribo fortunis rursus exuitur, à Sarchedone bona amissa recuperat. Iactatus variis periculis, Dei timorem non abiicit. Tobias, iunior, coniugio sibi iungit Saram, filiam Raguelis, qui erat consobrinus Tobiae senioris, & habitabat Ecbatanis, urbe Medorum regiâ.
units.tr: 216. Tobias, the elder, was taken into Assyria. From Shalmaneser he received wealth and a governorship; under Sennacherib he was stripped of his property again; and from Sarchedonus he recovered his lost goods. Tossed about by many dangers, he did not cast off the fear of God. Tobias, the younger, married Sarah, daughter of Raguel, who was a cousin of the elder Tobias and lived at Ecbatana, the royal city of the Medes.

units.la: 217. Asarhaddon, ultimus imperatorum Assyriorum, filius Sanheribi, exemplo avi & patris, in Samariae civitates colonos peregrinos introducit. Inter hunc & Sanhe-ribum ribum vulgo collocatur Sarchedon, seu, ut alii legunt, Nachordan, & ipse filius Sanheribi. Hunc dicunt clementiâ usum erga Judæos exules.
units.tr: 217. Esarhaddon, the last of the Assyrian emperors, son of Sennacherib, following the example of his grandfather and father, settled foreign colonists in the cities of Samaria. Between him and Sennacherib is commonly placed Sarchedonus, or, as others read it, Nachordan, who was also a son of Sennacherib. They say he dealt mercifully with the Jewish exiles.

units.la: 218. Merodach, rex Babylonius, fuit amicus regis Ezechiae.
units.tr: 218. Merodach, king of Babylon, was a friend of King Hezekiah.

units.la: 219. Manasses, rex XIV, Ezechiae F, Rehabeamum, authorem corruptæ religionis, & omnes barbaros populos impietate superauit. Captus à rege Merodacho, in triumpho Babylonem abducitur, tum carceri tetro & vinculis durissimis annos decem includitur. Agens autem inter catastas & catenas pœnitentiam, Deo placato in regnum restituitur, & quidquid antea prauè egerat, id publicè emendat. Regnauit diutius quàm regum quisquam, annos videl.55[?].
units.tr: 219. Manasseh, the fourteenth king, son of Hezekiah, surpassed Rehoboam, the author of corrupt worship, and all the barbarous peoples in impiety. He was taken prisoner by King Merodach, led in triumph to Babylon, and shut up for ten years in a foul prison and in the harshest chains. But while he did penance amid fetters and chains, God was appeased and he was restored to his kingdom, and he publicly made amends for everything he had done wickedly before. He reigned longer than any other king, namely fifty-five years.

units.la: 220. Esaias, propheta, Amosi F, regis Amasiæ frater suisse putatur: etenim Christum suum patruelem nominat. Fuit itaque doctor nobilissimus; sed & fidelissimus, & in linguâ suâ copiosus & eloquens. Regem Acham & Ezechiam in negotiis grauissimis, tempore calamitoso juvit consiliis, consolatione, & precibus. Dicitur ferrâ dissectus à Manasse.
units.tr: 220. Isaiah, the prophet, is thought to have been a son of Amoz and a brother of King Amaziah, for he calls Christ his cousin. He was therefore a most noble teacher, and also most faithful, and rich and eloquent in his own language. In most serious affairs, in a time of calamity, he helped Kings Ahaz and Hezekiah with counsel, consolation and prayers. He is said to have been sawn asunder by Manasseh.

units.la: 221. Micha, Habacuc, & Nahum sunt contemporanei tum Esaiæ, tum inter se.
units.tr: 221. Micah, Habakkuk and Nahum were contemporaries both of Isaiah and of one another.

units.la: 222. Amon, rex XV, filius Manassis, quamuis patris vincula & calamitatem novisset, tamen eo non modò nihilo melior, sed propemodum deterior fuit: ideò propter tyrannidem initio regni sublatus est à suis familiaribus.
units.tr: 222. Amon, the fifteenth king, son of Manasseh, although he had known his father's chains and misfortune, was not only no better for it but nearly worse. Because of his tyranny at the start of his reign he was therefore killed by his own courtiers.

units.la: 223. Iosias, rex XVI, Amonis F, ætatis anno octavo rex creatur, cui similis pietate post Davidem nullus vixit. Postremus in regum sepulchris conditur, neque post eum alius rex pius, aut laude aliquâ dignus in hoc populo vixit.
units.tr: 223. Josiah, the sixteenth king, son of Amon, was made king in his eighth year of age. No one after David lived who was like him in piety. He was the last to be buried in the tombs of the kings; after him no other king lived who was pious or worthy of any praise among this people.

units.la: 224. Helchias, sacerdos, auspiciis Iosiæ totum regnum à sordibus & impuritate superstitionis inanis repurgatum, in dignitatem veterem, Deoq; acceptam restituit.
units.tr: 224. Hilkiah, the priest, under the auspices of Josiah, cleansed the whole kingdom of the filth and impurity of empty superstition and restored it to its former dignity, which was acceptable to God.

units.la: 225. Sophonias, propheta, ante reformationem Iosiæ concionatur, & acriter incultum falsorum numinum inuehitur.
units.tr: 225. Zephaniah, the prophet, preached before the reformation of Josiah and fiercely attacked the worship of false gods.

units.la: 226. Hulda, aliis Olda, prophetissa, Helchiæ mater, maiore quàm pro homine & muliere sapientia prædita, ludü puellarem aperuit, & pietatis initia corruptis temporib. tradidit. Eam, libro legis inuento, tanquam cœlestis doctrinæ magistram consuli rex Iosias imperat.
units.tr: 226. Huldah, also called Olda, a prophetess, the mother of Hilkiah, endowed with wisdom greater than is usual for a man or a woman, opened a school for girls and handed on the beginnings of piety in times of corruption. When a book of the law was found, King Josiah ordered that she be consulted as a teacher of heavenly doctrine.

units.la: 227. Passur, hypocrita, & primi nominis sacerdos, Ieremiam de bellis, dissipatione, & exilio multa tristia & ominosa quotidie inculcantem, tanquam authorem seditionis, pugno percutit, & in carcerem templo propinquum coniicit. Huic similis fuit Semeia, pseudopropheta, qui Zephonia sacerdoti ambitioso & potenti adsentatus est, eumque libro inscripto comparauit Ioiadæ: Ieremiam vero in inuidiam, quantum potuit, adduxit. His adde Ananiam pseudoprophetam, Ieremiæ æmulum.
units.tr: 227. Pashhur, a hypocrite and a priest of the first rank, struck Jeremiah with his fist, because Jeremiah kept daily urging many sad and ominous things about wars, dispersion and exile, and branded him as a author of sedition, and threw him into a prison near the temple. Similar to him was Shemaiah, a false prophet, who flattered the ambitious and powerful priest Zephaniah and compared him with Jehoiada in a book bearing his name, while he stirred up as much envy as he could against Jeremiah. To these add Ananias, a false prophet, a rival of Jeremiah.

units.la: 228. Rechabitæ, à patre in mandatis acceperant, ne quid proprium haberent, neue vitæ totius tempore vinum unquam gustarent. Eorum obedientiam Ieremias, cum reprehensione totius populi, veribis grauissimis commedat, quòd contra patrem agere noluerint: populus verò ipsum Deum non vereatur contemnere, neque præsenti calamitate monitus, adhuc resipiscere incipiat.
units.tr: 228. The Rechabites had received from their father the command that they should have no property of their own and should never taste wine during the whole of their lives. Jeremiah, rebuking the whole people, commends their obedience in most weighty words, because they would not act against their father; but the people do not fear to despise God himself, and though warned by present calamity, they do not yet begin to repent.

units.la: 229. Ioachas, rex XVII, primus Iosiæ F, mente & factis impius, exul in Ægyptum mittitur à Nechao rege Ægyptio.
units.tr: 229. Jehoahaz, the seventeenth king, the first son of Josiah, impious in mind and deeds, was sent into exile in Egypt by Pharaoh Necho, the king of Egypt.

units.la: 230. Ioachimus, siue Eliakim, secundus Iosiæ F, fuit impius & infelix. Vinctus Babylonem abducitur.
units.tr: 230. Jehoiakim, or Eliakim, the second son of Josiah, was impious and unhappy. He was led in chains to Babylon.

units.la: 231. Vrias, propheta, cum Ieremiâ consentiens & contra regem Ioachimum acerbè locutus, proscribitur, & ad supplicium postulatur atque rapitur.
units.tr: 231. Uriah, a prophet, agreeing with Jeremiah and speaking bitterly against King Jehoiakim, was outlawed and demanded for execution, and was seized.

units.la: 232. Nechaus, rex Ægypti, Iosiam sibi bellum illaturum, missis nuntiis dehortatur, se trasiturum[?] per eius prouinciam sine maleficio, quòd ire iussus sit, mandato Dei, contra regem Medorum: sed Iosias suspectam habens eius fidem, petitis acquiescere noluit. Pugna igitur commissa Iosias occiditur, & Iudaea tota spoliatur ac fit tributaria. Postea Nechaus a Nebucadnezare superatur, & tota Ægyptus in Babyloniorum potestatem venit.
units.tr: 232. Necho, king of Egypt, dissuaded Josiah by sending messengers from waging war against him. He said that he would pass through his province without harm, because he had been ordered by God to go against the king of the Medes. But Josiah, regarding his good faith with suspicion, would not agree to the request. So a battle was joined, Josiah was killed, and the whole of Judaea was plundered and made tributary. Afterwards Necho was defeated by Nebuchadnezzar, and all Egypt came under the power of the Babylonians.

units.la: 233. Iechonias, rex XIX, Ioachimi F, anno pueritiae suae[?] octauo regnum accipit ab Assyrio. Populus fatuus eius aetatem contemnit, & contra Assyrium, seu potius Babylonium, res nouas molitur. Eam ob causam & rex puer, & mater vidua, & regni optimates, & ex urbibus artifices, & quicunque aliqua re eminerent, Babylonem transferuntur.
units.tr: 233. Jehoiachin, the nineteenth king, son of Jehoiakim, received the kingdom from the Assyrian in the eighth year of his boyhood. The foolish people despised his youth and began to stir up revolution against the Assyrian, or rather the Babylonian. For this reason the boy king, his mother the widow, the nobles of the kingdom, the craftsmen from the cities and all who were distinguished in any way were carried away to Babylon.

units.la: 234. Saraias, fuit Ieremiae familiaris. Ebedmelech, patria Æthiops, regis Zedekiae aulicus, salutem dedit Ieremiae in pædore carceris iacenti. Sic ergo homo externus liberauit prophetam, quem sui ciues perdere satagebant. Istius humanitatis a Deo hanc mei[?] [illegible, ~1 letter]edem retulit, ut in bello non caderet, & vitam, quam viro sancto dederat, ipse quoque lucraretur.
units.tr: 234. Seraiah was a familiar friend of Jeremiah. Ebed-melech, an Ethiopian by birth, a courtier of King Zedekiah, gave help to Jeremiah lying in the filth of the prison. So a foreigner freed the prophet whom his own citizens were eager to destroy. God repaid him for this kindness with this: that he would not fall in war, and that he himself would also gain the life that he had given to the holy man.

units.la: 235. Zedekias, rex XX, postremus ille & miserrimus, tertius Iosiae F, dictus antea Matthathias, fratri suo patruelia Babylonio substituitur: sed sacramenti immemor, & Ieremiae faciem non erubescens, à rege deficit. Eâ de causâ Nebucadnezar misso exercitu urbem obsidet, inque suam potestatem omnibus redactis finem imponit regno Iudaico, quod inde à Roboamo duravit annos 391.
units.tr: 235. Zedekiah, the twentieth king, that last and most wretched one, the third son of Josiah, previously called Mattaniah, was set up by the Babylonian in place of his nephew, his brother's son. But forgetful of his oath, and not ashamed before Jeremiah, he revolted from the king. For this reason Nebuchadnezzar sent an army, besieged the city, reduced everything to his own power, and put an end to the kingdom of Judah, which had lasted from Rehoboam for 391 years.

units.la: IX. Prosopographia, tempore ecclesiae ex- ulis, atque restitutae, talis est ex Ieremiâ, Eze- chiele, libris Esdrae, Nehemiae, Estherae, Iudi- tha, & Malachiae.
units.tr: IX. Prosopography of the Church in exile and after its restoration, drawn from Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the books of Ezra, Nehemiah, Esther, Judith and Malachi.

units.la: 236. Ieremias, Helciae sacerdotis F, ab vtero matris consecratur doctor Iudaeorum & gentium: à prima vsq; adolescentia ad vitae exitu homo afflictissimus. Tot enim pene hostes habuit, quot auditores. In docendo fuit indefatigatus, in castigando acer, in periculis inuictus, in vinculis liberrimus, inimicus omnium impiorum sempiternus. Optione sibi data, vel in Iudaea manendi, vel Babylonem migrandi, ruinas patriae habitare maluit. Tumultu populari in Aegyptum per vim ducitur, & iuxta urbem Taphnas tandem saxis obruitur, in loco celebri sepultus, ut scribunt Graeci.
units.tr: 236. Jeremiah, son of the priest Hilkiah, was consecrated from his mother's womb as teacher of the Jews and the Gentiles. From earliest youth to the end of his life he was a most afflicted man. He had almost as many enemies as hearers. He was untiring in teaching, sharp in rebuke, unconquered in dangers, most free in chains, and everlastingly hostile to all the wicked. When he was given the choice of remaining in Judea or migrating to Babylon, he preferred to dwell among the ruins of his homeland. In a popular uprising he was dragged by force into Egypt, and near the city of Taphnas he was at last overwhelmed with stones and buried in a famous place, as the Greeks write.

units.la: 237. Gedalias, vir nobilis & moderatus, Palaestinae praesectus a Babylonio relinquitur. Ieremiam benigne & honorifice tractat. Reliquiae Iudaeorum sub ipso vixerunt tranquille: sed ipse vitio credulitatis nimium laborauit.
units.tr: 237. Gedaliah, a noble and moderate man, was left behind by the Babylonians as governor of Palestine. He treated Jeremiah kindly and honourably. Under him the remnant of the Jews lived in peace, but he himself suffered greatly from his fault of gullibility.

units.la: 238. Ismael, tyrannidem affectat, regia stirpe inflatus, Gedaliam hospitem suum bene de se meritum per insidias euertit, Chaldaeorum praesidia eiicit, & stragem magnam Iudaeorum edit, tandem fuga ad Ammonitas so-cios suos sibi consulit.
units.tr: 238. Ishmael, puffed up with royal descent, aspired to tyranny. By treachery he overthrew Gedaliah, his host, who had deserved well of him. He drove out the Chaldean garrisons, inflicted a great slaughter on the Jews, and at last, in flight, sought safety for himself among the Ammonites, his allies.

units.la: 239. Iohanan, Ismaelis aemulus, Iudaeos ab eo captos in libertatem restituit. Autor fuit populo, ut metu Iudaeorum in Aegyptum se conferret: cui maxima contentione Ieremias repugnauit. Sed vicit Iohananis propositum: qui populum in barbaram prouinciam deduxit, & prophetam ligatum secum abripuit. Populus in Aegypto fame, bello, peste consumtus est, & incidit in Scyllam, dum Charybdim vult vitare.
units.tr: 239. Johanan, a rival of Ishmael, restored to freedom the Jews whom Ishmael had taken captive. He was the author of the plan that the people should betake themselves to Egypt for fear of the Jews; Jeremiah opposed this with the greatest vehemence. But Johanan's purpose prevailed. He led the people into a barbarous province and carried off the prophet with him in chains. The people were consumed in Egypt by famine, war and pestilence, and they fell into Scylla while trying to avoid Charybdis.

units.la: 240. Achabus, & Sedechias, pseudoprophetae, corruptores veræ doctrinæ, & vitiis omnibus contaminati, & hostes Ieremiae capitales, cum aliis impiis in seruitutem Babylonicam abducuntur, & ibi libidinis atque flagitiorum pessimorum conuicti, sententia Nebucadnezaris, in sartaginem feruentem coniiciuntur. Inde est sermone vulgi iactatum prouerbium, cum alicui malum extremum quis imprecaretur, Eueniat tibi, quod Achabo & Sedechia.
units.tr: 240. Ahab and Zedekiah, false prophets, corrupters of true doctrine, contaminated by every vice, and chief enemies of Jeremiah, were led off into Babylonian servitude with other wicked men.
