There, convicted of lust and the worst crimes, they were thrown by the sentence of Nebuchadnezzar into a seething frying pan. From this comes the proverb tossed about in common speech, when someone wished another the worst possible fate: May what happened to Ahab and Zedekiah happen to you.

units.la: 241. Baruch, famulus & amanuensis Ieremiae, de latere sui praeceptoris nunquam discessit, nullo in periculo eum deseruit, veram doctrinam & ipse propagauit, tum in patria, tum in Aegypto, quo deductus fuit una cum Ieremiâ.
units.tr: 241. Baruch, servant and scribe of Jeremiah, never departed from his teacher's side and never deserted him in any danger. He himself also spread true doctrine, both in his homeland and in Egypt, whither he was taken along with Jeremiah.

units.la: 242. Ezechiel, tempore regis Ioachimi profectus est Babylonem sponte, cum iis, quos ad migrationem Ieremias hortatus fuerat. Conspectu Dei per varia simulachra fruebatur. Occisus perhibetur à principe Ægyptio, quem suâ παῤῥησίᾳ[?] offenderat.
units.tr: 242. Ezekiel, in the time of King Jehoiachin, went voluntarily to Babylon, together with those whom Jeremiah had urged to migrate. He enjoyed the sight of God through various visions. He is said to have been killed by an Egyptian prince, whom he had offended by his frankness [παῤῥησίᾳ].

units.la: 243. Obadias, Ezechieli σύγχρονος[?], consolatur populum exulem, & invehitur in gentem Idumæam.
units.tr: 243. Obadiah, a contemporary [σύγχρονος] of Ezekiel, comforted the exiled people and attacked the Edomite nation.

units.la: 244. Pelatias, unus è 25. principibus, quos populus extulerat, adversa Deo consilia agitabat, & in summâ licentiâ vivebat, & à se dissentientes ferro necabat. Obiurgatus cum collegis ab Ezechiele, concione ipsius graui, nodum finitâ, conterritus, in ipso loci sacri vestibulo subitò expirauit. Quo repentino casu reliqui principes ad emendationem vitæ vocati sunt.
units.tr: 244. Pelatiah, one of the twenty-five princes whom the people had raised up, plotted measures hostile to God, lived in complete licence, and slew with the sword those who disagreed with him. Rebuked together with his colleagues by Ezekiel, in a sermon of his that was severe and finished the knot, he was struck with terror and suddenly expired in the very forecourt of the sacred place. By this sudden event the remaining princes were called to amend their lives.

units.la: 245. Arbaces, (seu Arbactus, Medus, sedem regiam è Nino in Ecbatana transtulit. Rex Babylonius sibi aliquem parem esse non ferens, magnum ei bellum infert, victū que in suam redigit potestatem. Ab hoc omnes Medorum reges dicti sunt Arbaces, vt Parthorum Arsaces, & Ægyptiorum Pharaones.
units.tr: 245. Arbaces (or Arbactus), a Mede, transferred the royal seat from Nineveh to Ecbatana. The Babylonian king, unable to bear anyone being his equal, waged a great war against him and, having conquered him, reduced him under his own power. From him all the kings of the Medes were called Arbaces, just as the kings of the Parthians were called Arsaces and those of Egypt Pharaohs.

units.la: 246. Holofernes, imperator regis cuiusdam, nomine Nebucadnezaris, quem ego putârim esse Merodachum, de quo supra num. 218. hic, inquam, Deum & homines contemnendo, manu Iuditha, fœminæ viduæ, proprio acinace, in lecto suo interficitur.
units.tr: 246. Holofernes, commander of a certain king named Nebuchadnezzar, whom I should think to be Merodach, of whom above, at no. 218, was killed in his own bed by the hand of Judith, a widow, with his own scimitar. He, I say, had despised God and men.

units.la: 247. Achior, princeps Ammonitarum, de statu populi Iudaici ab Holoferne interrogatus, de eius antiquâ origine, perspectâ sanctitate, & inuictâ virtute incorruptū dixit testimonium: propter quod ad arborem fuit alligatus, iussu Holofernis. Sed diuino miraculo seruatus, ritu gentilitatis relicto, inter ciues populi Dei recipitur.
units.tr: 247. Achior, prince of the Ammonites, when questioned by Holofernes about the condition of the Jewish people, bore unbroken witness to their ancient origin, their proven holiness and their invincible valour. For this he was tied to a tree on Holofernes' orders. But preserved by a divine miracle, he abandoned the rites of the Gentiles and was received among the citizens of the people of God.

units.la: 248. Iuditha, vidua Bethuliensis, pietate, castitate animi, formâ, diuitiis, eloquentiâ, æque excellens, Oziâ ducem animat, Holofernem exanimat, totumque regis Nebucadnezaris exercitum superat. Eius pedisequa, Abra, periculorum socia, fidelitatem suam dominæ probat.
units.tr: 248. Judith, a widow of Bethulia, equally outstanding in piety, purity of mind, beauty, wealth and eloquence, encouraged the leader Ozias, put Holofernes to death, and overcame the whole army of King Nebuchadnezzar. Her attendant Abra proved her fidelity to her mistress as a companion in her dangers.

units.la: 249. Oziâs,
units.tr: 249. Ozias,

units.la: 249. Ozias, dux Bethulienfis, minimè quidem fortis aut perseverans, alios audiens,illisque obsequens, bene meretur de populo Dei.
units.tr: 249. Ozias, leader of Bethulia, by no means brave or steadfast, but listening to others and yielding to them, nevertheless deserved well of the people of God.

units.la: 250. Joachimus, sacerdos, Assyriorum adventu nuntiato, angustiás montium, & aditus viarum claudit, per urbes & castella milites disponit: inprimis Dei iram jamiam grassantem, suadet mitigandam abstinentiâ & emendatione, promittitque praesens Dei auxilium poenitentibus. Audita Bethulienfium victoriâ, Deo gratias agit solenniter.
units.tr: 250. Joachim, a priest, when the arrival of the Assyrians was announced, closed the narrow mountain passes and the approaches of the roads, and stationed soldiers through the towns and fortresses. Above all he urged that the wrath of God, now raging, be appeased by abstinence and amendment, and he promised the present help of God to those who repented. When the victory of the Bethulians was reported, he solemnly gave thanks to God.

units.la: 251. Sufanna, Ioachimi uxor, non minus sanctitate, quâ forma praestans, justo Dei judicio liberatur à testimonio & judicio hominum injusto.
units.tr: 251. Susanna, wife of Joachim, outstanding in beauty but no less in holiness, was freed by the just judgment of God from the unjust testimony and sentence of men.

units.la: 252. Daniel, in universo Chaldaeorum regno, excelluit sapientiâ, fortitudine, & pietate, charus & utilis Nebucadnezari, Evilmerodacho, Belsazeri, Dario & Cyro, à quibus omnibus est & praemiis & honoribus affectus. Sepulchrum eius Babylone in angiportu multis seculis notum fuit.
units.tr: 252. Daniel, excelled throughout the whole kingdom of the Chaldeans in wisdom, courage and piety. He was dear and useful to Nebuchadnezzar, Evil-Merodach, Belshazzar, Darius and Cyrus, by all of whom he was honoured with both rewards and offices. His tomb was known for many centuries in a narrow lane at Babylon.

units.la: 253. Nebucadnezar, cognomento Magnus, post multas victorias, à Daniele institutus consequitur veri Dei notitiam: ab eodem admonitus, ut fastum nimium deponeret, viro Dei non obsequitur. Eiectus ig. in solitudinem, ibi obbrutescit animo & corpore. Ad sanitatem rediens, in solium rursus collocatur, Deumque animo grato & humili colit.
units.tr: 253. Nebuchadnezzar, surnamed the Great, after many victories, instructed by Daniel, attained knowledge of the true God. Though admonished by the same man to lay aside his excessive pride, he did not obey the man of God. Cast out into the wilderness, he was there brutalised in mind and body. Returning to health, he was again placed on the throne, and he worshipped God with a grateful and humble mind.

units.la: 254. Sadrach, Mefach, & Abednego, socii Danielis, propter stirpem regiam & ingeniorum ac formae excellentiâ, in andronem regium accersuntur. Brevi tempore ita eminent sapientiâ, ut praefecturis provinciarum ornentur: juvenes ad res maximas nati & accommodati. Erectum regi colossum cùm adorare nollent, in caminum ardente ligati conjiciuntur: sed servati à Deo, inde liberantur, & majoribus quàm antea dignitatibus euehuntur.
units.tr: 254. Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, companions of Daniel, on account of their royal descent and their excellence of talent and appearance, were summoned into the royal court. In a short time they so excelled in wisdom that they were adorned with the governorships of provinces, being young men born and fitted for the greatest affairs. When they refused to adore the colossus that had been erected for the king, they were bound and thrown into a burning furnace. But preserved by God, they were thence delivered and raised to still greater dignities than before.

units.la: 255. Aspenas, aulae Babylonicae praefectus, singulari amore & benevolentiâ complectitur Danielem & eius socios. Eodem erga Danielem animo fuit Arioch, regis apparitor.
units.tr: 255. Aspenas, prefect of the Babylonian court, embraced Daniel and his companions with singular love and goodwill. Arioch, the king's attendant, had the same attitude towards Daniel.

units.la: 256. Euilmerodach, succedit patri Nebucadnezari, facilis & beneficus in ecclesiam. Primo regni sui anno Iechoniam, quem pater eius 37 annos captiuum tenuerat, è vinculis produxit, honoribusque & munerib. afficit.
units.tr: 256. Evil-Merodach, succeeded his father Nebuchadnezzar, mild and beneficent towards the Church. In the first year of his reign he brought Jehoiachin, whom his father had kept captive for thirty-seven years, out of his chains, and honoured him with dignities and gifts.

units.la: 257. Belfazer[?], nepos Nebucadnezaris, impius, temerarius, & temulentus, Babylone obsidetur & interficitur à Dario Medo, ad quem hac occasione transfertur imperium Babylonis.
units.tr: 257. Belshazzar, grandson of Nebuchadnezzar, impious, reckless and drunken, was besieged at Babylon and killed by Darius the Mede, to whom the rule of Babylon was transferred on this occasion.

units.la: 258. Darius Medus, Danielem præ omnibus aliis maximè dilexit & euexit.
units.tr: 258. Darius the Mede loved and exalted Daniel above all the others.

units.la: 260. Cyrus, rex Persarum, à propheta Esaiâ, longè ante quàm est natus, rex designatur. Hic soluit captiuitatem Babylonicam, & optimè de populo Dei meretur, illustris Christi typus.
units.tr: 260. Cyrus, king of the Persians, was designated king by the prophet Isaiah long before he was born. He brought the Babylonian captivity to an end and deserved very well of the people of God, an illustrious type of Christ.

units.la: 261. Sesbasar, satrapa Cyri, missus præfectus in Iudaeam, vasa templi iussu regis deportat, & eiusdem iussu primum templi lapidem ponit, amicus & fautor Iudaeorum.
units.tr: 261. Sheshbazzar, governor under Cyrus, sent as prefect into Judea, carried away the vessels of the temple by the king's command, and by the same command laid the first stone of the temple. He was a friend and supporter of the Jews.

units.la: 262. Cambyses, Cyri F, monstro quàm homini similior, audax, libidinosus, crudelis, Dei & propinquorum contemtor. Patris mandatum de templo ædificando antiquauit.
units.tr: 262. Cambyses, son of Cyrus, more like a monster than a man: bold, lustful, cruel, and a despiser of God and of his kin. He annulled his father's command concerning the building of the temple.

units.la: 263. Zerubabel, Salathielis F, regis Iechoniæ nepos, Babylone nascitur, dictus alio nomine Berechias, primus dux post exilium Babylonicum. Dimissus à Cyro, templi à fundamentis extruendi habuit potestatem: estque opus difficillimum aggressus, non minore sapientiâ, quàm animositate.
units.tr: 263. Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, grandson of King Jehoiachin, was born at Babylon, and was also called Berechiah. He was the first leader after the Babylonian exile. Dismissed by Cyrus, he had the authority to rebuild the temple from its foundations, and he undertook this most difficult work with no less wisdom than courage.

units.la: 264. Iosua, sacerdos, Zerubabeli duci cauto & magnanimo, nullo loco temporeue defuit.
units.tr: 264. Joshua, a priest, was never absent from Zerubbabel, a prudent and magnanimous leader, in any place or at any time.

units.la: 265. Haggæus, & paulò post Zacharias, opus templi suis concionibus maturant.
units.tr: 265. Haggai, and a little later Zechariah, hastened the work on the temple with their sermons.

units.la: 266. Assuerus, id est, Xerxes, dominus 127 prouinciarum, coniuge superbâ Vasthi repudiatâ, Esther Hebraeam duxit, eique nomen Augustæ tribuit. Hamanem, Iudaeis insidias struentem, cum omni stirpe suâ fœdo supplicio extinguit. Estheræ coniugi potestatem dedit puniendi fortunis, carcere, exilio, morte eos omnes, qui aut in legem Dei, aut regia edicta deliquissent. Mardochæum porrò facit palatij præfectum, eique potestatem dat interficiendi hostes Iudæorum per omne imperium: suntque interfecta gentilium septuaginta quinque millia: unde solennitas Purim est instituta.
units.tr: 266. Ahasuerus, that is, Xerxes, lord of 127 provinces, having repudiated his proud wife Vashti, married the Hebrew Esther and gave her the title of queen. He destroyed Haman, who was plotting against the Jews, together with his whole family, by a shameful execution. He gave Esther, his wife, power to punish with loss of property, imprisonment, exile or death all those who had offended either against the law of God or against the royal edicts. He further made Mordecai prefect of the palace and gave him power to kill the enemies of the Jews throughout the whole empire; and seventy-five thousand of the Gentiles were slain. Hence the festival of Purim was instituted.

units.la: 267. Esdras de stirpe Aharonis, locum gratiæ primum apud Artaxerxem Mnemona obtinuit. Est alter à Zerubabele, qui magnum populi numerum in Iudæam reduxit. Aggressus est reformationem utriusque politiæ felici successu.
units.tr: 267. Ezra, of the stock of Aaron, first obtained favour with Artaxerxes Mnemon. There was another, after Zerubbabel, who led a great number of people back into Judaea. He undertook the reform of both the civil and the religious polity with happy success.

units.la: 268. Artaxerxes Mnemon, fuit beneficus erga Indæos. Anno regni septimo dimisit Esdram cum ingenti multitudine: & anno vigesimo Nehemiam, itidem cum numerosâ multitudine: cui ne quid in via aduersi accideret, comitatum militarem addidit.
units.tr: 268. Artaxerxes Mnemon was kind to the Jews. In the seventh year of his reign he sent Ezra away with a great multitude, and in the twentieth year Nehemiah, likewise with a large multitude. So that nothing adverse should befall him on the way, he added a military escort.

units.la: 269. Nehemias, tertius & postremus est, qui dispersum per gentiles provincias populum, in patriam sedem reduxit: quanquam non omnes sunt reducti, vt patet ex Act. 2. Debetur ig. templi inchoatio Zerubabeli, legum instauratio Esdræ, vrbis perfectio Nehemiæ.
units.tr: 269. Nehemiah was the third and last who led the people, dispersed among the gentile provinces, back to their homeland, although not all were brought back, as appears from Acts 2. The beginning of the temple is owed to Zerubbabel, the restoration of the laws to Ezra, and the completion of the city to Nehemiah.

units.la: 270. Malachias, vltimus prophetarum, nefarias templi restructi profanationes arguit.
units.tr: 270. Malachi, the last of the prophets, denounces the wicked profanations of the rebuilt temple.

units.la: 271. Manasses, sacerdos, lege maiorum contemta, Sanaballæ satrapæ Perfici filiam, vxorem ducit. Qui cùm flagitij admonitus esset à Nehemiâ, maluit soceri impii authoritatem & promissa sequi, quam salubriter admonentis pium admittere consilium. Quamobrem Nehemias vt ipsum animo intrepido castigauerat: ita iudicio constantissimo è sacerdotum ordine eiicit, & tanquam homine contaminatum exterminat, & è synagogâ, & è patriâ. Is nouum templum erexit, in monte Samariæ, vt Hierosolymitanum desereretur: ad quem alii sacerdotes eiusmodi connubiis inquinati, se conferebant, quibus domicilium & immunitatem Saneballa concedebat, non amore pietatis, sed odio Nehemiæ.
units.tr: 271. Manasseh, a priest, despising the law of his ancestors, married a daughter of Sanballat, governor of Persian Samaria. When Nehemiah admonished him of this crime, he preferred to follow the authority and promises of his impious father-in-law rather than to accept the wholesome counsel of a pious admonisher. Therefore Nehemiah, having rebuked him with a fearless spirit, expelled him with the most resolute judgement from the order of priests, and, as a defiled man, drove him out both from the synagogue and from his homeland. He built a new temple on Mount Samaria, so that the one at Jerusalem would be abandoned. Other priests tainted by such marriages betook themselves to it, and Sanballat granted them a dwelling and immunity, not from love of piety but from hatred of Nehemiah.

units.la: X. Prosopographia, tempore ecclesiæ à re- gibus Asiaticis vexatæ, ē libris Maccabæo- rum, est talis.
units.tr: X. Prosopography of the church harassed by the Asian kings, taken from the books of the Maccabees, is as follows.

units.la: 272. Alexander Macedo, iter per Syriam faciens, vrbis sacræ, & templo, & populo pepercit. Moribundus regna inter duces distribuit.
units.tr: 272. Alexander of Macedon, marching through Syria, spared the holy city, the temple and the people. On his deathbed he divided his kingdoms among his generals.

units.la: 273. Iaddus, summus pontifex, Alexandrum M. Hierosolymam infesto animo venientem placat humilitate & officiis, adeò quidem vt rex videns sacerdotem sibi obviam venientem de equo desiliret, & ei supplex honorem haberet, exercitu suo fine maleficio per regionem Iudæorum ducto.
units.tr: 273. Jaddua, the high priest, appeased Alexander the Great, who was coming to Jerusalem with hostile intent, by humility and courtesy. So much so that the king, seeing the priest coming to meet him, leapt down from his horse and showed him honour as a suppliant, while his army passed through the region of the Jews without doing any harm.

units.la: 274. Onias, Iaddi F, summus sacerdos, cognomento Prisc̃us, à Ptolemæo Lago variis iniuriis agitatur. Amicitiam coluit cum Spartanis, qui Abrahamum communem generis authorem habere sei-ac-titabāt. Quam amicitiam Ionathas Matthathiæ F, post multos annos renouauit, repetitā prioris fœderis mentione.
units.tr: 274. Onias, son of Jaddua, high priest, surnamed Priscus, was harassed with various injuries by Ptolemy Lagus. He cultivated friendship with the Spartans, who supposed that Abraham was the common ancestor of their race. Jonathan, son of Mattathias, renewed this friendship many years later, repeating the mention of the earlier covenant.

units.la: 275. Simon, summus sacerdos, Oniæ F, cognomento Iustus, templum nouis ædificiis ampliauit, vrbem validiorem reddidit, ciues authoritate rexit, munere denique sacerdotis functus est splendidissimè, quod de ipso testatur Sirachus.
units.tr: 275. Simon, high priest, son of Onias, surnamed the Just, enlarged the temple with new buildings, made the city stronger, ruled the citizens with authority, and finally discharged the office of priest most splendidly, as Sirach bears witness concerning him.

units.la: 276. Iosua, siue Iesus, filius Sirachi, patriâ Hierosolymitanus, vir & nobilitate & sapientiâ præstans, regnante Ptolemæo Euergetâ in Ægypto vixit, librumque abauo inchoatum, & ex antiquis hominum piorum commentarius collectum, absoluit & emulgauit.
units.tr: 276. Joshua, or Jesus, son of Sirach, a native of Jerusalem, a man outstanding both in nobility and in wisdom, lived in the reign of Ptolemy Euergetes in Egypt. He completed and published the book begun by his grandfather, a commentary gathered from the writings of ancient pious men.

units.la: 276. Eleazar, Oniæ alter F, Simonis frater, summus sacerdos, ab Antiocho Theo rege Syriæ multa accipit incommoda: sed à Ptolemæo Philadelpho eximiè colitur, qui supra centena millia Iudæorum suis redimens sumtibus, libertate donauit, & ab ipso impetrauit lxx interpretes, qui Biblia Hebraea in linguam Graecam transferrent.
units.tr: 276. Eleazar, the other son of Onias, brother of Simon, high priest, suffered many hardships from Antiochus Theos, king of Syria. But he was greatly honoured by Ptolemy Philadelphus, who, redeeming more than a hundred thousand Jews at his own expense, gave them their liberty, and obtained from him the Seventy interpreters, who were to translate the Hebrew Bible into Greek.

units.la: 277. Antiochus Magnus, rex Syriae, fuit pessimus patet prolis sceleratissimae. Eius enim filii fuerunt Seleucus, Antiochus,& Demetrius:quorum temporibus politiae Judaicae status ita commutatus est, ut nunquam postea in aliquam dignitatem durabile potuerit restitui. Fuerunt enim impii ex Judaeis homines, qui Dei aeterni sapientiam spernentes, ritus ethnicos sequerentur, & ad delendum Dei cultum, regum externorum amicitias & auxilia quaererent: pestes videl. religionis & patriae.
units.tr: 277. Antiochus the Great, king of Syria, was the worst father of a most wicked brood. His sons were Seleucus, Antiochus and Demetrius. In their times the state of the Jewish polity was so altered that it could never afterwards be durably restored to any dignity. For there were impious men among the Jews who, despising the wisdom of the eternal God, followed heathen rites, and, in order to destroy the worship of God, sought the friendship and aid of foreign kings: plagues, that is, of religion and of the fatherland.

units.la: 278. Seleucus Philopator, Antiochi primus F, primum Judaeis amicus, ad sacrificium & templum impensas de suo aerario suppeditauit: postea a Simone proditore eo impellitur, ut ad rapiendos templi thesauros, quaestorem suum Heliodorum cum potestate mitteret.
units.tr: 278. Seleucus Philopator, the first son of Antiochus, was at first friendly to the Jews, and supplied from his own treasury the expenses for the sacrifice and the temple. Afterwards, he was driven by Simon the traitor to send his treasurer Heliodorus with authority to seize the temple treasures.

units.la: 279. Onias II, Simonis Justi primus F, tanta gratia propter pietatem fuit, ut apud suos esset venerabilis: tanta dignitate, propter humanitatem, ut exteri quoque eum colerent. Heliodoro, spoliaturo templum, resistit. Jasonem fratrem suum iniqua molientem obiurgat: Simonem ꝓ[?]ditorem & Menelaum furem reprehendit. Propter eam libertatem ab Andronico misere interficitur.
units.tr: 279. Onias II, the first son of Simon the Just, was held in such esteem for his piety that he was venerated among his own people, and so dignified for his kindness that even foreigners honoured him. He resisted Heliodorus, who was about to plunder the temple. He rebuked his brother Jason for plotting wickedness, and reproved Simon the traitor and Menelaus the thief. For this freedom of speech he was wretchedly killed by Andronicus.

units.la: 280. Simon, templi thesaurarius, Oniae aemulus, secreta omnia Seleuco enunciat, eique templum spoliandum tradit.
units.tr: 280. Simon, treasurer of the temple, rival of Onias, disclosed all secrets to Seleucus, and handed the temple over to be plundered.

units.la: 281. Antiochus Epiphanes, rectius Epimanes, tam fuit perditus, ut illo nullum unquam prodigium inusitatius, nullum monstrum foedius fuerit. Urbe per dolum capta, intra triduumoctoginta hominum millia perimit, quadraginta ligat, totidem vendit: de templo auri argentique talenta mille & octingeta aufert, in eoq; statuam Jovis Olympii erigit: sacros denique libros cremat. Est illustris typus Antichristi.
units.tr: 281. Antiochus Epiphanes, more correctly Epimanes, was so depraved that no prodigy was ever more unusual, no monster more foul. The city having been taken by treachery, within three days he destroyed eighty thousand people, took forty thousand captive and sold as many. From the temple he carried off a thousand eight hundred talents of gold and silver, and in it he set up a statue of Olympian Jupiter; finally he burned the sacred books. He is a notable type of Antichrist.

units.la: 282. Jason, antea dictus Josua sive Jesus, Simonis alter F, Oniae frater, & nomen & religionem mutavit, homo teterrimus.Fratrem Oniam interfectum non dolet: pontificatum eius, ab Antiocho pecunia emit, ut que regi gratum faceret, lege Dei abrogata Graecos ritus instituit.
units.tr: 282. Jason, previously called Joshua or Jesus, the other son of Simon, brother of Onias, changed both his name and his religion; a most vile man. He does not grieve at the death of his brother Onias. He bought the high priesthood from Antiochus with money, and, to please the king, abrogated the law of God and introduced Greek rites.

units.la: 283. Menelaus, vero nomine Onias, Iafonis frater, ipsius impietatem in ritibus Graecorum imitatur, rapacitatem ipsius longissime superat. Missus ab eodem ad numerandum Antiocho tributum, subdolè sacerdotii nomen & honorem in se transfert, additis ad regis reditus priores trecentis argenti talentis annuis.
units.tr: 283. Menelaus, really named Onias, brother of Jason, imitates his impiety in the Greek rites, and far surpasses his rapacity. Sent by the same man to collect the tribute for Antiochus, he craftily transferred the name and honour of the priesthood to himself, adding to the king's revenues three hundred silver talents a year over and above the former sum.

units.la: 284. Andronicus, regis Antiochi procurator, nihil præter pretium dulce erat. Interfecit Oniam, corruptus pecunia Menelai. Vide n. 279.
units.tr: 284. Andronicus, procurator of king Antiochus, was sweet only for the price. He killed Onias, bribed by the money of Menelaus. See n. 279.

units.la: 285. Lysimachus, Simonis proditoris & Menelai sacrilegi frater, utroque nequior, pontificatum tumultuose administrat.
units.tr: 285. Lysimachus, brother of Simon the traitor and of the sacrilegious Menelaus, worse than both, administered the priesthood tumultuously.

units.la: 286. Mille martyres, metu persecutionis Antiochi, in speluncam fugiunt, ibique die sabbato occiduntur, cum ob religionem diei se nollent defendere.
units.tr: 286. A thousand martyrs, fearing the persecution of Antiochus, fled into a cave, and there on the sabbath day they were slain, because they were unwilling to defend themselves out of reverence for the day.

units.la: 287. Eleazar, doctor legis, canitie, sapientia, gravitate hostibus etiam suspiciendus, ætate nonagenarius, cum suillas carnes edere nollet, martyrio coronatus est.
units.tr: 287. Eleazar, a teacher of the law, venerable for his white hair, wisdom and dignity, so that even enemies looked up to him, a man of ninety years, when he refused to eat swine's flesh, was crowned with martyrdom.

units.la: 288. Septem fratres, quòd carnem suillam edere detrectarent, occisi sunt.
units.tr: 288. The seven brothers, because they refused to eat swine's flesh, were killed.

units.la: 289. Matthathias, Antiocho furenti, ex omni nobilitate, se primus opponit, & multa fortiter gerit pro causa Dei & patriæ. Morte propinquâ, Simonem propter prudentiam, & Iudam propter fortitudinem duces constituit. Atque hic incipit familia Affamonaorum.
units.tr: 289. Mattathias, when Antiochus was raging, was the first of all the nobility to oppose him, and bravely performed many deeds for the cause of God and of his country. When death was near, he appointed Simon as leader for his prudence, and Judas for his courage. And here begins the Hasmonean family.

units.la: 290. Iohannes, primus Matthathiæ F, interficitur à Iambriis.
units.tr: 290. John, the first son of Mattathias, was killed by the Jambrites.

units.la: 291. Simon, Matthathiæ secundus F, strenuam suo populo operam nauat tum viuente tum mortuo fratre Iudâ, itemque Ionathâ.
units.tr: 291. Simon, the second son of Mattathias, rendered strenuous service to his people, both while his brother Judas lived and after his death, and likewise Jonathan.

units.la: 292. Iudas, Matthathiæ tertius F, cognomento Maccabæus, robore leoni, armis giganti, impetu flammæ grassantifuit comparatus. Sulceptâ legis diuinæ, & populi afflictide&ti[?] defensione, semper ad orandum priùs, quàm ad præliandum accedit. Cum regibus Syriæ, Antiocho & Demetrio, & eorum legatis prælia lecunda fecit: nam Apollonium cæcidit, Seronem vicit, Gorgiam fugauit, Lysiæ 5 copias fudit, Timotheum ter repulit, Nicanori denique restitit. Præterea contra Ammonitas, Idumæos, Galaadiras[?], Galilæos, Arabes, & Philistinos grauia bella gessit, multasque vrbes populatus est. Hostes sæpe multos deleuit, ne vno quidem suo milite amisso, aut vulnerato. 10 Templum Hierosolymitanum purgauit. In prælio cum Bacchide, desertus à suo milite, stationem ipse non deserens, oppetit fortissimè.
units.tr: 292. Judas, the third son of Mattathias, surnamed Maccabeus, was likened to a lion in strength, to a giant in arms, and to a flame in its onrush. Having taken up the defence of the divine law and of the afflicted people, he always came to prayer before he came to battle. He fought successful battles against the kings of Syria, Antiochus and Demetrius, and their generals: for he cut down Apollonius, defeated Seron, put Gorgias to flight, routed the forces of Lysias, repulsed Timotheus three times, and finally withstood Nicanor. Moreover he waged grave wars against the Ammonites, Idumaeans, Galaadites, Galileans, Arabs and Philistines, and laid waste many cities. He often destroyed many enemies without losing, or even having wounded, one of his own soldiers. He purified the temple at Jerusalem. In battle with Bacchides, deserted by his soldiers, he himself did not desert his post, and fell most bravely.

units.la: 193. Eleazar, Matthathiæ quartus F, pro suâ gente & ipse nullum detrectauit periculum.
units.tr: 293. Eleazar, the fourth son of Mattathias, for his own people also shrank from no danger.

units.la: 15 194. Ionathas, quintus & vltimus Matthathiæ F, contra Galaaditas à Iudâ fratre missus, octo millia hostium vincit. Post Iudæ obitum dux electus, multa præclarè gessit. Tandem à Demetrio rege deceptus, & à Tryphone circumuentus, interficitur cum duobus filiis.
units.tr: 294. Jonathan, the fifth and last son of Mattathias, sent by his brother Judas against the Galaaditae, conquered eight thousand enemies. Elected leader after the death of Judas, he performed many deeds with distinction. At last, deceived by king Demetrius and ensnared by Tryphon, he was killed together with two sons.

units.la: 20 195. Asidæi, ex omnibus Israelitis viri optimi & fortissimi, Matthathiæ se adiunxerunt contra Antiochum, & cum filio eius Iudâ præliis multis, pro patriâ gestis salutariter, interfuerunt. Memineris populum hoc tempore diuisum esse in duas partes, quarum vnam constituebant 25 Asidæi, h.e. boni & pii, alteram apostatæ.
units.tr: 195. Hasideans, the best and bravest men of all the Israelites, joined Mattathias against Antiochus, and with his son Judas they took part in many battles fought for their country, with good result. Note that at this time the people was divided into two parts: one consisted of the Hasideans, that is, the good and pious, and the other of apostates.

units.la: 196. Apollonius, dux Samariæ, legatus Antiochi, vir crudelissimus, in Iudæam mittitur cum viginti hominum millibus, & vrbe sanctâ per fraudem occupatâ cædibus ibi grassatur, victus tandem & interfectus à Iudâ.
units.tr: 196. Apollonius, governor of Samaria and legate of Antiochus, a most cruel man, was sent into Judea with twenty thousand men. Having taken the holy city by fraud, he raged there with slaughter, until at last he was defeated and killed by Judas.

units.la: 30 297. Sero, dux inferioris Syriæ, famæ comparandæ gratiâ, & ipse exercitum contra Iudam educit, sed abillo fugatur.
units.tr: 197. Seron, commander of Lower Syria, wishing to win a reputation, himself led an army out against Judas, but was put to flight by him.

units.la: 298. Lysias, propinquus regis Antiochi, bella Iudaica primùm administrauit per legatos, Ptolemæum, Nicanorem, 35 & Gorgiam, qui hominum millia octo amiserunt diuersis locis: deinde ipse per se, vbi amisit peditum millia vndecim, & equites mille atque sexcentos. Tot calamitatibus sapientior factus Lysias cum Iudæis firmau[?]it pacem.
units.tr: 198. Lysias, a kinsman of King Antiochus, at first conducted the Jewish wars through his legates Ptolemy, Nicanor and Gorgias, who lost eight thousand men in various places. Then he went himself, and there he lost eleven thousand foot soldiers and sixteen hundred horsemen. Made wiser by so many disasters, Lysias concluded peace with the Jews.

units.la: 299. Nicanor, Patrocli F, Ptolemæi præfecti Phœniciæ & Cœlesyriæ legatus, regi Antiocho, cum viginti millib. militum auxilio venit contra Iudæos. Sed victus à Iuda, euadit scapha, & Antiochiæ cum ignominia vitam transfigit.
units.tr: 199. Nicanor, son of Patroclus, legate of Ptolemy, governor of Phoenicia and Coele-Syria, came against the Jews with an auxiliary force of twenty thousand soldiers for King Antiochus. But he was defeated by Judas, escaped in a small boat, and spent the rest of his life in disgrace at Antioch.

units.la: 300. Gorgias, Idumæorum dux, duobus Antiochis, Epiphani & Eupatori, patri atque filio militauit, longoque tempore vexauit Iudæam. A Iuda aliquoties impeditur, & duobus iustis præliis superatus, vrbium perfugia quæsiuit, & latrocinia exercuit.
units.tr: 300. Gorgias, commander of the Idumaeans, served under two Antiochuses, Epiphanes and Eupator, father and son, and for a long time harassed Judea. He was often hindered by Judas, and after being defeated in two just battles, he sought refuge in cities and carried on brigandage.

units.la: 301. Antiochus Eupator, Epiphanis F, bellum Iudæis infert, tantis viribus, quantis antehac Græcorum nemo fecerat. Sed bis à Iuda fuit superatus.
units.tr: 301. Antiochus Eupator, son of Epiphanes, made war on the Jews with greater forces than any Greek had used before. But he was twice defeated by Judas.

units.la: 302. Scythopolitani, & Nabathæi, multo fauore & liberalitate Iudæos prosequuntur.
units.tr: 302. The Scythopolitans and the Nabataeans treated the Jews with great goodwill and generosity.

units.la: 303. Demetrius Soter, factus Iudæis inimicus, Alcimum proditorem in vrbem mittit, & per Nicanorem & Bacchidem præter omnem modum sæuit. Nicanore interemto, Bacchideni summæ rei præficit: cuius ductu Iudæa fere tota subigitur, & Iudas Maccabæus interficitur. Ab Alexandro regnum Syriæ sibi vendicante impugnatus, societatem cum Ionatha inire voluit, eumque promissis & largitionibus pene infinitis solicitauit: sed Iudæi memores eius sæuitiæ & infidelitatis, cum hoste ipsius Alexandro se coniungunt, qui Demetrium victum & vita, & regno spoliauit.
units.tr: 303. Demetrius Soter, having become an enemy of the Jews, sent the traitor Alcimus into the city, and through Nicanor and Bacchides he raged beyond all measure. When Nicanor was killed, he put Bacchides in charge of the whole business. Under his leadership almost all of Judea was subdued, and Judas Maccabeus was killed. Attacked by Alexander, who claimed the kingdom of Syria for himself, Demetrius wished to make an alliance with Jonathan, and he tried to win him over with promises and almost endless largesse. But the Jews, mindful of his cruelty and faithlessness, joined themselves to Alexander, his enemy, who stripped Demetrius of his life and his kingdom after defeating him.

units.la: 304. Bacchides, regis Demetrii legatus, fuit artium bellicarum callentissimus.
units.tr: 304. Bacchides, legate of King Demetrius, was most skilled in the arts of war.

units.la: 305. Alcimus, dictus antea Ioachim, nefarius apostata & proditor, sacerdotium emit, & populum suum perdidit, quouis improbo deterior, quouis furioso amentior.
units.tr: 305. Alcimus, formerly called Joachim, a wicked apostate and traitor, bought the priesthood and destroyed his people. He was worse than any wicked man and more insane than any madman.

units.la: 306. Nicanor, legatus Demetrii, ad gentem Iudæorum extirpandam missus, non armis agens, sed insidiis, Iudam pene fefellisset. Cùm eius versutia celari diuinitus non posset, violentia agere incepit, sed à Iudâ victus est & interfectus.
units.tr: 306. Nicanor, legate of Demetrius, was sent to exterminate the Jewish nation. Acting not by arms but by ambushes, he almost deceived Judas. Since his cunning could not be concealed by divine means, he began to act by violence, but he was defeated and killed by Judas.

units.la: 307. Alexander, fortis extremæ homo, regnum paternum Syriæ repetens, Demetrio bellum facit, eumque Ionathæ auxilio superat. Ionathæ creato sacerdoti trabeam & coronam auream mittit.
units.tr: 307. Alexander, a brave man of humble origin, seeking to recover his father's kingdom of Syria, made war on Demetrius and defeated him with the help of Jonathan. He sent to Jonathan, whom he had made high priest, a purple robe and a golden crown.

units.la: 308. Ptolemæi Philometotis tempore Onias sacerdos templum in Ægypto, simile Hierosolymitano, condit, perperam intellecto Esaiæ vaticinio, quod est cap. 19.
units.tr: 308. In the time of Ptolemy Philometor, Onias the priest built a temple in Egypt like the one at Jerusalem, having misunderstood the prophecy of Isaiah, which is in chapter 19.

units.la: 309. Demetrius Nicator, seu Nicanor, Syriæ rex, Ionathā Iudæorum ducem, omnibus rebus, quibus potest, ornat, & eum inter amicos intimos numerat. Conspirantibus Antiochenis, ut regem opprimerent, unius Ionathæ beneficio conseiuatur. Is enim tribus duntaxat Iudæorum millib. adductis interficit centum & viginti ciuium Antiochenorum millia, vrbe incensâ & spoliatâ. Rex autem maximorum beneficiorum immemor, fœdus cum Ionathâ turpiter violat, & magnis Iudæos afficit incommodis.
units.tr: 309. Demetrius Nicator, or Nicanor, king of Syria, honoured Jonathan, leader of the Jews, with every distinction he could give and counted him among his closest friends. When the Antiochenes conspired to overthrow the king, he was saved by Jonathan's kindness alone. For Jonathan, bringing only three thousand Jewish men, killed one hundred and twenty thousand citizens of Antioch, and the city was set on fire and plundered. But the king, forgetful of these very great services, shamefully broke his covenant with Jonathan and inflicted great hardships on the Jews.

units.la: 310. Apollonius, Demetrii legatus, à Ionathâ & Simone fratribus male mulctatur.
units.tr: 310. Apollonius, legate of Demetrius, was severely punished by Jonathan and his brother Simon.

units.la: 311. Antiochus Theos, rex Syriæ, missis muneribus ad Ionatham & Simonem, amicitiam cum ambobus init, datisque honoribus amplis, eos sibi societate deuincit.
units.tr: 311. Antiochus Theos, king of Syria, sent gifts to Jonathan and Simon, entered into friendship with both of them, and bound them to himself by alliance, giving them ample honours.

units.la: 312. Trypho Ionatham illectum fraude capit, eumque cum duobus filiis de vitâ tollit, & Antiocho Entheo, pupillo suo, interfecto, regni Syriæ diadema sibi imponit: se per similis sui, blanda loquens, scelerata perpetrans, nulli fidus nisi vtilitatis suæ gratiâ.
units.tr: 312. Trypho, having lured Jonathan in by fraud, seized him, and took him and his two sons out of life. After killing Antiochus Entheus, his ward, he placed the diadem of the kingdom of Syria on his own head. Presenting himself as one of their own kind, speaking flatteringly, committing wicked deeds, he was faithful to no one except for his own advantage.

units.la: 313. Antiochus Sidetes, cognomento Pius & Soter, regnum patris recuperat, quod Alexander, Antiochus, & Trypho iniustè & fraudulenter tenuerant. Cum Iudæis fœdus iniit, eosque cæteris regibus humanius tractauit ab initio. Sed fortunâ ebrius, amicitiæ ipsorum renunciat, eisque plurima infert mala. Victus à Parthis ipse sibi manus infert.
units.tr: 313. Antiochus Sidetes, surnamed Pius and Soter, recovered his father's kingdom, which Alexander, Antiochus and Trypho had held unjustly and by fraud. He made a covenant with the Jews and at first treated them more kindly than the other kings had. But, drunk with good fortune, he renounced their friendship and inflicted many evils upon them. Defeated by the Parthians, he laid violent hands on himself.

units.la: 314. Iohannes Hircanus, Simonis F, Matthathiæ nepos, propter indolem præstantem dux paterni exercitus creatur, & Cendebæum Antiochi præfectum fugat, aliaque præclarè ac fortiter gerit. Clarus fuit tribus maximis rebus, principatu gentis, dignitate sacerdotis, & spiritu pro-phetiæ.
units.tr: 314. Iohannes Hircanus, son of Simon and grandson of Mattathias, on account of his outstanding character was made commander of his father's army. He put to flight Cendebaeus, the governor of Antiochus, and performed other deeds with distinction and courage. He was famous for three very great things: the leadership of the nation, the dignity of the priesthood, and the spirit of prophecy.

units.la: XI. Profopographia gentium ecclesiæ ad- versantium ex historiâ V. T. est eiusmodi.
units.tr: XI. Prosopography of the nations opposed to the Church, from the history of the Old Testament, is as follows.

units.la: 315. Gigantes, fuerunt multitudo ferox, nomine celebri & magnâ potentiâ ob corporis proceritatem, nata in perniciem ecclesiæ, inimica disciplinæ, propriâ virtute nitens, & ideo de terrâ tandem à Deo sublata.
units.tr: 315. Giants: a fierce multitude, famous by name and great in power because of their bodily stature. They were born to the ruin of the Church, hostile to discipline, relying on their own strength, and so at last were removed from the earth by God.

units.la: 316. Sodomæi, solum terrarum optimum colentes, nacti sunt doctorem Lothum. Ipsorum urbs omnis turpitudinis officina, scelerumque asylum evasit. Quâ de causâ cū tribus vicinis urbibus de cœlo funditus consumitur sulphure & igne, quintâ propter Lothum servatâ.
units.tr: 316. Sodomites: they cultivated the best land of the world and acquired Lot as their teacher. Their city became a workshop of every wickedness and a refuge for crimes. For this reason it was utterly consumed from heaven with its three neighbouring cities by brimstone and fire, while Lot was preserved on account of the fifth city.

units.la: 317. Sichemitæ, homines leves, malè tractantur à filiis Iacobi propter stupratam à Sichemo, regis filio, sororem ipsorum germanam. Execratur vir sapiens in suis concionibus, Samaritanos, Philistinos, & Sichemitas, designans hypocritas, tyrannos, & levem multitudinem.
units.tr: 317. Shechemites: a frivolous people, badly treated by the sons of Jacob because Shechem, the king's son, had violated their full sister. The wise man in his sermons curses the Samaritans, the Philistines and the Shechemites, calling them hypocrites, tyrants and a fickle multitude.

units.la: 318. Chananæi, generatim sic dicti, possederunt regionem cis & ultra Iordanem amplam & valde fertilem, ibique compararunt illustre imperium, & divitias ingentes. Sed donis Dei petulanter & perditè abusi, afflixerunt sanctos viros, qui inter eos vixerunt hospites & advenæ. Quare scelerum ipsorum mensurâ quasi completâ, extirpati sunt à Deo isti populi, Amorrhæi, Pherefæi, Chananæi, speciatim ita dicti, Hethæi, Gergesæi, Euæi, Iebusæi: eorumque regna & possessiones iuxta promissum & mandatum Dei, in Israëlitas, Semi & Abrahami posteros, dividuntur: & terram impiorum tandem semen iustorum hæreditatem accipit. In hac terrâ Christus est natus ex virgine.
units.tr: 318. Canaanites: so called in general terms. They possessed a region on both sides of the Jordan, broad and very fertile, and there they built up a famous dominion and immense riches. But, abusing the gifts of God wantonly and recklessly, they afflicted the holy men who lived among them as sojourners and strangers. Therefore, when the measure of their wickedness was as it were full, God rooted out those peoples: the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites (so named specifically), the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites and the Jebusites. Their kingdoms and possessions were divided, according to God's promise and command, among the Israelites, the posterity of Abraham and of Seth; and at last the seed of the righteous received the inheritance of the impious land. In this land Christ was born of a virgin.

units.la: 319. Amorrhæi, fuerunt gens ferocissima, & servitutis insolens. Inter eos habitauit Abraham, Mambris, viri boni & benefici, hospitio vsus. Duos ipsorũ reges vicit Moses: alios quinque Iosua fugauit, & de arboribus suspendit. Ipsorum conterranei fuerunt gigantes, cognominati Raphaim, q.d. medicos & seruatores, ob robur.
units.tr: 319. Amorites: a most fierce nation, unaccustomed to servitude. Abraham, a good and kindly man, lodged among them as a guest, at Mamre. Moses defeated two of their kings; Joshua routed five others and hanged them from trees. Their fellow countrymen were the giants called Rephaim, that is, as it were, physicians and saviours, from their strength.

units.la: 320. Pherefai, qui & Samarita, agriculturae & quaestui dediti, inter gentes Chananaeas valde opulenti fuerunt.
units.tr: 320. Perizzites, who are also called Samaritans: devoted to agriculture and trade, they were very wealthy among the Canaanite nations.

units.la: 321. Chananai, speciatim ita dicti, orti a Chanane Chami F,nominis atque nobilitatis inter suos gentiles praecipui semper extitere: meliorem etiam & abundantiorem terrae portionem tenuere: unde factum est, ut ex negotiationibus & quaestu, caeteris fuerint beatiores, & quia copiam sequitur insolentia, moribus quoque & studiis deteriores. Inter eos etiam gigantes habitarunt. Porro hoc nomen generatim pro omnib. istis populis, quos ira Dei sustulit, & sedes eorum ecclesiae tradidit, passim vsurpatur, ut vindicta paterni ludibrii, & veritas diuinae iustitiae, omnium mortalium & oculis & mentibus magis fit exposita.
units.tr: 321. Canaanites, so named specifically: descended from Canaan, son of Ham, they were always outstanding among their heathen neighbours for name and nobility. They also held the better and more abundant part of the land. Hence, from their dealings and trade, they were richer than the rest, and since abundance brings arrogance, they were also worse in morals and pursuits. Giants too dwelt among them. Moreover, this name is commonly used in general for all those peoples whom the anger of God removed and whose seats he gave to the Church, so that the vengeance for their father's mockery and the truth of divine justice may be set before the eyes and minds of all mortals.

units.la: 322. Hethai, Chebronem metropolim sibi condiderunt, vicinis molesti & formidabiles. Inter eos habitarũt gigantes, Enachim dicti, quasi torquati. Nam diuitiarum ostentatione erant superbi, & oppressione aliorum praeferoces[?].
units.tr: 322. Hittites: they founded Hebron as their metropolis, troublesome and formidable to their neighbours. Among them lived giants called Anakim, as it were "necklaced." For they were proud of the display of their riches and very fierce in oppressing others.

units.la: 323. Gergesæi videntur esse iidem cum Gergesenis, de quibus in euangelio, ita ut hi sint illorum reliquiae.
units.tr: 323. Girgashites seem to be the same as the Gergesenes mentioned in the Gospel, so that these are their remnants.

units.la: 324. Heuæi, montium Libani & Hermonis accolae, Iosuae diu restiterunt, nec in alienam potestatem redacti sunt vniuersi, ut restaret multitudo, quae Israelitas a verbo Dei desciscentes exerceret. Inter Heuaeos famosi fuerunt gigantes Nephilim, q.d. grassatores, hostes religionis, aduersarios pudoris, & inimicos disciplinae.
units.tr: 324. Hivites, inhabitants of the mountains of Lebanon and Hermon, long resisted Joshua, and they were not all brought under foreign power, so that a multitude remained to harass the Israelites who fell away from the word of God. Among the Hivites the notorious giants were the Nephilim, that is, as it were, plunderers, enemies of religion, adversaries of chastity and foes of discipline.

units.la: 325. Iebusæi, Gibeonem & Hierosolyma tenuerunt, viri strenui & bellaces. Nam vndique armis hostilibus circumuallati, vsque ad Dauidis tempora & vrbem Hierofolymam[?], & arcem Sionis tutati sunt. Inter ipsos fuere nobiles gigantes Emim, q. d. terribiles, feros, agrestes, & voluptarios. Atque hi sunt populi oriundi à posteris Chanaan.
units.tr: 325. Jebusites: they held Gibeon and Jerusalem, vigorous and warlike men. Surrounded on every side by hostile arms, they defended themselves down to the time of David, the city of Jerusalem and the citadel of Zion. Among them were the noble giants called Emim, that is, as it were, terrible, fierce, rustic and pleasure-loving. These are the peoples descended from the posterity of Canaan.

units.la: 326. Midianitæ, Abrahami ex Cetura posteri, fuerunt gens nobilis. Apud illos Moses ex Ægypto profugus exulauit, & sacerdotis ipsorum Iethronis filiam duxit. Gideon illos male multauit: unde vulgi sermone, cum alicui malum imprecarentur, iactatum fuit, Fiat illis sicut Midianitis.
units.tr: 326. Midianites, descendants of Abraham by Keturah, were a noble nation. Among them Moses, a fugitive from Egypt, lived in exile and married the daughter of their priest Jethro. Gideon punished them severely; hence in common speech, when people wished evil on someone, it was said: "Let it be done to them as to the Midianites."

units.la: 327. Cinæi, à Midianitis oriundi, dicti à Cinæo, Iethronis filio. Is enim vt populo per desertum eunti ductor esset, à Mose persuadetur, & victis gentibus Chananæis, inter Amalekitas sedem obtinet. Cinæorum omni tempore in Israelitas magna extiterunt merita.
units.tr: 327. Kenites, descended from the Midianites and named from Kenite, son of Jethro. For he was persuaded by Moses to be a guide to the people journeying through the wilderness, and after the Canaanite nations were conquered he obtained a dwelling among the Amalekites. The Kenites at all times rendered great services to the Israelites.

units.la: 328. Moabitæ, à Moabo Lothi F, orti, Israelitis perpetuò inimici fuerunt, vtpote quibus ex Ægypto euntibus viam & hospitia intercluserunt.
units.tr: 328. Moabites, descended from Moab, son of Lot, were always enemies of the Israelites, since they blocked their way and denied them lodging when they came out of Egypt.

units.la: 329. Ammonitæ, ab Ammone Lothi F, & ipsi hostes infensissimi Israelitarum; quibus errantibus, transitum; fesfis[?], panem & aquam non concesserunt.
units.tr: 329. Ammonites, from Ammon, son of Lot, were also the bitterest enemies of the Israelites; when they were weary and wandering, they refused them passage, bread and water.

units.la: 330. Idumæi, seu Edomitæ, posteritas Esaui, transitum negant fratribus suis, solum paternum repetentibus. De ipsorum terra ne pedis quidem vestigium Deus voluit dare Israelitis, quia eam Esauo in possessionem confirmauerat, ideoque libertatem diu tenuerunt, & reges multos fortes habuerunt. Gauisi sunt de Israelitarum infortuniis, & religione habuerunt pro ioco, eam modo probantes, modo reicientes, seruiendo nempe tempori, & victoribus gratificando. Tandem tamen, integro ferme sæculo ante Herodem, facti sunt Iudæi, abiecto deo gentis suæ Coze, ritibusque prioris idololatriæ antiquatis, & circumcisione vniuersaque Iudæorum religione admisså.
units.tr: 330. Idumeans, or Edomites, the posterity of Esau, denied passage to their brothers who sought their ancestral land. God would not give the Israelites even a footprint of their land, because he had confirmed it to Esau as a possession. Therefore they long kept their liberty and had many strong kings. They rejoiced at the misfortunes of the Israelites and treated religion as a jest, now approving it, now rejecting it, namely serving the times and currying favour with the victors. At last, however, almost a whole century before Herod, they became Jews: they abandoned the god of their nation, Qoze, the rites of their former idolatry were abolished, and they admitted circumcision and the whole religion of the Jews.

units.la: 331. Horrai, montis Seiris incolæ, inter Idumæos habitarunt. Regionem eorum, relictâ fratri Chananæâ, Efatuus occupauit.Israelitis ex Ægyptio euntibus soli præbuerunt iter, & cibum vendiderunt pecuniâ.
units.tr: 331. Horites, inhabitants of Mount Seir, dwelt among the Idumeans. Their region, left to Esau's brother, was occupied by Esau. They alone gave the Israelites a passage when they came out of Egypt, and they sold them food for money.

units.la: 332. Amalekita, nepotes Esaui, malè tractarunt Israelitas exules, & rerum omnium egenos. Nam cùm per re-gionem eorum iter facerent, extremos agminis carpserunt, & ægrotos fessosque in viis ferro sustulerunt. Moses autem eos non armis pugnando, sed precibus sanctis orando deiicit, & mandatum à Deo accipit, vt talem iniuriam inscribat fastis & monumentis, vt de tota gente, excidio & internecione, sumeretur olim supplicium. Ea victoria regi Saulo reseruata est: qui quoniam stirpitus Amalekitas nō excidit, ipse regno excidit. Agagum regem eorum Samuel frustillatim dilaniat. Tribus tandem Simeon totam illam gentem funditus deleuit.
units.tr: 332. Amalekites, grandsons of Esau, treated the exiled Israelites badly, who were needy of everything. For when they were making their way through their region, they attacked the rear of the column and with the sword cut down the sick and weary on the road. Moses, however, overthrew them not by fighting with arms but by holy prayer, and he received a command from God to inscribe such an injury in the annals and records, so that punishment would one day be exacted from the whole nation by destruction and slaughter. That victory was reserved for King Saul; but because he did not utterly destroy the Amalekites, he himself was cast out of the kingdom. Samuel hacked King Agag of theirs to pieces. Finally the tribe of Simeon utterly destroyed that whole nation.

units.la: 333. Philistini, nepotes Chami, fuerunt populus peculiariter nomini divino, & eius cultoribus infestus, negotiationibus & augurio deditus. Ipsorum Deus fuit Dagon, pubetenus homo, inferiori parte piscis; qui Græcis & Latinis est Triton. Inter eos summo in honore fuerunt gigantes, è quibus fuit Goliath.
units.tr: 333. Philistines, grandsons of Ham: a people especially hostile to the divine name and to its worshippers, given to trade and augury. Their god was Dagon, a man as far as the waist, with the lower part a fish, who is called Triton by Greeks and Latins. Among them the giants were held in the highest honour, and from them came Goliath.

units.la: 334. Ziphæi, locorum desertorum non procul à monte Carmelo accolæ, Davidem produnt Sauli.
units.tr: 334. Ziphites, inhabitants of the deserted places not far from Mount Carmel, betrayed David to Saul.

units.la: 335. Sidonij, à Sidone filio Chananis, Tyriorum vicini, studiis rei nauticæ & negotiationibus inventi, veram Dei scientiam amittunt, amissamq; fastidiunt.
units.tr: 335. Sidonians, named from Sidon, son of Canaan, neighbours of the Tyrians, invented the seafaring arts and trade; they lost the true knowledge of God and, having lost it, despised it.

units.la: 336. Tyrij, maximè nobiles inter Sytos, vixerunt longo tempore felices & inexpugnabiles.
units.tr: 336. Tyrians, the most noble among the Phoenicians, lived for a long time prosperous and impregnable.

units.la: 337. Samaritani, ab Ephraimo oriundi, à cultu veri Dei desciscunt. Vide suprà nu.214. Inter ipsos & Iudæos semper fuit capitalis dissensio.
units.tr: 337. Samaritans, descended from Ephraim, fell away from the true worship of God. See above, no. 214. Between them and the Jews there was always a deadly quarrel.

units.la: 338. Ægyptij, omnes gentes vicerunt superstitiositate; quippe qui serpentes, feles, olera, & vilissimas quasque res adorarunt. Hospites aliquando fuerunt patriarcharum, & altores populi Iudaici, instituti à Iosepho. Mutatisautem regum animis, nullum populum magis oderant quàm Iudaicum, inde à Mosis tempore vsque ad seruitutem Assyriacam, quâ multati sunt.
units.tr: 338. Egyptians, surpassed all nations in superstition; indeed they worshipped serpents, cats, herbs and the most worthless things of every kind. At one time they were hosts of the patriarchs and nourishers of the Jewish people, who had been settled by Joseph. But when the minds of their kings changed, they hated no people more than the Jewish, from the time of Moses down to the Assyrian servitude, by which they were punished.

units.la: 339. Babilonij, fuerunt primi, qui in orbe terrarum regnum possederunt. Ipsorum ciuitas antiquissima stadiorum trecentarum[?] octoginta quinque millia ambitu cōtinuit, & mirifica incrementa cepit. Vita ipsorum ita corrupta fuit omnibus deliciis, sceleribus, petulantiâ, vt extremis temporibus Roma à Iohanne apostolo & Sibyllis pingatur hac imagine.
units.tr: 339. Babylonians, were the first who possessed a kingdom in the world. Their most ancient city enclosed a circuit of three hundred and eighty-five thousand stadia, and it grew to a marvellous size. Their life was so corrupted by every luxury, wickedness and wantonness that in the last times Rome is depicted by John the apostle and the Sibyls under this image.

units.la: 340. Syri, populi circa Iudæam vndiq; circumfusi, antiquo nomine Aramæi dicti, & diuisi in Leucosyrios, Caelesyrios & Syrophenices, populo Dei omnibus temporibus sunt aduersati, & eius hostes auxiliis iuuerunt.
units.tr: 340. The Syrians, peoples scattered all round Judea, formerly called Aramaeans and divided into Leucosyrians, Caelesyrians and Syrophoenicians, have always been hostile to the people of God in every age, and have aided its enemies with their help.

units.la: 341. Arabes. Iudæis contermini, sæpe in regionem propinquam excursiones fecerunt, & latrocinia exercuerunt. Regina Arabum accessit ad Salomonem. Ipsorum coloni Nabathæi, filiis Matthathiæ, & Iudæis oppidis essis, præbuerunt hospitia, & consilio affuerant[?], tempore tristissimo.
units.tr: 341. The Arabs. Neighbours of the Jews, they often made raids into the nearby region and carried on brigandage. The queen of the Arabs came to Solomon. Their colonists, the Nabataeans, gave hospitality to the sons of Mattathias and to the Jews in their besieged towns, and stood by them with counsel in their most dismal time.

units.la: 342. Assyrij cum Iudæis bella fere continua gesserunt, cupiditate singularis imperij. Metropolis ipsorum Nineve fuit ampla trium dierum itinere.
units.tr: 342. The Assyrians waged almost continual wars with the Jews, from a desire for sole dominion. Their metropolis, Nineveh, was vast, requiring a three days' journey to cross.

units.la: 343. Ioppenses, & Iamnij, vultus quidem amicos Iudæis ostentabant, sed terra in eos committunt flagitia, inprimis Ioppenses. Iudas tamen Maccabæus hanc malitiam est vltus.
units.tr: 343. The Joppans and the Jamnites showed a friendly face to the Jews, but they committed outrages against the land and them, especially the Joppans. Judas Maccabeus nevertheless avenged this malice.

units.la: 344. Iambrij, cum Syris colludentes, Iohannem, Iudæ Maccabæi fratrem, capiunt, & ludibrio habitum obtruncant. Quam iniuriam gnauiter vltus est Ionathas frater.
units.tr: 344. The Iambrians, colluding with the Syrians, captured John, brother of Judas Maccabeus, and killed him, having made a mockery of him. His brother Jonathan avenged this injury bravely.

units.la: XII. Prosopographia, tempore ecclesiæ nascentis in N.T. talis est ex historia N.T.
units.tr: XII. Prosopography of the nascent Church in the New Testament, as drawn from the history of the New Testament.

units.la: 345. Iesus Christus, nascitur in plenitudine temporis ex Maria virgine, ex stirpe Dauidis. Genealogia ipsius naturalis describitur à Matthæo, legalis à Luca. Matthæus enim ita describit maiores Christi, vt Iacobus, qui penultimus est in istâ genealogiâ, sit pater Iosephi naturalis. Porrò Matthæus recensèt illos, ex quibus Christus ortus est secundùm carnem, vno Iosepho excepto: vt qui non fuerit naturalis pater Christi, sed putatiuus. Luca 3. verf.23. Lucas autem ita describit maiores Christi, vt Eli, qui penultimus est in istâ genealogiâ fit pater Iosephi legalis. Hîc in conspectu fit ista tabula. Dauid Maria, soror matris Domini. Eius filij ex Maria virgo. Ioseph, maritus Maria. Salome: cuius filij ex Zebedaeo Cleophas, maritus posterior Mariae, sororis matris Domini. Alphaeo, Iacobus minor seu iustus. Cleophâ Iacobus maior. Iohannes euangelista. Simeon. Iudas Thaddaeus. Ioseph iustus.
units.tr: 345. Jesus Christ is born in the fullness of time of the virgin Mary, of the stock of David. His natural genealogy is described by Matthew and his legal genealogy by Luke. Matthew so describes Christ's forefathers that James, who is second from last in that genealogy, is the natural father of Joseph. Moreover, Matthew lists those from whom Christ was born according to the flesh, with the single exception of Joseph, who was not the natural father of Christ but his putative father. Luke 3:23. Luke, however, so describes Christ's forefathers that Heli, who is second from last in that genealogy, is the legal father of Joseph. Here the following table is set out: David; Mary, sister of the mother of the Lord, whose sons by the virgin Mary [were Jesus]; Joseph, husband of Mary; Salome, whose sons by Zebedee [were James the Greater and John the Evangelist]; Cleophas, later husband of Mary, sister of the mother of the Lord, by whom [were the sons] Simeon, Judas Thaddaeus and Joseph the Just; Alphaeus, [father of] James the Less or the Just; Cleophas, [father of] James the Greater, John the Evangelist, Simeon, Judas Thaddaeus, Joseph the Just.

units.la: Porrò Matthæus recenset posteros Dauidis ex Salomone, Lucas ex Nathane. Et Christus quidem natus est ex Salomone iuxta promissionem Dei. 2.Sam.7.verf.12. & deinceps. Etsi enim regnum siue stirps regia defecit in Zedekiâ, vt patet suprà ex num.235: genus tamen Salomonis propagatum est per Iechoniam, qui genuit Sealthielem; Sealthiel verò genuit Pedaiam: Pedaia Serubabelem, qui non quidem rex, sed tamen dux populi Dei constitutus est à Cyro, & ἀρχ[?]ικὸν ἀξίωμα in stirpe Salomonis transmisit vsque ad Christum. Cæterùm quod dixi de patre Iosephi naturali & legali, hoc ita habet. Iacobus & Eli fuerunt fratres vterini, eiusdem matris, sed diuersorum patrum. Eli duâ vxore moritur sine liberis: Iacob huic ex lege Mosis semen excitauit: & è relictâ coniuge Eli suscitauit Iosephum, naturâ quidem filium suum, sed beneficio legis filium Eli.
units.tr: Moreover, Matthew reckons the descendants of David through Solomon, and Luke through Nathan. Christ was indeed born of Solomon, according to God's promise. 2 Sam. 7:12 and following. For although the royal line, or royal stock, failed in Zedekiah, as is clear above from no. 235, yet the line of Solomon was continued through Jeconiah, who begat Shealtiel; Shealtiel begat Pedaiah; Pedaiah begat Zerubbabel, who, though not indeed a king, was nevertheless appointed by Cyrus as leader of the people of God, and he transmitted the princely dignity [ἀρχικὸν ἀξίωμα] in the stock of Solomon down to Christ. As for what I have said about the natural and legal father of Joseph, the matter stands thus. Jacob and Heli were brothers of the same mother but of different fathers. Heli died without children after taking a second wife; Jacob raised up seed for him according to the law of Moses, and from the widow of Heli he raised up Joseph, who was indeed his own son by nature, but by the benefit of the law the son of Heli.

units.la: 346. Maria virgo, mater Christi, fuit non solum eiufdem tribus Iuda cum Iosepho, sed etiam ex eadem gente & cognatione, nempe Dauidica: ita vt personae a Matthaeo & Luca commemoratae, vtraque pertineant ad tribum Iudae.
units.tr: 346. The virgin Mary, mother of Christ, belonged not only to the same tribe of Judah as Joseph, but also to the same race and kindred, namely the Davidic. So that the persons mentioned by Matthew and Luke both belong to the tribe of Judah.

units.la: 347. Iosephus, fuit Mariae adiunctus quasi tutor, defensor, & testis, ut ita haberet caput, a quo regeretur & protegeretur una cum Christo filio, & assertorem pudicitiae.
units.tr: 347. Joseph was joined to Mary as a kind of guardian, protector and witness, so that she might have a head by whom she would be governed and protected, together with Christ her son, and a defender of her chastity.

units.la: 348. Zacharias, pater Iohannis, fuit sacerdos sed non summus, ex classe Abiae.
units.tr: 348. Zacharias, father of John, was a priest, but not the high priest, of the course of Abijah.

units.la: 349. Elisabetha, mater Iohannis, fuit ex filiabus Aharon, eademque cognata Mariae virginis; non quod Maria fuerit e tribu Leui, sed quia pater Elisabethae sibi iunxerat uxorem e tribu Iuda & cognatione B. virginis.
units.tr: 349. Elisabeth, mother of John, was of the daughters of Aaron, and she was also a kinswoman of the virgin Mary. Not that Mary was of the tribe of Levi, but because the father of Elisabeth had taken to wife a woman of the tribe of Judah and of the kindred of the blessed virgin.

units.la: 350. Magi ab oriente, qui Christum recens natum inuiferunt, non Arabes fuere, sed Persae, & quidem regulı, hoc est, toparchae ditionis Pe-sicae.
units.tr: 350. The Magi from the east, who came to see the newly born Christ, were not Arabs but Persians, and indeed petty rulers, that is, toparchs of the territory of Persia.

units.la: 351. Herodes, cognomento Magnus & Ascalonita, Antipatri Ascalonitae F,à Senatu Romano constituitur rex Iudae æ.Habuit decem uxores, e quibus plurimos suscepit liberos, nominatim tres filios, Archelaum, Antipam, & Philippum, inter quos ceu natu maximos, & Salomen sororem Herodis regnum est divisum, idq; ex formula testamenti, verum ita, ut filii isti non reges, sed tetrarchae fuerint appellati ab Augusto. Et Archelaus quidem successit patri in parte maxima imperii, videl. in Iudaea, qua excidit anno Christi ro[?], Viennam relegatus: Philippus autem factus est tetrarcha Ituraeae, & Antipas Galilaeae. Philippo nupta fuit Herodias, quam Antipas frater duxit uxorem, viuente adhuc Philippo. Antipae istius filii fuerunt duo Agrippae, videl. Agrippa, rex, vel potius ethnarcha siue tetrarcha Iudaeae, & Agrippa, rex, vel potius tetrarcha Chalcidicae. Prior ille Agrippa genuit filium sibi cognominem, qui differentiae causa vocatur Agrippa iunior, & fuit rex Chalcidicae, ultimus ex familia Herodiadarum. Is est, qui audiuit Paulum, Act. 25. & 26. Hic tria sunt obseruanda. Et primò quidem, Archelao Viennam relegato, Iudæa redacta est in formulam prouinciæ, ita vt ab illo tepore nullus vnquam postea Iudææ neque rex, neque ethnarcha fuerit. Quòd autem Agrippa senior & iunior appellantur non tantùm reges, sed reges quoque Iudæorum, id accipiendum est, neque de regibus, neque de Iudæis proprie dictis, hoc est, de Hierosolymitanis; sed de vulgata in Scripturis acceptione vocis rex, itemq; de adiacentibus & incorporatis Iudææ regionibus. Vera Iudæa, amoto Archelao, in formulam prouinciæ, sicuti dicebamus, redacta, Syriæ accessit, coepitque tum in eam mitti, qui vocabatur Procurator Cæsaris in Iudæâ, vel etiam Procurator Iudææ. Hucaccedit, quòd vulgus assuetum nomini regio, illud ipsis tribuerit, vtut Augustus illud ipsis ademerit. Deinde Herodes Magnus fuit Idumæus, neque tamen alienigena, sed religione Iudæus. Nam Idumæi integro fere seculo ante facti sunt Iudæi, hoc est, amplexi sunt religionem Iudæorum, fratrum suorum, reste Iosepho lib.13. c.17. Denique Herodes Ascalonita fuit alter ille Pharao, qui promulgauit & procurauit infanticidium illud, de quo Matth.2: Herodes Antipas è medio sustulit Iohannem, & irrisit Christum in passione: Herodes Agrippa senior de vita sustulit Iacobum, & carceri inclusit Petrum.
units.tr: 351. Herod, surnamed the Great and the Ascalonite, son of Antipater the Ascalonite, was appointed king of Judea by the Roman Senate. He had ten wives, by whom he had very many children, and especially three sons, Archelaus, Antipas and Philip. The kingdom was divided among them, and Salome, Herod's sister, as well, the eldest being given the greatest share, and this according to the form of his will; but these sons were not called kings but tetrarchs by Augustus. Archelaus indeed succeeded his father in the greater part of the realm, namely in Judea, from which he was removed in the year [of the birth] of Christ [blank], and banished to Vienne. Philip was made tetrarch of Ituraea, and Antipas of Galilee. Herodias was married to Philip, and Antipas, his brother, took her as his wife while Philip was still alive. The sons of this Antipas were the two Agrippas, namely Agrippa, king, or rather ethnarch or tetrarch of Judea, and Agrippa, king, or rather tetrarch of Chalcis. The former Agrippa begat a son named after himself, who, to distinguish him, is called Agrippa the Younger, and he was king of Chalcis, the last of the family of the Herodians. It is he who heard Paul, Acts 25 and 26. Three things are to be observed here. First, after Archelaus was banished to Vienne, Judea was reduced to the form of a province, so that from that time onward no one was ever again either king or ethnarch of Judea. As for the fact that Agrippa the elder and the younger are called not only kings but kings of the Jews, this must be understood neither of kings nor of Jews in the strict sense, that is, of the Jerusalemites, but in the common usage of the word king in the Scriptures, and likewise of the regions adjoining and incorporated with Judea. True Judea, after Archelaus was removed, was reduced to the form of a province, as I was saying, and was attached to Syria, and then began to be sent a man called the Procurator of Caesar in Judea, or even the Procurator of Judea. To this is added that the common people, accustomed to the name of king, gave that title to them, although Augustus had taken it from them. Second, Herod the Great was an Idumean, yet not a foreigner, but a Jew in religion. For the Idumeans had become Jews nearly a whole century before, that is, they had embraced the religion of the Jews, their brothers, as Josephus rightly says, book 13, chapter 17. Lastly, Herod the Ascalonite was that other Pharaoh, who issued and carried out that massacre of infants of which we read in Matthew 2. Herod Antipas removed John from the midst, and mocked Christ in his passion. Herod Agrippa the elder took Jacob's life and imprisoned Peter.

units.la: 352. Iohan.Baptista, natus ex coniugio Zachariæ & Elisabethæ, similí coniugio Abrahami & Sarae, vixit austeram vitam, vt qui pœnitentiam prædicabat, habitum pœnitentiæ præ se ferret. Docuit in deserto, hoc est, montanâ illâ regione, in quâ parentes ipsius habitabant, Luc.1. v.40. Neque enim potuit, vel debuit docere in loco tali, quem nemo inhabitabat. Desertum itaque in historiâ euangelicâ non significat locum ἀοίκητον, inhabitabilem, sed saltuosum & montanum, in quo greges pascantur: qualis erat ille Iudææ tractus, vbi sita Chebron, & aliæ vrbes. Porrò Iohannes fuit præcursor Christi fidelis & felix, primusque martyr noui testamenti incipientis.
units.tr: 352. John the Baptist, born of the marriage of Zacharias and Elisabeth, as Abraham and Sarah were of a similar marriage, lived a austere life, as one who preached repentance and bore the habit of repentance before him. He taught in the desert, that is, in that mountainous region in which his parents dwelt. Luke 1:40. For he could not, nor ought he, to teach in such a place, which no one inhabited. Therefore "desert" in the gospel history does not signify an uninhabitable place [ἀοίκητον], but a wooded and mountainous place in which flocks are pastured, such as that tract of Judea was where Hebron and other towns are situated. Moreover, John was the faithful and fortunate forerunner of Christ, and the first martyr of the New Testament that was beginning.

units.la: 353. Duodecim apostoli, fuerunt indiuidui comites Christi, & postea, duobus exceptis, doctores œcumenici. Ex iis Petrus & Andreas, Iacobus & Iohannes, omnium primò sunt vocati. Quò pertinet obseruatio Patrum, Christum vocationem suorum apostolorum inchoasse à binis fratribus, Petri scil. & Andreæ ; quemadmodum olim ad ministerium legis Moses & Aharon simul vocati sunt. Cur verò Petrus Andreæ fratri, & cæteris apostolis est præ的latus? Resp. Omninò debuit aliquis ordo esse inter apostolos, & is quidem non ex merito ipsorum, sed ex beneplacito vocantis. Cùm enim vocabantur, omnes erat pares. Quare omne id, quod Petrus est consecutus, ex merâ Christi vocantis & donantis gratiâ, non ex suo merito accepit. Vt verum sit in Petro, quod verum est in omnibus electis; Christum illi sua beneficia sine pretio védidisse, quod aiunt Esa. 55. verf. 1. Sed breuiter videamus de singulis apostolis. Petrus, alio nomine Simon, fuit vehemens & acer, primò strenuus confessor Christi, postea timidus defertor, dominum suum abnegans. Recollegit tam nseper[?] Dei gratiam, & post ascensionem Christi, euangelium longè lateque propagauit, factus apostolus Iudæorum. Martyrii coronam accepit Romæ, sub Nerone. Andreas, frater Petri natu maior, docuit in Scythiâ, Sogdianâ, Æthiopiâ interiori, & aliis locis, sub Vespasiano crucifixus, Patris urbe Achaiæ.Iacobus, filius Zebedæi,cognomento Maior, decollatus est ab Herode Agrippâ, adeoque breue admodum habuit apostolatus sui curriculum. Iohannes, Iacobi frater, apostolus & euangelista, fuit relegatus Epheso in Pathmum, indeque Ephesum reuersus, ibi apoplexiâ obiit. Philippus, prædicauit in Scythiâ & peragratâ Asiâ minori affixus est cruci cum duabus filiabus. Bartholomæus, prædicauit in Lycaoniâ, Syriâ, Indiâ, & Armeniâ, vbi iussu regis Astyagis excoriatus est. Thomas, cognomento Didymus, docuit in Æthiopiâ, Indiâ, & Taprobanâ. Matthæus, publicanus, alio nomine Leui, filius Alphæi, prædicauit & scripsit euangelium. Iacobus, filius Alphæi, cognomento Minor, Iustus, Oblias, & frater (id est cognatus) Domini, rexit potissimum ecclesiam Hierosolymitanam, & scripsit epistolam catholicam. Iudas Lebbæus, siue Thaddæus, frater vterinus Simonis Cana-nitæ, & Iacobi Alphæi, prædicauit euangelium in Mesopotamiâ, Ponto, & Persidè, scripsitque epistolam. Simon Cananites, siue Zelotes, annuntiauit euangelium in Ægypto, Libyâ, Persiâ, & regionibus ad occidentalem Oceanum. Inde vero reuersus Hierosolymam, fratri Iacobo successit in episcopatu. Meminei is nomen Cananites, non esse [?]ἰθνικὸν, sed [?]ἐγχωμιαστικὸν: quia Lucas illud interpretatur [?]ζηλωτὴν. Iudas Iscariotes, proditor Christi auarus & immanis, se ipse suspendit. In locum eius successit Matthias, qui fuit ex lxx discipulis Christi. Memineris hic, vulgare fuisse Hebræis, binomines & trinomines esse.
units.tr: 353. The twelve apostles were the individual companions of Christ, and afterwards, with two excepted, teachers of the whole world. Of these, Peter and Andrew, James and John were called first of all. To this belongs the observation of the Fathers that Christ began the calling of his apostles with two brothers, namely Peter and Andrew, just as of old Moses and Aaron were called together to the ministry of the law. But why was Peter placed before Andrew his brother and the other apostles? Answer: there ought necessarily to have been some order among the apostles, and this indeed not from their merit but from the good pleasure of the one calling. For when they were called, all were equal. Therefore whatever Peter obtained, he received from the mere grace of Christ calling and giving, not from his own merit. So that what is true of Peter is true of all the elect: Christ sold his benefits to them without price, as Isaiah 55:1 says. But let us briefly look at each of the apostles. Peter, otherwise called Simon, was vehement and keen, first a vigorous confessor of Christ, afterwards a timid deserter, denying his Lord. Yet he recovered by God's grace, and after Christ's ascension he spread the gospel far and wide, having been made apostle to the Jews. He received the crown of martyrdom at Rome under Nero. Andrew, the elder brother of Peter, taught in Scythia, Sogdiana, inner Ethiopia and other places, and was crucified under Vespasian at Patras, a city of Achaia. James, son of Zebedee, surnamed the Greater, was beheaded by Herod Agrippa, and so had a very short course of apostleship. John, brother of James, apostle and evangelist, was banished from Ephesus to Patmos, and returning from there to Ephesus, he died there of apoplexy. Philip preached in Scythia, and after traversing Asia Minor was fixed to the cross with two daughters. Bartholomew preached in Lycaonia, Syria, India and Armenia, where by order of King Astyages he was flayed. Thomas, surnamed Didymus, taught in Ethiopia, India and Taprobane. Matthew, a publican, otherwise called Levi, son of Alphaeus, preached and wrote the gospel. James, son of Alphaeus, surnamed the Less, the Just, Oblias, and brother (that is, kinsman) of the Lord, chiefly governed the church of Jerusalem and wrote a catholic epistle. Judas Lebbaeus, or Thaddaeus, full brother of Simon the Canaanite and of James son of Alphaeus, preached the gospel in Mesopotamia, Pontus and Persia, and wrote an epistle. Simon the Canaanite, or the Zealot, proclaimed the gospel in Egypt, Libya, Persia and the regions toward the western ocean. Returning from there to Jerusalem, he succeeded his brother James in the episcopate. I remember that the name Canaanite is not gentile [ἐθνικόν] but honorific [ἐγχωμιαστικόν], because Luke translates it as zealot [ζηλωτήν]. Judas Iscariot, the greedy and savage betrayer of Christ, hanged himself. In his place succeeded Matthias, who was one of the seventy disciples of Christ. Remember here that it was common among the Hebrews to have two names and three names.

units.la: 354. Paulus, fuit apostolus gentium, ita tamen, vt quoties data est occasio, vim muneris sui extenderet etiam erga Iudæos. Constat enim, ipsum in synagogis eorum studiose prædicasse Christum, & ad eosdem diuinam illam epistolam scripsisse. Sic etsi Petrus dicatur & fuerit apostolus Iudæorum: tamen id non impediuit, quin etiam ad gentes ipsius apostolatus porrigeretur. Vter vero horum apostolorum fuit inferior? Resp. Fuerunt pares omnes apostoli dignitate, vt ait Chrysostomus: at donis & laboribus fuerunt impares. Et hoc sensu Paulum non sine causâ præposuerimus Petro.
units.tr: Paul was the apostle of the Gentiles, yet in such a way that whenever an occasion arose he extended the scope of his office to the Jews as well. It is established that he diligently preached Christ in their synagogues and wrote that divine epistle to them. So although Peter is said to have been, and was, the apostle of the Jews, this did not prevent his apostleship from reaching also to the Gentiles. Which of these apostles was the inferior? Answer: All the apostles were equal in dignity, as Chrysostom says, but they were unequal in gifts and labours. And in this sense we have not without reason placed Paul before Peter.

units.la: 355. Marcus, euangelista, cognomine Iohannes, Petri discipulus & nepos ex sorore, & Barnabæ consobrinus, à Paulo & Barnabâ ad ministerium euangelii assumtus est, & ipsis deserris [?]hinc inde prædicauit; tandem factus episcopus ecclesiæ Alexandrinæ, finitimis locis circumquaque ab Ægypto vsque ad Pentapolin docuit euangelium.
units.tr: Mark, the evangelist, surnamed John, was a disciple of Peter, his nephew through his sister, and cousin of Barnabas.
